# KB: File structure — per-file operating essays

Moved VERBATIM out of CLAUDE.md (tier-2 pass). Each `### path` section is that file's full operating essay — invariants, incidents, gotchas. **READ the entry BEFORE modifying the file; UPDATE it in the same commit when behavior changes.**

### server.js

server.js              — BOOTSTRAP + WIRING ONLY (~1910 lines since the 2.325.0 拆分; the arch suite RATCHETS it ≤2100). **`refreshWebuiPids()` IS A HOT PATH, NOT BOOTSTRAP (2026-09-09 r2):** it rebuilds `webuiPids` from each pty-wrapper meta file PLUS that wrapper's direct children, and it runs IN-BAND on every kill (`src/ws-handler.js`, between `activeSessions.delete(...)` and `broadcastActiveSessions()`), 3 s after every create (`src/ws-create.js`) and twice from boot-restore. It asks `cli-identity.readChildPids` — **never a child process per session**: the `execFileSync('pgrep', ['-P', childPid])` it replaces blocked the loop **9,180.6 ms for 61 sessions at 1,560 MB RSS** (measured; the identical 244 pids come back in 2.3 ms), which is the Terminate+Resume that blanked userW's chat window for ~30 s. server.js is in BOTH halves of the test-architecture §45 spawn census — half (b) resolves its file set by looking up where `refreshWebuiPids` is DEFINED, so moving this function keeps its enforcement — and the four surviving spawns in this file (the auto-update `git pull` / `npm install` / `npm run build`, and `resolveCmd`'s `/usr/bin/which`) each carry a BOOT-ONLY reason there. Everything mechanical lives in src/server/* `create(deps)` factory modules: usage-pool-engine (pool auto-switch/estimator/anchors/sealed orders), session-stdout (setupSessionPty = caps.streamProtocol → src/server/stdout/ consumer lookup + attach since S5, plus onExit death classification / attachToDtach / session-meta store), boot-restore (migrations+restoreSessions+R6 reopen+keeper re-adopt), session-brain (parity comparator+sbSeenFirst+claudeSideEffects), account-usage-routes, mounts-plugins-wiring, cli-env (X display/adapters/CLI probes/model registry), dial-pairing, exit-routes, ops-routes (version/self-update/maintenance), incident-wiring, sysinfo-wiring, goal-sync, agent-tool-generators. server.js destructures each factory's exports under the SAME names, so grep-by-name still lands. Late-boot singletons cross as lazy getters; mutable `let` state as explicit `get*()`. **The boot auto-update (`git pull --ff-only` + install + build, before `listen`) is SKIPPED for a THROWAWAY root (2.369.163 integration):** `throwawayRoot` = the code lives under `os.tmpdir()` or /tmp — the hookRegistrationSafe rule, spelled inline because it runs before any module is wired. Every suite's scratch worktree used to fetch from origin into the SHARED .git on every boot (0.5–0.9 s boot without the pull, 2.5–15 s with it; a heavy RED). Pinned by test-incident (the `[auto-update] skipped: throwaway/temp server root` line + no `pull --ff-only`). `NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` still disables it anywhere.

### data/bin/editor/code

data/bin/editor/code   — Fake "code" script for Ctrl+G (generated by server; moved OUT of data/bin in 2.267.0 — data/bin is PATH-prepended into every local session and the fake `code` shadowed real VS Code there; EDITOR= stays the absolute path, boot unlinks a stale data/bin/code; remote layout was already ~/.vibespace/editor/). **ANCHOR RULE (2.267.2 regression, self-caught): ONLY `code` lives in EDITOR_DIR — every OTHER generator (vibespace-status/vibespace-hook.mjs/hook-register) and USAGE_STATUSLINE_CMD anchors on AGENT_BIN_DIR (= data/bin, the PATH dir); the 2.267.0 move dragged them all into editor/ because they shared the constant (tools off PATH + statusline pointing at a missing file + global hook registration rewritten). Before changing a shared path constant, grep every consumer. data/bin/editor/ is gitignored (generated; tracked generated files block self-update — 2.111.26 class).**

### data/bin/vibespace-hook.mjs

data/bin/vibespace-hook.mjs — Dual-harness hook (SessionStart→task context OR a baseline tools intro for no-task sessions, UserPromptSubmit→first-prompt context + status-override notices + per-turn micro-reminder, Stop→bookkeeping nudge (2.79.0, CLAUDE-ONLY registration): calls GET /api/agent/stop-check and emits {decision:'block', reason} when the server says the board state is stale — the agent gets ONE follow-up mini-turn to set status/mirror asks/log progress, gated by stop_hook_active (never loops), server-side staleness+cooldown thresholds (agents.stopNudgeStaleMinutes/CooldownMinutes, defaults 10/30min, clamped 1-240/2-720 — 2.89.0; an EXPLICIT 0 = every-stop mode: 0 stale = always stale, 0 cooldown = none — 2.210.0 user request; stop_hook_active/nudgeTurnActive still cap it at ONE mini-turn per user turn); codex's equivalent rides codex-chat-wrapper's turn/completed (maybeStopNudge → synthetic <vibespace-reminder> turn, nudgeTurnActive guard) since the app-server has no blockable Stop in JSON-RPC mode; generated at startup; env-gated no-op only when VIBESPACE_API/TOKEN are absent — a MISSING VIBESPACE_TASK_ID no longer no-ops (2.38.0), so any VibeSpace session still learns `vibespace-status`; emits ONLY nested hookSpecificOutput). Registered idempotently for BOTH events in ~/.claude/settings.json + ~/.codex/hooks.json by ensureAgentHooks — only the vibespace entry is ever touched. **TEMP-SERVER GUARD (2.225.1, real incident): a server running from under os.tmpdir() skips ALL global hook writes (register AND strip; hookRegistrationSafe) — a /tmp worktree smoke server once rewrote the global hook command to its throwaway path, and after cleanup every hook errored MODULE_NOT_FOUND for two days (the CLI snapshots hook config per session, so healing the file doesn't reach running sessions). Any test harness that boots server.js should also set VIBESPACE_SKIP_AGENT_HOOKS=1 (all four worktree smokes do); VIBESPACE_FORCE_AGENT_HOOKS=1 overrides.** **INTEGRATION MASTER SWITCH (2.190.0, settings category "Integration"): `agents.vibespaceIntegration` default ON; OFF = the model gets a pristine CLI. SCOPE = AGENT-VISIBLE integration ONLY (2.190.1, user decision): model-invisible plumbing is EXEMPT — the usage statusline, billing/account env, Ctrl+G editor, keeper transport all keep working either way. PER-FEATURE toggles under it (2.211.0, user request '注入context但不给ask/progress'): `agents.contextInjection` (group payloads/diffs; per-group injectContext stays the finer grain) + `agents.toolStatus`/`toolAsk`/`toolTask` — a disabled tool is neither TAUGHT (sessionToolsIntro()/renderContext's _toolsSectionParts/per-turn reminder/stop-nudge steps all compose from enabledTools(); teaching a refusing command trains dead ends) nor SERVED (its write endpoints 403 with skip-and-continue-do-not-retry guidance); toolStatus off also silences the stop-check arbiter (it is keyed on status staleness); contextInjection off falls back to the baseline tools intro; reads (GET /api/agent/task = `vibespace-task show`) stay governed by the master, not toolTask. Route smoke: scripts/test-tool-toggles.mjs (21 asserts).** Hook entries stripped live on toggle (persistence writeSettings' `onSettingsWrite` callback → stripAgentHookEntries; boot re-checks the setting so a flip-while-down converges; the boot ensureAgentHooks call is DEFERRED until after setupPersistence so the setting is readable), new spawns get NO VIBESPACE_API/tools-PATH/remote-prelude (keeper still ships; VIBESPACE_SESSION_TOKEN stays for Ctrl+G editor auth, inert alone since every consumer guards on api+token), and agent-routes gates every model-visible CONTENT response for pre-toggle sessions too: the three deliveries return empty (prompt-context also consumes-and-DROPS pending status-override notices — deferring them injected stale reminders on re-enable) and GET /api/agent/task 403s (it returns the same steering substance; `vibespace-task show` must not bypass the pristine state) while WRITE endpoints stay live. Both Install routes (local /api/agent-hooks/install AND host /api/hosts/:id/agent-tools/install) refuse while OFF; the Manage-Agents host row shows the residue + keeps Remove as cleanup. Dial spawns drop the `$HOME/.vibespace/bin` PATH segment too (leftover tools from earlier ON spawns must not be name-resolvable). Distinct from the data/.agent-hooks-optout marker (manual Manage-Agents Remove) — the setting never writes the marker, and re-enable does NOT override it. E2E: scripts/test-integration-toggle.mjs. vibespace-hook-register.mjs = self-locating installer distributed to remote hosts (P3); its `--uninstall` mode (2.129.0) strips ONLY our entry from the remote configs (foreign hooks untouched) — the Manage-Agents remote Remove path. **SSH→DIAL GRADUATION (2.248.0, B-6640; **AUTOMATIC since 2.311.0** — `hosts.onSshConnected` fires after every successful ssh device connect and the server graduates in the background. Gates, each of them a way to do something the operator did not ask for: setting `agentd.autoGraduate` (default on) + an operator-declared `agentd.publicUrl` (it must NEVER self-publish this instance to the relay — that side effect is the operator's choice) + per-machine `autoGraduate:false` + one attempt/machine/6h; failures serverNotice and leave the machine on ssh. The install half is `graduateHostToDial()`, shared by the button and the auto path. Test: scripts/test-auto-graduate.mjs): an ssh machine can install the daemon as a persistent service and DIAL BACK over ws — `POST /api/hosts/:id/graduate-dial` (`{serverUrl|viaRelay}`, `{remove:true}` rolls back). The record keeps `transport:'ssh'` and gains `deviceId`+`dialTokenHash`+`dialRoot`; `_deviceConnect` prefers the live dial link and falls through to ssh on ANY failure (never worse than before), `findByDeviceId` falls back to non-dial records so dial-in auth resolves, `onDialIn` evicts a cached ssh dm, `list()` exposes `graduated`/`dialLive`. INVARIANTS: ssh stays the bootstrap+rescue channel (never removed); the base URL is explicit>publicUrl>relay and the MACHINE is asked whether it can reach it BEFORE anything installs (unreachable ⇒ abort, stay pure-ssh — a daemon that can never dial in is worse than no daemon); `dialRoot` must mirror the installer's own derivation byte-for-byte (hostname-only + `tr -cd 'A-Za-z0-9.-'`) or removal tears down the wrong directory; removal always clears the local record even if the host is dead. E2E: scripts/test-graduate-dial.mjs (10 asserts against a real host; needs an ssh reverse tunnel so the host can reach the throwaway server). REMOTE-TEST GOTCHAS the harness encodes: server.js honours NO data-dir env (a worktree's own data/ IS the isolation), an inherited VIBESPACE_PASSWORD turns auth on and 401s everything, a worktree is at HEAD so uncommitted changes must be copied in, and `pkill -f vibespace-agentd` over ssh matches its OWN command line and kills the session (use `pgrep -f "[v]ibespace-agentd" | xargs -r kill`).** **BOUNDED DEVICE CONNECT (2.246.2/2.247.0, B-fa6f — userN's flapping H200s): `hosts.deviceBounded(id, connectMs=6000)` races device() against a deadline for every READ-ONLY/interactive data-plane consumer (~26 sites: discovery/RemoteFs/dirComplete/slab sync/usage harvest/mount heal/ports/exit) — the connect ladder runs up to ~2.7min and on a lossy path where TCP opens but the ssh banner hangs (ConnectTimeout only bounds the TCP connect, verified live) every surface sat on it BEFORE its own ssh fallback. THREE INVARIANTS (adversarial-review-hardened, do not regress): ① session-ESTABLISHING consumers keep the FULL ladder or ≥15s — findKeeperFor (adopt-vs-respawn: a deadline reads as 'no live keeper' → writer sweep SIGTERMs the healthy claude), _hostShell (accountsStatus rides it inside CREATE's linked/host-held rescue), homeDir (feeds the create cwd default, B-0d70 shape); ② the race OBSERVES the loser promise (p.catch(()=>{})) — an abandoned ladder's late rejection is an unhandledRejection = process crash on Node≥15; ③ device() DEDUPES in-flight connects per id (_deviceInflight → _deviceConnect) — without it every timed-out probe stacked another 13×ssh ladder under a 5s-polling sidebar. Any hosts-like TEST MOCK must also implement deviceBounded (two suites broke on the missing method). **B-218d FIXED in 2.247.1-2.247.3** (2.247.2: EXPLICIT-host ssh resumes probe findKeeperFor too — before, only host-inference and dial did, so a sidebar resume with the host selected always swept; 2.247.3: findKeeperFor rewritten — the ssh leg scanned only legacy run/ and NEVER saw agentd sessions, and grep-in-state-json only matches RESUMED spawns (--resume embeds the cid) — now ONE scan over both stores + a childPid→~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json lock leg for fresh spawns, returning {sid, kind} so the consumer routes to the right attach binary): findKeeperFor's agentd pipe sids are tagged `keeperKind:'agentd'` and the ssh branch adopts them via the attach-cli with a NO-spawn-spec cfg (the dial branch's contract) — before this, they were fed to the legacy keeper binary (which only reads ~/.vibespace/run) so the 2.218.0 keeper-attach optimization silently never worked over ssh and every such resume degraded to sweep+respawn. Legacy keeper sids (client discovery K lines) keep the old runTail; provisioning failure degrades to it too.** **NODE RESOLUTION (2.244.2-2.244.4, userN's Novita chicken-and-egg): hook entries register with the ABSOLUTE process.execPath (hooks run via /bin/sh with claude's PATH — nvm-managed node never resolves there, and claude is a native binary), and ALL FOUR register invocation sites (ssh prelude / dial install / manual Install / Remove) run a POSIX node finder (PATH → newest nvm → common paths) then EXPORT the found node dir onto the session PATH — a bare `node` invocation of the register silently no-op'd on dash hosts, so the fix could never apply itself AND every #!/usr/bin/env node agent tool was dead there. Any new remote code path invoking node must use the finder, never bare `node`.**

### data/bin/vibespace-task

data/bin/vibespace-task — Agent task-reporting CLI (STATIC tracked file, not generated — inline template-in-template escaping was unmaintainable): show [--full]/progress "summary" [--detail]/backlog/backlog-add/backlog-done/backlog-drop → /api/agent/task* (scoped to the session's own context task). **progress SUCCESS OUTPUT reminds the agent (2.210.0, the vibespace-ask 2.111.21 pattern): the activity log is agent-facing — deliverables (URLs/paths/results) must ALSO go in the chat reply (real pattern: agent logged a URL via progress and ended the turn without saying it).** **CHECKLIST REMOVED (2.121.0, user decision):** `plan-check/plan-uncheck/plan-add` are gone — a group-level list of agent WORK ITEMS never made sense (those live at the SESSION level = the agent's own todo list, surfaced as the card's Steps). The subcommands now print a redirect; `/api/agent/task-plan` answers old CLI copies (remote hosts) with 410 + guidance; stored `plan` arrays stay DORMANT in data/task-groups.json (never rendered/written; update() ignores plan patches; config-bundle import passes them through). **BACKLOG ADDED (2.122.0; CLAIM MODEL 2.123.0 — a DIFFERENT concept on the same shelf):** the group's PARKING LOT for NON-immediate items (deferred user decisions, "later" work; item = {**id: stable `B-xxxx`**, text, detail?, status open|done|dropped, **claimedBy: [session keys]**, addedBy/At, resolvedBy/At}); agents park via `backlog-add` when the user defers something (parking AUTO-CLAIMS for the caller) and are taught to NEVER start parked items unasked. Refs everywhere = id / 1-based OPEN-list index / unique substring; **the id travels** — the user copies it from the viewer and hands it to ANY member agent ("看一下 backlog B-ab12"), which runs `backlog <id>` (full item view, works on resolved items) and `backlog-claim <id>`. **INJECTION IS SUMMARY-ONLY + TARGETED (user directives): the hook never dumps the backlog** — renderContext gets `sessionKey` and emits a compact reminder block ONLY for open items THAT session CLAIMED (+ a one-line "N open — `vibespace-task backlog`" pointer otherwise); change events (PARKED/RESOLVED/DROPPED/CLAIMED/UNCLAIMED/reworded/REMOVED) ride the diff updates but reach ONLY sessions that created or claimed the item — diff matching is by the stable id (text edit ⇒ "reworded", not REMOVED+NEW). TASK.md/`show` carry the full open list with ids+claimants. One-time seed: dormant plan's unchecked items → open backlog items; id + creator-auto-claim backfill for pre-2.123.0 items (constructor, idempotent). **SUMMARY+DETAIL split (2.69.0):** progress entries carry a one-line `note` (what everyone sees inline — board rows, injected context marked `†`) + optional `detail` (≤6000 chars; TASK.md renders it as an indented blockquote, `show --full` prints it, the board's Activity rows expand on click) — this keeps the byte-budgeted injection dense without losing information. session-status records gained the same: `reason` = one-liner on chips, `detail` (≤2000) shown in Session Properties + `vibespace-status show` **PRIORITY (2.369.154):** `backlog-add "item" [--detail] [--priority high|normal|low]` and `backlog-edit <id> [--text] [--detail] [--priority]` (the server refuses a value outside the set by name, exit 1); `backlog` prints the list IN THE SERVER'S ORDER (sortBacklog — this static file ships to checkout-less hosts and never re-sorts, so its numbers stay the route's) with `!` high / `↓` low before the id and a `(you)` / `(you + N others)` / `(claimed by N)` / `(unclaimed)` tail (GET task's `you`); `backlog <id>` prints the priority. **A `#` is the number in the list the session was LAST SHOWN (2.369.154 r2):** the route remembers the ids it served to each session's GET task and resolves a number against them (a later add by anyone never moves what `backlog-done 3` means; a since-resolved item is refused, nothing changed); `backlog-done/-drop` print `resolved [B-xxxx] <text>` from the server's echo; the usage steers mutating verbs to ids. Gate: test-backlog-priority. **THE CLEANUP NUDGE (2.369.154):** `backlog-add` / `backlog-edit` / `backlog-claim` print the server's `nudge.text` on its own stdout line prefixed `note:` (the `note: ALSO claimed by` convention; exit code stays 0) when the answer carries one — never on done / drop / unclaim. Gate: test-backlog-nudge §4 (the real CLI over loopback + source pins with a cut-copy control).

### data/bin/vibespace-ask

data/bin/vibespace-ask — Agent CLI for the GLOBAL USER-TODO inbox (2.65.0, STATIC tracked): files items the USER must act on (decision/input/review) → POST /api/agent/user-todo (vsst_ scoped to own session). `"text" [--detail] [--urgency]` / list / resolve <id|text>; `help|-h|--help` and any flag-looking first arg print usage instead of filing (2.76.0 — a real agent filed the literal item "--help"); idempotent re-file by same text; the SUCCESS OUTPUT reminds the agent (2.111.21) that the inbox is only a notification mirror — the full content must ALSO go in the chat reply (real pattern: agents filed and ended the turn silently). **Semantics (2.76.1, user directive): MIRROR every chat question** — whenever an agent asks the user anything in chat / ends a turn waiting on them / sets needs-input|blocked|review, it must ALSO file the item (the user is often not watching that window), and the moment the user answers ANYWHERE (chat counts) the agent resolves it itself — taught in all three surfaces (SESSION_TOOLS_INTRO, renderContext tools section, the CLI's own usage text); taught in SESSION_TOOLS_INTRO + renderContext; distributed to remote hosts like the other tools

### data/bin/vibespace-status

data/bin/vibespace-status — Agent status tool (GENERATED at startup like data/bin/code — NEVER git-track it: tracking it dirtied the tree every boot and blocked `git pull --ff-only` in self-update (real incident 2.111.26); gitignored (NOTE: .gitignore has NO inline comments — a `path  # comment` line becomes the whole pattern and never matches, which silently re-tracked it once) and update.sh resets any regenerated tracked data/bin file before pulling. GENERATOR-TEMPLATE GOTCHA (P0 2.111.29): a shell example ending a single-quoted JS template string with `\\` rendered as `\'` → escaped the closing quote → every generated file was a SyntaxError and the whole CLI crashed on 2.111.24-28 — never end a JS template string with a bare backslash. WAITING STATES REQUIRE COMPLETE REASONS (2.111.24): blocked/needs-input/review need BOTH --reason (board chip) AND --detail (full context) — CLI pre-flight (show-lookup grace for same-state urgency tweaks) + agent-route both reject otherwise; done/working exempt; setting a waiting state prints a point-of-use reminder to also say it in chat + mirror via vibespace-ask)

### data/bin/vibespace-usage

data/bin/vibespace-usage — PASSIVE usage capture (STATIC tracked file, not generated; 2.60.0). A `statusLine` hook injected via `--settings` into LOCAL CLAUDE TERMINAL sessions only (2.62.0: the ws-handler injection is gated `backend==='claude'` — only the claude CLI understands `--settings`; un-gated it rode on `zsh -l` and codex spawns too, making every shell terminal (incl. the Manage-Agents Update/Login helpers) and local codex terminal exit instantly as "terminated"; NOT gated by the Integration master switch — 2.190.1 user decision: the switch scopes to AGENT-VISIBLE integration only, and the statusline is model-invisible plumbing) — the CLI feeds it the payload's `rate_limits` (5h/7d used_percentage+reset, "only after first API response" — and NOTHING else: model-scoped buckets like the Fable weekly cap are NOT in the statusline payload, verified vs the 2.1.206 payload builder) which it writes to data/usage-cache/<accountKey>.json (throttle 8s; **PRESERVES `scopedWeekly`/`scopedFetchedAt` from the existing file** — 2.70.0, clobbering them to [] every write is what made Fable vanish from the quota popup) + passes through the user's own statusline. Also harvests `model.id` → data/usage-cache/__models__.json (passive model discovery). ZERO Anthropic calls — this is why VibeSpace makes no background /api/oauth/usage poll by default (that off-CLI fixed-cadence sub-token call is the #1 ban trigger — see §ban-safety on accounts.js). Chat/stream-json has no statusline → those accounts show last-known. **THE ACCOUNT KEY IS THE LINK, RESOLVED PER WRITE, ONE REQUEST BEHIND IT (2026-09-07 + r3).** `VIBESPACE_ACCOUNT_KEY` is fixed at SPAWN, so a hot-switched pooled session filed every later reading under the member it STARTED on; ws-create also ships `VIBESPACE_ACCOUNT_LINK` (the credential SYMLINK the CLI reads) and `accountKey()` readlinks it. But the payload's `rate_limits` is the CLI's LAST API response — made with the credentials the link pointed at BEFORE a re-point — so resolving the link alone honoured a switch one request EARLY and the old member's numbers landed on the new one, stamped `fetchedAt: now`, where the anchor sweep turns any usage-cache write into ground truth (the B-b3cd odometer-flap class on the write path). The server's twin pins the slot for the TURN; a statusline has no turn, so it pins on the NUMBERS: a `.slot-<session_id>` sidecar beside the cache (deliberately no `.json` — every usage-cache scanner filters on that extension) holds `{key, fp}` for the last payload OBSERVED (updated even when the 8s throttle skips the write — a payload seen under the old target is still evidence about which credentials produced it), and while the link has MOVED but the fingerprint has NOT, the reading is left where it is. The first differing payload is the first one the new credentials produced. A session with no link writes no state file at all (it cannot switch under itself). **2026-09-08 — it asks the SHARED rule, and it had two defects of its own (round 3, reproduced).** The sidecar now records `{key, fp, win, at}` and calls the mirrored `decideLagShadow`, so it can also answer the case the fingerprint clause could not: a payload whose WINDOW is the previous slot's even though the numbers moved. **(a) It must hand that rule a RE-POINT age, and it was handing it an OBSERVATION age.** `st.at` dates the last render under the old slot, which necessarily PRECEDES the re-point that ended it, so it systematically overstates — and one ordinary render of an IDLE pooled terminal (30 min since its redraw, link re-pointed a second earlier) answered `shadow-expired` and filed the previous member's 96 % onto the low-usage one, second false pool switch and all, in a shape master's unconditional r3 rule had protected. The pool's re-point MINTS the symlink (`repointPoolSymlink` = symlink-to-temp + rename), so `fs.lstatSync(VIBESPACE_ACCOUNT_LINK).mtimeMs` IS the re-point instant (measured: 7200 s on an untouched link, 0.001 s straight after); unreadable or future-dated ⇒ `null` ⇒ UNKNOWN, which does not expire. `st.at` stays as forensics. **(b) It was the one value producer with NO window guard** — the engine guards every write and this file, at up to 8 renders a minute per account, guarded none: every path that reaches the write without a shadow (no link, unreadable link, re-point past the horizon, a payload the windows cannot place) wrote whatever `accountKey()` resolved. It now runs the mirrored `decideReadingTarget` against its own `establishedWindows()` (keyed off the CACHE FILES, like the engine's), re-filing onto the one matching account and otherwise REFUSING — writing nothing anywhere and recording the reason in `.window-refused.ndjson` beside the cache (no `.json`, per-day shard on overflow). A single shipped file has no identity-group table, so an org-merged login reads as TWO matches and is refused rather than re-filed: the conservative direction, and the server's guard still sees every later reading. **2026-09-09 r2 — IT STOPPED ENUMERATING WHAT TO KEEP.** The `out` literal listed the fields worth preserving, and that list is the most expensive line in this store's history: it has now silently deleted `scopedWeekly` (2.70.0), the org identity, `spend` (B-87fe), `corroborated`, the established window (which is why THAT lives in a sidecar) — and `limits`, the typed canonical half, measured against the REAL tool over a migrated copy of a real cache file: three limits in, ZERO out, the `overage` object gone with them, and the next reader re-deriving them under THIS producer's name and clock. Six losses, one mechanism, so the default is inverted: `out` now SPREADS the stored object and states only the fields this render measured (`fiveHour`/`sevenDay`/`overallStatus`/`fetchedAt`/`source`, plus `scopedWeekly` defaulted so a reader can still tell a claude snapshot from a codex one). It touches `limits` exactly once, and by REMOVING: it DROPS the `plan` limit — the only one it can measure, whose reading it has just written into the legacy buckets — so `liftCacheObject` reconstructs it with this object's own `source`/`fetchedAt`, and every other limit survives byte-identical with the provenance of the producer that DID measure it. A producer that cannot express a window state or another limit's age can never forge one, and this file never has to carry a second spelling of the model's window rules. It never AUTHORS the array on a not-yet-migrated file (a one-element list claiming to be all of them would delete that file's scoped cap the moment anything lifted it), and `corroborated` is the one field it deliberately does NOT inherit — that is a verdict about a different reading, and this producer has no observation to re-earn it. §⑮ of scripts/test-quota-model.mjs drives the REAL file; its negative control is a patched copy with the spread reverted to the enumerated literal. **MODEL-SCOPED WINDOWS (claude 2.1.274, measured in the binary's statusline schema — inc-mubu23bd-5vxi):** `rate_limits.model_scoped[]` = {display_name, utilization = the server row's PERCENT (the binary's `Yde` projection puts `s.percent` there; ÷100 unconditionally, never by magnitude — 2.369.99), resets_at ISO} beside the older `seven_day_<model>` fields; `scopedFromRateLimits` writes each as the scoped bucket of that NAME (the lane is decided by what names it — never into `seven_day`), an empty list states nothing (the previous entries survive: the 2.70.0 rule), and the limits this render measured (the plan + the named model caps, matched by NAME never by re-spelling the id) are dropped so the reader reconstructs them with this producer's provenance. The statusline never carries `seven_day_overage_included` (census ⑩); the reading-lag mirror block is byte-identical still. test-quota-model ⑲ TOOL drives the real file (percent, ISO reset, an un-named Opus keeps its age, an empty list retires nothing, a top-level `seven_day_opus` names its lane the same way).

### data/bin/vibespace-usage-scan

data/bin/vibespace-usage-scan — REMOTE-side usage ledger scanner (2.127.0, STATIC tracked; **PARITY-GUARDED since 2.275.0: it is a shipped SINGLE FILE (a host has no checkout ⇒ it cannot require the local walker), so it silently lagged its twin twice — the 2.265.0 subagents/workflows walk took 6 weeks to reach it. scripts/test-usage-walk-parity.mjs runs THE THREE walkers (local UsageHistory walk + this file + src/usage-walker.js) over one fixture and demands identical coverage + incremental-cursor behaviour; negative-controlled against the pre-2.271.0 walk. Any one-sided change fails it.**; shipped over ssh stdin per harvest, never argv): walks the host's ~/.claude/projects with remote byte cursors (~/.vibespace/usage-cursor.json), emits per-request NDJSON events (claude-only v1); cursor persists ONLY after stdout fully flushed (interrupted transfer ⇒ re-emit, rid-dedup absorbs). **R4 step 1 (2.286.0): daemon hosts prefer the `usage-scan` OP instead — src/usage-walker.js is the walk as a module BUNDLED into the daemon, run in a child process (single-artifact rule: the daemon re-execs its own bundle with `--usage-scan-child`), events streamed count-gated; the walker NEVER persists its cursor — hosts.harvestUsage commits it back over the device link (fsWrite+fsRename) only after the full transfer landed (two-phase; the script's flush-then-persist model LOST events on relayed dial paths when the link died mid-transfer with the cursor already advanced). Per-op capability gating: the daemon hello-ack `capabilities` array (['probe','transcript-op','usage-scan']) — consumers gate on it and throw fast, NEVER parse daemonVersion (unknown ops on old daemons get no reply = a hang until timeout). Fallback ladder: op → script-ship over the device link → ssh. E2E: scripts/test-usage-scan-op.mjs (13 asserts, real daemon).** **R4 step 2 (2.287.0): ①PUSH-triggered harvest — the daemon's discovery watch (now also `.codex/sessions`) pushes debounced `discovery-dirty`; hosts._armDirtyPush (armed at every _deviceConnect; client re-arms on reconnect like reverse forwards) fans it to discovery cache invalidation + server-side per-host debounced harvest kick (60s floor unchanged) — remote ledger/billing-popup freshness ≈1min for ANY activity incl. mid-turn/codex/external; the dirty signal previously had NO consumer. ②CODEX ROLLOUTS in all three walkers (synthetic rid = cumulative total, turn_context model/cwd persisted in cursor, input−cached split, heartbeats skipped, CODEX_HOME honored); ingestRemoteEvents honors `be` — remote codex usage lands in the ledger. Codex parity leg in test-usage-walk-parity (21).** Harvest chain: hosts.harvestUsage (15min/host idle throttle; **EVENT-DRIVEN since 2.284.3: a remote session's `result` kicks a prompt harvest with a 60s/host floor** — the ledger/billing-popup lag is ~1min, not 15; the pool control loop never depended on this cadence, it eats relayed stdout live via noteLive) → usageHistory.ingestRemoteEvents (**PER-ACCOUNT since 2.294.0**: resolves the real account by the SAME by-time attribution walk local events use — VibeSpace records the spawn account for remote sessions too, the ingest just discarded it; pool tag included. Only sessions VibeSpace never spawned (external terminals, pre-attribution) keep acct=<hostId>/atype='host'/billing 'remote-host', which now honestly means 'that machine's own login'. Quota side: /api/usage/refresh {host} = on-demand ⟳ with hosts.readRemoteOAuth (READ-ONLY remote token peek, never refresh, §ban-safety) → usage-cache/host-<id>.json → GET /api/usage `hosts` field (every configured host listed) → popup "Remote hosts" section (bars + per-host ⟳, class usage-host-refresh). **Walker v3 (codex per-message meta, 2026-09-06; mirrored line-for-line from src/usage-walker.js): codex events ADD `mid` = the `response_id` of the 0.153 `token_usage_record` that PRECEDES the token_count (parked in the CURSOR as `pendMid`/`pendTotal` so a harvest landing between the pair still pairs on the next run; adopted only when its `usage.total_tokens` equals `last_token_usage.total_tokens`; pre-0.153 rollouts get no mid — never invented) and `effort` (turn_context.effort, persisted like model). `rid` is UNCHANGED — it is the dedup key already baked into every permanent ledger; changing it would double-count every scanned rollout.
