validation is the PURE model's, the lifecycle the keeper's. Every route takes
`host` and refuses a non-local one by name; every failure is `{error, code}`;
the UI answers strip the CDP url and only the wrapper form (`wrapper:true`)
receives it (§5.1). `pinAnswer` is the ONE pin implementation for both
surfaces (records the pin on the conversation, stamps the live session,
re-points the running session's indirection through `browser-env.repointPin`).
**P1 second half:** `POST /api/agent/browser/resolve {handle?, argv?, wrapper?}`
is the ONE call the CLI's `--` form makes (layer ①'s `profile_changed` first,
then `profile_required` / `not_attached` / `ambiguous` / `profile_path_refused`
— every refusal typed `{error, code, handles, default?, was?, now?}`; the
"sub-agent" clause rides only when `session._subNormalizers` has an open
sidechain and is never the reason); `POST …/new-child` (a child handle + its
own env, `unset` naming the parent variables that would put it INSIDE the
parent's browser on rung C); `POST …/audit`; `new {adoptDir}` registers an
existing directory in place (the path refusal's remedy). A USER's pin / attach
/ detach queues a typed `browser-pin` / `browser-profile` notice through the
wiring's `notice` dep (session-status's queue, zero billed turns) and the pin
is persisted to the session's meta through `persistPin`; `POST
/api/browser/adopt` is §3.2.5's "new persistent profile from this session's
browser" — rung C moves the scratch dir (login kept), every other rung creates
an EMPTY profile and the answer SAYS the login was not saved. Wiring:
`tasksForSession` (the store's LIVE `groupsForSession`) feeds ownership checks.

  **P10 (2026-09-21):** STATUS gains `provider_needs_consent: 403` and `tier3_is_a_window_target: 409` (the smoke found both answering 500 before); both providers routes pass the keeper's `desktopConsent()` into `providerRows` so the `local-window` row's control follows the switch live (the keeper exports `desktopConsent` beside `hostKnown`).

### data/bin/vibespace-browser

**r-fix (2026-09-21):** `watch` states that on a shared, mediated profile the CDP fence refuses input and page-navigation COMMANDS, not script evaluation (the wrapper path refuses every command while paused, as before).

**P6 (2026-09-21; §6.2):** `new <label> --sharing owner|instance`; `use` prints the server's one-line `note` for a mediated attachment (you see and drive only your own tabs; input and navigation refused while the user drives); `profiles` marks `[shared, mediated]`, `status` marks a mediated lease; `printRefusal` spells `sharing_refused`'s `why` (no proxy ⇒ keep owner; a paired machine ⇒ run it here) and `mediation_no_cdp`. The CDP pair of a mediated attachment is withheld by `use --print` exactly like a reached browser's (§5.1).

**P4 second half (2026-09-17; §7.4):** `backend [--profile <h>]` prints the
backend this profile is on and every other row with its verdict (a row that
cannot be used says why and, for a missing key, that the USER must open ⚙ →
Integrations → `<id>`), its key source and its seats (`N used on this
instance / <the three-state sentence>`); `backend <name>
[--confirm-downgrade]` PROPOSES a switch — done directly only when this
conversation is the sole lease-holder and nobody drives, otherwise a "For you"
item and the agent is told to carry on meanwhile (a switch stops everybody's
browser); `blocked --url <u> [--why <code>] [--evidence <text>] [--tier 2|3]
[--remember]` records a CLAIM with the agent's name (the one-click "Open with
CloakBrowser" is the user's act; `--remember` files a per-site hint). The `--`
form TEES a navigation verb's stdout/stderr (never swallows them) so a real
403/429 prints `hint: may-need-cloak` — worded as a hint from the status code,
never a detection — and posts the URL with the audit call so the lease's
`lastUrl` is what a switch re-opens. `printRefusal` prints the way out of
`browser_restarting` (retry in a moment, the lease survives),
`backend_no_key`/`backend_seat_*` (`action.openIntegration`) and
`downgrade_*` (`waysOut`, the one-time confirmation). Gate:
test-browser-backend ④.

**P4 (2026-09-16):** `providers [--host <machine>]` prints every row with its
verdict here (or FOR that machine) and, for a row that cannot be used, the
exact typed reason, plus the §7.2.1 egress record's status; `new` takes
`--provider <id>`, `--host <machine>` (a PAIRED machine runs the browser) and
`--cdp-port <n>` (`--provider cdp`: reach an existing browser's loopback CDP
port — nothing is started) and says what it made (a directory here / on the
machine / reached over CDP); `profiles` shows `on <host>` and `cdp:<port>` on
the row; `use --print` WITHHOLDS the `AGENT_BROWSER_CDP` pair of a reached
browser and says so (§5.1: `use` never prints a CDP url — the subshell and the
`--` form carry it without printing it). Gate: test-browser-providers ⑤.

STATIC tracked, in `AGENT_TOOLS`; auth `VIBESPACE_SESSION_TOKEN`. `use` execs
a subshell with the attached env (`--print` prints the exports) and NEVER a
CDP url; `-- <args>` runs `agent-browser` against the attached profile with
this session's flags, adds `--pin-tab` when the server says the floor is met,
refuses `close --all` while another session is attached, and drops the lease
after a `close`; every answer names the profile it acted on (§3.8 layer ①).
**P1 second half (§3.7):** `--profile <handle>` (anywhere, taken OFF the argv
the wrapped CLI sees) or `VIBESPACE_BROWSER=<handle>` names ONE attachment;
with two or more a bare `--` command is refused `profile_required` listing
every handle and the default, a filesystem path is refused
`profile_path_refused` with the `new <label> --adopt <dir>` remedy, a set the
USER changed refuses the next command ONCE with `profile_changed` (was → now)
— all printed with their codes; `use <ref> --alias <h>`, `new-child` (prints
the child's env), `status` (the set with handles, `*` the default, children),
`pin <handle|label|id>`; after every wrapped command ONE audit line is posted
(verb only). Gate: test-browser-handles.

### src/browser-switch.js
**P4b install action (§7.4 failure form (1)):** `CLOAK_PACKAGE` + `INSTALL_CODES` (closed) + `installVerdict({proof, proofOk, exe, host, running})` — "measure first, then install" as a decision: host ⇒ `install_local_only`, an answering executable ⇒ `already_installed` naming the path, a flight ⇒ `install_running`, a record that is not `measured` (it names its own refusal) / fails its discipline / names no version ⇒ `install_precondition_unmet`, else ok with the spec PINNED to `proof.version`; `installArgv({spec, prefix})` (into OUR prefix, never `-g`; a non-spec is refused before any argv exists) and `binFromPackageJson(pkg)` (string / the `cloakbrowser` key / the first entry — the package's own bin, never a guess). The control the design names — a verdict that skips the measurement — answers ok for the refused record and is the suite's negative control.

PURE (imports nothing; CJS so the keeper, the routes, the ORCH key consumer
AND the bundle share ONE spelling of every refusal) — **agent browser P4
second half (2026-09-17; design §7.4 / §7.5 / §7.6, D17 / D32–D34, round
8)**: the live backend switch and the key-consumer half as DECISIONS; nothing
here touches a file, a process or the network. One sentence per invariant:
the version ladder (`versionLadder`) answers BEFORE a byte moves, reading the
registry's `lastChromiumMajor` beside the directory's own `Last Version` and
taking the HIGHER when they disagree (refusing one legitimate downgrade is
cheaper than allowing one that destroys a profile), a lower target is
`downgrade_refused` naming both majors with two ways out (upgrade / clone
through export-import, saying what that drops — sessionStorage and
non-extractable CryptoKeys), and nothing recorded, or a target whose major is
not yet known, is `downgrade_unknown` — refused until ONE explicit human
confirmation; the fingerprint seed is minted ONCE (`seedForSwitch`, from crypto
bytes the keeper hands it, a positive 31-bit integer) and carried through
every later switch, never re-minted per launch, and `fingerprintChange` /
`fingerprintNote` word the dialog from the FACT (chromium→cloak GAINS a
fingerprint, the reverse LOSES one; cookies cross untouched either way);
seats are THREE STATES (`seatState`: known-fresh within `SEAT_TIER_STALE_MS`
= 7 d carrying the reading's age / known-stale saying what the LAST tier was
and constraining nothing / unknown = this key never launched), the total
comes from the FIRST REAL LAUNCH (`tierFromLaunch`; nothing recognisable ⇒
null, never a fabricated number) and never from Test or a poll, and an
UNKNOWN or STALE total never satisfies the ceiling test (`seatVerdict` refuses
only while known-and-fresh — `unknown` is neither 0 nor ∞); the ceiling
wording forks on key SOURCE (the user's own key: every seat is on this
instance, so the holders are NAMED and stopping one is offered; the cluster
default: this instance cannot see other users' browsers, so NO profile is
listed, the sentence says the seats are shared and `action.openIntegration`
is the way out — a refusal may only state what its own reason knows);
`classifyLaunchFailure` turns a licence/concurrency launch failure into
`backend_seat_taken` (the criterion is the family of words `SEAT_TAKEN_RE`
until §12.40 is measured — said in the comment, waiting to be narrowed), and
under a cluster default it says the seats are shared fleet-wide ("stop one of
yours" is the wrong advice); `KEY_ROWS` carries the six rows' VENDOR env names
(`vendorEnvFor` emits only the fields that carry a value; `VENDOR_ENV_NAMES`
all pass through `agentEnv` by rule — exactly why the cluster may inject ONLY
under the store's `VIBESPACE_INTEGRATION_*` prefix) and the per-row EGRESS rule
(`testHostFor`: a constant for browserbase/browseruse, the host INSIDE the
field the user typed for browserless/kernel, the region for agentcore, none
for cloak; a host it cannot derive is `host_underivable`, never "let us try
the default"; `testRequestFor` puts the key in a HEADER, never the URL, which
every error path logs); `launchArgsFor` = `--executable-path <p> --args
--fingerprint=<seed>` for cloak (the two shapes upstream supports) and `-p
<name>` for cloud — the key never rides argv; `siteHintVerdict` keys per-site
memory by EXACT host (never a registrable domain — that needs a public-suffix
list, a second source of truth that expires) with `by`/`at`/`why`, and `tier`
is legal ONLY while `backend === null` (`hint_tier_with_backend` — once a
backend is named the tier is derived, never stored twice, §7.6 rule 2);
`blockedClaim` is made by the agent of a conversation (a claim `by:'server'`
is refused; the record has no field for a detection) and `blockedText` says
WHO, never "detected"; `navHint(403|429)` is a typed HINT naming its source;
`switchVerdict` is THE GATE in this order and no other — the row exists →
not a no-op → the capability control for THIS machine (`backend_unavailable`
naming what is missing / `provider_needs_local_key` BEFORE `resolveKey` is
ever called, leg viii) → `canSwitchTo` of the target AND the current backend
(`switch_refused` for cdp / local-window, `switch_export_only` naming the
lossy path for cloud) → the key resolved ONCE (`backend_no_key` +
`action.openIntegration`) → the ladder → seats → direct vs PROPOSAL (a browser
somebody is DRIVING is never interrupted, even by the user's switch; an
agent's switch while another session holds a lease, or on a profile it does
not own, is a proposal naming the affected sessions); `switcherRows` = every
backend with its verdict WRITTEN ON IT, the masked SOURCE chip (`your own key`
/ `cluster default · <label> (seats shared…)` / `not configured`), the seat
state and the chip; `backendChip` = `chromium 146` / `cloak 146 (free)` /
`cdp`; `restartingRefusal` = the NAMED gap. Gate: test-browser-backend ①
(the ladder matrix, the seed, the three seat states with the unknown-as-0 and
unknown-as-∞ controls, the fork, the classifier, the derived host driven with
two `apiUrl`s, the hint/claim rules, and the gate's ORDER asserted through a
recording `resolveKey`).

  **P10:** `blockedText` words a tier-3 claim as "a window on your own desktop — your act: the real-desktop switch, then the agent uses vibespace-window; nothing escalates by itself" (tier 2: "your act in the switcher"), still WHO said it and never "detected"; the actual escalation decision is window-desktop's PURE `hintAction` (a tier-only hint = a suggestion whose act is `open-window-target`, never `auto`).

### src/server/browser-backend.js

ORCH (requires the PURE switch model only) — **agent browser P4 second half
(2026-09-17; design §7.5 / round 8's runner registration)**: THE KEY CONSUMER
of the track. ONE module declares the six registry rows' consumer, registers
their Test runners and resolves their keys, because the shared layer's
consumer census only finds three names that know about each other when they
are one module. `keyFor(id)` = the literal per-row `resolveIntegration('<id>')`
table (`RESOLVE`) — the ONE place a plaintext value leaves the integration
store on this track, handed straight to the keeper for the ONE child's env;
`sourceOf(id)` = the MASKED `publicView` (`source`, `clusterKey`,
`clusterLabel`, `why`, `testedAt`, `lastOk`) for the switcher's SOURCE chip —
never a value, asserted on the returned object; `registerTests()` registers
all six with `store.registerTest` (a row that declares a `test` and registers
nothing is a dead control the shared census reddens; no store = said and
empty). The runners ARE the track's egress declaration: `cloak` is shape-only
— it validates the `cb_…` shape through the row's own validator (empty = the
free tier, legal), starts NO process, opens NO socket, downloads NO byte (the
tier is read at the first real launch, behind the two preconditions a card
opened to paste a key may not trigger); each `cloud:*` makes exactly ONE
bounded read-only GET to the ONE host `testHostFor` derives from that row's
own fields, the key in a header, `redirect:'manual'`, 2xx = ok, 401/403 =
"refused this key", an underivable host = the named refusal and NO request,
`agentcore` reports itself unsigned (this build cannot sign AWS requests, so
the key was NOT exchanged); `fetchImpl` is injectable so the gate records the
host each runner reached. Outside these Tests this track's server sends no
third-party request. Created by mounts-plugins-wiring BEFORE the keeper
(server.js now creates the integrations wiring ahead of it) and handed to the
keeper as `keys`. Gate: test-browser-backend ② (legs iii, v, vi, vii) +
test-integration-registry (f) (the six runners registered through the real
wiring).

### src/lib/browser-switcher.js
**P4b install action:** the cloak row disabled with `backend_unavailable` carries an "Install CloakBrowser…" control read off the view's `install` verdict — enabled only when the server says ok (title = `npm install <spec>`), otherwise disabled with the verdict's reason under it, "Installing…" while `state.running`; a click POSTs `/api/browser/install`, toasts the spec and refreshes. The same control lives on Manage Agents' "CloakBrowser (browser backend)" row (src/lib/manage-agents.js, local machine only, read through `GET /api/browser/install`; a transport failure hides the row).

CLIENT — **agent browser P4 second half (2026-09-17; §7.4 UX / §7.5 the
source chip / §7.6 rule 2 / D33)**: nothing is decided here.
`openBrowserSwitcher(app, {profileId, sessionId?, preselect?})` draws `GET
/api/browser/switcher` in a `createModalShell`: the profile + its chip (and
"switching…" while a switch is in flight), the agent's `blocked` claims (the
sentence says WHO claimed it; "Open with CloakBrowser" preselects the cloak
row — the switch is the USER's act, and the seats + fingerprint sentence are
shown before anything moves; Dismiss DELETEs), every backend as a radio row
enabled or DISABLED WITH ITS REASON (no row hidden; the current one marked),
the SOURCE chip from the MASKED view (`Your own key` / `Cluster default ·
<label> (seats shared with other users)` / `Not configured`) and an "Open
Integrations" button wherever the row's `action.openIntegration` says so
(`app.openIntegration(id)` — "no key" is said BEFORE the click; the typed
`backend_no_key` refusal is the last net), the seat line in THREE states
composed HERE from the server's `{state, total, age}` with the device's own
`t()` (the channels r2 rule: the server sends structure, the client says the
words), the fingerprint sentence from `fingerprintChange`, ONE checkbox for a
downgrade the ladder cannot judge (`needsConfirm`), "Make this the profile's
default backend", and the per-site memory section (each row deletable; adding
one is a USER claim posted as `site`, because `host` names a MACHINE on every
browser route); `POST /api/browser/switch` — a refusal toasts its sentence and
deep-links its `action.openIntegration`, a `proposal` toasts what was filed,
a switch toasts the re-opened count and the fingerprint sentence. Re-rendered
from `browser-profiles-updated` while open, the ws handler removed BY NAME on
close; every server string through textContent; theme vars only.
`installBrowserSwitcher(App)` adds `openBrowserSwitcher`, `browserChipFor`
(the digest's `chips`) and `browserBlockedFor` (the digest's `blocked`). Its
words are in zh + ja (the i18n check in the build); the routes it draws are
driven by test-browser-backend ④.

### src/browser-serve.js

SHARED (fs/os/path + the PURE model + browser-facts; the daemon bundles it) —
**agent browser P4 (2026-09-16; design §3.6 row 3 / §7.3 / D5 (b))**: the
`browser-serve` OP TABLE (`version` / `status` / `start` / `stop` / `cdp-url`,
closed — an unknown op is refused by name) + `runBrowserServeOp(bs, action,
params)`, the ONE implementation that runs where the profile browser lives:
in-process for device #0, inside the agentd for a paired device. The hub names
a PROFILE ID only (`bp-<8 hex>`, else `bad-request`) and the machine composes
and owns `~/.agent-browser/vs-bp-<id>` (0700) itself — a hub can never point a
device at an arbitrary directory. The CDP url a machine answers is ITS OWN
loopback (§6.1); it never listens on a LAN. `start` is reuse-or-spawn through
the CLI's own `open` with the timeout OFF; `stop` is `close --all` then a
bounded wait — a pid that survives the grace is REPORTED (`left`), never
signalled by this op. Every op answers `{ok, …}` or `{ok:false, code, error}`
— never a throw across the wire. ONE facts instance per PROCESS (`install()`),
never per connection. Gate: test-browser-providers ② (over the fake
`agent-browser`) + ③ (a REAL daemon).

The daemon installs its browser-serve facts over `daemonEnv(process.env)`, never
the raw process env (the 2026-09-14 agent-env rule merged with P4a, re-carried by
the r0 rebase onto 2.369.130): a daemon born from the server env must not hand the
server's secrets to the browser probe.

### src/server/browser-access.js

ORCH — **ONE way to reach a profile browser on ANY machine (P4)**, the
opencode-access shape on purpose: `call(hostId, action, params)` picks the
transport (falsy/`local` = the shared runner in-process; a paired device = the
`browser-serve` agentd op; an ssh host without a daemon = REFUSED
`host_needs_daemon` — a silent local fallback would start the browser on the
wrong machine) and turns a machine-side `{ok:false}` into a coded throw so
callers see one shape. `forwardCdp(hostId, remotePort, {remoteUrl})` = the
hub-side loopback listener (`net.createServer` on 127.0.0.1:0, each connection
piped into `device.tcpForward(remotePort)` — PortForwardManager's shape, the
device resolved PER CONNECTION so a re-dial never leaves a stale handle),
REFERENCE-COUNTED per (hostId, remotePort): two records may name one port (a
profile browser's own port and a `cdp` profile pointed at it), so a release
drops ONE reference and the listener closes at zero, never under the other
record's feet; concurrent first callers join ONE listen. For the LOCAL machine
no forward is made. `shutdown()` is the only unconditional teardown. An
unwired process refuses LOUDLY (`host_unavailable`). Gate:
test-browser-providers ④ (bytes round-trip over a fake tcpForward).

### src/server/egress-proxy.js

ORCH — **the allowlisting egress proxy (P4, §7.2.1 "make the boundary
enforcing rather than observed")**: a tiny HTTP forward proxy on the hub's
loopback — `CONNECT host:port` (TLS passes through untouched) and absolute-form
`GET http://…` — admitting a host ONLY when the PURE `egressVerdict(host,
allowlist)` says so and answering `403` with the verdict's own sentence
otherwise (a blocked fetch is a NAMED refusal in the browser's network log,
never a hang); the allowlist is re-read per request (liveApply), loopback and
link-local targets are refused by the verdict itself (never a way back into the
hub's services), origin-form requests are 400 (it is a proxy, not a server). No
auth (loopback only, like the stream port), no caching, bounded header read.
Started LAZILY by mounts-plugins-wiring only when `browser.cloak.enabled` is on
and a plan is asked for — a fresh instance listens on nothing. Gate:
test-browser-providers ⑥ (real loopback sockets).

### scripts/measure-cloak-egress.mjs

**The §7.2.1 measurement, as a script (P4)**: modelled verbatim on
src/local-oracles.js — `env -i HOME=<empty> PATH=… strace -f -qq -e
trace=network`, every `connect(AF_INET|AF_INET6)` counted, a DNS `:53` connect
counted as INET (resolving a vendor host is already the decision to talk to it)
— over the four runs the design names (first launch / second launch from cache
/ launch with a license key / 10-minute idle). It NEVER installs or downloads
anything: it measures the binary already on the machine and, when none is,
prints the refusal record by name (`binary_absent`) — which is exactly what
`src/browser-profiles.CLOAK_EGRESS_PROOF` carries today (run 2026-09-16 on the
dev box: strace present, no `cloakbrowser`/`cloakserve`, nothing downloaded).
Its output is pasted into that constant; the `version` it names is the version
the counts describe, so an unpinned auto-download invalidates the record.

### src/keeper-limits.js

PURE constants home every process keeper counts and bounds by (sample cadence,
CPU/RSS thresholds, cooldown, `CONCURRENT_CAP`); the browser keeper reads it
here, the desktop-app keeper and opencode-serve read the same object on master.

### src/browser-trace.js

**r-fix (2026-09-21, D35's side doors):** `redactParams` also turns a single-character `press`/`keydown`/`keyup` key into «1 key» (a named key or chord stays — a gesture, not content) and a `select`'s value/values/label/option into a length — a secret typed key-by-key or chosen from a list leaves no characters on disk or on the card.

**P6 (2026-09-21):** the housekeeping row carries `sharing` and `mediated` (`B.isMediatedProfile`) so the panel can say which profiles are instance-shared.

**PURE** (imports only the sibling PURE registry model for the provider rows;
CJS so the recorder, the routes, the CLI AND the bundle share ONE spelling of
every rule). Agent browser P5 (2026-09-18, design §4.5 / §6.4 / §7.1 / §8
step 3, D7 / D8 / D35). THE ACTION TRACE: `TRACED_ACTIONS` is the closed
action table (click / fill / press / mouse* / scroll / navigate … → the KIND of
position an entry records); anything not in it — `get`, `snapshot`, `launch`,
`boundingbox`, `screenshot`, `wait` — is an OBSERVATION and is never traced
(`isTracedCommand`). `redactParams` keeps a fill's value and a type's text as
`«N chars»` and an upload's file NAMES only (the §3.7 audit rule applies to the
trace); `commandText` rebuilds the human-readable command from the REDACTED
params. `positionOf` = point (CSS px) / box (the target's `{x,y,width,height}`
from ONE `get box <selector>` probe) / target-without-box saying why / keys /
scroll / navigation. A result is judged by its ERROR, never by `success`
(measured on 0.32.0: `false` on every result, clicked or not). `afterFramePick`
= the first frame ≥ 400 ms after the result, else the latest by 1.5 s (`same`
when nothing repainted). `entryFor` = the record `{id, at, sessionId,
browserKey, profileId, scope, action, kind, text, params, ok, error,
durationMs, position, before, after, afterSame, url}`. RETENTION
(`traceRetentionPlan`): 7 d, then 200 MB per profile oldest first — every
removal names its rule, every kept group what it holds. `recordingVerdict`
refuses BY NAME (off / not ours / not local / below the 0.37.0 floor).
HOUSEKEEPING: `sweepScope` = exactly the provider rows with `ownsDir` on this
machine; `queueVerdict` refuses `cloud:*` / `local-window` / `cdp` / a remote
record as `not_ours`; `housekeepingVerdict` answers a state from the closed
`HOUSEKEEPING_STATES` (`not-ours` / `in-use` / `live` / `recent` — in-flight
grace with its age / `stale` / `kept`) with its `why` and NEVER answers
"delete"; `forgetVerdict` refuses while leased or running; `orphanCandidates` =
a Chromium-marker directory no record names; `orphanPathVerdict` = a top-level
dir under the base only. THE CLIENT'S DOM-FREE HALF (P5 client, 2026-09-21):
`commandDrivesBrowser` + `toolCommandText` (claude's string / codex's argv
array) gate the tool card; `traceWindowFor` = a card's window (its ts − 2 s →
the next message's ts + 2 s, or now); `unionWindow` = ONE fetch for many cards;
`assignEntriesToWindows` gives each entry to EXACTLY ONE card — the one with
the latest ts that was RUNNING when the action happened (500 ms skew; an entry
only later cards can hold goes to the earliest of them); `overlayGeometry` =
the dot / rect in the DRAWN picture's px; `frameUrl` only ever names an entry
id + before|after; `bytesText` ('—' for unmeasured); `traceSummary`;
`positionText`; `timelineLabel`. Gate: test-browser-housekeeping ① + ⑥.

### src/server/browser-trace.js

**ORCH** (P5). THE RECORDER hangs on two seams and decides nothing: the
bridge's TAPS (`browserStream.tap(sessionId, profileId, cb)` — every
`command` / `result` / `frame` / `url` record of a live relay; a tap holds a
viewer-less relay open at `TRACE_TAP_FPS` = 4, never drives, never counts as a
viewer, NEVER starts a browser) and the keeper's LEASE SEAM (`onLease`: attach /
browser-ready arm a tap, detach / lease-dropped / browser-stopped disarm it).
A traced `command` snapshots the LAST frame held as the before-picture; the
matching `result` starts the after-clock and, for a target action, ONE bounded
`get box <selector>` under the lease's own session (its `boundingbox` command
is itself never traced). The entry lands as 0600 files (`<id>.json`,
`<id>-before.jpg`, `<id>-after.jpg`) + a line in `index.ndjson` under
`data/browser-trace/<profileId | ephemeral>/`, is pushed to the live view's
viewers as a `trace` stream record and to every client as
`browser-trace-appended` (never the bytes). `browser.actionTrace` (default ON,
D35) gates the whole thing. THE SCREENCAST (D7 opt-in per profile): `record
start <file>` / `record stop` under the lease's session, `record: true`
profiles only, refused below the floor with the refusal kept for the panel;
files under `data/browser-recordings/<profileId>/<sid>-<ts>.webm`. THE SWEEP
(hourly + boot) applies the PURE plan to traces AND recordings and logs what it
removed and why. HOUSEKEEPING: sizes by `du -sb` in a CHILD (never a sync walk —
98 GB lived under `~/.agent-browser` on the design's machine), cached 10 min;
`orphans()` under `~/.agent-browser`; `forgetProfile` RENAMES the directory
beside itself (`<dir>.forgotten-<ts>`) and files a ledger row in
`data/browser-forgotten.json` BEFORE the record goes; `deleteForgotten` is THE
one permanent deletion (a `.forgotten-` directory under the base, a human's
click); `adoptOrphan` labels a directory in place (§8 step 3). `list({sessionId,
browserKey, anyOf})` matches by the webui id OR the key (a resume re-carries the
key while the id churns). Every housekeeping change broadcasts
`browser-housekeeping-updated`. Wired in mounts-plugins-wiring AFTER the
keeper reconciled its leases (a tap never starts a browser, so the order is
load-bearing); shut down from server.js. Gate: test-browser-housekeeping ②–⑤.

### src/routes/browser-trace.js

Thin over the two above; `host` refused by name (local-only in this release).
`GET /api/browser/actions?sessionId=&conversation=&browserKey=&profile=&from=&to=&limit=`
— ONE conversation's actions by the live session's key, else the bindings
store's key for the CLI's own `conversation` id (a STOPPED conversation's
cards still find their actions — the point of a review; the wiring hands the
routes a `browser-bindings` reader that reads the file per ask), else a
`browserKey` given outright (validated); at least one of the three; **nothing to
match by ⇒ an honest EMPTY answer, never every entry** (the client-half suite
caught the route answering everything for an unbound conversation). Answers
`{sessionId, conversation, browserKey, keyFrom: session|conversation|given|null,
traceOn, entries}`. `GET …/trace/:id` (never the bytes) · `GET
…/trace/:id/frame/before|after` (image/jpeg + nosniff + private cache) · `GET
/api/browser/housekeeping` (the panel's whole view — nothing here is a
deletion) · `POST …/housekeeping/sweep` · `PATCH /api/browser/profiles/:id`
`{record?, label?, notes?}` (anything else refused by name) · `POST
…/profiles/:id/forget` (409 leased / running, 400 not_ours) · `POST
/api/browser/orphans/adopt {dir, label}` · `POST /api/browser/orphans/forget
{dir}` · `POST /api/browser/forgotten/:fid/delete` (THE one permanent deletion)
· `GET /api/browser/recordings/:profileId[/:file]` (video/webm|mp4, no-store).
Statuses by the closed `STATUS` table. Gate: test-browser-housekeeping ④.

### src/lib/browser-trace-view.js

**2.369.145:** the fetch path is `/api/browser/actions` (EasyPrivacy's `/trace?sessionid=` blocked the old `/api/browser/trace?sessionId=` in every content blocker — the card said "server unreachable" for a request the server never saw); the row's third state `untraced` (the server answered with no browser key: the keeper never started that browser) says "not traced" by name, never "no recorded actions".

**P6 (2026-09-21):** a mediated row shows a `shared` chip whose title is the confinement sentence (zh+ja).

**CLIENT** (P5 client half, 2026-09-21; design §4.5 / D35). Draws the trace on
three surfaces and decides nothing. THE TOOL CARD: chat-renderers'
`browserTraceHolderHtml(block, msg)` puts a `.chat-browser-trace` holder (its
`data-trace-ts` = the card's own instant, a button, a summary, a thumbnail
strip, a list) on ALL THREE card shapes (pending / error / generic) of a shell
tool call whose command drives the agent browser — the PURE gate over claude's
string or codex's argv array, never a tool name; `createCardTraceLoader(view)`
(ONE per ChatView) fills them: `observe(el)` is called from
`_applyElementMarks` — the ONE hook every element-making path passes through
(create / swap / gap), so a rebuilt history, a paged-in slab and a live card all
get their strip — holders are batched for 150 ms into ONE fetch over the union
of their windows, `assignEntriesToWindows` gives each card exactly its own
actions, thumbnails ALWAYS (D7 (c): the after-frame of every action, the
before-frame when nothing repainted, ≤12 with "+N earlier"), the full list
(time · command · result · position kind + line · before/after thumbs) behind
the card's own button; the summary says `N action(s) · M failed`, or honestly
why not (trace off / no conversation id / waiting for actions on a running
card / none recorded); a `browser-trace-appended` broadcast for this session or
its key re-queues the cards whose window may hold it (600 ms debounce). A
view-only (`view-…`) window asks by its CONVERSATION id, never by its window
id. THE ENTRY DIALOG (`openTraceEntryDialog(app, entry, list)`): before / after
side by side, the position DRAWN on the picture after the image lands (a dot
for a point, a rectangle for the element's box — `overlayGeometry` in the drawn
picture's px, right at any dialog width), the command, action + position line,
result + duration, page, profile, ← / → through the list the click came from,
and §6.4's retention sentence. THE TIMELINE (`createTraceTimeline(app,
{sessionId})`, the live view's third pane): `load({profileId})` seeds ONE scope
(the profile's, or `ephemeral`) from GET, `push(entry)` grows it from the
stream's `trace` record (deduped by id), newest last, click = the dialog. Every
frame is drawn through `img.src` (never markup); every wire string through
textContent; the module never assigns innerHTML (pinned). THE BROWSER PROFILES
PANEL (window type `browser-profiles`, singleton, openSpec
`{action:'openBrowserProfiles'}`, ⚙ → Tools → Browser profiles… at order 35
gated on the profile digest, `app.openBrowserProfiles({focus})` installed by
`installBrowserTrace(App)`): the housekeeping view over `GET
/api/browser/housekeeping` — one row per profile (label + legacy/host chips +
the backend chip from `app.browserChipFor`, the STATE worded from the closed
`HOUSEKEEPING_STATES` with its `why` under it, the size — "not measured" for a
not-ours row —, the trace digest, the recordings with a live "recording" mark or
the refusal's reason, the per-profile screencast checkbox = `PATCH
{record}` (D7; disabled with the reason for not-ours / remote), "Set aside" =
`POST …/forget` behind a confirm that says what moves where), the ephemeral
row, the UNREGISTERED DIRECTORIES under `~/.agent-browser` (size, last use,
"Adopt…" = an input dialog for the label → `POST /orphans/adopt`, "Set aside"
→ `POST /orphans/forget`), the SET ASIDE ledger (from → to, when; "Delete
permanently" = THE one permanent deletion, a danger-styled confirm →
`POST /forgotten/:fid/delete`; a deleted row says when), the sweep line +
"Sweep now". The hint repeats §6.4 in the user's words and says the action
trace is OFF when it is. Re-rendered (1.2 s debounce) from
`browser-housekeeping-updated` / `browser-profiles-updated` /
`browser-trace-appended`; the ws handler is removed on close; every action
goes through the in-app dialogs, never a native one (pinned). Gate:
test-browser-housekeeping ⑥ (the PURE helpers, the WIRING PINS — the 2.355.0
lesson: an unstaged caller is a green suite over dead code —, the panel's
state words / window type / ⚙ row / install / dialogs / the one deletion, and
the i18n census over every `t()` literal); test-window-types + test-contributions
carry the type / action / owner / gear-row census rows.

### docs/agent/browser-manual.md

**P4 (2026-09-16)**: the verb table gained `providers [--host]` and `new`'s
`--provider/--host/--cdp-port`, and one bullet ("Other providers and other
machines") says what a paired-machine profile and a `cdp` profile are, that a
reached browser's CDP pair is withheld by `use --print` too, and that their
live view is not available yet.

**P1 (2026-09-16)**: the manual gained the `vibespace-browser` section (named
profiles, the lease, what `use` does and does not print, the `close --all`
rule, the pin) and its "not available yet" sentences about shared profiles
were replaced; the tools intro's isolated sentence now points at
`vibespace-browser new/use` instead of telling the agent to wait.

The manual `vibespace-docs browser` serves (registered in `AGENT_DOC_TOPICS`,
`src/agent-routes.js`), beside the one budgeted line in the tools intro —
**a line that is now chosen by the session's OWN recorded rung (r5)**:
`browser-profiles.isolatedVariant` (D/C/N/H) gets the "this session has its own
browser, `close --all` closes only yours" sentence, and every other session
(rung `none`, the feature off, a resolver that threw, a session predating it)
gets the manual's own words for the shared browser, because telling a shared
session that `close --all` is safe is the incident P0 exists to stop. It
describes what SHIPS: the four variables and what they mean for the agent, the
TWO config files the generated config is built from and the one boundary of
that (the session directory's `agent-browser.json`, once, for the whole
session — r3), the three things to stop doing (`--profile` / `--session` /
`--namespace`), and the honest limits — a remote host decides the user-data-dir
itself (its own per-key dir when its config names a profile, the CLI's
throwaway dir otherwise), one local corner gets nothing at all (a profile-naming
config with neither D nor C deliverable — the names alone would make the browser
fail to start), nothing watches the browser, a login does not survive, there is
no live view and no handover yet, shared named profiles are a later phase, and
the CLI's own 103-byte socket-path limit (`$HOME` + 65 bytes for our name shape
⇒ a home longer than 38 characters would break every command) — which r4 now
closes by setting `AGENT_BROWSER_SOCKET_DIR` at an owned 0700 directory only
when the CLI's own root is over the limit, so the manual names it as the FIFTH
variable the session may carry and tells the agent what the refusal means if it
ever still appears (the directory could not be used and the journal says why).

### transcript-service.js

  transcript-service.js — ONE interface over the transcript parse stack (R3 of docs/design-three-tier.md; 2.283.0 step 1 = server-hosted, HTTP read family rerouted through it). **SWITCHED LIVE in 2.292.0** — remote page/turnmap/searchIndexed/status/taskState run as `transcript-op` on the owning machine (parsed KBs on the wire, no whole-file pull). LADDER not replacement: device op → transcript-cache pull + local parse → honest error; capability-gated (an old daemon is never asked — unknown ops hang), failures log throttled and degrade. TWO CARVE-OUTS, both load-bearing: ① a LIVE session never reads from the device (the server owns the stdout buffer overlay + live normalizer — the device would drop the un-flushed tail); ② the huge-file SEEK family switched ATOMICALLY in 2.293.0 once the daemon gained a `searchFull` op — `gapInfo` returns an OPAQUE HANDLE (`\0device:<host>` or the local path) that every follow-up (slab/search/turnmap) honours, so line numbers never come from two sources (the route already treated fp as opaque, so nothing above the service changed); device streaming search degrades honestly to one batch. Ladder test: scripts/test-transcript-switchover.mjs (7). **2.285.0 step 2: the DEVICE DAEMON hosts the SAME service** — agentd's `transcript-op` op (lazy-constructed, no buffer overlay device-side — the stdout overlay stays a server concern) runs page/turnmap/searchIndexed/status/taskState/gapInfo/gapSlab/fullTurnmap next to the bytes and streams JSON over a count-gated byte channel (read-range contract); client = DeviceManager.transcriptOp. DARK: no production consumer until the parity substrate soaks (retirement-order law). scripts/test-transcript-parity.mjs (19 asserts) pins BYTE-IDENTICAL results across in-process vs real-daemon — incl. >½MB multi-window payloads, a ~36MB fixture's real seek family, codex, and honest unknown-method/missing-file shapes. Its first run caught the tool-card ts bug (below). SafeFs/transcript-worker degrade INLINE inside the bundle (worker file absent next to the bundle → spawn fails → sync fallback, by design). **B-21e4 item 5:** `view()` warms through `harnessOf(backend).store.warmTranscript(id, cwd, {remote})` (claude parse-cache warm as before; codex thread/read fallback for a missing rollout, local only) — no backend ternary.

### session-store.js

  **NO claude model reader lives here (B-6b6d round 2)** — and the long comment where one used to be is the reason. Round 1 shipped `lastClaudeTurnModel` (tail scan for the last MAIN-THREAD assistant record's `message.model`) as the claude descriptor's `store.lastTurnModel`; it is REMOVED, because that field answers *which model served a turn* and the ladder asks *what should this resume command*. Two measurements decided it: (a) across the whole local corpus (2650 transcripts / 3.5 GB) **zero** `message.model` values carry a `[…]` context-variant suffix while the CLI's own `model_refusal_fallback` records prove conversations running `claude-fable-5[1m]`, so commanding the served id silently turns a 1M conversation into a 200k one on every resume; (b) a classifier reroute is an ASSISTANT record already ON the fallback model carrying a `{type:'fallback',from,to}` block, with the `system/model_refusal_fallback` record written 2–10 lines AFTER it — round 1's ≤20-line backward look-back matched 1 of 139 reroutes, and 16.8% of main-thread assistant records sit inside a reroute run. So a claude resume commands NEITHER model nor effort and the CLI's own session record (variant-exact) decides. Re-adding a reader is one hook in `src/harnesses/claude.js` if a future CLI ever records the commanded value.

  session-store.js     — SessionMessages + JSONL parsing + session discovery helpers. **THE LOCAL SWEEP'S PID-REUSE RUNG IS A RECORDED TWIN OF THE SWEEP'S IDENTITY RULE (B-3185 r3, RADIUS CORRECTED IN r4):** `isLockClaude` prefers B-2104's `procStart` match (no fork) and falls back to `isProcessClaudeAsync` = `ps -o comm=` + `.includes('claude')`. **r3 recorded this twin as "the local sweep's PID-reuse fallback" and that described only HALF of it: the SYNC `isProcessClaude` had one caller — `/api/kill-pid`'s local branch — so the substring rule GATED A SIGTERM. r4 deleted the sync half (that route now asks `isCliProcess` for both CLI names, like its own remote branch) and what survives is DISCOVERY-ONLY: one caller, `isLockClaude`'s no-`procStart` fallback (macOS locks write `procStartFt`; Linux answers with the file read first), deciding whether a card reads RUNNING and nothing else.** It is not an executable test the way it looks, either: `comm` is 15 bytes the process may set for itself (node renames its main thread to `MainThread`, so an npm-installed `node …/claude-code/cli.js` answers NO) matched as a SUBSTRING (`claude-keeper` answers YES) — the "4277 processes, same 16, zero divergence" measurement was of THIS box's native install, not of the rule. It stays un-ported because the rung that reaches it is macOS, where `isCliProcess` is SYNCHRONOUS and a per-lock blocking fork is the 2.242.0 event-loop stall this async family exists to avoid; adding a `comm` rung to the shared predicate instead would widen a KILL path. **It must never move back onto one** (test-writer-sweep §14 asserts the single caller and the sync twin's absence). It has a live parity gate too — scripts/test-local-discovery-device.mjs asserts device-facts sweep === local sweep, which compares the two rungs on every run (its fixture must therefore be a REAL binary named `claude`, never a `#!/bin/sh` script: the kernel gives that argv[0] `/bin/sh` while `comm` stays `claude`). **Merge is POSITION-PRESERVING (2.74.0):** surviving buffer records interleave at their true chronological spot (anchor = jsonl index of the last buffer record that deduped; a rotated buffer's unmatched head anchors just before the first match) instead of all appending at the end — end-append made an EARLIER turn's stream-json-only `result` replay AFTER a still-running tool_use, flushing the live pending tool card to ✗ Interrupted on every server restart (real report), and scrambled turn boundaries in the replay. **`chatStatus()` IS THE ATTACH/HTTP TWIN OF THE LIVE COMMAND-LIST OP (§2.6), AND ITS RULE IS AN ORDERING (round 3):** the tail scan records the POSITION of the newest `commands_changed` and of the newest `init`, and the push replaces the frame's `slashCommands` only when it is genuinely newer (plus the degradation branch: an init that declares no list cannot erase the push before it — live, `_emitSlashCommands` returns early on such a record, so the last thing that SPOKE stands). Applying the push unconditionally was actively harmful, not merely absent: a buffer holds one init per SPAWN (33 in one real conversation here), so `[…, commands_changed, …, init]` is the ordinary shape of a resume or wrapper respawn, and `applyStatus()` runs AFTER `loadHistory`'s render loop — the pre-restart list OVERWROTE the correct one the slab's own init-card side effect had just set, and was then mixed with the newest frame's `terminalSlashCommands`. The invariant the twin exists for is that **a window that opens after the push agrees with one that watched it happen**, so the gate drives the SAME records through both paths (scripts/test-init-frame.mjs `chatStatus twin`, with the pre-fix rule kept as the negative control).

  **ZERO SPAWNS PER SESSION IN THE LOCAL SWEEP (2026-09-09).** `discoverClaudeSessions` now starts AT MOST ONE child process — `tmux list-panes`, and only where a tmux binary is on PATH — however many locks and live sessions the machine has. Three decisions carry it: (a) the parent of a lock's pid comes from `/proc` via `cli-identity.readPpid`, so `findTmuxTargetAsync` costs no fork, and an EMPTY pane map short-circuits before it even reads (that is the shape on every machine without tmux); (b) the children of a live session's `_childPid` come from `cli-identity.readChildPids`, so the per-session `pgrep -P` is gone AND with it the 15 s `_childPidCache` that existed only to blunt it — the cache was also a correctness cost, because a wrapper that forked a new claude inside the window stayed unmapped; (c) `getTmuxPaneMapAsync` asks `tmuxOnPath()` (fs.statSync over the PATH entries, memoised 60 s — never a `which`, which would be one more fork) and caches its map for `TMUX_MAP_TTL_MS` = 4 s so a create/kill burst shares one. `isLockClaude` keeps B-2104's `procStart` file read first and, where there is no usable stamp, now asks THE identity (`isCliProcess`) on any procfs machine — the DAEMON snapshot's own rule (`pidLooksClaude`), one implementation — leaving the `ps -o comm=` twin reachable only where there is no /proc at all. The SYNC tmux twins (`getTmuxPaneMap`/`findTmuxTarget`) are DELETED: they had no callers (the old kb line "sync variants remain for boot paths" described boot-restore's own `execFileSync` calls) and they spelled the retired per-pid fork. Measured, same fixture, same box: 50 locks + 50 live sessions went **101 spawns / 360.8 ms → 1 spawn / 6.6 ms**; at 1.5 GB RSS **7,140.6 ms → 74.2 ms** (cold) and **3,540.9 ms → 1.0 ms** (warm); at userW's shape (61 locks, no tmux, 1.5 GB) **8,441.8 ms / 123 spawns → 3.0 ms / 0 spawns**. Gate: scripts/test-discovery-spawn.mjs (the census over the real sweep with master's own module as the negative control) + test-architecture §45 (the grep-derived spawn census, in the build). **r2: the sweep was only ONE of the two readers of "what did this wrapper fork"** — the other, `refreshWebuiPids()` in server.js, is on the KILL path and was still spawning a synchronous `pgrep -P` per live session; see the server.js entry. The lesson for this file is the census's, not the sweep's: §45's file set is now DERIVED, so the next reader of a fact this module owns cannot be invisible to it.

### codex-chat-wrapper.js (P2 verbs, 2.369.20)

  data/bin/codex-chat-wrapper.js — **2.369.157 r4: a failed or empty post-reset `account/rateLimits/read` emits `rate_limits_updated {error, onDemand:true, afterReset:true}` (was `catch { }` — the server could not tell failed from late).** **2.369.157 r3: `codex-reset-credit` emits the post-reset `rate_limits_updated` BEFORE `reset_credit_result` (the server decides the pool on the account's cache; answering first let an eval in the ≤ 20 s re-read gap move the pool off the account the credit had just re-opened) — the answer is emitted whatever the re-read did; pinned by test-codex-pool R15.** **USER-RECORD PRODUCER RULES (round 3-4, 2026-09-07): our copy is spelled `userInputToContent(encodeUserInput(text, attachments))` — the exact inverse of what we SEND, so it matches codex's rollout copy block for block (a hand-rolled attachments-first array doubled every image message on reload); EVERY submission that will not be committed AS WRITTEN is withdrawn with `retractUserRecord(id, reason)` → `event_msg webui_user_retracted` — `turn/start`/`thread/queue/add` threw, the queued item was removed by the user or by Stop before it ran, the wrapper ANSWERS it itself (a slash command: ONE gate `isWrapperSlashCommand`, retracted BEFORE `applySlashCommand` runs because `/compact` takes minutes), or **the `edit` verb REWROTE its text while it waited** (the sixth path, merge review 2026-09-07: the submission really does RUN, just with different words — codex commits the NEW text and can therefore never retire the claim our PRE-EDIT bubble made; gated on `queuedFullText(item.input) !== text` because a no-op save still commits as-written, on the SUCCESS branch only because a failed update leaves the queued text untouched, and by the row's own `cid` so an INHERITED row — which has no record of ours yet — is a no-op). **There is no write-time marker (round 4 deleted `webui_no_commit`): a typed message also has the SERVER's preview copy (`CodexAdapter._buildUserPreview` → `session.buffer`, ws-handler) under the same `webui_msg_id`, it lands FIRST and is the copy that CLAIMS, so anything the wrapper writes on its own record is unreachable — the retraction names the ID, which both copies carry.** The retraction makes the merge withdraw that record's twin CLAIM (an unconsumable claim deletes an unrelated message later), never removes the bubble, and an item the app-server had already drained (`{deleted:false}` = it RAN) is never retracted. The queued peer copy carries its cid as `webui_queue_id`.** chat-input: slash commands are served by the WRAPPER (`applySlashCommand`: /compact → `thread/compact/start` (real compaction; `context_compacted` from the contextCompaction item or the RPC), /review → review/start uncommittedChanges, /model + /effort → the set-* verbs, `command_applied` notice), then **queue-while-busy**: `meta.activeTurnId` set ⇒ `thread/queue/add` + `queued_input` event, never `turn/start` (codex steers a regular turn / rejects review+compact turns). Both `wrapper_meta` records advert `slashCommands`; CodexMessageManager stores them in `_status.slashCommands`, fills the init card and patches it in place (edit op) when they arrive after the card. Live item visibility: mcpToolCall/dynamicToolCall/webSearch/imageView/contextCompaction are recorded as function_call/function_call_output twins (names chosen for collapseKindOf: `mcp__<server>__<tool>` → mcp fold; web_search → search fold, view_image → image fold since 2.369.33/34). The imageView stub records `{path}` only while codex's own rollout copy of the same call carries `{path, detail}` and an `[{input_image, image_url:data:…}]` output twin — the normalizer's call_id dedupe + input_image lifting (2.369.43) is what keeps that ONE card; the stub contract itself is pinned by test-codex-p2-wrapper and test-image-cards.. **Race guard**: `turn/completed` can be processed before the `turn/start` reply's promise resolves (same stdout chunk) — `completedTurns` makes startTurn skip re-marking a finished turn active. Pins: scripts/test-codex-p2-wrapper.mjs (30); test-chat-frame-guard's stub completes turns at once. **Fork echo (B-21e4):** the wrapper's session_meta record dedupes `forked_from` (`[...new Set(chain)]`, own id dropped) and echoes `forked_from_id` from the thread/start|resume|fork response (`Thread.forkedFromId`, 0.153.4 bindings); the fork BOUNDARY ordinal is not on the wire — only the rollout's own session_meta carries it, and extractCodexThreadMeta reads it from the file. **webSearch completion = codex's OWN rollout shape (2.369.43, owner: every card read `{"query":"","action":null}` / "(empty)"):** the v2 WebSearchItem is an EMPTY stub at item/started (query '', action null — the function_call recorded there is the pending card and stays so) and complete only at item/completed, which the wrapper records as `event_msg web_search_end {call_id, query, action, results?, error?}` (key order mirrors codex-rs; `results` omitted when the item has none, `error` only when present) — NOT a function_call_output of raw JSON. The normalizer renders it (src/search-card.js), so the live record and the rollout's own web_search_end are one renderer and one card (the two copies fingerprint-dedupe on re-attach or edit the same call_id in place). Pin: test-codex-p2-wrapper (stub emits the real started-stub + completed pair; asserts the event shape, key order, no output twin, ONE complete card with the rendered result list). **imageView parity (2026-09-06):** a real `ImageView` item carries a `file://` URL (48/48 in the 0.153.4 corpus) and the normalizer strips it when it routes the rollout's own `item_completed` copy — the wrapper's live `view_image` twin strips it too, or the ONE card (both copies use the item id) rewrote its own text on re-attach. Pin: the same suite asserts the stripped path in the live `function_call` arguments + output AND that feeding the rollout copy afterwards leaves one card with unchanged text. **The 0.153.4 rollout writes NO `web_search_end`** (it persists the search as `item_completed` `Extension web.search`) — the wrapper's `web_search_end` is a LIVE-only relay of the same v2 item under the same `exec-…` id; see the cli_version table in the codex-message-manager.js essay before changing either side. **THE INPUT QUEUE — QUEUED vs STEERED (2026-09-06, owner ask; §queue-steer):** the wrapper OWNS the queue but does not KEEP it — `thread/queue/list` is the truth, re-read on every `thread/queue/changed` (the notification carries only `{threadId}`) and published as ONE typed event `queue_changed {items:[{id, msgId, preview≤120, ts, kind, from}], turn_id}` (fingerprint-deduped; also at boot and at each `turn/started`, so a client attaching mid-turn can rebuild the strip from the buffer). `queueMeta` (clientUserMessageId → {kind, msgId, ts, from}) is registered BEFORE the `thread/queue/add` RPC — the change notification's refresh can beat the add's own reply, and an item whose msgId we learn late renders with no bubble chip. The `queue-op` stdin verb serves `steer` / `remove` / `steer-all`. **MEASURED ON A LIVE 0.153.4 app-server, all four load-bearing (the design assumed a `thread/queue/remove` that does not exist):** ① the removal verb is `thread/queue/delete {threadId, queuedSubmissionId}` → `{deleted:true}`; the ClientRequest enum (printed verbatim by the server's own unknown-method error) is add/list/update/delete/reorder/start — **no `remove`** ② `turn/steer {threadId, input, expectedTurnId, clientUserMessageId}` → `{turnId}`, and it does **NOT** dequeue the item even when it carries that item's own clientUserMessageId ⇒ the wrapper deletes it or the message runs twice ③ several `turn/steer` calls inside ONE turn are accepted ⇒ `steer-all` is sequential steers in queue order, each keeping its own input (images + per-message ids survive), never one concatenated blob ④ a `thread/queue/add` on an IDLE thread starts a turn by itself — the app-server drains its own queue, we never call `turn/start` for a drained item. **ORDER IS STEER-FIRST, DELETE-ON-SUCCESS:** a steer failing is a DESIGNED path (`cannot steer a review turn` / `cannot steer a compact turn` = CodexErrorInfo::ActiveTurnNotSteerable, and `expected active turn id \`X\` but found \`Y\`` when the turn ended between the click and the RPC), and on that path the item must stay queued IN PLACE — which delete-first could not restore (re-adding appends). The wire carries only `{code:-32600, message}` (the typed CodexErrorInfo variants never reach the client), so `classifySteerFailure` discriminates on the message TEXT — deliberately, with the strings quoted from the binary's own table. Every outcome rides `queue_op_result {op, id, msg_id, ok, reason, detail}`; a steer that succeeded but whose delete failed reports `ok:true, reason:'steered-not-dequeued'` so the user is warned about a possible double run instead of it happening silently. A REFUSED `steer-all` emits ONLY the per-item result (which carries the real reason AND the real turn kind) and logs the abort to the wrapper journal — the `{op:'steer-all', ok:false, reason}` summary it used to emit as well rendered a SECOND card from the same failure, and, carrying no `kind`, made the normalizer name a compact turn "review" (round-1 review). The `ok:true, done:N` summary stays: the normalizer renders no card for a successful op. **STOP CLEARS THE QUEUE (owner decision 2026-09-07 — the ACP divergence is closed):** the `interrupt` verb runs `clearQueueForStop()` FIRST and only then `turn/interrupt`. A foreign `error` is recorded as the CHILD's `sub_agent_activity {kind:'errored', detail:<message>}` — a collab activity row, never this conversation's failure. Every foreign notification passes `foreignThreadOf(params)` FIRST; a foreign-thread `agentMessage` becomes an attributed `agent_message` record (`{type, id, thread_id, author, recipient, content:[output_text], phase, delivery, msg_type}`, author from `meta.subagents` = the agentPath→threadId map learned from `subAgentActivity`, else the thread id), every other foreign kind is DROPPED with a once-per-thread log + a `meta.foreignDrops{total, threads{<tid>:{dropped, agentMessages, agentPath}}}` counter. An OWN-thread `agentMessage` whose text starts with the inter-agent envelope (`Message Type: … / Task name: … / Sender: /root/x`) is ALSO an `agent_message` (author = the Sender line) — it was written FOR another agent, never a reply to the user. **The ENVELOPE is the only signal; `delivery === 'async'` is NOT (B-7473 integration 2026-09-06, MAJOR):** on an own-thread `agentMessage` that flag marks a question/async reply the USER is meant to read, and treating it as inter-agent DROPPED the text from the transcript entirely (an asked question simply vanished). Pinned with the stub: an own-thread `delivery:'async'` message with no envelope must appear as an assistant message. **`meta.agentPath`** (this thread's own path, the reference point that makes a message inbound or outbound) is ASSIGNED from the thread/start|resume reply when it carries one and echoed in the wrapper's `session_meta` record — it used to be READ in three places and never written; 0.153.4's `Thread` struct carries agentNickname/agentRole/parentThreadId but NO agentPath (checked against the installed binary's serde field list), so the '/root' default is what a VibeSpace-spawned thread actually is, and a RESUMED sub-agent conversation gets its real path from codex's own `session_meta` at line 0 of its rollout. `subAgentActivity` items fill the map and emit the live `event_msg sub_agent_activity` (the 0.153.4 rollout carries the same fact as `item_completed/SubAgentActivity`; the normalizer routes both to ONE path). Every item record now rides `recordItem()`, which stamps the notification's `thread_id`/`turn_id` — **both are stripped from `recordFingerprint` (codex-session-store) and `CodexMessageManager.recordKey`, or every buffer record becomes a stranger to its rollout twin (double cards on each attach)**. `caps.threadScoped: true` adverts it. `AGENT_ENVELOPE_RE`/`parseAgentEnvelope` are MIRRORED in src/codex-message-manager.js (a shipped single file cannot require it) — change one, change both. Pins: test-codex-p2-wrapper ④ (stub pushes a child agentMessage / an own-thread envelope one / a subAgentActivity / a plain root reply ⇒ exactly ONE assistant record). RESIDUE: records a PRE-B-7473 wrapper already wrote keep their root-assistant shape (the normalizer cannot tell them from a real reply) — they age out with the buffer; only NEW traffic is gated, and a restart of that session is the immediate cure.

### plugin-loader.js / plugin-manifest.js / plugin-client.js (Plugin Ph2 minimal, 2.369.24)

  The plugin system's first runtime slice (docs/design-harness-plugins.md §3.2–3.3). **Trust model as shipped**: iframe tier = untrusted UI (opaque origin, the published-pages CSP posture — NEVER add allow-same-origin; the bridge exposes only namespaced localStorage, toasts, close); server tier = a separate PROCESS with an IPC-only API (`route`/`tool`/`shutdown`) — plugin code is never require()d into the orchestrator; agent tools = generated shims that carry the calling session's vsst_ token to `/api/agent/plugin-tool/<id>/<name>` (cookie-exempt prefix ⇒ the route validates the bearer itself; unknown token = 401). Invariants: an invalid manifest is LISTED with its errors (never silently skipped) and cannot be enabled; enable/disable is atomic + broadcast; a crashing plugin restarts with backoff and is parked after 5 crashes/10min (never a crash loop against the box); shims are regenerated on every change and removed on disable; `hostVersion` is read from `<rootDir>/package.json` (never a relative require — the 2.341.1 lost-binding class). Trusted client modules, contributed settings/themes/keybindings, install UI, capability enforcement and remote shim shipping are the next slices (B-bb56/B-93f9). **SECURITY POSTURE after the 2.369.43 review (kb-bugfix-invariants “PLUGIN SECURITY BATCH”): a manifest is untrusted input — its free text may reach generated code only as a JSON literal (jsLiteral) and is sanitized once in the validator (cleanText); a declared fs path is collapsed — and its `*` wildcard MODELLED as the string prefix node actually matches (2.369.44) — before the forbidden-root test; contributed agent tools NEED consent (a shim is a program on every session PATH, outside the sandbox — the shipped hello-plugin example is consent-gated now); consent is recorded per PACKAGE (contentHash + source) and the reset is keyed on the REGISTRY RECORD, not on a folder having been replaced (2.369.44 — consent outlives a hand-deleted plugin dir), so replacing the code behind a trusted id disables it and re-prompts; proxied /x/* replies are data (nosniff + sandbox CSP, no document content-type from an untrusted plugin).** Pins: scripts/test-plugin-security.mjs (62) + scripts/test-plugin-loader.mjs (43: validator matrix + the shipped docs/examples/hello-plugin driven end to end — assets/CSP/traversal, IPC routes, tool + shim + 401, lifecycle).

### window-types.js (client window-type registry, Plugin Ph1)

  window-types.js — the first client contribution-point registry (2.369.19, docs/design-harness-plugins.md §3.2 `windows[]`): `registerWindowType({ type, icon (svg), label, replay(app, spec) → winInfo|null, persist?, singleton? })`, `getWindowType`, `windowTypeIcon`, `replayOpenSpec(app, spec)`. replayOpenSpec used to be an 18-case switch with no default — an unknown `openSpec.action` was silently dropped; now it warns + emits telemetry `openspec-unknown`. Core registers every existing kind at module load in the module that owns the window (session-lifecycle chat/terminal, file-viewer/editor, usage/settings/task/workflow/session-props/browser/jobs/desktop…), byte-identical behaviour; `TYPE_ICONS` (tab-group.js) is now a live view over the registry so existing importers keep working. A plugin's `windows[]` contribution will call the same registerWindowType. Pins: scripts/test-window-types.mjs (53: DOM-free node import, fake type dispatch, unknown-action warning, the exact core type/action sets, no switch/TYPE_ICONS literal left).

### contributions.js / gear-menu.js / appearance-panel.js (client commands + menus + keybindings registry, Plugin Ph1; the ⚙ menu TREE since 2.369.124)

  contributions.js — the second client contribution-point registry (docs/design-harness-plugins.md §3.2 `commands[]` + `menus[] {where, when, group}` + `keybindings[]`), built to window-types.js's rules: DOM-free at import (only telemetry-client), node-imported directly by its gate. `registerCommand({ id, title (string | ctx→string), run(ctx), when?(ctx), icon?, signal? })`, `registerMenuItem({ menu, command | label+run, id?, group?, order?, when?, label?, labelHtml?, disabled?, style?, tooltip?, children?, expand?, separator?, kind?, icon?, danger?, keepOpen?, decorate?, signal? })`, `menuItems(menu, ctx)` → showContextMenu-shaped items, `registerKeybinding({ key, command, when?, inTerminal?, signal? })` + `installKeybindings(document, { signal, getCtx })` (ONE bubble-phase dispatcher, app-lifetime AbortController in app.js), `runCommand(id, ctx)`. **Semantics (do not regress):** items sort by group ('navigation' first, then lexicographic), then `order`, then registration; `when` gates SURFACES (menus/keys) — `runCommand` never consults it (VS Code executeCommand); **SEPARATORS ARE EXPLICIT contributions** (VS Code's automatic between-group rule cannot reproduce the hand-built window menu, which joins Minimize and Close with NO rule when the session block is absent) and leading/trailing/doubled ones collapse; an EMPTY `children` result drops the item (the legacy `if (groups.length)` guards); `mod` = ctrl OR meta (the app's `(e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey)` convention), unlisted modifiers must be up; keys inside `.xterm` never match unless `inTerminal`; later bindings win. **Loud:** duplicate/malformed registrations THROW at module load; `runCommand` of an unknown id THROWS + telemetry `command-unknown`; an unknown command named by a menu item / keybinding warns once + telemetry (`menu-unknown-command` / `keybinding-unknown-command`) and is skipped; a throwing `when()` hides the item and warns once; a throwing keybound command is logged + `command-failed`. Every register* returns dispose() and honours `signal` — the plugin host API (plugin-client.js `api.registerCommand/registerMenuItem/registerKeybinding/runCommand`, ids namespaced `plugin:<id>:<slug>`) binds all three to the plugin's AbortController so contributions leave with the plugin; `api.registerMenuItem` REFUSES a `submenu:true` head without an explicit id SLUG (verifier r2 nit: the host's generated `item-N` id used to smuggle an id-less head past the registry's explicit-id rule — a head no member could name in `parent`). **Core dogfoods it, byte-identical:** the sidebar card menu = `session.*` commands + `registerSessionCardMenu()` in session-card.js (ctx `{ app, state, settings, s, card, event, displayName, customName, originalName, onRename, agentOpts }`); the window title-bar/taskbar/window-list menu = `window.*` commands + `registerWindowMenu()` in taskbar.js (ctx `{ app, id, win, s, switchSubmenu, closeLabel }`; `showWindowContextMenu`'s wrapAct fires `onAction(kind)` after items AND submenu children — Task Groups / Move to Desktop — never the Switch-window submenu; the session block REUSES `session.restart` (Restart / Resume labels via the item label override), `session.locate`, `session.properties`); the ⚙ menu = gear-menu.js `registerGearMenu()` (since 2.369.124 a TREE — see the gear-menu.js essay below; `buildGearMenu(app, pop)` renders with escHtml'd labels; mobile-nav's gear shares it via `_showGlobalSettings`). **THE TREE (2.369.124, docs/design-gear-menu-hierarchy.md §2c):** `submenu:true` marks a HEAD (needs an explicit `id` + `label`; forbids command/run/expand/children/separator — its members come through `parent`) and `parent:'<head id>'` files ANY item (a row, a separator, an `expand`, or another head) under it. Validation is LOUD wherever the chain is already known at registration (non-string parent, self-parent, a registered NON-head parent, a parent from another menu, a head chain deeper than two levels — checked from above AND from below, a cycle — the closing edge points at the record being registered, which findRec cannot see, so it is checked explicitly); a parent registered LATER is legal (module load order is not a contract). Resolution is LAZY at `menuItems()` over the VISIBLE heads: an unknown / `when`-hidden / non-head parent warns once (`parent:<menu>:<id>`) + telemetry `menu-unknown-parent` and the row **falls to top level — never dropped** (a lost row is the silent-failure class; the same rule surfaces a disposed head's members). A head's members become its `children` (same sort — NOTE group sorts BEFORE order inside a head too, so members carry no `group` — same separator collapse, `expand` splices INTO the head), an EMPTY head drops itself (the existing empty-submenu rule) unless it carries a `panel` (its content); the produced head item has `submenu:true`, `children`, no `action`, and the renderer hints `panel(ctx)` / `caption` / `keepOpen` / `checked` (a boolean on choice rows) pass through validated; a FUNCTION caption is ALSO handed through unresolved as `captionOf` (verifier r2, 2026-09-21: the Appearance head kept its build-time `14px` beside a stepper that said 15) so the renderer can re-evaluate it LIVE — a string caption carries no captionOf. showContextMenu consumers still read `children` (they know nothing of heads); the gear renderer is the only tree renderer today. Command mode registers every single-key action as `activeWindow.*`/`layout.*`/`desktop.*`/`session.new`/`sidebar.toggle`/`browser.open`/`explorer.open`/`commandMode.toggle`; the palette registers `session.palette`. **SIDE BY SIDE AS VERBS (split UX chunk 2, 2026-09-23, docs/design-split-ux.zh.md R1 ②③ / R2 — no drag ever splits, so the menu and the keys ARE the entries beside the tab strip's button):** the 'window' menu gains, inside `1_window` after Task Groups, ONE `window/side-by-side` submenu **Show side by side ▸** whose children are "**Beside {name} (on the right)**" per OTHER tab of the window's chain (name = the title's part before ` — `), each calling `wm.bindSplit(thisWin, thatWin, {side:'right', announce:true, focus:'anchor'})` — the verb NAMES the side (this window left, the named one right), never a pointer, and the focus stays on the window right-clicked (split r1: it used to land on the named partner); gated on `c.win._tabChain` with ≥ 2 tabs, `layout !== 'split'`, and NOT `app.isMobile` (the phone shows one pane, R6). A split chain offers `window.unsplit` (**Unsplit** → `wm.unbindSplit(chain)`, also on a phone) and `window.swapSides` (**Swap left and right** → `wm.swapSplit(chain)`) instead; all three carry kind `split` (the window list re-renders after them). A chain-less or ONE-tab window gets none of them, so the pre-registry matrix stays byte-identical (the gate's matrix runs every state with no chain AND with a one-tab chain). A tab's right-click opens THAT tab's own window menu (chunk 1), so the submenu excludes the window it was opened on. The live view's own `window/browser-bind` row (Snap beside / Unbind, order 35) is unchanged and its bind is now announced too (`toggleBind` → `announce:true` ⇒ the 5 s Undo toast); on a bound live view both vocabularies show (Unbind and Unsplit do the same act). Command mode: `chain.toggleSplit` (**`v`**: a tabs chain ⇒ `wm.splitActive(chain, {announce:true})` — the active tab left, the most recently used other tab right; a split ⇒ `unbindSplit`), `chain.swapSides` (**`V`**), `chain.unsplit`, `chain.splitBeside` (ctx `partnerId` ⇒ `bindSplit(active, partner, {side:'right', announce:true, focus:'anchor'})`), all on the ACTIVE window's chain; no group of ≥ 2 tabs (no active window, no chain, a one-tab chain, an unknown partner) ⇒ the toast "Group two windows first", `V`/unsplit on a tabs chain ⇒ "Not shown side by side" — never a silent no-op. The armed `[CMD]` hint lists `v split`. The command-mode block now closes over `registerCommand, showInputDialog, showToast, t` (the gate injects all four). **Their KEY DISPATCH deliberately stays where it was** (NOT registerKeybinding): the legacy checks are modifier-LENIENT (Ctrl+K opens on Ctrl+Shift+K too; Ctrl+\ ignores shift) and run in the capture phase in a load-bearing listener order, while the registry matcher is strict and bubble-phase — migrating them would change behaviour. Each register block is self-contained (`export function registerX() {…} registerX(); // end registerX`) so the gate can extract + replay it with its closed-over names injected. **THE FIRST CORE `registerKeybinding` CHORD (2026-09-07): `chat.steerNow` / `alt+enter`** (chat-view.js — see its essay). The pattern a future core chord copies: the COMMAND is registered ONCE at module scope behind `hasCommand()` (a duplicate id THROWS by design, so a per-instance registration would die on the second window), while the KEYBINDING is per instance, carries that instance's AbortSignal and a `when` that scopes the chord to the window the keystroke happened in — which is also what makes N simultaneous registrations of one chord legal (an unconditional duplicate pair throws; conditional ones are VS Code's own model). The dispatcher ctx is app-wide (`{ app, event }`), so the command resolves its target from `ctx.view` (an in-process caller handing itself in) or from the mounted view whose container holds `event.target` — never a "last focused" guess. The composer's own keydown routes through `runCommand` rather than calling the handler, so keyboard, button and plugin all run ONE verb. File-explorer menus (file-explorer-ops.js) are NOT migrated (out of the slice). Gate: scripts/test-contributions.mjs (functional in node + the three menus diffed against VERBATIM legacy builders over a state matrix + the REAL ws-handler default + wiring pins). **2.369.131: All Settings… is a direct row after Manage agents… (not the Appearance footer, not a Help child).**

MEMBERS CARRY NO `group` (inside a head, group sorts before order): the external owners file themselves — channels-panel 10 / channel-outbox 20 / integrations-window 30 under `comm`, desktop-app-launcher 30 under `tools` (Usage 10 · Background Work 20 · Plugins 40 · rule 50 · the plugin-windows `expand` 60) — and this block never learns their names. `buildGearMenu(app, pop)` = ONE renderer, TWO MODES chosen by `gearMenuMode(app)` (`app.isMobile || matchMedia('(hover: none)').matches` ⇒ accordion): FLYOUT = `.gs-flyout` appended INSIDE its head (a DOM descendant — mouseleave never fires when the pointer moves into it), `right:100%` (the popover is right-anchored), `data-popover` (utils.js attachPopoverClose treats a mousedown in it as ours), opened by 120 ms hover intent (`HOVER_INTENT_MS`; mouseleave cancels the timer, entering another head swaps, entering a plain row closes the deeper levels) AND by click / Enter / ArrowLeft — a click never toggles closed (the showContextMenu tap lesson: emulated mouseenter may already have opened it); clamped into the viewport on every open, measured in VIEWPORT px and written as layout px (/uiScale, the popover is a fixed body child under the body zoom). ### ws-handler.js (heartbeat + attach rebuild)

  ws-handler.js — **r1 of agent groups (2.369.159): `isTypedInput(chunk)` (exported) decides whether an `input` chunk stamps `session._userInputAt`** — a chunk made ONLY of the terminal's automatic answers (TERM_QUERY_RESP_RE) and focus events (`\e[I` / `\e[O`, DEC 1004) is the emulator, not a person, so it no longer flips a machine turn into a user turn (which would hand that turn the next-turn group reports). `chat-input` still stamps unconditionally. Gate: test-channel-groups §4c (focus / CPR / OSC / DA ⇒ no flip; a key, Enter, an arrow, typed text + a focus event ⇒ flip) + the §4b pin. **r2: MOUSE REPORTS are not typing either** — the CLI enables SGR mouse tracking, so a wheel scroll / click / release in the terminal (`\e[<b;x;yM|m`, X10 `\e[M` + 3 bytes; `TERM_MOUSE_RE`, the shape terminal.js strips under Ctrl+G) no longer stamps `_userInputAt` (a person scrolling to LOOK in the hand-off→hook window turned the woken, billed turn into a user turn that carried every group's report). Gate: §4c wheel/click/release/X10 rows + the typed-text-beside-a-wheel control.

  ws-handler.js — **2.369.157 r2 (design-reset-credits): the `codex-reset-credit` ws case is GONE.** It wrote the verb straight to the pty behind only the caps gate — a second writer outside the engine's `writeResetCredit`: no spend ceiling, no per-identity floor, no origin, so its failure walked the switch/wait ladder as an AUTO attempt (reproduced: 0 ledger charges, the pool switched and a wait armed). A person spends a credit through `POST /api/accounts/:id/reset-credit` (the confirm dialog); an old client's frame gets the `default:` `unknown-type` answer. `codex-read-limits` stays, gated on `quotaProbe === 'rpc-rate-limits'`. Census: test-reset-credit-ui §4 (writers / case labels / readers over every server-tier file); pins: test-harness-contract SITES + test-codex-pool.

  ws-handler.js — **`default:` case (Plugin Ph1): the `switch (data.type)` had NO default, so an unknown type vanished — no log, no telemetry, no reply, the sender waited forever.** Now `noteUnknownWsType(telemetry, type)` logs once per type per 10 minutes with the running count (a chatty stale client cannot flood the journal), records telemetry `ws-unknown-type` per occurrence, and replies `{ type:'error', code:'unknown-type', message, unknownType, reqId? }` — **deliberately WITHOUT sessionId**: ws.js routes session-scoped handlers by `d.sessionId`, and every client `error` consumer (chat-view's branch, terminal's per-session handler, session-lifecycle's create/attach/view handlers) keys on `msg.sessionId`/`msg.reqId` — a session-scoped error frame is what flips a live window into the exited/read-only path, and an unknown TYPE is not a dead session. `reqId` IS echoed so a `ws.request()` caller fails fast. `telemetry` joined WS_CTX_CONTRACT for it.

  ws-handler.js — **2.369.16 (userW inc-mtndq0vb): the first-attach history rebuild is TIME-SLICED and single-flight (`normalizers.rebuildHistory` → `convertHistoryAsync`, ~25ms slices yielding to the loop; concurrent attaches await one promise; live records arriving mid-rebuild queue on `session._rebuildQueue` and replay in order; `_historyLoaded` set after success). Every live record enters a session normalizer through `normalizers.feedLive(session, msg)` — a direct `session._normalizer.processLive` call is a gate bypass (test-attach-rebuild counts them = 0). Rebuilds are FIFO (one at a time — fair slicing landed every window at the total time) and the attach re-acks every 10s with `{progress}` while waiting/converting (client ladder extends on fresh acks, 15min bound), then re-checks the session is still live before sending `attached`. The heartbeat lives in src/server/ws-heartbeat.js and is STALL-AWARE with TWO detectors: tick lateness AND a 1s loop-gap pulse (a 30–35s block starting right after a ping ends with the tick only seconds late but the pong unread — the review's blind band); a tainted round terminates nobody, bounded at 6 consecutive pong-less tainted rounds; terminations are logged + telemetered. The old inline interval terminated a live client after a 4-minute rebuild stall and dropped its queued kills. `kill` replies `killed {sessionId: REQUESTED id, resolvedId, ok, reason}` to the requester in both outcomes (`exited` only reaches attached clients) — the client's `killSession` sends the backendSessionId fallback frame as a one-shot and resend-chases only the plain kill (a resent fallback would kill the resumed successor), with its watchdog disarming the request.**
