  ws-handler.js — **`queue-op` (2026-09-06, the ONE new case for QUEUED vs STEERED):** `{op:'steer'|'remove'|'steer-all', id}` validated against `capsOf(session.backend).inputModes` — a CAPABILITY, never a backend id (the frame-file-by-backend-id incident's rule). `queueOps:false` ⇒ "<Harness> owns its own input queue"; `steer` on a `steer:false` harness ⇒ "<Harness> cannot steer: a message sent during a turn runs after it. You can remove it instead." `adapter.formatQueueOp` is the second line of defense (its throw becomes the same refusal). **A SECOND GATE, the RUNNING WRAPPER:** `wrapperCaps(BUFFERS_DIR, id, socketPath).inputQueue` (the sidecar advert the wrapper itself writes) — or, for a REMOTE wrapper whose sidecar lives on ITS OWN machine, the in-band proof `session._normalizer.queuePublished()` — must also be true — the caps row describes a KIND of agent, while a dtach session started before this release satisfies the row and would have its `queue-op` frame dropped SILENTLY. Its refusal names the wrapper's start time and says "Terminate + Resume the session to get the controls"; the verdict is re-read every time (never cached negative — a wrapper resuming a huge thread writes its sidecar late; the 2.364.1 law). Every refusal is `{type:'error', code:'queue-op-unsupported', scope:'action', sessionId, error, message}` — and the CLIENT rule is an EXPLICIT SET, not "anything coded": **a per-session `error` is a scoped refusal (renders in chat, window untouched) when it carries `scope:'action'` or one of `SCOPED_REFUSAL_CODES` (input-rejected, not-codex-chat, queue-op-unsupported); everything else is the attach failure it used to be read as** (inc-mt2arppw was `input-rejected`; `not-codex-chat` had been read-only'ing live windows the same way ever since — but `ended-during-attach`, raised right here after the history rebuild, is CODED AND FATAL and must keep taking the view-only rescue; round-1 review caught the over-generalization). The attach payload gained `queue` (`session._normalizer.queueState()`) + `queueSupported`, and `created` carries `queue: []` + `queueSupported: false` (a just-spawned wrapper has reported nothing yet; its own baseline `queue_changed` turns the controls on) — the 2.368.4 enumerate-every-window-birth rule. **THE VERB TABLE (2026-09-07):** the gate is now `capsOf(backend).inputModes.queueVerbs` — no verbs ⇒ "<Harness> owns its own input queue", an undeclared verb ⇒ its OWN sentence from `queueVerbRefusal(op, label)`, each of which says what happens to the message anyway (a refusal that only says "no" leaves the user wondering whether it is lost). The frame grew `afterId` (carried ONLY when the client sent one, because `null` MEANS the front) and `text`; every refusal also carries a machine `reason` beside the sentence. The wrapper gate became a VERB gate too: `wrapperCaps().queueVerbs` (sidecar) or the normalizer's in-band `queueVerbsPublished()` (remote), with a wrapper that adverts `inputQueue` and no list mapped to `LEGACY_QUEUE_VERBS = remove/steer/steer-all` — an old build must neither be asked for a verb it would drop nor lose the verbs it does serve; a verb it does not serve is refused by NAME, listing what it does serve. The attach payload gained `queueVerbs` next to `queueSupported`, so the client renders exactly the controls this process will honour — **`null`, never `[]`, when the server knows nothing** (`created` always, `attached` when neither sidecar nor in-band list is readable): an empty ARRAY is a real answer the client INTERSECTS with, and sending it for "unknown" hid the entire strip from a session the server was serving the legacy three for (round-2 review). **ROUND-2 SERVER HARDENING (2026-09-07):** ① every refusal ECHOES `op` and `id` — this reply never becomes a `queue_op_result`, so the id is the only way the strip can find the row it marked pending (those rows spun forever); ② `edit` is the one verb carrying USER TEXT into a RAW PTY STDIN write, so it is bounded twice, both loudly: `QUEUE_EDIT_MAX_CHARS` (20000 — the wrapper's OWN cap, the one above which it publishes no `text` and therefore offers no edit control; parity-pinned) and, after the frame is built, `QUEUE_OP_MAX_BYTES` (64 KiB, the same threshold the `input` case treats as the shredding line — JSON escaping can multiply a control-char string sixfold, so the char cap does not imply the byte one). Both constants live in src/server/wrapper-files.js beside `LEGACY_QUEUE_VERBS`, which itself moved to the PURE `src/backend-caps.js` because the CLIENT applies the same mapping.

The user bubble a queued message came from wears the state instead: `_stampQueueChip(msgId, 'queued'|'steered'|'removed'|null)` joins through `userMessageIds` and rides the ordinary `edit` op, so an open window updates in place. Three rules that took a chip's lifecycle to get right: ① `queued_input` stamps the chip and returns — the old system card is gone, and survives ONLY as the fallback when there is no bubble to stamp (a peer/job message has no `webui_msg_id`), because a queued message must never be invisible ② an item that leaves the queue with no explicit steer/remove was drained by the turn ending, so its chip CLEARS — a bubble that keeps claiming to be queued forever is a lie ③ a failed `queue_op_result` becomes a VISIBLE notice, and `queueOpFailureText` (PURE, exported for the suite) words every branch in terms of what happens to the message NOW ("stays queued and runs when this turn ends" / "will simply run next" / "already ran"). The ACP normalizer carries the byte-identical trio. Two more, from the round-1 review: ④ the user bubble is stamped with **`webuiMsgId`** where `userMessageIds` is written — the map is server-side only, and the CLIENT chip has to join a rendered bubble back onto its queue row (without the stamp every chip click answered "That message is no longer queued") ⑤ `queuePublished()` — a wrapper that has never emitted a `queue_changed` (i.e. one that predates this release, but still emits `queued_input` as it has since 2.369.20) gets the OLD system card instead of a chip, because a chip there could never clear and never be acted on; the meta op carries `supported:true` so the client learns the same fact in band. **image_gen / sleep / elicitation card paths (2.369.58):** `_processImageGenEvent` and `_processSleepEvent` are the ONE renderer each fact funnels through — `item_completed Extension image_gen.generation` (rollout, the live wrapper's mirrored copy, and codex-thread-read's synthesis) and the ≤0.130 `response_item image_generation_call` all route into the first; `Extension clock.sleep` into the second. Canonical cards: `image_gen` with input `{prompt, path}` and output `status: <status>` + `saved <path>` (base64 `result` NEVER enters a card — the 2.369.35 law), `sleep` with input `{durationMs}` and output `slept 30s` (`formatSleptMs` is the ONE server-side duration formatter; the renderer's countdown formats a DIFFERENT thing, time remaining). Both are `collapseKind: null` — VISIBLE work, because a 20-minute wait folded into "N tool calls" is precisely how a deliberate pause reads as a hang. `_processServerRequest` also renders `mcpServer/elicitation/request` through the existing AskUserQuestion family (`kind:'user_input'`, rows from the wrapper's `payload.questions`; `mode:'url'` falls back to the plain approve card), and `isAllowedServerDecision` spans all five reply vocabularies. **TWO EFFORT FACTS, NEVER ONE (2.369.62):** `_status.effort` = what the CURRENT (or last) turn is running at — the value `_attachUsageMeta` bakes onto every message of that turn — and `_status.effortNext` = the pick that applies from the next turn. Conflating them is how a turn codex ran at 'ultra' reported 'xhigh' on every message: the live buffer held exactly ONE `turn_context` (the wrapper's synthesized copy, quoting a stale spawn env) for a session whose whole life was one app-server-started turn. `_noteEffort(live, next, emit)` is the ONE writer, so every carrier lands the same way — `turn_context` (a record that names an effort also SETTLES the pending question: `effort_next` present = a re-pick is waiting, absent = nothing is), the wrapper's `wrapper_meta` pair (the FALLBACK that makes a mid-turn attach honest when no turn_context is in range), and codex's own `thread_settings_applied` (the THREAD's effort = the NEXT turn's; it must NOT relabel the turn in flight, and only answers "now" before any turn has named one). It also EMITS `{op:'meta', subtype:'effort', data:{effort, effortNext}}` — chat-view routes it to `ChatStatusBar.setEffort`, so a `/effort` typed into the chat or another client's pick moves the chip live instead of waiting for a re-attach. Gate: scripts/test-codex-effort-meta.mjs. **`webui_queue_id` — the SECOND-CLASS user identity (2026-09-07):** the wrapper stamps it on the bubble it writes for a submission it never typed (an INHERITED queue item entering the turn). `_processResponseMessage` reads it into the same `webuiMsgId` field the chip joins on (`_stampUserIdentity`, the ONE writer of the bubble-id ⇄ userMessageIds pair), but it is deliberately second class: it does NOT suppress peer detection (most of the owner's 25 inherited items were agent-to-agent messages and must keep their labelled card, which a `webui_msg_id` would have turned into an anonymous "You" bubble), and `recordKey` STRIPS it (with `webui_queue_via` / `webui_after_commit`) exactly like `webui_peer` so the buffer copy and codex's rollout copy of that message mint the SAME message id — either may be the one that survives the merge. **Round 2:** such a bubble is also marked `midTurn` on the MESSAGE, and `_finalizeStreaming`'s backward scan treats it like a peer card (`m.role === 'user' && originKind !== 'peer-message' && !m.midTurn` is the boundary). It deliberately does not CLOSE the streams it landed among (finalizing there fragmented the reply — the 2.368.16 class), so it must not HIDE them from the scan either: without the exemption a reply left open when the turn ended stayed `status:'streaming'` forever — a phantom spinner on a dead, read-only conversation, on every `convertHistory` attach. `item_completed:UserMessage` stays an explicit member of `ITEM_COMPLETED_SKIPPED_TYPES` (its response_item is the bubble).

| cli_version | how a search persists | `results` |
|---|---|---|
| 0.120 / 0.125 / 0.130 | `event_msg web_search_end {call_id:'ws_…', query, action}` **+ an id-less Responses-API `web_search_call {status, action?}` on the next line** — the TWIN | never (1698 ends, 0 with the key) |
| 0.149.1 | `web_search_end` only (`call_id:'exec-…'`), no `web_search_call` anywhere | always (35/35) |
| **0.153.4 (installed)** | **no `web_search_end` at all** — only `event_msg item_completed {item:{type:'Extension', kind:'web.search', id:'exec-…', query, action, results}}` | always (245/245, `[]` = really none) |
| live (wrapper) | `function_call web_search` at item/started (EMPTY stub = the pending card) + `web_search_end` at item/completed (the v2 item relayed) | as the item carries |

  Three 0.153.4 rollouts with 20/43/30 searches rendered ZERO cards because `item_started`/`item_completed` sat in `SKIPPED_EVENT_TYPES` — and a skipped type emits no telemetry, so nothing said so. `_processEvent` now dispatches `item_completed` to `_processItemCompleted` BEFORE the generic skip (which the type stays in, for every other kind). **All carriers land on ONE card keyed by the item/call id** (the Extension id IS the exec-… id the wrapper's live card uses, so live + rollout edit the same card): `_finalizeToolCall` merges `{query, action}` into the input (mergeToolInput) and renders results through `renderSearchOutput` (src/search-card.js). **Dispatch is an explicit ALLOWLIST on `item.type`** (`ITEM_COMPLETED_SKIPPED_TYPES`, exported + pinned), never a fall-through: an unrecognised TOP-LEVEL type fires `codex-unknown-record:item_completed:<type>` once per type, an unknown Extension kind `…:item_completed:Extension:<kind>`, an unknown sub-agent kind `…:item_completed:SubAgentActivity:<kind>` — the telemetry means "never seen upstream", so a type we deliberately do not card is in the allowlist instead. **0.153.4 `item_completed` census (all 25 rollouts, snapshot 2026-09-06 — the corpus is LIVE: two scans an hour apart differed ~4%, so the RATIOS are the claim, not the totals; `item_started` is NEVER persisted — 0 records):** RENDERED ELSEWHERE ⇒ skipped by name — Reasoning 1480 / AgentMessage 84 carry an id that IS a response_item id (1480/1480, 84/84); CollabAgentToolCall 5 carries the function_call's call_id (5/5); CommandExecution 588 + FileChange 135 have no id twin but each is the RESULT of the `exec` custom_tool_call in front of it (876 `exec` calls, the only shell tool name in the corpus), whose card already shows the command and its output — **0.153.4 has NO standalone `apply_patch` tool call at all (0 in the corpus; the earlier "apply_patch exec count == FileChange count" claim was false): a patch rides the SAME `exec` call, whose input text carries the `*** Begin Patch` payload, and 135/135 FileChange items follow an exec naming the changed file**; UserMessage 31 is the already-rendered prompt; SubAgentActivity started 18 + interacted 214 carry the id of the tool CALL that caused them (spawn_agent 18/18, send_message 197 + followup_task 17), which renders its own card; ContextCompaction 1 is deliberately unrouted — the live wrapper emits its own `context_compacted` for the same item and the two spellings do NOT fingerprint-dedupe in the buffer⇄rollout merge, so routing it would print the notice (and bump turnIndex) twice on every live session; **known cost: a rollout-ONLY rebuild shows no compaction notice.** **ONLY CARRIER, so routed here: `Extension web.search` 245 → the search card, `Extension image_gen.generation` 3 → the existing image_gen card path (`revisedPrompt` in, `status` + `savedPath` out — the 3 MB base64 `result` NEVER enters a message, the 2.369.35 binary law), `ImageView` 54 → the view_image card path with `file://` stripped (the wrapper strips it too, so the live and rebuilt copies of that one card are byte-identical), `SubAgentActivity` kind `completed` 32 (over 18 distinct threads) → the `sub_agent_activity` card path.** The sub-agent completion is the second carrier this CLI MOVED: 0.153.4 persists no standalone `sub_agent_activity` event at all while 0.149.1 persists 349 of them (started 64 / interacted 277 / interrupted 8 / completed 0), and the completed records' id `subagent-completed-<uuid>` twins nothing — a sub-agent finishing was recorded NOWHERE else, so `_processSubAgentActivity` (extracted from `_processEvent`, now shared by the standalone event, the thread/read mapper and item_completed) CREATES the card when no 'started' opened one and is keyed by THREAD so any repeat is idempotent. Terminal kinds only: routing 'started'/'interacted' would double-render against their spawn/send cards. Old-vs-new whole-corpus replay: 0.153.4 gains exactly 18 Sub-agent cards and changes nothing else (search 246 / image 56 / bash 911 identical), 0.149.1 is card-for-card identical, telemetry 0 in both. **Twin pairing (0.120-0.130) is POSITIONAL:** one slot holds the immediately preceding SEARCH record (end or id-less call — intervening records never touch it, and both handlers overwrite it), so an orphan call later in the file with the same action never pairs with a stale end. Whole-file replays: the 0.125 file = 96 orphan calls then 104 end+call twins ⇒ 200 cards; the 0.130 file (2,119,710,127 bytes = **2.0 GiB**, 1,116,410 lines — `ls -l` on the named rollout; the first cut said "512 MB") = 1524 ends + 1324 calls (every call an adjacent twin) ⇒ 1524 cards, 0 empty, 0 'no results'. An end with action `{type:'other'}` is twinned by a call carrying NO action key at all — keyed apart they rendered the owner's exact second empty card (`{"query":"","action":null}` / 'status: completed'), so `searchActionKey` puts `{type:'other'}` and no-action in ONE bucket. An orphan call still renders its `status: …` card and `action` stays the OBJECT (the client's title chip reads `action.queries/url`); an orphan carrying NO action either (exactly ONE such record in the whole local corpus, 0.120.0) is LABELLED — head `web search (no details recorded)`, input `{note:'no details recorded'}` from the shared `NO_SEARCH_DETAILS` — so no card can reproduce the owner's reported empty shape `{"query":"","action":null}` / 'status: completed' byte for byte (old-vs-new replay of the 0.120.0 corpus: that shape 1 → 0, card count unchanged); `web_search_begin` (never persisted; live-stream tolerance) = pending card if none, else a query patch that keeps it pending. Gate: test-codex-history's web-search block — VERBATIM 0.153.4 records (search / other / openPage / findInPage-with-url-null / results:[] / image_gen / ImageView, cut from named rollouts + ordinals, anonymised) + verbatim 0.120.0 twin records + PATTERN replays of three whole rollouts (scripts/fixtures/codex-web-search-patterns.json: the real record order and action identity; `expectedCards` is ground truth computed OUTSIDE the normalizer) + the live+rollout one-card check + the unknown-kind telemetry control. **Regenerate the fixture** by re-walking ~/.codex/sessions READ-ONLY, grouping by `session_meta.cli_version`, and emitting E/C tokens per search record (`E~` = end with `{type:'other'}`, `C-` = action-less call).

  **MULTI-AGENT VISIBILITY (B-7473; supersedes the two card shapes above):** `item_completed` LEFT the skip set — corpus-scanning every local 0.153.4 rollout showed it is the ONLY carrier of sub-agent activity there (214 `item_completed/SubAgentActivity`, ZERO `event_msg sub_agent_activity` — that shape exists only on the wrapper's live stream). **ONE router, ONE dispatch (B-7473 integration 2026-09-06 integration):** `_processItemCompleted` is the ALLOWLIST router described above — it runs FIRST in `_processEvent` (the type stays in the generic `SKIPPED_EVENT_TYPES` as the fall-through, and test-codex-history pins the ORDER, not the membership), skips the `ITEM_COMPLETED_SKIPPED_TYPES` twins by name, routes Extension web.search / image_gen.generation / ImageView to their card paths, and sends EVERY SubAgentActivity kind to `_processSubAgentActivity`; anything else fires `codex-unknown-record:item_completed:<type>` (Extension kinds namespaced as `…:Extension:<kind>`) once per type.
  **SUB-AGENT LIFECYCLE — ONE implementation, ONE shape (the merge rule; state it before changing either side):** `_processSubAgentActivity` ① ALWAYS learns `agentPath → agent_thread_id` into `status().subagents` (that map is what makes an agent NAME clickable; it is learned even when no row is drawn), ② renders the fact as a one-line collab ACTIVITY row — **the old standalone "Sub-agent" tool CARD is RETIRED** (a card per lifecycle event buried the conversation; the row carries who/kind/thread plus the click-through), ③ draws NO row when the record's own id IS a rendered call: on 0.153.4 `started`'s id is the `spawn_agent` call_id (18/18) and `interacted`'s the `send_message`/`followup_task` call_id (197+17), and that call already drew its own collab row — the durable `_collabSeen` marker `call:<id>` (set when the collab call renders, NOT the `_collabByCall` entry, which is deleted when the call's output arrives) makes the suppression order-independent. Terminal records synthesise `subagent-completed-<uuid>`, twin nothing, and always draw. Dedupe keys `sa:<thread>:<kind>:<id>` and `sa:<thread>:<kind>` (a repeated 'started' is idempotent; 32 'completed' records over 18 threads ⇒ 18 rows). Three carriers, one path: the 0.149.1 standalone `event_msg sub_agent_activity` (349 records) and the wrapper's LIVE stream, the thread/read mapper (src/codex-thread-read.js), and 0.153.4's `item_completed`. A FOREIGN thread's `error` arrives here too, as kind `errored` with the message in `row.detail` (hover) — a child's failure is never the root's task_failed. Sub-agent traffic is a first-class `collab` shape on the message — `{dir:'in'|'out'|'spawn'|'wait'|'activity', agentPath, agentName, nickname, msgType, encrypted, target, cellId, threadId, kind, detail, rows:[…]}`: an inbound PLAINTEXT payload becomes an ATTRIBUTED **sub-agent report** (role 'tool', **collapseKind 'report'** — its OWN fold kind since B-7473 integration 2026-09-06, deliberately NOT in the default `chat.collapseKinds`: a child's written answer is CONTENT, and folding it under 'agent' hid the thing the owner opened the window to read; the rows stay 'agent' — envelope stripped, body rendered as markdown by the renderer), while encrypted inbound, outbound `send_message`/`followup_task`, `spawn_agent`, `wait` and lifecycle events are ONE-LINE rows that COALESCE into a single message (edit-in-place live, same on rebuild). The collab tool family never becomes a tool CARD: its `message` argument is a fernet blob upstream, and `collabDetailOf` only ever reads plaintext keys (prompt/description) — **no encrypted blob may reach a rendered string**. Twin dedup: live (wrapper, id `msg_…`) vs rollout (id `amsg_…`) by id, else by the CONTENT leg within the turn — the two ids differ, so the (author, text) leg is what actually kills the owner's duplicate. **That content leg only exists where there IS content (B-7473 integration 2026-09-06, MAJOR, measured on the owner's real root rollout):** an ENCRYPTED inter-agent message has `body === ''` and `msgType 'MESSAGE'` for EVERY message, so the `(turn, author, msgType, body)` key degenerated to one key per (turn, author) and SILENTLY DROPPED distinct messages — the verifier measured 101 of 140; re-measured on the same (still-growing) rollout at 3648 records, 120 of 168. Every one carries a distinct id AND a distinct blob, so the id leg never fired. Now: the (author, msgType, body) leg fires only when `body` is non-empty; an encrypted message dedupes by ID plus a discriminator taken from the fernet blob's first 32 chars (version + timestamp + IV). Pinned with three VERBATIM encrypted records from one agent in one turn ⇒ 3 rows coalesced into ONE "3 messages · water_research" item, never 1 (negative-controlled: the old key scores 1). `session_meta.agent_path` (own meta only) sets `status().agentPath`, the reference point that makes a message inbound or outbound. Labels/HTML come from the PURE src/collab-row.js. Gate: test-codex-0153 ⑥ (fixtures verbatim from the real 0.153.4 root rollout) + test-codex-subagents. **ONE IDENTITY PER SUB-AGENT (round-5, MAJOR, measured on the owner's real root rollout at 4807 records):** codex names the same child TWO ways — the OUTBOUND legs (`spawn_agent`/`send_message`/`followup_task` arguments) carry a BARE `task_name`/`target` ("interior_research"), while the spawn OUTPUT (`{"task_name":"/root/interior_research"}` — the proof of the intended shape), every inbound `agent_message` author and every SubAgentActivity record carry the absolute agent path. Keying rows on the raw value split each agent in two: **36 distinct row identities for 20 real children**, the fold header drew the same agent as two chips, the "N sub-agents" count over-reported, and the `agentPath → threadId` map (absolute keys) never matched an outbound row — **98 of 409 rows carried no thread id and therefore had NO click-through at all**. `absAgentPath(name, ownPath)` normalises any value WITHOUT a '/' to `(status().agentPath || '/root') + '/' + name` at the ONE place each row is built (collab tool call, agent-message envelope leg, spawn output, SubAgentActivity), so chips / map lookup / back-fill / summary all see one identity: after = **20 identities, 20 map entries, 408/409 rows with a thread id** (the 409th is the agent-less `wait` row) and the message/report/row counts UNCHANGED. `_noteSubagentThread` carries the BELT: its back-fill also matches a row whose own path has NO '/' against the key's last segment — deliberately one-directional, because two parents may each own a child named `research` and mapping one onto the other's thread would open the WRONG conversation (a wrong answer is worse than a missing one; negative-controlled). **ERRORS ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE (round-5, MINOR):** every other lifecycle kind repeats the same fact, so `(thread, kind)` is the right coalescing for them — but an `errored` record carries a MESSAGE, and that key silently dropped every error after a child's first, differently worded or not. `errored` now keys on `sa:<tid>:errored:<id>|<detail>`: a genuine re-read of one record collapses (both legs equal) while two differently-worded failures never do, EVEN IF their ids collide — the wrapper's synthesized `foreign-error-<tid>-<Date.now()>` was not unique for two failures inside one millisecond (it now appends a counter too, but the key does not depend on that). No eviction on that lane on purpose: `_collabSeen` also holds the durable `call:<id>` double-render markers and an FIFO sweep would drop one while its twin is still to come. Pins: test-codex-subagents ④ (real-shaped fixture: one identity, every row's thread id, one map entry, the same-leaf-name negative control, three distinct errors ⇒ three rows, the id-collision case, and 'completed' still coalescing).

**LIVE WORKFLOW DETAIL (2.369.118).** `task_progress` records also carry `usage {total_tokens, tool_uses, duration_ms}` and, for a Workflow run, `workflow_progress` = a LIST of `{type:'workflow_phase', index, title}` and `{type:'workflow_agent', index, label, phaseIndex, phaseTitle, agentId, model, state, lastToolName, lastToolSummary, attempt, startedAt, promptPreview}`. The tree is INTERMITTENT (heartbeats omit it), so it is latest-value FIELD-WISE: PURE `normalizeWorkflowProgress(list)` (exported; strings bounded, ≤200 agents, prompt preview dropped) returns null for a payload without a tree and the branch keeps `taskInfo.workflow` as held; `taskInfo.usage` refreshes on every record. Live stream only — the transcript never carries task_progress — so chat-renderers' `workflowLiveHtml` (phases → agent chips: label · state dot · last tool; tally + usage) is a live-session affordance and the post-hoc View Workflow window stays the history surface; chat-view re-renders a WORKFLOW tool card on its taskInfo edit through `_swapMessageEl` (agent cards are excluded — their live status line is drawn by `_onSubagentMessage` and a re-render would wipe it). Gate: test-task-lifecycle.

**UNKNOWN EVENT = THE FALL-BACK CARD (2.369.119 → .120, owner: "未知的 event 不要直接过滤掉" → "正常放在对话流里作为兜底").** `_processMessage`'s switch gained a `default:` and `_processSystem`'s unknown-subtype breadcrumb gained a body: a top-level type not in `KNOWN_IGNORED_RECORD_TYPES` (what the server consumer owns — tool_progress / set_in_progress_tool_use_ids / rate_limit_event / compact_progress / command_lifecycle / stream_event / keep_alive / _stdin_ack / _remote_state — plus the transcript's bookkeeping rows: last-prompt / custom-title / agent-name / permission-mode / mode / pr-link / atis-latch / file-history-* / cost-state / summary / progress) or a system subtype not in `HANDLED_SYSTEM_SUBTYPES` ∪ `KNOWN_IGNORED_SYSTEM_SUBTYPES` (thinking_tokens / background_tasks_changed / task_updated / hook_started / compact_boundary / success — the 2026-09-20 census's bookkeeping) goes through `_noteUnknownRecord(kind, name, raw, emit)`: EVERY such record, history and live alike (a rebuild renders the same cards — it is the catch-all renderer, not an alert), `noticeKind: 'unknown-record'`, block `{type:'unknown_record', kind, name, harness, record}` with `unknownRecordJson` (the WHOLE record pretty-printed, bounded at 64 KB). The codex twin is `_noteUnknown(kind, type, raw, emit)` on the top-level record path. chat-renderers `renderSystemMsg` draws the red-bordered "Unknown event" card (`.chat-unknown-event`, the record behind a "Full record" expander); chat-run-summary classifies it as kind `unknown` ("{n} unknown events") and `chat.collapseKinds` offers the toggle UNCHECKED. Adding a name to an ignored list is a DECISION that it deserves no card. Gate: test-unknown-records (incl. the consumer-type census: every `msg.type === '…'` the server consumer handles must be declared ignored).

### turn-state.js / rewind-ops.js (B3 turn truth — design-harness-features §2.5 / §2.10 / §2.11 / §3.5)

  **src/turn-state.js — PURE authoritative turn state.** "Is a turn running right now" backs the Stop button, auto-resume's *it is already working* skip, the attach payload's `isStreaming` and the session-card chips — and every one of them used to read a flag we INFERRED from record shapes (a `result` ends the turn; a `user` record starts one), the fuzzy area both 2.339.2 (stuck thinking) and 2.369.16 (attach storm) landed in. Claude Code 2.1.257 publishes the fact itself: `{type:'system', subtype:'session_state_changed', state:'idle'|'running'|'requires_action', uuid, session_id}` — its own `.describe()` reads *"'idle' fires after heldBackResult flushes and the bg-agent do-while exits — authoritative turn-over signal"*, i.e. strictly LATER than the `result` we used to end turns on. **The record only exists when `CLAUDE_CODE_EMIT_SESSION_STATE_EVENTS` is in the CLI's env** (`if (a.CLAUDE_CODE_EMIT_SESSION_STATE_EVENTS) mu({type:"system",subtype:"session_state_changed",state:e})`, read out of the binary), so `src/adapters/claude-code.js` SETS it on every **chat** spawn (owner decision 8(c): the ONE spawn default this batch changes, pure observability; NOT on terminal spawns — the stream-json parse is its only reader and nothing verified what the TUI's yield sink does with an extra record). `agentEnv()` is a DROP table, so the env passes through with no allowlist edit — never add it to AGENT_ENV_KEEP. Exports: `isTurnState` (unknown state ⇒ NEVER coerced to idle), `turnStateEffect(state,{hasLabel})` (what a state means for `_isStreaming` + the spinner label — `requires_action` is a LIVE turn paused on the user, and a bare `running` does not stomp a live tool label). **A turn state may only write a spinner line that stays TRUE for the rest of the turn (round 8, reproduced defect):** the wire's resume record is a bare `{state:'running'}` carrying no tool name, so nothing can RETRACT a line whose truth ended with the pause — the round-7 shape wrote `'waiting for you'` at `requires_action` and the very next `running` (whose job is "leave the derived label alone") faithfully preserved it for the whole tool run, contradicting a chip that had already flipped back. So `requires_action` writes **no line at all** (its voice is the status-bar chip), leaving exactly the two writes that cannot go stale: `''` on `idle` and `'thinking...'` onto an empty line. That is also what makes the consumer's `hasLabel: !!session._streamingLabel` sound — whatever is on the line when a `running` arrives is still true, `reconcileAttachStreaming({turnStateSeen,turnState,isStreaming,sidecar})` (ONE attach decision: rung ① the harness's own last state wins in BOTH directions; rung ② the wrapper sidecar stays the 2.339.2 backstop but is a DERIVED observer, so under authority its settle window is 30s instead of 3s and a heal that fires anyway is flagged `staleAuthority` → telemetry `turn-state-stale` + `session._turnState='idle'`, because a lost `idle` record must never wedge a session on "thinking" forever; a sidecar can only END a turn, never start one; an unreadable sidecar heals nothing). **PURE because the decision is made in TWO places** — the live consumer (`src/server/stdout/claude-stream-json.js`) and the ws attach path — and a twin between those two is the whole stuck-thinking family. Session fields: `_turnState` (last observed), `_turnStateSeen` (the latch that stands the derived writes down — false forever on an old CLI, which is the DEFAULT path, not an error path), `_inProgressTools`. Caps: `turnState:'authoritative'|'derived'|null` + `inProgressTools:bool` in src/backend-caps.js, mirrored in BACKEND_META (test-harness-contract deep-compares both keys in both directions). The tool-granular twin is claude's `set_in_progress_tool_use_ids {op:{action:'add'|'remove', ids}}` (*"Surfaces use this to show which tools are running"*) — consumed card-less in the same consumer, resolved to a SET, pushed as `tools-in-progress`, and carried on the attach payload; a PENDING card is not a RUNNING one (between parse and execution a tool can sit on a permission prompt). **That whole lane is DORMANT and `inProgressTools` is `false` everywhere (round 4, measured on the WIRE): 2.1.257 hands the record to a host callback and returns (`n.onInProgressToolUseIDs?.(e.op); return`), so it never reaches a stream-json consumer — a probe in the wrapper's exact spawn shape saw 6 tool_use / 6 tool_result and 0 records while `session_state_changed` arrived on the same stdout, and 24 production buffers hold 212 tool_use blocks and 0 records.** The consumer, broadcast, attach field and `.chat-tool-inflight` dot are kept as written-and-pinned code; the ONLY thing that may flip the cap is test-stdout-registry's wire-reachability leg (`scripts/probe-claude-stdout.mjs`, one read-only turn, loud SKIP without a CLI) observing one — it asserts caps⇄wire agreement in BOTH directions and its failure message names the two files to edit. Client: `chat-status-bar.setTurnState` draws a chip ONLY for `requires_action` (idle/running are already said by the composer's spinner — one fact must not have two voices), `chat-view._onToolsInProgress` toggles `.chat-tool-inflight`. **Session death retires BOTH, through ONE named owner** (round 8): `chat-view._retireLiveClaims()` — called from the `exited` branch — clears the compaction stage, `setTurnState(null)` (nobody reports a state any more; never `idle`, which would be a claim about a dead process) and `_onToolsInProgress([])`. It exists as one method because the previous version retired only the compaction stage from that branch, so "which claims does session death retire" had no home and a terminated session kept a pulsing "waiting for you" chip forever; a NEW live claim is added there and gets a row in test-turn-truth-ui ⓪b's CLAIMS table. **Gates:** test-stdout-registry (real-shape fixtures + the env-absent degradation leg + the pure reconciler table), test-attach-rebuild (reconciliation table + wiring pins), test-harness-contract (caps rows + client mirror + "the 'authoritative' claim is backed by the consumer actually driving _isStreaming"), test-turn-truth-ui (375×667 chrome).

  **src/rewind-ops.js — PURE retraction semantics.** Two harnesses tell us on the live stream that part of the conversation has been TAKEN BACK, and both were dropped on the floor. claude: `{type:'tombstone', message:<the retracted Message>, uuid, session_id}` — *"Emitted when a previously-yielded message is superseded or removed from the transcript (e.g., streaming→non-streaming fallback removes a partial orphan). Consumers that render or persist the stream should remove the referenced message"* — and we do BOTH, so a retracted half-message lived in the transcript forever. codex: `{type:'event_msg', payload:{type:'thread_rolled_back', num_turns:N}}` — `ThreadRolledBackEvent` has exactly ONE field (0.153.4 serde dump) and `thread/rollback`'s param doc defines it: *"The number of turns to drop from the end of the thread"*; it sat in `SKIPPED_EVENT_TYPES` since the codex normalizer existed, so a rollback made from the codex TUI left ghost turns on screen. The **rollout carries the identical payload** the live stream does (verified on the owner's two real rollouts that contain it: num_turns 11 → 45 messages struck, num_turns 1 → 2), so ONE handler covers both reads — the §6 union-survey rule. Both land on ONE normalized op `{op:'meta', subtype:'rewound', data:{harness, toMessageId, numTurns, ids, kind, ts}}`; exactly one of toMessageId/numTurns is non-null and BOTH keys are always present (a null is a statement, an absent key is a gap). **MARK, NEVER SPLICE:** removing entries would shift every index under `slice(offset,limit)` and change `total` under a client mid-pagination — the machinery three paging incidents came out of. `kind` decides the treatment: `'superseded'` (claude) is HIDDEN, following the CLI's own instruction, because the canonical copy is right beside it; `'rollback'` (codex) is STRUCK IN PLACE with a "rewound" tag, because hiding it would silently rewrite what someone remembers reading. **HONEST STATUS (round 4): the codex half is VERIFIED (`thread_rolled_back` exists in 3 real local rollouts) and is the retraction lane that actually runs today; the claude half is UNVERIFIED — 0 `tombstone` records in 24 production buffers, 0 in the live wire probe, and 0 of 7450 files under `~/.claude/projects/`, so the persisted path cannot produce one either.** It is NOT disproven the way `set_in_progress_tool_use_ids`/`compact_progress` are (those go to host callbacks; this one is `yield`ed onto the query stream at 185068785 / 185075330) — it simply needs a server REFUSAL-FALLBACK (`ks.type==="refusal_no_fallback"` / the `server_fallback` + `api_refusal_category` branch), which is not deterministically triggerable and which we will not provoke to satisfy a test. `_processTombstone` and the `superseded` rendering stay as dormant, test-pinned code. A codex turn is counted by USER messages, not by our `turnIndex` (that counter also advances on task_started and on compaction — one codex turn spans up to two of them: 24 user records under 30 turnIndex groups on a real rollout); already-rewound messages are skipped so two rollbacks in a row each take N LIVE turns; `num_turns` beyond what we ever rendered reports BOTH numbers instead of claiming N were struck. Both normalizers drop rewound messages from `turnMap()` (the minimap must not point at a ghost turn), and the codex side ALSO threads `noticeKind` through `_create` — it was silently dropped there since 2.369.20, the exact 2.227.4 gap the claude normalizer documents. **Gates:** test-codex-history (three turns + `thread_rolled_back` num_turns=1 ⇒ two rendered, WITH the negative control that renders three without the record; live/rebuilt agreement; double rollback; over-deep rollback), test-stdout-registry (tombstone leg + the negative control for a tombstone naming a message we never rendered), test-turn-truth-ui (the two treatments measured in chrome).

  **Compaction stage (§2.11) — `system/status` is the lane, `compact_progress` is shape parity.** THE WIRE (round 4, a REAL AUTO compaction captured verbatim in data/session-buffers/sess-5-1788332329337.buf lines 57-62; pre_tokens 997587 → post_tokens 11159, duration_ms **174751**): `system/status {status:"compacting"}` → `system/hook_started SessionStart:compact` → `hook_response` → `system/status {status:null, compact_result:"success"}` → `system/compact_boundary {compact_metadata:{trigger:"auto",…}}`, and **zero** `compact_progress` records. The CLI's host callback `onCompactEvent` CONSUMES `compact_progress` (`case"compact_progress":P.main.applyCompactProgress(x.event);return`, offset 201341255 — a TUI spinner store) and forwards only its `sdk_status` twin, which `HRt` (198800990) maps to this record (`{type:"system",subtype:"status",status,compact_result?,compact_error?}`, 190037796); the whole channel carries just two values (15 `sdk_status` emitters, all `"compacting"` or `null`) plus a `"requesting"` the forwarder filters out itself (`function wJt(e){return e!=="requesting"&&k5()}`, 198800730). So the consumer drives §2.11 from `system/status`: `{status:'compacting'}` sets `session._streamingKind='compacting'` + the label and broadcasts a `compact-progress {event:'compact_start'}` frame; a `hook_started` while that kind is set names the hook phase (gated on the kind — hook_started is in 13 of 24 production buffers and is none of this branch's business in a normal turn); `{status:null}` with `compact_result`/`compact_error` (or while compacting) clears the kind and reports the OUTCOME. **This is also the ONLY lane that sees an AUTO compaction** — the one nobody typed `/compact` for, which ws-handler's send-site label structurally cannot see and which is the only compaction a long session ever hits; the Stop two-step guard (2.365.0) now arms from it. NEGATIVE CASE, in code and in tests: the SAME subtype carries the CLI's permission-mode echo (`_r(p,P)` = `{status:null, permissionMode}`, 199038328) — an outcome field (or the absence of `permissionMode`) is what makes the record ours, never `status:null` alone. `'status'` is in HANDLED_SYSTEM_SUBTYPES, card-less like `api_retry`. The client keeps ONE frame shape for both lanes and KEEPS the terminal stage: `chat-renderers.compactHintText()` is the one sentence under "Compact now", the hardcoded *"…takes 1–2 minutes — do not press Stop…"* apology is its FALLBACK, and a finished compaction reports success/failure instead of silently reverting to an apology for something that already ended. **But a KEPT terminal stage belongs to the compaction it describes, not to the view forever (round 5).** Nothing ever cleared `_compactStage`, so the FIRST compaction of a view — including the AUTO one this lane newly covers, which no user action precedes — permanently replaced the guidance every later "Prompt is too long" card exists to give (the button's sentence read "Compaction finished." instead of the rewind-and-retry instruction; reproduced at 375×667 against the real bundle by replaying the production AUTO frames with no card on screen). `compactInFlight()` is the ONE predicate: `setCompactStage` still rewrites every hint ALREADY on screen (a card that WATCHED the compaction keeps its outcome — round 4 intact), while `appendContextFullCard` renders `compactFallbackHint()` unless a compaction is actually running. **AND A CLAIM ABOUT *RIGHT NOW* NEEDS ITS OWN CLOSING (round 6).** Round 5 closed the TERMINAL half; the NON-terminal half stayed open. `session._streamingKind === 'compacting'` is a claim about this instant, the client mirrors it as the held `_compactStage`, and `compactInFlight()` gates the WHOLE guidance card — but only the `status:null` outcome record retired that claim OUT LOUD. The other two turn-lifecycle exits (`result`/`compact_boundary`, and the harness's own idle `session_state_changed`) cleared `_streamingKind` SILENTLY. A compaction that ends with no outcome record is a real wire shape, not a theoretical one — a PreCompact hook that BLOCKS it makes the CLI emit a bare `sdk_status status:null` with no metadata (which this branch correctly refuses to read as an outcome), and ws-handler's `/compact` send site sets the kind BEFORE the CLI has said anything at all — so the client kept "Compacting: running <hook> hooks…" forever and every later "Prompt is too long" card lost the rewind-and-retry sentence it exists to give (reproduced on the real engine: frames `["hooks_start"]`, `_streamingKind` already null, no `compact_end`). Fix = ONE named `retireCompaction(sess, sid)` — acts only when the kind is 'compacting', clears it and broadcasts `compact_end` — called at BOTH exits; on the normal path the outcome record has already cleared the kind, so there is never a second frame. `result: null` on purpose: round 5's law holds at the new exit too, so the card says "Compaction ended.", never "finished". The suite pins both exits' frame sequences, two negative controls (a SECOND turn end broadcasts nothing; an ordinary turn produces no frame at either exit) and a WIRING PIN on the call sites — a THIRD exit's silence is visible only through that. The browser leg no longer hand-writes the frames: it runs the REAL consumer in node, takes what it actually broadcasts, and replays THAT into the real client. **And "ended" is not "succeeded":** a `compact_end` with no outcome is a real wire shape — a PreCompact hook that BLOCKS the compaction makes the CLI emit a bare `sdk_status status:null` with no metadata (`if(ye.blockedBy)…onCompactEvent({type:"sdk_status",status:null})`), and the dormant `compact_progress` lane hardcodes `result:null` on every frame — so only the CLI's own `"success"` is reported as finished and an empty outcome says "Compaction ended." (new zh/ja keys). **The declared lane `{type:'compact_progress', event: hooks_start{hook_type} | compact_start{hint_text?} | compact_end}` is kept as a reader for shape parity only** — no VibeSpace-spawned CLI has ever emitted one. Its round-2 lesson still stands and is still pinned, because inside the CLI the emitters and the schema disagree: the zod union (offset 179096059) says `hook_type`/`hint_text` while **every producer builds camelCase** (183979983 / 183980713 / 185190125 / 185193937 / 185195701 / 185198872 / 185209427 / 192261073), the CLI's own consumer reads `t.hookType` / `t.hintText` (189086200), and `grep -aob 'hint_text:'` finds exactly ONE hit — the schema literal. So that reader takes **both spellings at ONE point** (`ev.hook_type ?? ev.hookType`, `ev.hint_text ?? ev.hintText`), declared-first, and publishes the same normalized broadcast. **Invariants: (1) a record shape is what the EMITTER writes, not what the schema declares; (2) a record that EXISTS is not a record that ARRIVES — dump the emit sites AND look at our own stdout, because a suite that synthesizes the record can never tell "we parse it right" from "it never came".** test-stdout-registry pins the `system/status` sequence against the production capture (start / hook stage / outcome / error) with four negative controls (compact_boundary adds no second frame; a permission-mode echo inside and outside a compaction changes nothing; hook_started in a normal turn is invisible), keeps the camelCase/snake_case parity legs for the dormant lane, re-dumps the binary when a CLI is installed (SKIP with the reason otherwise), and runs the wire probe — whose leg ⓕ′ measures that the probe left NOTHING behind (scripts/probe-claude-stdout.mjs), **applying the SWEEP'S OWN RULE rather than one of its own (round 6)**: the sweep spares leftovers younger than 10 minutes because a CONCURRENTLY RUNNING probe owns them (two worktrees pushing minutes apart really do overlap), so an assert of ABSOLUTE ABSENCE turned the mandatory pre-push gate red on exactly the case the sweep exists to spare — and blamed the sweep. The probe now REPORTS its rule (`cleaned.staleMs`, `cleaned.spared:[{name,ageMs}]`) and both readers (the project-dir scan and `discoverClaudeSessions`) filter by it, measured in BOTH directions on the SAME directory (fresh ⇒ both readers pass and it IS visible; backdated past the threshold ⇒ both name it). Leg ⓕ″ then drives the probe's contracts DETERMINISTICALLY against a FAKE claude in an isolated HOME+TMPDIR (zero vendor cost, and the fake leaves the real CLI's footprint — transcript + per-session env dir + a ledger of both — so "left nothing behind" is never vacuous): stale swept / concurrent spared / own footprint gone, and the RAW CAPTURE's two symlink attacks. Round 5 had moved that capture from the 0700 mkdtemp dir to a PREDICTABLE name directly in /tmp, and `fs.writeFileSync` FOLLOWS symlinks — /tmp's sticky bit stops another local user deleting our file, not CREATING that name first, so a planted `/tmp/vs-wire-probe.last.jsonl -> victim` had the victim truncated and rewritten with CLI stdout under the developer's uid on every non-docs push (reproduced). It now lives at `<tmp>/vs-wire-probe-raw-<uid>/last.jsonl`: a dir this uid owns, created 0700 and re-checked with `lstat` (the DIR name can be planted too), opened `O_NOFOLLOW|O_CREAT` — **no O_TRUNC** (round 7: this line used to say there was one, and the code deliberately omits it; truncating inside the open would empty somebody else's plain file BEFORE the fstat that learns whose it is, which is the hole the block exists to close) — then fstat-verified (regular file, our uid) and only then `ftruncate`d, and anything unexpected SKIPS the capture WITH A REASON instead of writing where it was not asked to; the sweep skips that dir and retires round 5's old filename.

  **ROUND 7 — the same three questions, one layer down.** (a) **A GUARD IS PINNED ON THE WRITE THAT BREAKS IT, NOT ON THE CALL SITE.** Round 6's `retires === 2` detects a DELETED call and is blind to a FOURTH exit clearing the kind itself (reproduced: a `system/vs_fake_silent_exit` branch writing `session._streamingKind = null` left all 168 asserts green, pin included). `endCompaction(sess, sid, {result, error, announce})` is now the ONE WRITER of the cleared kind — `retireCompaction` is its guarded wrapper, the outcome record calls it with the CLI's verdict, the dormant `compact_progress` lane calls it with `announce:false` because it publishes its own frame — and test-stdout-registry pins a CENSUS of `_streamingKind = null` writes in that file at exactly ONE (comment lines excluded), so a fifth exit is a new write and goes red by construction. A second, BEHAVIOURAL leg reads the consumer's OWN vocabulary (every literal compared against `msg.type`/`msg.subtype`) and drives each shape through the real consumer with the kind armed: the law is "either the claim survives, or a `compact_end` went out in the same record". (b) **SESSION DEATH IS THE THIRD EXIT.** The wrapper dying is the exit no record can announce: the server retires through the consumer's own bound `session._retireCompaction` (session-schema row) BEFORE the `exited` broadcast, and the client retires locally in the `exited` branch via `ChatView._retireCompactionStage()` — a server that CRASHED sends no frame at all, and 'exited' is the one thing the view always learns. Both are guarded (`compactInFlight()` / kind === 'compacting'), so a session that never compacted is never made to claim one ended, and both send `result:null` — ENDED, never "finished". (c) **THE SWEEP EXPORTS ITS CLOCK, NOT JUST ITS THRESHOLD.** Round 6's readers re-derived staleness at ASSERTION time, so a leftover the sweep spared at 9m58s was flagged at 10m01s — the mandatory gate going red on exactly the case the sweep exists to spare, again. `cleaned` now carries `sweptAt`, `spared` is built by the SAME pass that decided (name + the age measured THEN), and both readers use that clock AND exclude the spared names — a decision, not a measurement. (d) **THE FAKE CLI NAMES THE INTERPRETER RUNNING THE SUITE** (`#!${process.execPath}`, its directory on the probe's PATH): `#!/usr/bin/env node` against a PATH of `<fakebin>:/usr/bin:/bin` is unrunnable on an nvm-only box / the project's own node:22-slim image / an actions/setup-node runner, and leg ⓕ″ then died on `path.dirname(undefined)`, taking ~65 later asserts with it. The leg is now a labelled block: a probe that could not run gets ONE loud red naming its `skip` reason and bails, never a crash. test-turn-truth-ui adds the round-5 legs: the production AUTO frames replayed with NO card on screen, then a card appended and asserted actionable again, with three negative controls (a card built while a compaction is IN FLIGHT still opens on the live stage; the card that watched it keeps its outcome; only `"success"` says finished).

  **Per-element marks must be RE-DERIVED, never remembered by an element (`chat-view._applyElementMarks`, round 2).** Both of the client-side marks this batch added — the retraction strike/hide (`_applyRewound`) and the executing-tool dot (`_onToolsInProgress`) — were written straight to the DOM at their origin, and **FOUR code paths build an element for a message**: `_onCreateMessage` (also the paging path, via `_renderDetached`), the status-transition re-render inside `_onEditMessage`, `_rerenderVisible` (the compact-mode toggle), and — round 3 — `_renderGapMsg` (the huge-session seek renderer in chat-view-seek.js). The two replacement paths carried over `dataset.msgId/ts/line` and the run open/closed marks and nothing else, so a mark died on the first re-render. **The claude tombstone case ALWAYS gets one:** the message it retracts is a *streaming partial orphan*, and `MessageManager._finalizeStreaming` emits `{op:'edit', id, fields:{status:'complete'}}` for exactly that message at the next `result` — so the retracted answer came back on screen one record later, while an attach/rebuild (which reads `msg.rewound` off the normalizer) still hid it: the precise live-vs-rebuilt divergence the create path's comment claims cannot happen. The in-flight dot had the same shape with a worse tail — for a long-running tool the next `set_in_progress_tool_use_ids` delta may never come, so scrolling the card out and back silently un-marked it forever. The fix is NOT a third copy of the mark code at each site (that is the same miss with more copies): ONE `_applyElementMarks(el, msg)` called at every place an element is **BUILT FOR A MESSAGE**, which asks the VIEW STATE what the element should be wearing (`msg.rewound` → `_markRewoundEl`; `this._inFlightTools` → `.chat-tool-inflight`, toggled so it is idempotent). A new per-element mark is added there and is correct in all four paths. **Round 3 corrected the RULE, not the mechanism.** It was first written as "every place an element enters `this._elements`" — and gap-slab elements are deliberately kept OUT of that map (they sit outside the virtual window's accounting), so the hook skipped `_renderGapMsg` entirely and a retraction reached through a seek slab rendered as ordinary live history. Reachability is not theoretical and it is the §2.10 failure itself: past 34MB (`JSONL_HEAD_BYTES + JSONL_TAIL_BYTES`) the seek path is the ONLY way to read the earlier history, `transcript-service.gapSlab` normalizes each slab through the same message manager, and codex carries `thread_rolled_back` in the ROLLOUT — so `msg.rewound` genuinely arrives there. Measured at 375×667 before the fix: rollback `{display:'block', opacity:1, tags:0}`, superseded `display:'block'`, executing card `::after` width `auto`. **A count written in prose cannot fail**, which is why the enumeration is now a test: the suite's leg ⓪ (no chrome needed) counts every `.renderAssistantMsg(` call under `src/lib/` and demands a `_applyElementMarks` call within 2000 chars of each, with a synthetic marked/unmarked pair as its own negative control. **Gate:** test-turn-truth-ui leg ⑤ measures COMPUTED STYLE (display / opacity / tag count / `::after` width) at 375×667 across the three rebuild paths and leg ⑥ measures the same five elements built through `_renderGapMsg`, each with two negative controls — a never-retracted message and a pending-but-not-executing tool card, which must stay unmarked (re-deriving must not mark everything). Neutering the round-2 fix turns exactly its three asserts red; neutering the round-3 call turns leg ⓪ plus leg ⑥'s three asserts red (`display block / [block,1,0] / auto`) while both controls stay green.

### src/server/session-stdout.js — SESSION LIVENESS AFTER RESTORE (2026-09-09)

  **THE PROMISE THIS SECTION EXISTS FOR: a dtach session survives a server restart BY DESIGN, so a restored session must STREAM to an attached client without the user typing anything.** Three pieces, one rule each, all in `attachToDtach` / `setupSessionPty` and all gated by scripts/test-restore-liveness.mjs.

  **① OBSERVE THE OPEN.** `deviceMgr.openSession()` resolves as soon as the `open-session` control frame is WRITTEN; the daemon's answer lives on `handle.ready` (`session-open` / `session-error` / the 2.271.0 T1-6 pre-ready link death). The daemon branch never awaited it and ran `setupSessionPty` on the shim regardless — an open the daemon never completed is then a **silently dead pty**: no journal line, the session still LIVE in the sidebar, and nothing to re-attach because the shim's `onExit` never fires either. It now races `ready` against `DEVICE_OPEN_READY_MS` (5 s; measured open→ready on a real local daemon is 8 ms worst of 10 for `sh`, 2 ms for `dtach -a`, 11 ms for 12 concurrent opens — scripts/dbg-daemon-open-latency.mjs) and falls back to the LOCAL pty on either outcome, saying which session fell back and why. A `ready` that resolves after we abandoned it kills its handle, so two dtach clients never relay one session; the rejection is consumed on both paths, so master's unhandled-rejection line (one context-free string, no session id) is gone.

  **② THE PROBE IS A READ, NOT A WRITE.** `dtach -a <sock> -E -r winch` emits its redraw kickoff `\x1b[H\x1b[J` to the attaching client immediately **even when the program inside is silent** (measured 1 ms locally, 2–50 ms through the daemon; the terminal branch already strips it as the "attach preamble"), so a healthy attach always produces a byte within milliseconds and a dead bridge never does — for chat AND terminal, with no stdin write and no wrapper cooperation. Writing a probe LINE was rejected on measurement: chat-wrapper acks any stdin line but then forwards an unrecognised JSON line to claude's stdin and wraps a NON-JSON line as a user message (**a billed turn**), and the sessions this probe exists for are by construction running the PREVIOUS release's wrapper (2.361.1 skew), so a new no-op verb cannot be assumed. `ATTACH_PROBE_MS` 4000 + `ATTACH_PROBE_CONFIRM_MS` 600: the confirm stage is there because a blocked event loop runs the **timers** phase before the **poll** phase, and the incident's own boot carried a 30 s loop gap — without it the verdict fires ahead of bytes that had long since arrived on the socket. A silent LOCAL attach only warns (the socket is stale; re-attaching locally would repeat it and the pty's own exit drives the bounded ladder); a silent DEVICE attach heals, `ATTACH_PROBE_MAX_HEALS` 2 so a systemically silent bridge is never a heal loop — CONSECUTIVE, reset to 0 by any attach that produces a byte (the same shape as `_reattachAttempts`; a lifetime cap would spend a long-lived session's two heals on unrelated hiccups days apart and leave the third one dark, which is the incident).

  **③ ONE HEALER, ONE LIVENESS FACT, TWO TRIGGERS.** `reattachLocalPty(id, session, why, {resend})` is the only local re-attach in the product — the attach probe calls it, and so does ws-handler's "Broken pty stdin detected" detector, which used to spawn its own `pty.spawn(DTACH_CMD, …)` copy. `session._lastPtyDataAt` is stamped by a listener registered FIRST in `setupSessionPty` (the one place every pty — local node-pty or `daemonPtyShim` — is wired) and read only through `ptyQuietSince`. It replaces the detector's old `session.buffer.length` comparison, which is a strict SUBSET of "did anything come back": the terminal branch swallows the attach preamble outright and a chat consumer need not append every byte. `ptyQuietSince` uses `>=`, not `>` — the stamp is milliseconds, both callers take `since` immediately before the thing they time, and the losing side of that tie RE-SENDS the user's keystroke.

  **daemonPtyShim had to grow a listener SET** (src/server/dial-pairing.js): its `onData`/`onExit` held ONE slot each, so the second registration silently REPLACED the first — and since the liveness stamp is registered FIRST, what dies is the STAMP, not the consumer (corrected by B-ae4b; this paragraph used to say the reverse): the stdout consumer keeps streaming while `ptyQuietSince` reads "silent" for a bridge that is relaying bytes, so the attach probe heals a healthy daemon attach and the broken-stdin detector loses its "bytes came back" rescue. `dispose()` removes only its own callback. **B-ae4b (2.369.164):** the three other ducks that reach `setupSessionPty` — the R6 pipe create shim (src/ws-create.js), its verbatim boot re-open twin (src/server/boot-restore.js) and the OpenCode serve terminal (src/server/opencode-pty-bridge.js) — still had ONE slot; all four now share the PURE listener SET in src/pty-duck.js, and test-pty-duck (fast) is the census + the functional legs through the real `setupSessionPty`.

  **BYTES CAN ARRIVE BEFORE THERE IS A LISTENER.** The daemon's session channel exists from `conn.sessions.set(chan, …)`, which runs before the open-session frame is even written, so DATA on that channel is protocol-legal before `session-open`; `ready` is a promise, so it settles a microtask after the SYNCHRONOUS dispatch of every frame in one socket read (mux `_feed` drains all complete frames in a loop). A byte in that gap reaches a null `handle.onData` and is dropped — invisible on a chatty session, and on a SILENT one it deletes the probe's only evidence, i.e. the guard fires on a healthy daemon. `attachToDtach` therefore installs a buffering `h.onData` the moment `openSession` resolves and replays it once the shim's listeners exist, and `armProbe` takes its window start as a PARAMETER so a preamble we successfully caught is not read as silence. HONEST MEASUREMENT: a daemon patched to answer `session-open` and write a data frame in the same tick coalesced into one client read **0/8** on this box (scripts/dbg-open-coalesce.mjs — the reader is scheduled between the two writes here), so the suite drives that shape directly through a fake handle instead of waiting for a coalescing it cannot cause; the negative control (the real module with only the replay removed) loses the byte AND heals a bridge that was working.

  **BOOT ORDERING.** server.js starts `deviceMgr.connect()` and calls `restoreSessions()` on the very next lines, so on a cold boot the link is still being established — in the production journal the connect was in flight for the WHOLE restore. The daemon path is now taken only when `deviceMgr.status().connected` is ALREADY true; otherwise a local pty is available in the SAME TICK. Of the two options: awaiting the link would put the whole spawn + version handshake + bundle upload + re-exec (~40 s, measured in that journal) in front of every session's restore and would stall the boot outright if the daemon never came up; migrating a working local pty onto the daemon afterwards is a teardown + re-attach on a bridge that is already relaying, i.e. a second blind window bought for nothing. WHAT IT COSTS, precisely: `attachToDtach` has exactly two callers — boot-restore (now local) and the re-attach ladder in `setupSessionPty`'s onExit, which fires long after 'routing ENABLED' and still takes the daemon. New sessions never took this path at all (ws-create spawns `dtach -c` under its own node-pty).

  **r5 (2.369.157): the `no-start` MARKER IS PERSISTED — `persistNoStart(sockFile, meta, {readSessionMeta, writeSessionMeta})` writes `heldPoolOrigin:'no-start'` into a pool-billed meta (has `accountId`) with no stamp and no `createdAt` BEFORE any writer runs (both restore paths), and `heldOriginOf` honours it before looking at `createdAt`: the rename / codex thread-meta writers persist the boot-filled `createdAt` (`{...prev, createdAt: session.createdAt}`), so the second restart used to name the pool default at the previous BOOT with confidence. Both helpers are exported (test-codex-pool §R17b r5 drives them over a meta store, control = the r4 text).**   **r4 (2.369.157): boot-restore also restores WHERE the stamp came from (`_heldPoolOrigin: heldOriginOf(meta)`, both restore paths): a ledger-derived stamp the engine persisted stays `ledger`; a meta with no stamp AND no `createdAt` is `no-start` — the restore fills `createdAt` with the boot instant, and the ledger would otherwise name the pool default AT THE BOOT with confidence (the rule answers `unknown`).**   **THE HELD POOL STAMP SURVIVES THE RESTORE (verifier r3, 2.369.157 — test-restore-liveness §4 ④).** The same end-to-end restore (real worktree server, the self-upgrading daemon, zero input) also proves the design-reset-credits stamp: a session-meta carrying `accountId` + `heldPoolMember` restores as a process that still speaks as that member — the `active-sessions` billing badge (`sessionAuth` → `accounts.poolMemberOfSession`, the ONE rule) answers `Cx Alpha` although the pool default was moved to `Cx Beta` with the server DOWN — and the CONTROL meta without the stamp (a process older than every slot-transition row of its pool ⇒ `unknown`) follows the link (`Cx Beta`). The accounts are written by an AccountManager over the worktree's own data/ (CODEX_HOME pointed at scratch) between two boots; nothing touches ~/.codex.

  **ENV.** The local attach now spawns with `agentEnv()` like every other agent spawn (the ws-handler re-attach already did; the spawn-hygiene law). The daemon open passes only `{TERM, COLORTERM}`, which agentd merges over its own process env: `/usr/bin/dtach` in ATTACH mode consumes no environment at all (its only env consumer is the `execvp` on `-c`/`-n` CREATE, and the agent CLI lives inside the dtach MASTER with the env it was spawned with), so shipping the whole server env over the mux would put every secret in it into a control frame for no effect.

### mounts.js

  **AT-REST ENCRYPTION MOVED OUT (P0b, design §14.7):** the inline `_key()`/`_enc()`/`_dec()` are gone; `_enc`/`_dec` delegate to `src/secret-box.js` on the SAME `data/.mounts-key` (decision 24 — the key file does not move), the ciphertext format is byte-identical (parity-pinned both directions by scripts/test-secret-box.mjs, so no stored mount secret is re-encrypted), and the ONE behaviour change is the fix mounts inherits: a key file that exists but cannot be read is now a TYPED error instead of a silently minted replacement key that orphaned every stored ciphertext (the bare `catch` at the former :360-367).

  **`applyDriveToken(id, token, client?)` — A CLIENT SWITCH LANDS WITH ITS TOKEN (2.369.165, integrations 4a, D2 of docs/design-integrations-per-account.zh.md §6).** The optional `client` (`{clientPreset}` or `{clientId, clientSecret}`, the body's `client` on `POST /api/mounts/:id/drive-token`) is written TOGETHER with the token: a record never holds a new client beside the old token (the Edit dialog's silent save, `invalid_client` at the next refresh). The two forms EXCLUDE each other — a custom id wins at resolve (`_driveClient`), so a preset stored beside a leftover custom id would mint under the preset and refresh under the custom client; a preset CLEARS `clientId` + `clientSecretEnc`, a custom client clears the preset; a custom id without its secret is refused by name before anything is written. Google Drive records only (refused by name otherwise) — a Gmail switch lands through `update()`'s PATCH `{clientPreset, token}`, which already writes both in one save and restarts the sync. The children bounce exactly as for a plain re-authorize. Gate: test-mount-oauth-probe §4 (a real MountManager in a scratch dir, mount/unmount stubbed).

  mounts.js            — MountManager (rclone mounts, MULTI-SOURCE: typed records s3/drive/onedrive/gmail/webdav/sftp/vibespace/rclone via _rcloneFor; detached + boot adoption; one-click rclone install (data/bin, pinned 1.65.2); guided Google Drive OAuth (2.226.2: all four OAuth entry points render the auth URL as a copyable row — consent completable from ANY browser, paste-back relay finishes; popup-block reported honestly); rclone.conf import; per-mount S3 share minting mc→STS; NATIVE cephfs type (2.109.1, all-flash deployment storage — kernel `sudo mount -t ceph`, per-user quota, env-provisioned My storage VIBESPACE_CEPHFS_* replaces S3, no CSI; **2.237.2: _mountCephfs ensures a no-op /sbin/modprobe shim before EVERY attempt — mount.ceph hardcodes that path and treats exit-127 as fatal, so a kmod-less image broke every connect even with the ceph module loaded host-side (a container can never modprobe the shared kernel; when kmod existed the call always failed harmlessly). Never remove the shim 'because modprobe exists in the current image'**); flat-connections model — no special my-storage slot, env auto-migrates to a normal mount. **SUBMOUNT model (2.108.0→2.108.2, user-refined twice): ANY top-level storage record can hold submounts — children reference the parent via `parentId` + their own path fields (`remote:path`) and resolve connection through `_connOf()` at use time (addChild allows any non-child parent; no nesting). `kind:'credential'` now means CREDENTIAL-ONLY (root unmountable — bucket-scoped token): UI shows a key ICON in place of the status dot (no text badge, user directive) and NO Connect action; mount() auto-heals kind on a later successful root probe — refreshing the credential's token/keys heals every child (update() bounces mounted children). A credential itself mounts fine when its token can list the remote root (GDrive, account-wide keys); mount() AUTO-DETECTS bucket-scoped tokens (pathless s3-family + root-list probe AccessDenied → convert to credential + guidance) because the fuse mount otherwise "succeeds" and EIOs on every IO (the FishR2 trap — real bucket was `example-prod-data`; S3 names are lowercase). AccessDenied WITH a path fails fast pre-mount with a check-the-bucket-name error (v2Auth probe extension; v2Auth stays undefined so a fixed path re-probes). addChild/convert/remove-guarded; export re-links children by parent NAME. Drive re-auth: startDriveAuthForMount(id) runs the guided OAuth with the mount's own client creds, applyDriveToken() writes back + reconnects children — the invalid_grant recovery path; **D2 at the server (2.369.165 integrations r1): `update()` calls `_refuseClientSwitch(m, patch)` FIRST — a top-level Drive/Gmail record holding a token whose RESOLVED client (`_clientIdentity`: custom id wins (Gmail id+secret), else preset, else the resolver's fallback; the secret is not the identity — sidebar-mounts `_mountClientSwitch` is the client twin) would change without a `token` in the patch throws `code:'client-change-needs-reauth'` (route 409); `applyDriveToken`'s `client` must name a preset (`''` = built-in) or a custom id — `{}` throws, never reads as built-in;** **applyDriveToken accepts drive AND onedrive AND cloud holders (2.268.8 — it rejected non-Google types, leaving the edit-dialog re-auth button dead for them), and the client re-auth surfaces word themselves per provider (`_oauthProviderNames` in sidebar-mounts.js), never hardcoded "Google Drive". ONEDRIVE REQUIRES RESOLVED drive_id+drive_type IN CONFIG (2.268.8, real report: every fresh native add failed with rclone's cryptic "upgrading from older versions" error — imported rclone.confs worked only because the conf carried both): `_resolveOneDriveDrive` (Graph /me/drive, region-aware GRAPH_BASE) runs as a mount-time backstop when driveId is missing (error recorded into _errors — "token expired" wording surfaces the row re-auth button) + after each re-auth write-back; explicit driveId never overridden. Test: scripts/test-onedrive-resolve.mjs.** Non-env mounts expose ALL connection params in the edit dialog PREFILLED with their real current values, SECRETS INCLUDED (2.108.8, user directive: no more blank "=default" fields — `_showEditMountDialog` fetches the decrypted config via `GET /api/mounts/:id/config`/`config()` and fills every input, keys/tokens/passwords/rclone params too; single-user instance, inputs stay type=text); save is a DIFF — a field is sent only when it changed from the fetched original (unchanged secrets aren't needlessly re-encrypted; server ignores an emptied secret so clearing one is a no-op there), an emptied rclone per-param row removes it. Only my-storage locks connection fields (edit shows name+mountpoint only; `config()` returns `{envLocked:true}` with no secrets). **HUNG-MOUNT DEFENSE (2.108.3, real outage)**: a fuse mount to an unreachable backend (home-LAN SMB host from a datacenter pod) hangs every IO — node's libuv THREADPOOL fills with stuck fs ops and the whole server stops answering while the event loop stays idle (ep_poll; /login 130s → readiness dead → pod out of Service). mount() runs a post-mount child-process `ls` probe (6s guard; error-exit=responsive, only a STUCK child trips) and startHealthWatchdog() sweeps every mounted record (60s + 15s-after-boot, covers boot-ADOPTED mounts that skip mount()) — hang ⇒ lazy unmount + `_killMountDaemon` (exact /proc cmdline argv match — a wedged rclone survives fusermount -uz) + desired=unmounted persisted + row error. Never probe mountpoints with node fs — child processes only. 2.108.4: pathBlocked() circuit breaker — mount() blocks the root for the WHOLE connect window and hang-detection blocks 90s; a files.js router middleware fails every op under a blocked root fast with 503 (an open explorer window otherwise stuffs the pool during the probe window — real follow-up incident); UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE=32 at the top of server.js (before any pool-touching require). **2.109.0 STRUCTURAL FIX: src/safe-fs.js worker_threads pool** — every LOCAL user-path fs op in routes/files.js runs in a worker with its OWN libuv pool + per-op deadline + kill/respawn (path resolution/traversal stay in main; worker executes the resolved absolute path only; ?host= untouched; app.locals.safeFs wired in server.js, inline fallback if the pool fails). Revoked/expired share SURFACING: _probeMountpoint is 3-state (ok/error/hung) + _probeBackendAccess (uncached rclone lsf re-auth, gated to _revocable = imported/vibespace/expiring) catches a 401/403 that a cache-served mountpoint ls hides → row shows "connected but every file errors" (clears on re-grant). 2.108.5 SELF-MOUNT GUARD: a vibespace-bridge record whose bearer token exists in OUR OWN MountTokens store points back at this instance — fuse→HTTP→self deadlocks the threadpool (real incident); refused at add/import/mount via mounts.selfTokenCheck = mountTokens.has(raw) (no lastUsedAt bump)**. **DIRECT CEPHFS SUBTREE SHARING (2.111.7): sharing a folder from a cephfs My-storage mount calls an in-cluster minter (env VIBESPACE_CEPHMINT_URL/_TOKEN) to mint a PATH-SCOPED cephx key (`ceph fs authorize <fs> client.vibespace-share-<rand> <path> <r|rw>`) and emits a `vibespace-cephmount:v1:<b64>` link; import → a normal `cephfs` mount that KERNEL-mounts the subtree directly (full flash bandwidth, no WebDAV relay). Key scoped to exactly the subpath (mds allow r path=…), recorded in `_state.shares` (kind:cephmount), revoke deletes it cluster-side. Env-gated — absent the minter, sharing falls back to the WebDAV bridge; cross-cluster/external always uses the bridge. mintCephShare/parseCephMountLink/revoke path in mounts.js; canCephShare in list(); `_showCephShareDialog` UI. Helm: storage.existingClaim (mount a pre-made PVC — the home-SC migration lever) + cephMint.{url,token}.** **2.110.0 HARDENING (user directive 最稳定+性能最好+自动恢复): every rclone mount runs `--vfs-cache-mode full` with a PERSISTENT per-mount cache dir (data/vfs-cache/<id>, root overridable VIBESPACE_VFS_CACHE_DIR; setting mounts.vfsCacheMaxSizeGB default 10G) — dirty writes survive a daemon crash and resume uploading on remount (verified live: SIGKILL 0.5s post-write → auto-remount → object lands); bounded IO (--timeout 60s --contimeout 15s + retries) so flaky backends error instead of hanging; new flags gated via _rcloneHasFlag (old system rclone falls back to writes mode). AUTO-RECONNECT supervision: desired now ONLY reflects user intent — internal teardowns (hang defense) keep desired=mounted and _healthSweep's dead-mount branch remounts with backoff 1→2→5→10min (_maybeAutoRemount; _noteReconnectBackoff), auth-class errors (denied/revoked/expired/AccessDenied…) excluded from retry so the actionable message survives; unmount(id,{internal:true}) is the internal teardown that doesn't rewrite intent; mount() is wrapped by a _connecting guard (one connect in flight per record). rcloneBin() NFS trap: executing the 57MB binary from a network FS demand-pages it per exec (~22s measured) — _fastBin copies it once to ~/.cache/vibespace keyed by size+mtime (22s→0.03s), detection via /proc/mounts longest-prefix fstype**) **OAuth-death detection (2.368.6, real OneDrive incident): a dead refresh token hides behind a HEALTHY-looking mount — fuse dir cache keeps listings working while every download fails 'unauthenticated: Unauthenticated' (EIO on every file open, zero UI signal). _oauthBacked mounts (drive/onedrive/cloud/rclone-OAuth) now get the fresh-process backend probe on a slow clock (10min; every sweep while an auth error shows or the mountpoint fails), the denied-regex knows the OAuth phrasings (unauthenticated/invalid_grant/InvalidAuthenticationToken), the health message names the fix (re-authorize), and the client button regex matches it. Gated by scripts/test-mount-oauth-probe.mjs (15). Do not narrow _revocable back to 'my own Drive can(not) expire' — it can. SECOND HALF (2.368.7): an EIO-wedged daemon SURVIVES fusermount -uz, so the re-auth bounce stacked a fresh daemon on the dead-token one and changed nothing (4 leaked daemons found); unmount() now polls _daemonAlive and kills survivors BEFORE resolving (bounce callers mount() right after — a later kill would murder the fresh daemon), and mount() kills any stale daemon before spawning. Never resolve an unmount while the daemon lives. TRUE ROOT CAUSE (2.368.8, corrects 2.368.6's dead-token diagnosis): the token was ALIVE — refresh/list/upload all worked, only the /content DOWNLOAD endpoint 401d (Microsoft's migrated consumer OneDrive vs rclone 1.65.2; A/B with identical config: 1.69.3/1.75.0 download fine). Pin bumped to v1.69.3 (stays in the Cloudflare-STS-safe 1.63–1.69 range) + restore() self-heals data/bin/rclone to the pin at boot (nothing else ever re-runs the installer — a pin bump alone reaches no existing install). The sweep also runs _probeBackendRead (1-byte cat of the first root file) because this failure mode PASSES lsf — auth-class failures must be located per-ENDPOINT (refresh/list/upload/download), never collapsed into 'token dead'.** **STRANDED WRITES (2.369.15, real OneDrive "is not empty, use --allow-non-empty" incident): a mount point that is NOT mounted is a bare local directory, and anything written there (the task store's generated TASK.md recreated a whole tree while OneDrive was down) both disappears once the storage reconnects and blocks that reconnect. Never `--allow-non-empty` (it hides the files). `_ensureMountpointDir(mp, {quarantine:true})` on BOTH connect paths (rclone + cephfs; never on the mount-point edit path) moves leftovers aside to a sibling `<mp>.stranded-<ts>/` — never delete, never merge — recreates the mount point empty and broadcasts a level-2 server-notice naming the path and items. `shadowedBy(p)` = the registered storage whose mount point contains p but is not mounted (gmail/credential records excluded; `isMounted(m, live)` accepts a pre-read /proc/mounts): files.js refuses every op under it with 503, task-groups skips its TASK.md and retries on every `mounts-updated` (the wiring tees the broadcast into `onMountsUpdated` + one boot resync after mounts exist — the constructor's boot regen runs before them). New server-side writers into user paths consult `shadowedBy` first. Gated by scripts/test-mount-stranded.mjs (26).**

### harnesses/ (the harness registry — S1/S4/S6, 2.369.18–22)
