  **`settings` + `configFiles` (docs/design-harness-settings.zh.md §2, 2.369.123)** — every descriptor carries `settings` = its PURE table `HARNESS_SETTINGS.<prefix>` by OBJECT IDENTITY (like `caps`; shell null; a generic ACP harness `HARNESS_SETTINGS[id] || null`) and `configFiles` = `{ <id>: cliConfigFile(table.files.<id>, {createIfMissing}) }` — the CLI config files VibeSpace may WRITE, each built OVER the table's own `files` entry so `rel` is one array (claude `settings` = ~/.claude/settings.json, never created by us; codex `hooks` = ~/.codex/hooks.json + `config` = ~/.codex/config.toml, both created when missing — the dir must exist). **`inject.hookFile` IS one of those objects** (claude → `configFiles.settings`, codex → `configFiles.hooks`): the hook entries and the managed keys share the file object, so the path is never spelled twice (test-harness-contract pins the identity). `validate()` runs `assertSettingsContract`: `checkTable` with the descriptor's context — prefix = `settingsPrefix`, every cli-config row's file declared + writable + same rel, every `live` verb a method of `h.Adapter.prototype` — and for a `register()`ed harness the contributor rules (prefix = its own id, never a built-in one). `isBuiltin(id)` is exported (cli-env ships a contributed harness's table on /api/home; the schema refuses to unregister a built-in). Gates: test-harness-contract (identity pins + spawn conformance with a synthetic never-consumed row as the negative control), test-harness-settings §1.

  **`store.lastTurnModel` / `store.lastTurnEffort` (B-6b6d)** — "what did this CONVERSATION last run at", for the resume ladder (src/resume-continuity.js). The hook's PRESENCE is the declaration that this harness can answer, so there is no second boolean to drift: **codex** declares both (its rollout writes a `turn_context` per turn), **opencode** declares the model (`serve.facts().sessionModel`, round 2), **claude** declares NEITHER (round 2 — its transcript cannot express the model's context variant and records no effort at all; see src/session-store.js), **shell** and the generic ACP harness neither. ws-create asks the descriptor and never branches on a backend id — this is where the B-21e4 codex-only env post-fill went. A hook returning `''` means "this conversation has nothing recorded" ⇒ the instance default, LOGGED; a missing hook means "this harness cannot answer" ⇒ send nothing.

  src/plugin-manifest.js — PURE manifest validator + the consent vocabulary (Ph2 2.369.24, Ph4 2.369.30): validateManifest(raw, {hostVersion, folderName, homeDir, forbiddenRoots}) normalizes tiers (none|iframe|module; "trusted" = alias), clientEntry, contributes windows/agentTools/routes/settings(boolean|string|number|select)/themes, capabilities.server {fs.read/write (abs or ~, no .., never covering a forbidden root), childProcess (spawn⇒childProcess warned), net (declared only)}; needsConsent(m) = module tier, any declared server capability, OR any contributed agentTool (2.369.43 — a generated shim is a program on every session PATH, outside the plugin sandbox); capabilitySummary(m) = [{id,text,params}] the SAME items server (409 payload) and client (dialog via t(text, params)) render; capabilitiesHash(m) = key-order-independent fingerprint of the consent surface (tier/server/capabilities/agent tools/routes) — array order is significant by design. **2.369.43 hardening: cleanText() strips control chars + U+2028/U+2029 from EVERY free-text field (description/label/window title/tool description/setting+theme labels) — free text ends up in generated code, so it is sanitized ONCE here; normalizeFsPath COLLAPSES the path (own segment walk — the file has ZERO requires by design) before the forbidden-root prefix test, because node's permission model collapses `//`, `/./` and `/.` (`--allow-fs-read=/.` = the whole filesystem); the fs-write summary says "write AND read" (permissionArgs adds a read grant per write path).** **2.369.44: normalizeFsPath also MODELS node's `*`** — node reads a declared path only up to the FIRST `*` and grants every path whose STRING starts with what came before it (probed against node v24: `--allow-fs-read=/t/a/*` and `/t/a/*/ignored` both read `/t/a/b/c/f.txt`; `/t/a/z*` reads `/t/a/zz.txt` but not `/t/a/b/…`; `/*` reads /etc/hostname). Treating a pattern as a plain path let `["/*"]` and `["<parent-of-a-forbidden-root>/*"]` pass validation and grant the install/data dir. Now: at most ONE `*`, only as the LAST character (a mid-pattern `*` is refused LOUDLY — it grants everything before it and silently ignores the rest); the containment test runs on the literal prefix (`r.startsWith(prefix)` — a wildcard over a parent of a forbidden root is forbidden, and `…/dat*` catching `…/data` too); `/` and `/*` are refused with or without roots; `/dir/*` is never collapsed into `/dir*` (different grants — the latter also covers `/dirty`), and the accepted pattern is stored VERBATIM so the string the owner consented to is the string node gets. **B-7638: the collapse rule and the wildcard rule MEET at `~/.*`** — node only collapses a LONE `.` segment, so `<home>/.*` is the prefix `<home>/.` (dotfiles), but collapsing the dot HERE emitted `<home>*`: a string prefix covering the whole home directory AND every sibling path that starts with those characters (`/home/u*` reaches `/home/u2/…`). A home-dir glob may not widen to every user, and the widening was invisible — the manifest said one thing and node was handed another — so a `.` segment immediately before `*` is REFUSED with the prefix it would have produced (write the directory `…/` or a literal name prefix). `~/.config/*`, `~/./*` (a lone `.` node itself collapses) and `~/.ssh` are unaffected. Invariant: no other module mutates or reinterprets a manifest — and any rewrite this file performs on a declared path must be one node performs too, or it must refuse.

Invariants: never delete user data; never a shell string; the id comes from the manifest (update refuses a different id); the uploaded temp file is removed on EVERY exit path (the source whitelist once threw above the try/finally).

setEnabled(id, on, {trusted}) throws 409 {consentRequired, capabilities, changed} when consent is needed and absent; startChild forks server.js under `node --permission` (permissionArgs: plugin dir read + data dir rw + declared fs paths, write implies read, --allow-child-process only when declared; NODE_OPTIONS stripped; the child 'error' event is handled — ERR_IPC_CHANNEL_CLOSED from a send racing an exit would crash the host), classifyExit turns an ERR_ACCESS_DENIED stderr into the panel's one-line error; routes: /plugins/<id>/* serves declared theme JSON (any tier) → the module entry SAME-ORIGIN as javascript only while isTrusted (else 403 consentRequired) → iframe ui/ under the sandbox CSP; POST /api/plugins/install (JSON or multipart field `file`), DELETE /api/plugins/manifests/:id (uninstall → trash), POST …/:id/update, GET …/:id/capabilities; a CR/U+2028/U+2029 in a description used to end the `//` comment and execute — the shim runs outside the sandbox with the session token and ships to every host); install() resets enabled+trust unless the package is byte-identical AND from the same recorded source (update() keeps consent and records the new hash) — **2.369.44: that reset is gated on the REGISTRY RECORD, never on `r.replaced`**: enabled/trust live in data/plugin-registry.json keyed by id and outlive the directory, so with a hand-deleted (or half-installed) plugin folder there was nothing to "replace" and the next, DIFFERENT package under that id landed pre-enabled and pre-trusted with its client module served same-origin and no dialog at all; proxied /x/* replies always carry nosniff + `sandbox; default-src 'none'` and an untrusted plugin's document content-type is downgraded to text/plain; the intentional-stop mark is a Symbol on the CHILD (rec._stopping mis-filed a fresh child's crash while the old one was still exiting).** Node's permission model does NOT restrict network — documented in the dialog and docs/plugins.md.

  src/lib/plugins-ui.js — …Ph4 (2.369.30): Install plugin… dialog (path/git/github-release JSON, .vsp multipart), per-plugin ⋯ menu (Show capabilities… / Update / Uninstall with showConfirmDialog), Enable → 409 consentRequired ⇒ _pluginConsentDialog (capability items via t(item.text, item.params), 'Enable (trusted)') ⇒ enable with trusted:true; tier/trust badges, notices, client-module errors — every manifest string escHtml-ed. **HARNESS BACKGROUND SERVICES (2026-09-07):** the ⚙ → Plugins card for `opencode-serve` (state line running/starting/parked/runaway/turned-off, an env-forced notice that DISABLES the controls instead of offering a button that can only fail, Start/Stop + one "Run this service whenever VibeSpace runs" switch, no config box) (the env-forced card is the ONLY control surface for an ops-forced instance, which is safe because the keeper now guarantees nothing is RUNNING under `VIBESPACE_OPENCODE_SERVE=0` — see src/opencode-serve.js) AND the FIRST-USE offer used from the session lifecycle: `maybeOfferHarnessService(backend,{needsService,retry})` → `_harnessServiceState` (a fresh `/api/plugins/<id>/status`, falling back to the broadcast-cached BACKEND_META.service so a network blip never claims the service is off) → `_harnessServiceDialog` (createModalShell, NEVER a native confirm: what it does, that it is loopback-only and stops when disabled, "Not now" / "Enable & start") → `enableHarnessService` (POST enabled + start, then poll ≤25s and run the caller's `retry` — the pending action continues, and a service that never answers TOASTS what state it is in instead of spinning forever). We record the "asked" flag on EITHER answer (an accepted-then-disabled service is exactly when the sidebar's hidden-history row must appear), and ONE offer is in flight at a time (a layout restore can open five history windows in a tick; joiners still get their own retry).

  src/codex-session-store.js — …S3: `collectCodexThreadMetas()` (pass 1, pure facts: the ~/.codex/sessions walk with a PER-DIRECTORY mtime cache — unchanged mtime older than 2s ⇒ cached listing, no readdir — + extractCodexThreadMeta's per-file cache) and `assembleCodexThreads(facts, {activeSessions, openThreadIds})` (pass 2: live/external/stopped, forkedFrom sources hidden); `listCodexThreadsAsync` runs pass 1 + the /proc scan as transcript-worker ops (`codexThreadMetas`, `codexOpenThreads`; inline fallback when the pool is down) so the 5s poll never walks the tree on the loop; `listCodexThreads` (sync twin) is unchanged for user-action consumers (capture, migration map, spawn baseline). Liveness = discovery-facts.listOpenCodexRolloutPaths (ONE /proc-or-lsof implementation shared with the daemon snapshot). dirCacheStats() for tests. **FORK ORDINAL (B-21e4, codex 0.153 paginated forks):** `resolveCodexForkAncestry(threadId, wrapperChain)` → `[{id, untilOrdinal|null}]` oldest→newest is what `CodexSessionMessages._ensureParsed` prepends: the wrapper's `forked_from` chain merges WHOLE as before (superseded incarnations; turn-scoped fingerprint dedup unchanged) ∪ codex's OWN `forked_from_id` parents whose boundary is KNOWN (a 'Referenced' fork's rollout holds none of the parent's records — only `history_base.end_ordinal_exclusive`/`forked_from_ordinal_exclusive`, PARENT-numbered), cut with `cutRecordsAtOrdinal` (records without a top-level `ordinal` are kept; the walk is depth-8, cycle-safe, and an id in both sources takes the boundary). A sub-agent's `subagent_history_start_ordinal` is CHILD-numbered and its rollout already copies the inherited context ⇒ never an ancestor. Native fork parents are NOT hidden by `assembleCodexThreads` (they are their own conversations; only the wrapper chain hides); entries carry `forkedFromId/forkedFromOrdinal/historyMode` (additive). Bounded caveat: parseCodexSessionJsonl is tail-only (32MB) — a Referenced fork off a bigger parent reads its tail, which the boundary rejects (bounded, never wrong records). Gate: scripts/test-codex-0153.mjs ①. **RECORD PROVENANCE (round 3, 2026-09-06):** `_ensureParsed` tags every file's records with THAT file's thread id before merging — `tagRecordThread(records, id)` sets a NON-enumerable `__threadId` (never in JSON.stringify ⇒ fingerprints, wire payloads and caches unchanged; `sortRecords` re-attaches it on its spread copy; `recordThreadOf(record)` reads it) on the ancestry cuts and the thread's own file alike, covering the remote-jsonl cache and the thread/read cache because both are served through parseCodexSessionJsonl. Gate: scripts/test-acp-harness.mjs (107) — cancel-during-await, queued+interrupt, Stop-drops-the-queued-nudge, Stop-inside-the-stop-check-round-trip, deny-with-no-reject-option, exit-0-before-initialize, each with a positive control. **THE BOOKKEEPING NUDGE IS OURS, NOT THE USER'S (B-7638, three residuals):** ① a Stop landing INSIDE the `/api/agent/stop-check` round trip must not be followed by a nudge turn — the answer lands after the interrupt (activePrompt is already null), so the old code walked into runPrompt and BILLED a turn the user had just stopped, with a reminder appearing out of nowhere as the only trace; the interrupt bumps `stopEpoch` and aborts the in-flight request, and an answer whose epoch is gone is discarded with a logged reason (the latch is never set, so the NEXT completed turn nudges normally). ② when it queues behind a running turn it queues with `silentQueue` — a `queued_input` for an internal reminder painted a "Queued" chip on a bubble that does not exist (peer messages already ride silentQueue); it still appears in `queue_changed` as kind 'system', so the strip stays honest about what is waiting. ③ the 'queue-cleared' notice counts USER entries only — a dropped PEER message is not the user's to re-send either (it goes back to the delivery ladder and arrives on its own), so nudges AND peers are subtracted; the log line keeps the true total (`dropped=N (nudges=M, peers=P)`). **THE INPUT QUEUE (2026-09-06):** ACP v1 has no queue verb, so `promptQueue` IS the queue — and therefore the wrapper is its PUBLISHER: `queue_changed {items:[{id,msgId,preview,ts,kind,from}], turn_id}` on every push/drain/drop/remove (plus an empty baseline right after the session is up), `queued_input {msg_id, turn_id}` where the old "Queued — runs after the current turn" NOTICE used to be (the state is now a chip on the bubble; codex parity, one client path), and the `queue-op` stdin verb for `remove` only. A steer that somehow reaches this wrapper answers `queue_op_result {ok:false, reason:'not-steerable'}` — `backend-caps.inputModes.steer=false` stops it at the ws layer and `AcpAdapter.formatQueueOp` refuses it with a reason, so this arm exists purely so nothing is ever dropped in silence. `remove` obeys the same two rules Stop already obeyed: a removed PEER entry goes back to the delivery ladder (`peer_result ok:false`, the consumer re-stashes), and a removed NUDGE entry clears `nudgeTurnActive` (per-turn state dies with the turn it belongs to). Removing an id that already drained answers `reason:'gone'` — never a fake success. **Stop reports its drop as removals**: each dropped entry gets its own `queue_op_result {op:'remove', ok:true, msg_id, reason:'stopped'}` BEFORE the emptied republish — the normalizer clears the chip of anything that leaves the queue with no result (= "it ran"), so a bare empty `queue_changed` told the user their message had RUN when Stop had thrown it away (round-1 review). Order is the fix; the result stamps `Removed` first and the republish then leaves those bubbles alone. **REORDER + EDIT (2026-09-07):** `promptQueue` is a local array, so the verb table adds `reorder` and `edit` as splices — driven by the SAME relative frame the codex wrapper translates (`afterId:null` = the front; an anchor that has left puts the entry BACK where it was and answers `reason:'anchor-gone'`), with the same exclusion rule for edit (the first text block takes the new words, every other content block stays in place) and the same two refusals: a PEER entry is not yours to rewrite and a NUDGE entry is VibeSpace's own bookkeeping (`reason:'not-editable'`), an empty edit is `reason:'empty-text'`. `run-now`/`run-all` are declared FALSE for a structural reason, not an unfinished one: this queue only HAS entries while a prompt is running (an idle wrapper dispatches immediately), so "run it now" could only ever answer busy — a frame that arrives anyway says exactly that (`reason:'not-startable'`). Entries carry their full `text` (user entries only) so the client's edit control opens the message rather than the preview, and `ACP_QUEUE_VERBS` is advertised in the sidecar AND on every `queue_changed`. Pins: test-acp-harness (reorder/edit/anchor-gone/empty-edit/not-startable + the advert parity with the caps row; negative control: an anchor-ignoring reorder fails the leg).

WHY: the ACP harness has no transcript files (OpenCode keeps sessions in ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db), so stopped OpenCode conversations never reached the sidebar. `opencode serve` (verified 1.18.29, OpenAPI at /doc) exposes that store on 127.0.0.1. THREE PIECES: (1) OpencodeServeClient — fetch over a base URL, 1.5s default timeout, every failure an OpencodeServeError {status, code: timeout|network|http|NotFoundError…}; listAllSessions = /project × `/session?scope=project&directory=<worktree>` deduped (VERIFIED 1.18.29 on the real store: a bare `directory=` is an EXACT-directory filter — `directory=/` lists NOTHING, which the first live run caught as "0 sessions"; `scope=project` lists the whole project; a serve's bare /session is scoped to ITS cwd's project, so the iteration is the safe shape); v1 `/session/:id/message?limit=` returns the NEWEST N, so the first user message comes from v2 `/api/session/:id/message?limit=3&order=asc`; fork = POST /session/:id/fork?directory= (body {messageID?}) → the new Session (title "<parent> (fork #n)", no parentID — parentID means a SUB-AGENT child). Basic auth only when OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD is in the spawn env. (2) createServeLocator — ONE instance per VibeSpace: reuse data/opencode-serve.json {port,pid,startedAt,command,cwd} when /global/health answers AND its own project is safe (a previous server's child that outlived a SIGKILL restart; never killed by stop() — only our own child is), else spawn `<cmd> serve --port <free> --hostname 127.0.0.1 --log-level WARN` detached + stdio ignored under agentEnv() **from its own empty data/opencode-serve/cwd** (2.369.50 — see WHERE IT RUNS below), wait ≤20s for health (1.2s locally), write the record atomically, probe /doc ONCE → onCaps({fork}) (the CLI version comes from /global/health — /doc's info.version is the API doc's own "1.0.0") — the ONLY writer of capsOf('opencode').fork (setVerifiedCap in backend-caps, PURE in-place row mutation) which cli-env then BROADCASTS as 'harness-caps-updated' (open clients learned fork:false from /api/home BEFORE the lazy start — the notify law). Keeper: exit → respawn after 1s·2^n (≤30s), crash counter resets after 60s of uptime, PARKED after 5 crashes (loud in user actions, silent in the poll), stop() on process exit (stopOnExit) — a SIGKILLed server leaves the serve running for the next boot to reuse. Started LAZILY by the first discovery, never at boot, only when cli-env resolved the CLI AND autostart is on: `VIBESPACE_OPENCODE_SERVE=0` disables it explicitly, and the test-harness belt `VIBESPACE_SKIP_AGENT_HOOKS=1` disables it implicitly (every worktree smoke sets it and SIGKILLs its server — a spawned serve outlives that kill and would pile up per `npm run ci`; `VIBESPACE_OPENCODE_SERVE=1` wins over the belt); with autostart off a RECORDED live instance is still reused, otherwise discover is [] and user actions name the switch. **WHERE IT RUNS AND WHAT IT MAY TOUCH (2.369.50, the 2.369.42 runaway — full incident in kb-bugfix-invariants):** OpenCode boots an INSTANCE per DIRECTORY and each instance recursively indexes + inotify-watches that tree (`fff-*` fast-file-finder + `notify-rs` threads). Measured with /proc against a real 1.18.29 serve: the v1 routes (`/session`, `/session/:id`, `/session/:id/message`, `/project`) boot NOTHING; **every** `/api/session/{id}/…` v2 route boots an instance for that session's `location.directory` (+19 indexer threads, +180 MB, a full-tree watch). So: (a) the serve runs from `data/opencode-serve/cwd`, an empty directory made into a throwaway git repo by `ensureServeCwd` — OpenCode's project resolution walks UP for a git worktree, so a plain directory inside the checkout resolves the WHOLE VibeSpace checkout and a FAKE `.git` does not stop the walk, while with no repo above it the project is the `'/'` catch-all (a README next to it says why; `git init` failing only degrades the isolation, loudly). Accepted side effect: while our serve runs it pins the store's mutable `'global'` project row worktree to that empty dir — the field is last-writer-wins and every `opencode` invocation rewrites it, sessions carry their own `directory`, and our listing is worktree-independent. (b) NAMING uses v1 only, byte-capped. (c) `listAllSessions` takes the DIRECTORY-LESS listing first and only issues `scope=project&directory=` for worktrees passing `bootstrappableWorktree` (never `'/'`, `$HOME`, `os.tmpdir()`, nor the vcs-less `'global'` row — a real project row carries `vcs`, the API's own signal, so no fs call is needed); skipped worktrees surface in `facts.state().skippedWorktrees`. (d) `forkSession` — the one call handing a directory to a mutating endpoint — calls `POST /instance/dispose?directory=` afterwards (best effort; the forked session stays readable). **RUNAWAY GUARD:** the child's own `/proc` (`readProcUsage`) is sampled every 60s; >150% CPU sustained ≥5 min, or RSS >2 GB on a single sample, STOPS it, parks the locator `parkedKind:'runaway'` with the numbers in `lastError`, `console.error`s what to turn off, fires telemetry `opencode-serve-runaway`, pushes `harness-store-updated` and refuses to respawn for an hour (then exactly one retry). An unreadable /proc never parks anything; the locator never signals `process.pid`. **BOOT SELF-HEAL:** a recorded serve whose `GET /project/current` worktree is `'/'` or `$HOME` (a 2.369.42 leftover — its record also has no `cwd`) is SIGTERMed and replaced from the isolated cwd; a record written by this code (matching `cwd`) skips the probe, and a FAILED probe never churns a healthy instance. **AUTOSTART** is `agents.opencodeServeAutostart` (default ON, live-read through a function): `VIBESPACE_OPENCODE_SERVE=0/1` wins, `VIBESPACE_SKIP_AGENT_HOOKS=1` forces off, else the setting.  (3) createFacts — the store members: discover({activeSessions}) = 10s list cache → 10s negative cache (returns the LAST GOOD list, [] before any) → refresh bounded by the 1.5s budget (client({budgetMs}) returns null while the serve boots; a HUNG serve costs ≤1.5s, pinned <2s) — NEVER throws, NEVER stalls the 5s /api/sessions poll; entries {backend:'opencode', backendSessionId, sessionId, sessionKey, cwd=directory, startedAt=time.updated, status live|stopped (live = an activeSessions opencode session holds the id; 'external' is undetectable — another process driving the same sqlite leaves no signal), name, agentKind primary|subagent (parentID), parentThreadId, webuiId/Name/Mode, opencode:{slug,agent,model,projectID}}; names = discovery-facts nameFromText over the FIRST user message read from the **v1** `/session/:id/message` list (the WHOLE conversation oldest-first — v1 `limit` is the NEWEST N so it cannot page from the front), capped at NAME_MAX_BYTES=1MiB by the client's streaming `maxBytes` (over the cap → code `too-large` → the title fallback; six unbounded whole-conversation fetches into this process is an OOM). THE v2 asc endpoint IS SMALLER AND MUST NEVER BE USED HERE — it boots an instance (2.369.42). ≤6 lookups per tick (progressive, no burst), cached per id, retried every 60s while a session has no user message, fallback = OpenCode's title unless it is the "New session - <date>" placeholder; readConversation(id) (8s, LOUD: not installed / parked / unreachable / 404 all name the cause) and forkSession(id,{cwd}) (refused with code unsupported when the OpenAPI lacked the fork path); **sessionModel(id) (B-6b6d round 2)** = the model this conversation is on, as `provider/model`, for the resume-continuity ladder — the opencode descriptor's `store.lastTurnModel`, so an OpenCode resume keeps its own model instead of taking `opencode.defaultModel` (a NEW-session default).
