  src/opencode-serve.js — OpenCode serve-mode STORE FACTS (S9 of design-harness-plugins §2.4, B-03f2; SHARED — facts about a machine). WHY: the ACP harness has no transcript files (OpenCode keeps sessions in ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db), so stopped OpenCode conversations never reached the sidebar. `opencode serve` (verified 1.18.29, OpenAPI at /doc) exposes that store on 127.0.0.1. THREE PIECES: (1) OpencodeServeClient — fetch over a base URL, 1.5s default timeout, every failure an OpencodeServeError {status, code: timeout|network|http|NotFoundError…}; listAllSessions = /project × `/session?scope=project&directory=<worktree>` deduped (VERIFIED 1.18.29 on the real store: a bare `directory=` is an EXACT-directory filter — `directory=/` lists NOTHING, which the first live run caught as "0 sessions"; `scope=project` lists the whole project; a serve's bare /session is scoped to ITS cwd's project, so the iteration is the safe shape); v1 `/session/:id/message?limit=` returns the NEWEST N, so the first user message comes from v2 `/api/session/:id/message?limit=3&order=asc`; fork = POST /session/:id/fork?directory= (body {messageID?}) → the new Session (title "<parent> (fork #n)", no parentID — parentID means a SUB-AGENT child). Basic auth only when OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD is in the spawn env. (2) createServeLocator — ONE instance per VibeSpace: reuse data/opencode-serve.json {port,pid,startedAt,command,cwd} when /global/health answers AND its own project is safe (a previous server's child that outlived a SIGKILL restart; never killed by stop() — only our own child is), else spawn `<cmd> serve --port <free> --hostname 127.0.0.1 --log-level WARN` detached + stdio ignored under agentEnv() **from its own empty data/opencode-serve/cwd** (2.369.50 — see WHERE IT RUNS below), wait ≤20s for health (1.2s locally), write the record atomically, probe /doc ONCE → onCaps({fork}) (the CLI version comes from /global/health — /doc's info.version is the API doc's own "1.0.0") — the ONLY writer of capsOf('opencode').fork (setVerifiedCap in backend-caps, PURE in-place row mutation) which cli-env then BROADCASTS as 'harness-caps-updated' (open clients learned fork:false from /api/home BEFORE the lazy start — the notify law). Keeper: exit → respawn after 1s·2^n (≤30s), crash counter resets after 60s of uptime, PARKED after 5 crashes (loud in user actions, silent in the poll), stop() on process exit (stopOnExit) — a SIGKILLed server leaves the serve running for the next boot to reuse. Started LAZILY by the first discovery, never at boot, only when cli-env resolved the CLI AND autostart is on — and **autostart is DEFAULT OFF since 2026-09-07** (owner decision): the switch is the built-in `opencode-serve` PLUGIN (src/plugins.js), so nothing starts a third-party background daemon on a fresh instance. With the PLUGIN off a RECORDED live instance is still reused (adopting costs nothing and the panel keeps a Stop button for it), otherwise discover is [] and user actions name the plugin — **but the OPS kill switch is authoritative over ADOPTION too (2026-09-07 follow-up)**: the reuse rung runs BEFORE the autostart gate, so `VIBESPACE_OPENCODE_SERVE=0` used to stop us STARTING a serve while happily adopting the one that outlived the last restart — a third-party daemon indexing under an instance whose panel disables every control BECAUSE it is forced off. Under the switch a recorded serve is SIGTERMed + its record cleared (the same replace path an unsafe worktree uses), and `install()` runs that ladder ONCE at boot (setImmediate, unref) so an instance nobody polls does not inherit one either. Also: the isolated cwd is only materialised when it can be USED (a record to compare, or a spawn we are allowed to make) — a service nobody turned on creates nothing, not even the throwaway git repo. Also exported here: `start()` (an explicit user start CLEARS a previous `stop()` and any crash/runaway park — a user asking for it IS the deliberate retry) and `stop({killRecorded})` (the process-exit path leaves an ADOPTED serve for the next boot; the plugin's disable passes killRecorded so "off" means the process is gone). **WHERE IT RUNS AND WHAT IT MAY TOUCH (2.369.50, the 2.369.42 runaway — full incident in kb-bugfix-invariants):** OpenCode boots an INSTANCE per DIRECTORY and each instance recursively indexes + inotify-watches that tree (`fff-*` fast-file-finder + `notify-rs` threads). Measured with /proc against a real 1.18.29 serve: the v1 routes (`/session`, `/session/:id`, `/session/:id/message`, `/project`) boot NOTHING; **every** `/api/session/{id}/…` v2 route boots an instance for that session's `location.directory` (+19 indexer threads, +180 MB, a full-tree watch). So: (a) the serve runs from `data/opencode-serve/cwd`, an empty directory made into a throwaway git repo by `ensureServeCwd` — OpenCode's project resolution walks UP for a git worktree, so a plain directory inside the checkout resolves the WHOLE VibeSpace checkout and a FAKE `.git` does not stop the walk, while with no repo above it the project is the `'/'` catch-all (a README next to it says why; `git init` failing only degrades the isolation, loudly). Accepted side effect: while our serve runs it pins the store's mutable `'global'` project row worktree to that empty dir — the field is last-writer-wins and every `opencode` invocation rewrites it, sessions carry their own `directory`, and our listing is worktree-independent. (b) NAMING uses v1 only, byte-capped. (c) `listAllSessions` takes the DIRECTORY-LESS listing first and only issues `scope=project&directory=` for worktrees passing `bootstrappableWorktree` (never `'/'`, `$HOME`, `os.tmpdir()`, nor the vcs-less `'global'` row — a real project row carries `vcs`, the API's own signal, so no fs call is needed); skipped worktrees surface in `facts.state().skippedWorktrees`. (d) `forkSession` — the one call handing a directory to a mutating endpoint — calls `POST /instance/dispose?directory=` afterwards (best effort; the forked session stays readable). **RUNAWAY GUARD:** the child's own `/proc` (`readProcUsage`) is sampled every 60s; >150% CPU sustained ≥5 min, or RSS >2 GB on a single sample, STOPS it, parks the locator `parkedKind:'runaway'` with the numbers in `lastError`, `console.error`s what to turn off, fires telemetry `opencode-serve-runaway`, pushes `harness-store-updated` and refuses to respawn for an hour (then exactly one retry). An unreadable /proc never parks anything; the locator never signals `process.pid`. **BOOT SELF-HEAL:** a recorded serve whose `GET /project/current` worktree is `'/'` or `$HOME` (a 2.369.42 leftover — its record also has no `cwd`) is SIGTERMed and replaced from the isolated cwd; a record written by this code (matching `cwd`) skips the probe, and a FAILED probe never churns a healthy instance. **AUTOSTART (2026-09-07 — the setting `agents.opencodeServeAutostart` and the `VIBESPACE_SKIP_AGENT_HOOKS` smoke belt are BOTH GONE):** the decision is ONE pure function here, `decideAutostart({env, pluginWantsUp})` — the ops override `VIBESPACE_OPENCODE_SERVE=0/1` wins (`serveEnvOverride`, the single parse of that var, also read by the plugin panel so it can show "forced by the environment"), else the `opencode-serve` plugin record (`enabled && desiredUp`); DEFAULT OFF. cli-env passes it as a FUNCTION over `plugins.wantsServiceUp(SERVICE_PLUGIN_ID)` so enabling takes effect without a restart, and the descriptor names its control plugin as `store.servicePlugin` so `/api/home` can carry `plugins.serviceState()` on the harness row (the client's first-use prompt and the sidebar's hidden-history row gate on THAT, never on a backend id). With default OFF a fresh smoke instance starts nothing, which is why the belt could be deleted. **A DELIBERATELY-OFF SERVICE IS NOT A BROKEN STORE (2026-09-07 follow-up):** `/api/home harnesses[].storeReason` is now the SAME predicate as the live `harness-store-updated` push — `storeFailureReason()` in src/server/cli-env.js, exported for the gate — and it fires ONLY on a PARK (crash loop / runaway). The old half also fired on "not ready and the keeper's autostart flag is off", which was the ops kill switch alone while autostart defaulted ON; with the plugin default OFF it became the normal shipped state, and app.js turns every reason into a RED ERROR TOAST ⇒ one per page load, on a fresh instance, after "Not now", and on instances that never had OpenCode. Off-ness travels on `row.service` instead and is shown passively (sidebar row + ⚙ card); the sidebar row also renders for the ops-forced case now, with no Enable button, since nothing the user clicks there could work.  (3) createFacts — the store members: discover({activeSessions}) = 10s list cache → 10s negative cache (returns the LAST GOOD list, [] before any) → refresh bounded by the 1.5s budget (client({budgetMs}) returns null while the serve boots; a HUNG serve costs ≤1.5s, pinned <2s) — NEVER throws, NEVER stalls the 5s /api/sessions poll; entries {backend:'opencode', backendSessionId, sessionId, sessionKey, cwd=directory, startedAt=time.updated, status live|external|stopped (see THE S9 REMAINDER below — 'external' became DETECTABLE, with positive evidence only), name, agentKind primary|subagent (parentID), parentThreadId, webuiId/Name/Mode, opencode:{slug,agent,model,projectID}}; names = discovery-facts nameFromText over the FIRST user message read from the **v1** `/session/:id/message` list (the WHOLE conversation oldest-first — v1 `limit` is the NEWEST N so it cannot page from the front), capped at NAME_MAX_BYTES=1MiB by the client's streaming `maxBytes` (over the cap → code `too-large` → the title fallback; six unbounded whole-conversation fetches into this process is an OOM). THE v2 asc endpoint IS SMALLER AND MUST NEVER BE USED HERE — it boots an instance (2.369.42). ≤6 lookups per tick (progressive, no burst), cached per id, retried every 60s while a session has no user message, fallback = OpenCode's title unless it is the "New session - <date>" placeholder; readConversation(id) (8s, LOUD: not installed / parked / unreachable / 404 all name the cause) and forkSession(id,{cwd}) (refused with code unsupported when the OpenAPI lacked the fork path). RECORD SYNTHESIS messagesToAcpRecords(messages, session) → 'acp-events' so the unchanged AcpMessageManager renders a stopped conversation read-only: session{how:'serve', model '<providerID>/<modelID>', mode=agent} · user text parts (non-synthetic first, else synthetic; `ignored` dropped) + "[file: name]" lines → {kind:'user', msgId} · assistant text → agent_message_chunk (messageId = part id, one card per part) · reasoning → agent_thought_chunk · tool → tool_call (kind from the tool id: read→read, glob|grep|list|ls→search, edit|write|patch|multiedit|apply_patch→edit, bash|shell→execute, webfetch|websearch|codesearch→fetch, todowrite|todoread|plan→think, else other; rawInput {tool,…input}, locations from filePath|path|file) + tool_call_update (completed|failed, output/error text, edit oldString/newString as a diff block; running/pending = in_progress with no update) · subtask → completed tool_call "Task: <description>" · compaction/retry → notice · a modelID/mode change between assistant messages → config · assistant end → prompt_end (MessageAbortedError→cancelled, other error→error, completed→end_turn; an open assistant message gets none) · step-start/step-finish/snapshot/patch/agent skipped. OpencodeServeSessionMessages extends AcpSessionMessages: live (the activeSessions membership fact from createSessionMessages, or a non-empty buffer) = the wrapper journal as before — a just-spawned live session with an empty journal is NOT read from the serve (the wrapper's session/load replay would double); stopped = records on prepare() (transcript-service awaits it at its three reader sites; a caller that does not gets an empty reader, never a wrong one). The installed singleton (install() by cli-env; facts() = NULL_FACTS when unwired: discover [] silently, user actions say "not configured"). **THE S9 REMAINDER (B-eac2, 2026-09-07) — every one of those "NOT wired" endpoints, measured on a real 1.18.29 serve before it was wired:** **ROUND 4 (the third adversarial pass, all three reproduced first):** ①**THE PTY FAMILY HANDS THE SERVE NO `directory`** — it was the one NEW path that took a directory from the USER, and `?directory=X` is exactly what BOOTS the instance for X while NOTHING in the pty family releases it (only `POST /instance/dispose` does, which is why `forkSession` calls it). Same-origin A/B, fresh serve per arm, target = a 200-dir/4046-file repo, /proc `Threads` + `inotify wd` over `/proc/<serve>/fdinfo/*`: WITH the query base[16,0] → open [44,204] → close [41,204] → open/close ×2,×3 still [41,204] (never freed, so N terminals on a node_modules-bearing repo reproduce the 30 021-watch shape of 2.369.42 and the only backstop is the runaway guard, whose remedy is to SIGTERM the whole serve and park it for an hour); WITHOUT it [16,0] → [45,4] → [42,4] and `readlink /proc/<shell>/cwd` is the SAME target in BOTH arms — the query buys the SHELL nothing, the `cwd` BODY field is what places it. So ptyList/ptyCreate/ptyGet/ptyResize/ptyRemove/ptyTicket/ptyConnectUrl all drop it and land on the DEFAULT instance (our own empty throwaway repo, the 4 watches). **CHANGE THEM TOGETHER OR NOT AT ALL**: the pty REGISTRY is per instance — measured, `PUT /pty/{id}?directory=X` on a pty created without the query answers 404 PtyNotFoundError and vice versa — so a half-migrated family is a terminal that opens and can never be resized, closed or reaped; the mock now models both facts (instance booted by the QUERY only, per-instance registry incl. the ws upgrade) and the gate carries the real-serve /proc delta with the old shape as the control. ②**`reapPtys()`, because a serve pty OUTLIVES us.** `session._opencodePtyId` was written in ws-create and read NOWHERE, and `ptyList()` was never called: a serve pty is deliberately not dtach-restorable (`socketPath` is null), so a SIGKILL/OOM restart — or ANY restart while the serve was ADOPTED from data/opencode-serve.json, where `state.child` is null and our exit hook has nothing to kill — left the shell running with nothing able to reach or kill it (verified: a pty survives our socket closing and is re-connectable; it only 404s once its own shell exits). The sweep runs on the READY EDGE of each serve PROCESS (`${pid}:${port}:${startedAt}`, idempotent — a routine notify must not re-sweep and race a terminal being opened), asks the DIRECTORY-LESS `GET /pty`, and KEEPS `live.ptys` (every pty THIS process opened — registered before the ticket call, so the open→session-register window is not a kill window) UNION `heldPtyIds()` (server.js → cli-env → facts; the field's first consumer). A failed listing does NOT mark the serve swept, so it retries on the next ready edge. **ROUND 5 (the fourth adversarial pass, both reproduced first):** ①**THE WARM `que_…` MAP OUTLIVED THE SERVE THAT MINTED IT.** `/question` is answered out of ONE serve process's own memory (real 1.18.29: a fresh process answers `[]` whatever the last one held), and `readConversation` joins an OPEN ask to the warm map, re-reading the authoritative list ONLY when that map is EMPTY — so a keeper respawn / new port / replaced adopted instance left every open ask joined to a `que_…` nobody holds: an answerable card whose Submit can only 404, the exact dead Submit `stale` exists to prevent. The map now carries the serve PROCESS it was filled under (`live.questionsFor` = the reaper's `${pid}:${port}:${startedAt}` key): a map stamped for a DIFFERENT process is not known, it is UNKNOWN — `pendingQuestionsFor` answers `[]`, so the read re-lists and the card renders `stale`; `answerQuestion`/`rejectQuestion` take their cold-map re-read; `state().pendingQuestions` stops claiming asks belonging to a dead process. AND every lane `connected` DROPS the map before re-reading it (`refreshQuestions`, beside the busy-map `statusMap()` the reconnect already paid for) — drop FIRST, so a failed read leaves unknown (⇒ stale, honest) instead of known-from-a-serve-that-is-gone. ②**THE LANE ONLY RUNS WHILE THE SERVICE DOES.** `install()` armed it unconditionally, and `lane.start()` arms an `fs.watch` on the USER's real store (resolved from the env THIS server runs under) plus an SSE reconnect loop with its own timers — so on the shipped default (plugin OFF, 2.369.59: nothing of ours runs or watches) a fresh instance held an inotify watch on `~/.local/share/opencode` and an unrelated `opencode` process's writes woke a server whose OpenCode feature was off (measured on a real boot: 1 inotify wd in `/proc/<pid>/fdinfo` while `sse.lastError` said "the background service is off"). The lane now follows ONE predicate — the SAME decision the keeper spawns on (`opts.autostart` = decideAutostart) OR a serve that is actually READY (the ADOPTED case the decision does not cover) — re-evaluated on every locator state change, so enabling the plugin brings it up with no restart and disabling tears down socket, timer and watch. Gated by a REAL boot with the plugin off (0 watch handles, no record, not even the throwaway `data/opencode-serve/cwd`) whose positive control is the same instance with the plugin turned on through the real route. **ROUND 7 (the sixth adversarial pass, both reproduced first) — THE CHECK BELONGS AT THE ACQUISITION POINT, and round 6's rule applies one layer UP.** Round 6 made the live lane's `stop()` terminal for an arm already in flight; but nothing the user clicks starts that lane — `install()` starts it from what the KEEPER publishes (`laneWanted = st.ready || wantsAutostart()`), and `locate()` tests `state.stopping` only at ENTRY. Every rung below that entry reaches `adopt()` — the ONE place `state.client` is ever assigned — after an await `stop()` cannot cancel: the reuse `/global/health` probe (a BUSY recorded serve that outlived a VibeSpace restart answers in hundreds of ms; 1.18.29 takes ~1.2s cold), `unsafeReuseReason`'s `GET /project/current`, `ensureServeCwd`'s `git init`, and the ≤20s boot wait — which is precisely the "starting…" window a user gives up in. So a Disable landing in one of them re-published `ready:true` for a service that was OFF, RE-ARMED the runaway-guard interval `stop()` had just cleared, and through `laneWanted` built a BRAND-NEW live lane whose own `laneStopped` is false by construction: the user's real OpenCode store watched again, and FIRING (`onExternal` ⇒ `opencode-updated` ⇒ a fleet-wide /api/sessions sweep) for a feature they had just turned off — with `state()` reporting `stopped:true` and `ready:true` at once, and the client pointing at a process `stop({killRecorded})` had already SIGTERMed. Two more windows in the same shape: a stop inside `git init` still reached the spawn (a brand-new third-party daemon started AFTER "off" — refused only by luck, because `_ocStop` writes the plugin record before calling `stop()` and `autostartOn()` is re-read; a stop that is authoritative must not depend on a SECOND fact), and the boot loop's old `return null` walked away from a child it had spawned, leaving a live `opencode serve` plus a record the NEXT boot would ADOPT. Fixes: `adopt()` refuses when `state.stopping` (the acquisition point — one guard covers every rung, present and future); `locate()` re-checks after the isolated-cwd await, after the reuse health probe and after `freePort()`; and the boot loop bails through `abandon()`, which SIGTERMs the child and clears the record only when it names that port (`why` is set only when WE decided, so a child that crashed on its own keeps `onChildExit`'s honest `lastError`). Gated by scripts/test-opencode-s9.mjs's ROUND 7 legs — three windows × {no disable = the positive control that a normal boot still adopts and watches, disable = zero published client / zero lane / zero fs.watch / zero `onExternal`}, each with a NEGATIVE CONTROL built from this very file with exactly these checks removed (it must publish `ready:true` after the stop, arm a lane, leak an inotify wd and fire; its 6 replacements are asserted to match their expected counts so a stale control fails loudly). **ROUND 8 (the seventh adversarial pass, reproduced first) — A LEVEL IS NOT A CANCELLATION.** Round 7's guards all asked `state.stopping`, which `stop()` raises and the very next `start()` lowers, so they were not terminal across a **Disable→Enable pair**: `start()` cleared the flag while `ensure()` still held the in-flight `locate()`, so the Enable JOINED the cancelled ladder instead of beginning one, and that ladder then published what it had gathered BEFORE the stop. Measured through the same real wiring (`_ocStop` then `_ocStart`, Disable at T and Enable at T+50 ms inside the 700 ms reuse probe): TWO adoptions — the Enable's own ladder spawned and adopted a serve, then the stale ladder adopted `source:'reused'` on the exact port `stop({killRecorded})` had SIGTERMed and whose record it had deleted, overwriting the live one and leaving the spawned child untracked. Fix = per-attempt cancellation, the shape round 6 used for the lane: `state.stopEpoch` is bumped by `stop()` AND by every new `locate()`, which captures `const epoch = ++state.stopEpoch` and passes it to `adopt(port, pid, source, epoch)` and every post-await check (`cancelled(epoch) = state.stopping || epoch !== state.stopEpoch`) — a cancelled attempt can never become valid again and only the NEWEST attempt may take ownership; `stop()` also detaches the in-flight attempt (`ensuring = null`) so the Enable starts its OWN ladder (without it `start()` resolves the cancelled run's null — a click reported as "did nothing"), and `ensure()`'s settle handler only clears the slot it still owns. `abandon()` writes `why`/`lastError` only while `state.stopping` holds (a run cancelled by a newer ladder must not narrate over it), SIGTERMs the child in its CLOSURE, and keeps its `state.child === child` null CONDITIONAL — a no-op on every path today (`stop()` nulls that slot first; after an Enable it belongs to a newer ladder), pinned by a leg whose mock child records kills by phase. Gated by scripts/test-opencode-s9.mjs's ROUND 8 legs with 2 single-mechanism controls (drop the epoch ⇒ two adoptions, the last a SIGTERMed process; drop the detach ⇒ the Enable's `start()` resolves null) plus one that removes `abandon()`'s SIGTERM. **ROUND 9 (the eighth adversarial pass, reproduced first) — A RECORD YOU DO NOT OWN.** Round 8's `ensuring = null` is what lets an Enable start its own ladder, and therefore the first thing that makes TWO ladders concurrent — at which point "the record on disk is mine" stops being true by construction. Every post-await site had the epoch check except the reuse rung's two `clearRecord()` calls: the verdict `await unsafeReuseReason(probe, rec)` was followed by an unguarded `killPid(rec.pid) + clearRecord()`, and the dead-pid arm ran after a 1.5s health probe with none either. Measured through the same wiring (Disable at T+1000 ms inside the VERDICT probe, Enable at T+1050 ms): the stale ladder woke at ~T+1400 ms and DELETED the record the Enable's spawn had just written, leaving a live `opencode serve` the next boot can neither adopt nor kill. Fix: every record clear is OWNED — `clearRecord({port, pid})` refuses when the record on disk names a different serve (`abandon()`, `onChildExit()` — the port travels from the spawn site because `state.port` is still null during a boot wait — and `parkRunaway()` all name theirs; `stop()`'s clears stay unconditional and say why: it is synchronous and bumps the epoch first) — AND both reuse-rung actions sit behind `cancelled(epoch)`. Port alone is not identity: `freePort()` can hand a cancelled ladder's port straight to the ladder that cancelled it, so abandon's old `r.port === port` test would have deleted the newer record; the pid discriminates. Gated by ROUND 9's legs: two windows (the verdict probe, the dead-pid arm) × {no disable = the positive control that the replacement really happens and is recorded, Disable→Enable = the record still names the live serve and the cancelled ladder signals nothing}, a PRE-FIX control that restores the exact reproduced shape (record gone, serve orphaned) — its 3 replacements are asserted to match their expected counts, so a stale control fails loudly — one single-mechanism control per layer, a port-recycle leg for `abandon()`, and a positive control that a genuinely dead recorded pid is STILL cleared by an uncancelled ladder. **ROUND 10 (the ninth adversarial pass, reproduced first) — THE RECORD WE WERE ABOUT TO OVERWRITE.** Rounds 7-9 hardened this rung against a CONCURRENT ladder; this one needs no concurrency at all. The reuse rung owned exactly ONE arm of an unanswered `/global/health`: a DEAD recorded pid (`else if (!cancelled(epoch) && !pidAlive(rec.pid)) clearRecord(owned)`). An ALIVE one — a wedged serve, or simply one past the 1.5s budget — fell THROUGH to the spawn, whose `writeRecord` then buried it. Measured through `install()` + `locator.start()` with a listening-but-silent serve and a live recorded pid: the recorded process is still running while data/opencode-serve.json names the NEW port, and not one line is logged. Neither the runaway guard (it samples OUR child) nor `stop({killRecorded})` (it reads the record) can ever reach that process again, while OpenCode keeps indexing and inotify-watching whatever it had booted — the 2.369.42 shape arriving through a different door, on every restart. Fix: **`settleRecordedServe(rec, owned, probe, epoch, willSpawn)`** — "we are about to overwrite this record" is a DECISION with named outcomes, never a fall-through. Dead pid ⇒ clear. Not going to spawn (no CLI / service off) ⇒ `'keep'`: nothing overwrites it, so nothing may act on it — it still NAMES the process `stop({killRecorded})` would signal. Otherwise **`classifyRecordedPid` (PURE, the procfs reads injected)** decides what that live pid IS: `'ours'` (running `serve` with the RECORDED `--port`, under our own uid — the port is the discriminator, not argv[0], because the launcher may re-exec its runtime), `'other'` (a different uid, THIS server process, or a different command line ⇒ the recorded serve is GONE and the record is stale bookkeeping we may delete — but that pid must NEVER be signalled: a recycled pid is somebody else's program), `'unknown'` (procfs said nothing — no /proc on this platform, hidepid, a zombie's empty cmdline). `'ours'` gets ONE longer confirm probe first (`RECORD_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT_MS` 4s — a cold 1.18.29 answers in ~1.2s, and SLOW must not read as WEDGED; if it answers we ADOPT it and nothing is stopped), then a warn naming pid/port/budget, a SIGTERM (never `process.pid`: the classifier answers `'other'` for our own pid, so a self-kill is unreachable), a BOUNDED wait for the exit, and only then the clear. Anything left — an unverifiable live pid, or one that ignored the SIGTERM — is `'blocked'`: no kill, no spawn, and a PARK (`parkedKind:'blocked'`) whose `lastError` names the pid, the port, the record file and both ways out. The park is the loud channel on purpose (`storeFailureReason` speaks only for a park), it re-tries on its own `BLOCKED_RETRY_MS` cooldown through the generalized `state.retryAfter` gate (the state can heal without the user: the serve may answer again, or the process may exit) — and a park's DEADLINE belongs to the park that set it, so `start()` clears it and a crash park declares none, or the terminal-until-restart crash park would inherit a blocked park's elapsed cooldown and quietly restart itself (its own 3-replacement control), and the ⚙ Plugins card carries its own row so a blocked record is never described as a crash loop. Gated by ROUND 10's legs: the fixed run (exactly ONE live serve, the record names it, one SIGTERM by pid, one warn), a PRE-FIX negative control (its 2 replacements restore the fall-through ⇒ two live serves, the record naming the new one, zero signals and zero log lines), the unverifiable and the SIGTERM-ignoring variants (no kill, no spawn, an honest `lastError` that /api/home reports through the REAL `storeFailureReason`), the recycled-pid variant (never signalled, the stale record cleared), a PURE verdict table plus the same call against a REAL process through the REAL procfs readers, and four positive controls (a healthy record still adopted untouched, a SLOW one adopted by the confirm probe, a service that is OFF left alone entirely, a genuinely dead pid still cleared). **ROUND 11 (the tenth adversarial pass) — A VERDICT THAT CAN NEVER BE REACHED IS AN OUTAGE, AND THE ONE BUTTON A PARK LEAVES ENABLED.** Round 10 hung two of its five outcomes on a `/proc` read, and macOS — "full support" in the README — has no `/proc`: there `readProcCmdline` answers null for EVERY pid, so the `'unknown'` REFUSAL fires on every stale record whose number has been recycled, parking the store dark forever with a red toast on every page load and an error naming an unrelated process. So (a) the readers gained the PORTABLE rung the agent CLIs already use — `readPsIdentity` = `ps -p <pid> -o uid=,args=` (execFile, 2s, memoised 1s) behind procfs, a VALUE read and never an existence probe (that stays `pidAlive`'s `kill -0`, the discovery-facts `pidLooksClaude` ladder); (b) `classifyRecordedPid` gained a fourth verdict `'blind'` = THIS HOST CANNOT ANSWER AT ALL, told apart from `'unknown'` by `hostCanIdentify()` — one probe of our OWN pid through the INJECTED reader, memoised for the process, warned once — and `'blind'` behaves like the pre-round-10 path (clear the stale record, signal NOTHING, spawn) because a live pid carries no information on a machine that can name no process; `'unknown'` keeps the park for what it actually means, *the reader answers about other processes and about this one it did not*; (c) `stop({killRecorded})` routes its kill through the SAME verdict (`decideRecordedKill`): the pid of a serve we are TALKING to (`state.client` is the identity proof, no /proc question asked) or a recorded pid whose verdict is `'ours'` — otherwise NOTHING is signalled, the record is still cleared (the user's "off" outranks the file) and `lastError` names what was left alone and why. Before this it SIGTERMed `state.pid || rec.pid` behind a self-pid guard: exactly the pid the blocked park had just refused to touch, from the ONE control the ⚙ card leaves enabled in that state. Legs: a pure four-verdict table; the `ps` rung driven DIRECTLY over three real fixtures and asserted to reach the SAME verdicts procfs does (including a spaced argv word, where the two spellings genuinely differ and the verdict must not); both readers stubbed absent ⇒ no park, one spawn, zero signals, one host-level warn (negative control: with `'blind'` removed the same machine parks BLOCKED forever); the discrimination leg (blinding ONLY the recorded pid still BLOCKS); and Disable-in-a-blocked-park ⇒ zero signals + record cleared + an honest `lastError` (negative control: with the verdict route removed it SIGTERMs that pid), with positive controls that Disable still stops an adopted serve and never complains about a recycled one. **S9 RESIDUALS (2026-09-07).** (a) **A deliberately-OFF service is not a broken store.** `storeFailureReason` reads `parked` and nothing else, so the `blocked` park this very module raises — a live recorded serve we can neither identify nor stop — SURVIVED the Disable that answered it: /api/home stayed red and the toast fired on every page load for a service the user had just switched off. `stop({killRecorded})` now retires a `blocked` or `runaway` park after clearing the record (the park is a retry schedule for a record that is now gone). A `crash` park is deliberately NOT retired — it is terminal until an explicit `start()`, which already clears every park, and retiring it here would make Disable→Enable quietly forget a crash loop. `lastError` stays as history for the ⚙ card; what goes is the CLAIM that the store is broken right now. (b) **`hostCanIdentify()` memoises the YES only.** "This platform has a readable process table" never changes back, so caching `true` is free — but `false` is one reading of one probe, and the probe misses for reasons that are about the MOMENT (EMFILE/ENOMEM, a `ps` fork lost to a load spike, /proc still being mounted in a container at boot). Caching that turned a transient miss into a PERMANENT capability downgrade, and the downgraded answer is verdict `'blind'` — the one verdict that clears a live recorded pid's record and spawns over it without ever identifying it. A NO is re-probed (at most once per settlement/stop, which is where the callers already are); `data/bin/vibespace-opencode-op` carries the same rule and the parity table drives both. (c) the identity ladder is no longer this module's: see src/cli-identity.js.
  • **ROLL BACK / RESTORE.** Client methods `revert(id,{messageID,partID})` / `unrevert(id)` + facts `revertTo` / `unrevert`. **v1 ONLY, and that is a measurement, not a preference:** with /proc against a fresh serve, `POST /session/:id/revert` restored the working tree (hello.txt really disappeared) while the process stayed at 16 threads / 0 `fff` indexer threads, whereas ONE `POST /api/session/:id/revert/clear` took it to 37 threads / 19 indexer threads / +165 MB — the v2 stage/clear/commit trio is the instance-booting family, so it is deliberately not wired and `unrevert` IS the v1 "clear". There is NO v1 "commit"; the next prompt commits, which is what the UI says. The staged state rides the Session's own `revert` field: `messagesToAcpRecords` emits a `notice` (noticeKind `'revert'`, text from `revertNoticeText`) immediately BEFORE the message it rolled back to, so a rolled-back conversation SAYS so wherever it renders, and the discover entry carries `opencode.revert` so the chat's message-metadata popup can offer "Restore" only while one is actually staged.
  • **THE ASK CARD.** `GET /question` + `POST /question/:id/{reply,reject}` (both boot no instance). A `question` tool part becomes the harness-neutral `permission_request` with `kind:'user_input'` — the SAME card claude's AskUserQuestion uses — carrying `via:'opencode-serve'` so the ws layer answers it on the serve's route instead of a session's stdin (a stopped conversation opened read-only has no process here at all). Verified shapes on a real turn: the pending request is `{id:'que_…', sessionID, questions:[{question, header, options:[{label,description}], multiple?, custom?}], tool:{messageID, callID}}`, an answered part carries `state.metadata.answers = [["Blue"]]` (one array of labels per question, in order), and `POST /question/:id/reply {answers:[["Blue"]]}` completed the turn. `askAnswersToPositional` converts the card's question-text map back to that positional form and splits a comma-joined multi-select ONLY when every piece is a known option label (a free-text answer containing ", " survives intact). RELOAD SURVIVAL: the transcript only knows the tool CALL id, the live route wants the `que_…` id, so `readConversation` joins them (re-reading `GET /question` once when the live map is cold — a just-restarted server); an ask with no live request behind it is marked `stale` and the card renders it WITHOUT a Submit that could only fail. **REACHABILITY, measured:** `opencode acp` (the mode our live sessions run in) does not expose the `question` tool at all — the model itself listed its tools and there was none — and question events are per-PROCESS, so this lane fires for turns the SERVE drives, not for our own ACP sessions. That is recorded here rather than hidden behind a card nobody can reach. **`answerQuestion` re-reads `GET /question` when the warm map does not know the request**: the card's answers are keyed by question TEXT, so converting them to OpenCode's positional form needs the question list, and a server that restarted between rendering the card and the user pressing Submit had an empty map — it refused its own user's answer with "no answers". Positional answers need no lookup and skip it.
  • **THE SERVE TERMINAL** — see src/server/opencode-pty-bridge.js below.
  • **THE LIVE LANE** — see src/opencode-events.js below. The 10s list-cache timer is GONE while the lane is healthy: `discover` refreshes only when an event marked the cache dirty (with a 1s serial-burst floor, because five browser tabs each poll /api/sessions), and falls back to the timer STRUCTURALLY when the lane is down — a broken lane must not freeze the sidebar forever. **The dirty signal NOTIFIES** (`onChange`, wired in src/server/cli-env.js): the sidebar caches this list too, so a change nobody asked about — a TUI writing the same sqlite — is pushed as `opencode-updated {kind:'store'}` instead of waiting for that browser's own 5s poll. Coalesced at 2s and with streamed message parts excluded, because each push costs EVERY open client one /api/sessions discovery sweep and our own opencode turns write that sqlite too. **A (re)connect also PRIMES the busy map** from `/session/status`: `session.status` frames are its only other source, so a serve that was already running a turn when the stream came up read `stopped` for the length of that turn — rung 1 of honest liveness blind exactly when it matters.
  • **'external' LIVENESS, with positive evidence only** (`deriveStatus`): `live` = one of OUR sessions holds the id; `external` = either this serve's own `/session/status` says busy/retry (in-process truth, no directory needed, boots nothing) OR the row's `time.updated` MOVED while we were not the ones moving it, within `EXTERNAL_WINDOW_MS` (90s) — the cross-process signal, since another opencode's events never reach our bus but the sqlite row it writes does reach our list, and the store-watch lane makes us re-read within ~0.4s. Anything else is `stopped`; the label DECAYS on its own, and `state().liveLaneHealthy` says when we cannot see at all, so the honest answer is a fact in the panel rather than a lie on every row. Verified against two real serves on one store: an external write flipped the row to external, our own write stayed live, and stale evidence decayed back to stopped. **"WE" INCLUDES THE USER'S OWN CLICK (round 3, a reproduced defect): "we were not the ones moving it" originally meant only *a live session of ours holds this id*, so every mutation through our OWN serve routes on a STOPPED conversation — roll back, restore, answer/reject an ask — moved `time.updated` and was then attributed to a stranger for 90s** (reproduced 3/3 through the real product routes: the card dimmed to opacity .7, its title read "Running in unsupported terminal (PID ?)", the Fork… row vanished from its menu, and a sidebar filtered to exclude 'external' lost the conversation entirely — all from the user's own click). `noteOwnWrite(id, session)` writes the mutation down and `ownWriteVerdict` consumes it: **by VALUE where we have one** — MEASURED on 1.18.29, `revert`/`unrevert` return the row's FINAL `time.updated` and nothing bumps it afterwards (0ms delta at +250ms…+8s), so the listing that reports exactly what we wrote is ours no matter how late it arrives, a listing carrying an OLDER value (one that was already in flight while we wrote) keeps the entry, and the first value PAST ours is somebody else's and says so immediately — and by a short `OWN_WRITE_WINDOW_MS` (10s) clock only for the actions that return no Session (an answered ask; the reply/reject paths therefore re-read `/question` even for positional answers, because the question is the only thing that names the conversation they are about to move). Fork writes nothing down and that is measured too: forking does not move the SOURCE row, and the fork's own row is a first sighting. The gate carries both directions — our own roll-back stays stopped on a REAL store, while a SECOND real `opencode serve` writing that same store still reads external.
NOT wired, with the reason: the v2 `/api/session/:id/revert/{stage,clear,commit}` trio (measured instance boot, above) and `POST /sync/history` — the DURABLE cross-process event log, which DOES carry another process's writes (proven: a session created by a second serve appeared in the first serve's history), but whose first read has no "from now on" cursor and would download the whole log; the list re-read the store-watch triggers is bounded and answers the same question. Gates: scripts/test-opencode-serve.mjs (135) + scripts/test-opencode-s9.mjs (the remainder: roll-back/restore incl. "the v2 family is never requested", the ask card end to end incl. the stale case and the free-text-with-comma control, the pty bridge over a real websocket, the live lane replacing the poll with a negative control for the timer fallback, liveness with three negative controls, wiring pins, and a REAL-BINARY section that SKIPS WITH EVIDENCE when `opencode` is absent) + scripts/test-opencode-remote.mjs (the three rungs cannot drift). test-opencode-serve details: (mock serve in scripts/dev/mock-opencode-serve.mjs, which MODELS the instance boot: any v2 per-session route adds `state.instances`, so 'a whole discovery tick bootstraps ZERO instances' is a real assert, plus a spawn-cwd spy, the '/'-worktree boot self-heal, the runaway guard driven by a fake /proc reader + fake clock, dispose-after-fork and the byte cap — mock serve in scripts/dev/mock-opencode-serve.mjs, which MODELS the instance boot: any v2 per-session route adds `state.instances`, so 'a whole discovery tick bootstraps ZERO instances' is a real assert, plus a spawn-cwd spy, the '/'-worktree boot self-heal, the runaway guard driven by a fake /proc reader + fake clock, dispose-after-fork and the byte cap); manual: `node scripts/dev/opencode-serve-live.mjs --measure [seconds]` runs the REAL loop against the REAL store and prints CPU/RSS/threads/indexer-threads/inotify-watches (healthy = single-digit CPU%, flat RSS, 0 indexer threads, 0 watches).
  src/opencode-events.js — THE LIVE LANE that replaced OpenCode's 10s list poll (S9 remainder piece (d), B-eac2; SHARED — node builtins only, the daemon bundles it). TWO SOURCES, because one of them is provably blind and saying so is the point. ① `GET /global/event`: measured with /proc, it boots NO OpenCode instance and needs no `directory`, so it is the ONE subscription per serve; frames are `{directory, project, payload:{id,type,properties}}` and a `server.heartbeat` lands about every 10s (undocumented, observed on the wire) — which is why an open socket with NO frame for 45s is treated as DEAD and aborted, not as idle. `createEventStream` reconnects with 1s·2^n backoff (≤30s) and re-asks the LOCATOR each time, so a serve that respawned on a new port is followed. ② `fs.watch` over the store dirs (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode`, `~/.local/share/opencode`, and the serve's own `GET /path` home when it differs — resolved lazily, because before the serve exists we do not know whose HOME it runs under): **THE MEASURED BLIND SPOT** — a SECOND opencode process on the SAME sqlite (a TUI, another serve) produces NO frame on `/global/event` at all (reproduced: serve A subscribed, serve B created a session, A's stream carried only `server.connected` + heartbeats for 30s while A's `GET /session` listed it immediately). The store is shared, the event bus is per process, so SSE alone cannot replace the poll; the watch never READS the db, only its mtime events, is debounced 400ms, and an unwatchable dir degrades to "no external signal" LOUDLY once and is retried on the next reconnect. `classifyEvent` is PURE: one testable table from event type → {kind, sessionId, dirty:{sessions|conversation|questions}, status, question, …}; an UNKNOWN type is `kind:'other'` with NO dirty flags, so an OpenCode upgrade can never make us drop a lane. `createLiveLane` is the pair behind one `state()` — `{sse:{connected,…}, watch:{watching,failed,active,…}}` — and "healthy" means BOTH, which is exactly the condition under which the timer refresh is allowed to be gone. **The lane FOLLOWS the serve, on an EDGE**: while nothing is reachable the stream is in backoff (up to 30s), so `install()` wraps the locator's own `onState` and calls `lane.kick()` when a port becomes READY or CHANGES — enabling the plugin, or a keeper respawn on a new port, goes live at once. It must be the edge and not every `notify()`: the runaway guard samples /proc once a minute, and kicking on each of those would re-open the SSE socket for nothing (both directions are pinned in scripts/test-opencode-s9.mjs). **AND THE SLEEP IS PART OF THE SOCKET (round 3, a reproduced defect): `kick()` originally reset `attempts` and aborted the fetch controller — but during a backoff there IS no fetch to abort, and nothing cleared the `setTimeout` the loop was sitting in, so the kick only shortened the NEXT wait.** Since the service ships OFF, "nothing to connect to" is the normal state before first use, so this was the first-use path, not a corner: measured 25.1s from "the serve is ready" to "the lane is healthy" end to end (and 11.0s to the next connect attempt in the unit shape), during which `laneHealthy()` is false and the 10s timer this feature replaced is still the only source of freshness. The loop's sleep now keeps its resolver (`wake`), and `kick()`/`stop()` both wake it before aborting — 51ms after the fix, with the regression driving the REAL stream to a ≥3s pending backoff so a sub-second reconnect cannot be an accident of a short timer. **ROUND 4 — the lane could LIE about itself, two ways, both closed.** `active` is what `laneHealthy()` switches the list-refresh fallback OFF on, and it was true for ANY directory that merely existed; meanwhile `armWatch()` ran at `start()` — before any serve — and latched (`watchTried` was only reset when the watch attached NOWHERE), so the documented "resolved LAZILY once the serve answers GET /path" never ran on any machine where `$HOME/.local/share/opencode` already exists, which is every machine that has ever run opencode. Reproduced with the real wiring: `state().liveLane.watch` = the SERVER process's store with `liveLaneHealthy` true, and a session created by a SECOND opencode process on the serve's REAL store never appeared (8s of 100ms-spaced `discover()`, ZERO `GET /session` issued because the lane claimed health); the same probe with the serve's actual store saw it in 493ms. In the default deployment the two resolve to the same dir (agentEnv keeps HOME/XDG_DATA_HOME), so this was a latent gap plus a FALSE HEALTH SIGNAL — and a false `active` is worse than none, because it is the flag that turns the fallback off. Fixes: `createStoreWatch` refuses a directory with no `opencode.db` (recorded in `failed`, `active` stays false ⇒ the timer fallback stays on and the next reconnect re-arms — the serve creates the db at boot); and `armWatch(why)` RE-RESOLVES on every `connected` against the serve's own `GET /path` home, re-arming only when the dir set actually DIFFERS (`watchedDirs` + a `rearms` counter in `state()`), so a reconnect storm cannot churn the watchers. **ROUND 5 — the lane is only STARTED while the service is on.** Nothing changed in this module: `start()` still arms the watch and the stream, and that is exactly why `install()` (src/opencode-serve.js) may not call it while the OpenCode background service is OFF — a lane that merely has nothing to connect to still holds an fs.watch on the user's store. The owner of "may this run at all" is the locator's autostart decision; this module owns only "how well is it running". **ROUND 6 — and `stop()` is TERMINAL for an arm already IN FLIGHT.** Round 5 gated whether the lane may START; both of its starts are async before they own anything, so a disable landing in the gap still leaked. `armWatch()` awaits `resolveDirs()` (the serve's `GET /path` on a 2s budget — spent in full exactly when the serve is parked or absent, the state a user turning the service off is in), and the continuation used to assign `watch = createStoreWatch(...)` onto a lane nobody holds: an fs.watch on the user's real store unreachable by any later `stop()` or `uninstall()`, and a LIVE one — a write to `opencode.db-wal` still fired `onExternal` ⇒ `markDirty` ⇒ an `opencode-updated` broadcast ⇒ every client re-running /api/sessions for a feature that was OFF (measured: 1 inotify wd at a 0 ms disable and at a 1200 ms disable, and with the keeper PARKED). `connectOnce()` had the same shape around `locator.client({budgetMs:8000})`: a stop there aborted a controller that did not exist yet and the continuation opened an SSE subscription the serve then held open forever (heartbeats keep it under the 45s idle abort), with `state().sse` reporting `stopped:true` AND `connected:true` at once. So: `laneStopped` is set FIRST in `stop()`; `armWatch()` re-checks it on entry AND hands the built watch to the single attach point `attachWatch()`, which closes it rather than store it; `resolveDirs()` skips its second round trip when the lane died during the first; `connectOnce()` re-checks `state.stopped` after the locator and after the fetch settles. The lane is SINGLE-USE by construction (`stopLive()` drops it, `armLive()` builds a fresh one per enable), which is what makes a one-way door safe — `kick()` is a no-op once stopped. Gated by scripts/test-opencode-s9.mjs's ROUND 6 legs, each run twice: once against this file and once against a copy with exactly these guards removed (the negative control MUST leak, and its replacements are asserted to match once each so a stale control fails loudly).
  src/opencode-remote.js — THE OP TABLE (S9 remainder piece (e), B-eac2; PURE — imports nothing). `OPENCODE_OPS` maps an op name to {member, required[], build(params), result(v)} and `runOpencodeOp(facts, op, params)` executes it against a facts object. That is the WHOLE machine-side implementation, and all three rungs use it: the local rung (hostId falsy, in-process), the `opencode-serve` agentd op (the daemon bundles src/opencode-serve.js and calls this same function against ITS facts), and — mirrored, because a checkout-less ssh host cannot require it — data/bin/vibespace-opencode-op. `checkOpParams` refuses an unknown op WITH the known list and a missing param WITH the op and key names, so no rung can fail as an unexplained 500. Gate: scripts/test-opencode-remote.mjs parses the shipped script's own OPS object and fails on any op the table has and the script lacks (or vice versa), compares result KEYS rung by rung against a mock serve, and pins the three-touch rule on the device side. **The daemon holds its facts in a MODULE-LEVEL `ocFacts`, never on `this`**: inside a Mux control handler `this` is the MUX — the CONNECTION — so a per-`this` cache is rebuilt on every reconnect and each `install()` arms another live lane (an SSE subscription + fs.watch handles) while the old one keeps running; a dial-out device reconnects on every link blip, which makes that leak silent and unbounded. The suites assert the declaration sits ABOVE `serveConnection` and that `this._ocFacts` appears nowhere. **Rung choice** (src/hosts.js `opencodeOp`): a DIAL device has no ssh fallback and rethrows the device error (2.271.0 T3-6 — the ssh path would misdiagnose it); an SSH host falls through on ANY device failure, like the usage-scan and transcript rungs, because the daemon may be old, down or mid-upgrade and the shipped script answers the same question. That fallback is FREE: the daemon's locator and the script use the SAME record `~/.vibespace/opencode-serve.json`, so the ssh rung REUSES the daemon's serve instead of starting a second one (pinned).
  data/bin/vibespace-opencode-op — REMOTE-side op runner for checkout-less ssh hosts (STATIC tracked, shipped to ~/.vibespace/bin; the documented single-file exception, same class as vibespace-usage-scan). Reads `{op,params}` on stdin, prints ONE `{ok,result}|{ok:false,error}` line. It carries the full 2.369.50 resource discipline onto someone else's machine: the serve is started from its OWN empty `~/.vibespace/opencode-serve-cwd` git repo (never $HOME — OpenCode's upward worktree walk would adopt it), ONLY v1 routes are used, the listing is directory-less and never bootstraps a project row that is not ours, every response read into memory is byte-capped, the record is written atomically, and a healthy recorded serve is reused instead of spawned per call. **AND THE RECORD IS SETTLED BEFORE ANYTHING OVERWRITES IT (round 11 — this file was the UNFIXED TWIN of the round-10 local bug):** `locate()` used to probe the recorded port and, on ANY non-answer, spawn a second serve and rewrite the record, orphaning a live `opencode serve` on a machine with no keeper, no runaway guard, no park and no ⚙ card — nothing there can ever reach it again. Now: dead pid ⇒ delete the record + spawn · a pid the identity ladder (`/proc` then `ps -p <pid> -o uid=,args=`, a VALUE read; `kill -0` stays the liveness probe) proves is NOT that `serve --port <recorded>` ⇒ stale bookkeeping, deleted, never signalled · a host that can identify no process at all ⇒ same (a live pid means nothing there) · verified ours and still silent after a LONGER confirm probe ⇒ SIGTERM + bounded wait, then clear · unidentifiable, or still running after the wait ⇒ `fail()` naming the pid, the port, the record path and both ways out, instead of spawning over it (there is no park out here — the honest failure IS the channel, and the hub surfaces the machine-side message). PARITY-PINNED as a DECISION, not just as a data walk: scripts/test-opencode-remote.mjs lifts this file's `classifyRecordedPid` out of its source and drives it and the module's over ONE 16-row table (a row per decision boundary — `serve` vs `server`, port-present vs absent, exact vs prefix port match, the four verdicts), pins the three budgets to the module's exported constants, and then runs the REAL script through each verdict against a real silent socket and real processes, with a PRE-FIX copy as the negative control (it starts the second serve and orphans the first). `read` ships the RAW v1 messages — the 'acp-events' synthesis stays in ONE place (the hub's `messagesToAcpRecords`, applied by the access layer), proven record-for-record identical to the local rung. The pty ops REFUSE with the reason (the serve's pty websocket is loopback-only on that host). Its rows are always `status:'stopped'` and that is deliberate, not a lag: liveness rung 2 is a LEDGER across listings (and, since round 3, across our own writes), and a one-shot ssh invocation has no memory between calls — so this rung claims nothing rather than guessing. The paired-device rung keeps the ledger because the daemon's facts live per PROCESS.
  src/server/opencode-access.js — the ONE way to reach the OpenCode serve on ANY machine (ORCH; wired once from mounts-plugins-wiring so server.js stays inside its size ratchet, and published as a module singleton `access()` that ws-handler / ws-create reach without a server.js cross). `call(hostId, op, params)` picks the transport and nothing downstream ever asks "is this remote?" again. Two normalisations live here because they must be identical on every rung: `readConversation` synthesises records from the ssh rung's raw messages with the SHARED function, and `publicView` strips the serve ws url + auth header from anything a ROUTE returns (they are how the SERVER connects; only ws-create's bridge sees them, through `openPtyBridge`). `LOCAL_ONLY_OPS` refuses the pty family for a remote machine BEFORE the transport is used, naming why.
  src/server/opencode-pty-bridge.js — THE SERVE TERMINAL (S9 remainder piece (c), ORCH). `opencode serve` owns real ptys and streams them over a websocket; this connects to it SERVER-SIDE and presents `{pid,onData,onExit,write,resize,kill}` — the same duck the daemon pipe-session shim uses — so ws-create can hand it to `setupSessionPty` and the xterm window, input, resize, the buffer file and every window action work with ZERO terminal-side changes. THE SERVE PORT NEVER REACHES THE BROWSER. Verified on the wire against 1.18.29: `GET /pty/{id}/connect` upgrades with NO ticket on an unsecured loopback serve (and `POST /pty/{id}/connect-token` answers PtyForbiddenError there, so the bridge mints one when it can and connects without one when it cannot); TEXT frames are terminal output; BINARY frames are `\0`-prefixed control json (`\0{"cursor":73}`) and rendering them would paint json into the user's shell; frames written in reach the pty. Resize is NOT on the socket — `PUT /pty/{id} {size:{rows,cols}}`. The pty belongs to the SERVE, so a dropped socket RECONNECTS (5 tries, backoff) instead of ending the session, and input typed meanwhile is queued (bounded at 200 — a dead socket must not grow memory). **But "the serve does not have this pty" is a VERDICT, not a hiccup (round 3, measured on the wire): after the shell exits, `GET /pty/<id>` answers PtyNotFoundError and the upgrade is a plain HTTP 404 — which the bounded reconnect burned all five rungs against (800+1600+2400+3200+4000 ≈ 12s of a dead-but-open terminal, plus five bogus `socket error: Unexpected server response: 404` warnings) before the window admitted the shell was gone.** `ptyGone(message)` is PURE (404/410 terminal; 502/503, ECONNREFUSED, ECONNRESET, "socket hang up" transient — a truth table in the gate) and the `error` handler sets a `gone` flag that short-circuits `close` into ONE honest log line + `onExit`; the mock serve now answers 404 to an upgrade for a pty it no longer has, exactly like the real one, so the end-to-end leg can assert ONE upgrade attempt and an exit under a second. Known limits, deliberately: it is LOCAL-only (a remote serve's ws is not reachable from the hub — a device would need the port-forward data plane), and a server restart leaves the pty alive on the serve without re-adopting it. **ROUND 4:** the bridge's `pty-close`/`pty-resize` calls still carry `cwd` on the wire (the op table's shape) but the CLIENT no longer turns it into a `directory` query — see src/opencode-serve.js: opening a terminal used to boot and permanently watch the user's whole worktree. The "a server restart leaves the pty alive on the serve without re-adopting it" limit above is now BOUNDED rather than open: it is still not re-adopted (no re-bridge), but `facts.reapPtys()` removes it on the next serve ready edge, so a stranded shell no longer runs forever. **B-ae4b (2.369.164): the duck holds a listener SET** (`ptyListeners({hold: 500})` from src/pty-duck.js). Its one slot met setupSessionPty's two registrations (the liveness stamp first, the terminal consumer second) since 2.369.82: the held banner was flushed into the FIRST registrant — the stamp — and the consumer that replaced it got nothing, so the serve terminal opened blank again (the exact bug the hold was written for), and the stamp was dropped for every later byte. Now the held bytes are replayed in a microtask to EVERY listener registered in the first tick, live bytes keep their place behind the replay, and every `onExit` listener fires (test-pty-duck §2 over the mock serve).
  src/routes/opencode.js — the OpenCode action routes (roll back / restore / asks / status / todos). Every route takes `host` and passes it straight to the access layer; every MUTATING route broadcasts `opencode-updated` (persistent state → other browsers see it without a refresh); every failure answers `{error}` with the machine-side reason (fetchJson never throws, so a 200-with-nothing would be a silent failure of a user action). Full shapes: docs/kb-api.md.
  src/harnesses/index.js — ONE descriptor per agent harness (claude.js, codex.js, shell.js, opencode.js via acp.js) = identity, `caps` (the backend-caps row), `Adapter` + `adapterConfig(cfg)`, `Normalizer`, `wrapper` file, `store` (locateTranscript/transcriptDirs/conversationIdField…), `quota` (S4 QuotaSignalSource: normalize/signalFromStream/probe/classifyAuthFailure — claude-quota.js/codex-quota.js/null-quota.js; the pool engine's probe dispatcher routes on `quota.probe`), `inject` (S6: kind hooks|wrapper|acp, hookFile, hookEvents, sessionStartHonoured — agent-tool-generators builds HOOK_FILES/HOOK_EVENTS_FOR from it; agent-routes' seen-gates consult sessionStartHonoured), `creds` (S2, 2.369.26-27: subsDirName/authFile/spawnEnvVar/loginLabel/defaultIdField/keychainSensitive/parseAuth(dir) + files/bumpFile/hostFactsKey/longLivedToken/supportsApiKeys/remoteSymlinks/ensureTargets/probe/seedDir(dir) [codex: sharedHome()] — accounts.js resolves dirs/auth/labels/default-account/export files/import seeding/delete/verdict host-facts/pool-swap bump/spawn env var/remoteCreds ship shape through `_credsOf/_acctDir/_readAuthFor/_remoteCreds`; readSubCreds/readCodexSubAuth/_seedConfigDir/_seedCodexDir/_codexSharedHome are shims over it; createPool validates capsOf().pool + registry. Deliberately still dispatched: resolveForSpawn (claude oat/api-key ladder vs codex CODEX_HOME) and the claude-only hostSubs held-check), `settingsPrefix`. API: `HARNESSES` (built-ins), `get/has/list/ids` (unknown id THROWS — never a claude fallback), `register/unregister` (plugin tier-5; built-ins immutable), `assertQuotaContract`. adapters/index.js and normalizers.js are built from it. Conformance: scripts/test-harness-contract.mjs runs the same assertions over every registered harness (descriptor keys, adapter base methods + buildSessionArgs, normalizer duck contract incl. injectPeerCard/convertHistoryAsync, wrapper file + caps advert, store, settings keys, client BACKEND_META row, inject shape, wiring pins). S7 (2.369.23) client META caps + settingsPrefix parity pinned here (2.369.26 — the pins missed their 2.369.23 commit: a patch batch aborted before the suite). S3 (store, 2.369.31) and S5 (stdout pipeline per descriptor — see the HARNESS STDOUT entry below) are landed. S5 decision: the descriptor names its live-stdout consumer ONLY through `caps.streamProtocol` (the backend-caps row it already carries); there is deliberately no `stdout:{protocol}` field — a second copy is a twin waiting to drift, and the contract suite pins that none exists. **store.warmTranscript (B-21e4 item 5):** the OPTIONAL pre-read hook `(id, cwd, {remote}) → Promise` every history consumer awaits through the descriptor before constructing a reader — ws-handler attach + view-only and transcript-service.view (the claude-only `warmSessionJsonlAsync` ternaries are gone): claude = the worker parse-cache warm (unchanged), codex = the thread/read fallback for a missing rollout, a harness without it skips.

### gmail-sync.js

  gmail-sync.js        — GmailSync (2.134.0, backlog B-64db): Gmail-as-a-folder — a 'gmail' mount = local dir of .eml files synced READ-ONLY from the Gmail API (GYB-style; NOT FUSE). Own loopback OAuth for gmail.readonly (rclone authorize is drive-only; same guided UX incl. remote paste-back); seed = STREAMING + CHECKPOINTED (2.136.1-4): each page downloaded then a CROSS-RESTART cursor persisted — a DATE (`state.seedOldestMs` → `before:<sec>`), NOT the messages.list pageToken (pageToken is only stable within one run; new mail between runs shifts/expires it and silently skips OLD mail the incremental never back-fills — real user catch). historyId anchored at seed START (covers mail arriving during a long seed). Total for the N/total bar comes cheaply from users.getProfile `messagesTotal` (whole mailbox) or labels.get `messagesTotal` (label filter), persisted as `state.seedTotal` (free-text query → indeterminate). Progress broadcasts throttle (indeterminate 2.5s — a fast cadence rebuilt the card and restarted the bar animation, stuttering it 'in the first third'; the bar is a symmetric pulse so a mid-anim rebuild is invisible). Incremental via history.list (404 = expired → reseed; dir tree IS the dedup index — msg id in filename tail, _seenIds recurses one date/label dir level), messages.get?format=raw → base64url → .eml (atomic tmp+rename, RFC2047-decoded subject slug in name). Client id/secret from VIBESPACE_GDRIVE_CLIENTS presets (they carry gmail scope) or custom — NO built-in fallback. mounts.js integration: isMounted=worker alive, health sweep skips fuse probing (dead worker → auto-restart), unmount stops worker but keeps files (it's the archive), mode forced ro. Viewer: src/lib/eml.js (dependency-free browser-safe MIME parser, 41-case test) + file-viewer _renderEml (header card, text/html toggle, html in sandbox="" iframe, attachment blob downloads). **2.151.0 incremental-freeze fix (real 3h hang):** history.list lists ADDED ids that can be deleted by fetch time (spam auto-purge; guaranteed with includeSpamTrash) — the per-message 404 failed the whole pass and the cursor only advances after a COMPLETE pass ⇒ every 120s retry re-listed + re-404'd the same dead id forever. _writeGone404 skips gone messages (both paths); all API/token fetches bounded (AbortSignal.timeout 60s/30s) so a wedged socket errors into the backoff.   transcript-worker.js — heavy JSONL transcript work OFF the main thread (2.235.0, the userL degradation follow-up): a persistent SafeFs-hosted worker pool (SafeFs gained opts.workerPath/inlineRun generalization + in-flight ref()) running the EXISTING sync implementations by requiring the same modules — worker-side mtime+size caches, zero duplication.
