### agentd/

  agentd/               — CS refactor (B-5052) machine agent — ALL milestones' protocol+device side COMPLETE and acceptance-tested (2.140.0–2.146.0; docs/design-remote-cs.md + M0 addendum + milestone record). THREE flags, DEFAULT ON since 2.158.0 (CS graduation — local=device#0; automatic legacy fallback preserved). **ONE MACHINE MODEL since 2.160.0 (B-f3e8, resolves the user's 2026-07-15 insight that row inconsistencies = two underlying concepts): a machine is a host record, transport ∈ {ssh(absent), dial}** — the pairing credential lives ON the dial record (`dialTokenHash`, redacted from list(), migrated ONCE from dial-tokens.json via hosts.migrateDialTokenFile → `.migrated`; LOSSLESS is load-bearing: in-field daemons hold the raw tokens); roster/test/unpair = /api/hosts + POST /api/hosts/:id/test (hosts.test dial branch = mux runCmd probe) + DELETE /api/hosts/:id (server unpairDialDevice: mounts+token-file+live-stream teardown); /api/agentd/devices is GONE; `hosts-updated` broadcasts on pair/unpair/dial-in/out; hosts.dirComplete rides the device link (dial machines get real remote autocomplete); sidebar has ONE _buildHostRow for all transports + a 'This machine' local row (local=device#0 made visible). The flags: `agentd.sessions` (M1: local sessions run in the daemon — dtach attach inside agentd, survives server restarts), `agentd.remoteSessions` (M2: remote chat = persistent pipe session in the remote daemon via the vibespace-agentd-attach bridge, keeper-run-identical contract so chat-wrapper is untouched; auto install/refresh at spawn), `agentd.dataPlane` (M3 switchovers: RemoteFs fs ops / discovery raw-facts synthesized into the ssh-script line format→UNCHANGED parser / transcript INCREMENTAL slab sync (append-only delta via read-range — no more whole-file remote-jsonl pulls) / usage harvest via run-stream; per-path ssh fallback; hosts.device(id) = per-host DeviceManager registry). mux.js = length-prefixed binary mux (chan0 JSON control + credit-flow-controlled byte channels; data() SPLITS at the window — all-or-nothing starved big writes; zero deps, shared by daemon+server = invariant #3). **CONTROL-OVERTAKE INVARIANT (2.187.0, real incident): chan0 control is credit-EXEMPT, so a completion marker (fs-done/stream-exit) OVERTAKES data still queued behind the 256KB window — any "resolve on the done marker" consumer truncates big transfers to exactly INITIAL_WINDOW bytes.** fsReadRange/runStream are COUNT-GATED (resolve when the counted bytes landed; daemon reports `sent`, run-stream exits on 'close' not 'exit', both pace under window pressure via onWritable); the incident: a 45MB remote transcript cached as a 256KB prefix stamped complete → permanently ancient chat history (fetchSessionJsonl now also refuses to stamp meta for bytes not received + caps on FETCHED delta not total size; **2.188.1: cache-valid additionally requires the cached FILE to hold meta.size bytes — a pre-fix stump over a STOPPED transcript passed size/mtime forever since the self-heal only fired on remote-file change**). Any NEW byte-channel consumer must gate on a byte count, never on a control-channel done. Test: scripts/test-agentd-bigread.mjs. agentd.js = daemon (flock singleton, setsid, 0700 unix socket, multi-server, vsht_ hello auth, self-upgrade→versioned dir→re-exec (2.185.2: the re-exec PRESERVES the original argv via reExecArgv — dropping `--dial/--dial-token` re-exec'd a dial device into LISTEN mode and wedged the link behind the singleton, the userW-class 'device goes offline after updates' root cause); pipe-sessions = keeper semantics in-daemon (setsid child + buffer/fifo + offset reattach + sentinel + drain-only-never-respawn); **pipe-child identity is exec-PROOF startTime, never cmdline (2.184.1, real userL outage: chat children spawn as `sh -lc '… exec env … claude'` so cmdline loses argv0 — every daemon upgrade re-exec then misjudged the live claude as a recycled pid, synthesized a crash sentinel (session died, claude orphaned) AND made kill-pipe-session a no-op; adopted children additionally get a liveness watcher because a non-child can't be wait()ed — no watcher meant no exit sentinel ever; test-agentd-adopt.mjs guards both)**; fs-op incl read-range byte-chan slab; discovery snapshot w/ tailIds/headCwd/userLines enrichment + fs.watch dirty push; run-cmd (argv-only bounded); run-stream (unbounded stdout on byte chan); tcp-connect (loopback only = VNC bridge shape); **serve-folder (2.150.0; WEBDAV since 2.151.0, device-folder-mount): a minimal in-daemon read-only WebDAV subset (OPTIONS/PROPFIND Depth 0-1/HEAD/GET+Range; zero deps, mirrors src/webdav.js) bound to 127.0.0.1 that rclone `webdav`-mounts via tcp-connect (src/device-mount.js) — the plain-`http` backend was the 2.150.0 stall: it requests a fixed 128MB range per read then waits ~6s on the keep-alive connection after the clamped 206; webdav requests sane ranges and reads in ~7ms (verified). GOTCHAS: clamp ranged end to size-1 (rclone asks 128M ranges → clamp or truncated EIO); the SERVER-side bridge net.createServer MUST be `{allowHalfOpen:true}` + attach the data listener BEFORE `await tcpForward` (curl/rclone half-close a GET's write side + write-then-read, both lose bytes otherwise); NEVER do sync fs/exec on a device mountpoint from the process hosting the bridge — the blocked event loop can't pump the tunnel, the FUSE read never completes, SELF-DEADLOCK (the acceptance test hung itself this way for a whole debug cycle; a dir `ls` still 'works' off rclone's dir-cache, which hides it; test IO now runs in async children w/ watchdog — production safe by construction: bridge in the server, reads from other processes/safe-fs workers). Still not a MountManager UI type (next step). **SSH-BRIDGE STDIN EPIPE (2.241.1, userN's exit-code-1 crash): the client.js ssh-transport wrapper writes to child.stdin — pipe errors arrive ASYNC as 'error' events on the stdin socket itself (the wrapper's on('error') only covered the child process; the write try/catch only stops sync throws), so a dying ssh child during the heartbeat PING was an UNCAUGHT write EPIPE that killed the whole server 28s after an update restart. stdin/stdout error events are swallowed; 'close' drives mux teardown+reconnect. Any new pipe-wrapped transport must attach error listeners on the PIPE STREAMS, not just the process.** dial-in device consumption = DeviceManager `stream` transport + server deviceForDial(id) wrapping a dialed-in ws stream — **deviceForDial NEVER reuses a stop()ed DeviceManager (2.169.0, real userW outage: hours of phantom-offline against a healthy dialed-in Mac): stop() is terminal (_connectLoop throws 'stopped' forever), so a stopped dm is evicted like a stale stream and a failed connect() never stays cached; any new dm.stop() caller must not leave the object in agentdDialDevices**. Dial chat TERMINATE kills the device-side claude via the daemon's `kill-pipe-session` (client killPipeSession) + rm's the session token over the device link — the ssh-only teardown threw for dial and silently orphaned claude (double-JSONL-writer class). Pairing commands render `/api/device-dial`; `/api/agentd-dial` is a PERMANENT alias (in-field daemons hold it in dial.json); env `VIBESPACE_DEVICE_ROOT` preferred, `VIBESPACE_AGENTD_ROOT` honored forever. **RE-PAIR / IDENTITY ROTATION (2.170.0, the userW-incident class): the daemon re-reads dial.json on EVERY dial attempt and the host-token file on EVERY hello — a re-pair heals a RUNNING daemon within one retry; never cache either at startup (the cached identity dialed a dead pairing forever while the singleton blocked its replacement + launchd respawn-spammed). The installer replaces a running same-root daemon (cmdline-verified kill); macOS singleton verifies the lock pid via `ps` (no /proc — recycled pids read as "already running" forever). Multi-instance = one root/daemon per instance (`~/.vibespace/device@<dialhost>`), re-pair replaces within a root.** **REVERSE forward tcp-listen/tcp-accept/tcp-unlisten (2.148.0, the NAT-traversal tunnel)** — daemon binds 127.0.0.1:<port> ON THE DEVICE, accepts push back over the mux as new byte channels (chan ids from 0x40000000 — never collides with server-allocated 2..N; the tcp-accept control MUST precede channel data), server pipes them into its own loopback port; on link death the listener is DISOWNED not closed (port stays bound → reconnecting server re-owns same-port via connect-loop re-registration → remote mounts heal in place); both tcp paths backpressured (credit-after-drain + mux.onWritable resume); --stdio ssh bridge mode; --dial ws dial-out (Transport B; ws-min.js = hand-rolled RFC6455 client — the `head` bytes-with-the-101 upgrade trap is handled, dropping them ate first frames on fast reconnects)). client.js = DeviceManager (transports local/ssh, openSession/openPipeSession/fs*/runCmd/runStream/tcpForward/reverseForward/discovery). Server: /api/agentd-dial upgrade branch (dial-token gated, verifies hosts.dialTokenHash since 2.160.0) + dial-pair mint (writes the hash onto the dial host record; /api/agentd/devices + /api/device-mounts RETIRED in 2.160.0 — roster/test/unpair = /api/hosts, mounts = /api/machine-mounts, see machine-mounts.js). Pairing dialog has per-OS commands (mac/linux bash; WINDOWS EXPERIMENTAL via /agentd-install.ps1, PS 5.1-compatible + win32 named-pipe SOCK in the daemon; the ps1 now also persists state\dial.json + registers a logon SCHEDULED TASK, so a Windows device survives a reboot). **EVERY URL in those commands must come from `httpBase` (= `r.relayUrl || location.origin`), NEVER location.origin directly (2.246.0 bug): a relay-paired device correctly dialed the relay but was handed origin-based installer/bundle URLs its network cannot reach — it failed before the daemon ever started.** MULTI-INSTANCE pairing: dial-out installs root at ~/.vibespace/agentd@<dialhost> (per-instance daemon/tokens/bundle; installer exports VIBESPACE_AGENTD_ROOT — forget that and the daemon reads the default root's token). INSTALLER GOTCHA (2.152.1, real Mac report): macOS has NO setsid(1) — the installer's unconditional `setsid node …` started NOTHING and printed ✓ anyway (stderr redirected into agentd.out); now setsid-or-nohup + kill-0 verification before claiming success. **NODE-FREE PAIRING (2.246.0): the installers (bash AND ps1) no longer REQUIRE node — resolution order is `--node` override → OUR private `$ROOT/node/bin/node` → PATH → newest nvm → common absolute paths → PROVISION (pinned official tarball from nodejs.org/dist, verified against that release's SHASUMS256.txt, smoke-run, then atomically `mv`d into `$ROOT/node`; `--node-only` = resolve/print/exit, the support probe). Private-BEFORE-PATH is deliberate (a launchd plist pointing at an nvm path dies at the user's next nvm upgrade); nvm-before-common-paths is the `curl|bash`-is-non-login lesson (nvm.sh never sourced ⇒ the #1 false 'no node'). Everything lands INSIDE the root, so `rm -rf $ROOT` uninstalls the runtime too — and because agentd's `spawnEnv()` prepends `path.dirname(process.execPath)`, the `#!/usr/bin/env node` agent tools resolve on a machine that never had node (2.244.4 chicken-and-egg, solved structurally). **AND THE DAEMON IS BORN SANITIZED (2026-09-14, src/agent-env.js): `_spawnLocal`, the `--stdio` bridge's spawn and the upgrade re-exec all hand a new daemon `daemonEnv(process.env)`, and `spawnEnv()` merges every child over that same sanitized base — never raw `process.env` — because the daemon is a SECOND HOLDER of the server env that outlives its restarts, and a real pipe-session claude was measured carrying a cluster integration secret a previous server life had handed the daemon (test-agentd-session's holder leg + test-integration-registry §6(h)).** CONSEQUENCE: a provisioned device is PINNED to that node forever (no OS security updates) until the pin is bumped — documented in docs/device-agent.md § Node runtime. RULE: every later node/npm invocation in the installers uses the resolved absolute `$NODE_BIN`/`$NODE_DIR/npm`, NEVER bare `node` (launchd/systemd get no PATH of ours). set -e footguns in that block: `[ -e x ] && mv` and bare `x=$(cmd|pipe)` under pipefail both exit the script — keep new predicates inside `if`/`|| true`. musl + 32-bit Windows refuse honestly with fix instructions (official builds are glibc/64-bit only). Instance-side fallback mirror `GET /vibespace-node/:version/:file` (server.js, auth-exempt, fixed upstream + strict filename allowlist + disk cache in data/node-cache/) for devices that reach this instance but not nodejs.org. Tests: scripts/test-node-bootstrap.mjs (19 asserts, local HTTP fixture + a bwrap node-free sandbox; covers tamper/unlisted-checksum refusal, re-use, nvm discovery, override).** E2E: scripts/dbg-pair-smoke.mjs (17 asserts, REAL daemon dial + mount chain + UI rows). Build: npm run build:agentd → data/bin/vibespace-agentd.js + vibespace-agentd-attach.js (both gitignored artifacts). Tests (all green, 3 environments incl the devbox real-ssh + fleet test pod): test-mux/-agentd/-agentd-session/-agentd-remote/-agentd-robustness (bidi/jitter/latency/concurrency)/-agentd-wired/-agentd-dial/-agentd-m3m4 (18 scenarios)/-agentd-switchover (real-host legacy-vs-device cross-checks). u-vstest soaks with ALL flags on. **2.369.12 push阶梯(inc-mtl78uhs)**: mountpoint的~/$HOME按机器home展开+去尾斜杠(liveness探针比裸路径); rclone daemon子进程--log-file写入dialog tail的同一日志(真实原因不再被--daemon吞掉); macOS阶梯=rclone nfsmount(≥1.66, 免macFUSE)→FUSE mount(有macFUSE时)→mount_webdav, 每级失败都保留展示; 设备rclone pin v1.69.3, 自有旧安装force重装, 系统rclone不动; method 'rclone-nfs'与umount家族同处理.

### machine-mounts.js

  machine-mounts.js    — MachineMounts (B-f3e8 2.160.0 — HostMounts 2.147.0 + DeviceMounts 2.153.0 collapsed into ONE manager; records carry dir:'push'|'pull', keyed by hostId, store data/machine-mounts.json, both legacy stores constructor-migrated → .migrated; routes /api/machine-mounts* (POST :hostId {dir,…}), broadcast machine-mounts-updated). PUSH = mount THIS instance's folder ON the machine, OS-aware (Linux rclone/FUSE; macOS rclone/macFUSE else native mount_webdav — macFUSE probed ON the Mac since 2.160.0, the old check read the SERVER's /dev/fuse; Windows rclone/WinFsp else net use; rclone auto-installed remote-side w/ unzip→busybox→python3 fallbacks). Transport: _davBase prefers the agentd REVERSE-FORWARD TUNNEL (remote mounts http://127.0.0.1:<port>/dav over the device link — NAT-proof; dial machines tunnel-ONLY, ssh falls back to agentd.publicUrl); tunnelPort per record. PULL = the machine's folder mounted INTO this workspace over hosts.device(hostId) (serve-folder→tcp-forward→rclone webdav ro — works for ssh AND dial identically); live chain in-memory, restore()/onMachineLinked heal recorded pulls + re-own push tunnel ports (a re-dial means the daemon RE-EXECED → stale handles torn down first, real Mac report 2.158.1) + 90s child-process-ls health sweep (never node fs on a fuse mountpoint). unmount = best-effort remote teardown but ALWAYS token-revoke + record-drop (dead machine can't hold a credential); host removal → onMachineUnpaired drops all its mounts. GOTCHAS (real e2e catches): mint() returns {raw, rec} not {token,id}; NEVER execFileSync in anything sharing the process with /dav (event-loop block = FUSE IO hang); detached remote rclone needs FULL fd redirect (</dev/null >/dev/null 2>>log) or the ssh ControlMaster never frees; setsid is LINUX-ONLY — conditionally prefixed (macOS died at command-not-found with the error swallowed into the remote log, now tail'd back into the dialog); **TRAILING SLASH on a pull's shared path 403'd EVERY file (2.168.0, real userW Mac→VibeSpace report): the daemon serve-folder confines with `root + path.sep`, so a root ending in `/` (e.g. `/Users/me/Downloads/`) double-slashes the prefix (`…Downloads//`) — the root listing passes but every subpath 403s → rclone "couldn't list files: 403 Forbidden", mount never comes up. PUSH was immune (mountPush runs path.resolve). Fix strips the trailing slash in THREE places: mountPull (intake), _up (heals an existing record without a device-daemon update), serveFolder (daemon defense) — dbg-pair-smoke now pulls a trailing-slash path so its file-read assertion guards it.** Tests: test-machine-migrate.mjs (migration guard) + test-host-mounts(-tunnel).mjs (push e2e) + dbg-pair-smoke.mjs (pull e2e over a real dialed daemon)

### exit-proxy.js

  exit-proxy.js        — ExitProxyManager (task #164, 2.186.0): ON-DEMAND egress — an agent borrows a paired machine's network for a SINGLE command (a region / internal-VPN / fixed source IP), NOT the whole session. Two tiers via the `vibespace-exit` CLI (data/bin, static tracked, in AGENT_TOOLS): `use <machine>`/`url` = the device daemon serves a zero-dep in-daemon SOCKS5 (serve-socks/unserve-socks ops, CONNECT-only, DNS-on-exit) on its loopback, the server reaches it via the existing tcpForward and binds local `socks5h://127.0.0.1:<port>` (tool stays local, egress = the machine; proxy-aware TCP only); `run <machine> -- cmd` = execute natively on the machine via runCmd (universal fallback: ICMP/UDP/proxy-unaware/its DNS). Opt-in per machine (hosts.allowExit, default off — SSRF into its LAN; Remote-tab ↗ toggle). Routes: /api/exits + /api/hosts/:id/allow-exit (cookie UI) + /api/agent/exit[/use|/run] (vsst_). The loopback-only tunnel boundary holds (tcp-connect stays never-a-general-proxy; the SOCKS server is the one sanctioned egress, inside the machine owner's network). Tests: test-agentd-socks.mjs + test-exit-proxy.mjs

### port-forward.js

  port-forward.js      — PortForwardManager (B-0b60 tunnel path, 2.165.0): vscode-style port forwarding over the agentd data plane — NO frps/public exposure. detect(hostId) = `ss -tlnH || lsof -nP -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN` over dm.runCmd (lsof matched FIRST — its `(LISTEN)` suffix; an ss IP:port pattern also matches an lsof line; 2.177.0: ss runs with -p for process names, the /proc/net fallback resolves socket inodes→proc via a bounded /proc/*/fd scan, and _classify flags known NON-web daemons `hidden` (both ports UIs fold them behind '+N system listeners', the watch never toasts them; DBs deliberately stay visible); 2.180.0 (B-16d9): scans carry the pid and _classifyOrphan flags LOCAL listeners whose /proc/<pid>/cwd readlink ends ' (deleted)' (zombie dev server from a removed worktree — userL's 2×6GB next-servers) — watch announces each pid once incl. the baseline sweep, ports UIs show an 'orphan' tag + Kill (POST /api/ports/kill-orphan re-verifies deleted-cwd at kill time, never kills a healthy process)); ### plugins.js

  plugins.js           — PluginManager (2.140.0, B-2d44): generic host-capability plugins — install + PERSISTENT state (~/.vibespace/plugins/<id>/, home=PVC in fleet) + boot replay (enabled+desiredUp → restart with server) + guided setup + status. First plugin TAILSCALE: dual mode (kernel via /dev/net/tun+NET_ADMIN(sudo) / userspace --tun=userspace-networking + SOCKS5 localhost:1055), system tailscaled detected-never-managed (own --socket/--statedir coexist), login = capture `tailscale up`'s auth URL (Drive-OAuth pattern), node key in statedir ⇒ pod rebuild reconnects sans re-login. Routes /api/plugins* (server.js); UI src/lib/plugins-ui.js (⚙ → Plugins…); helm optional tun device (tun.enabled → NET_ADMIN + device-plugin resource). Second plugin FRP (2.166.0, B-0b60 public-URL half): runs frpc on the instance → a shared frps RELAY, so a forwarded machine port can be PUBLISHED to the public internet as a shareable link. Relay addr/port/token INJECTED via env `VIBESPACE_FRPS_ADDR/_PORT/_TOKEN` (fleet infra, NEVER in the repo — absent ⇒ `configured:false`, plugin no-ops). frpc runs with a base config + a local admin API (127.0.0.1:7400) + `includes` proxies dir; `frpPublish(name, localPort)` writes a per-port proxy toml, `frpc reload`s, polls the admin `/api/status` for `running` (retries a new public port in `VIBESPACE_FRP_PORT_MIN..MAX` on collision — the relay is fleet-shared), returns `http://<relay>:<port>/`. PortForwardManager.publish/unpublish wire it to a forward (persisted, re-published on restore). The relay itself (frps) is set up per the PRIVATE deploy dir runbook (the PRIVATE deploy repo, frp/), NOT this repo. **SUBDOMAIN mode + double-NAT pairing (2.183.0, B-5c1e): with `VIBESPACE_FRPS_SUBDOMAIN_HOST` set (or the plugin's subDomainHost config), frpPublish emits `type:https`+`https2http` proxies → `https://<sub>.<host>/` (persisted preferSub survives restarts). The Pair-a-device dialog's `viaRelay` option self-publishes the instance's own PORT and uses the relay subdomain as the dial base (bundle fetch + device-dial WS both route through it) — so a NAT'd instance can pair a NAT'd device (relay bridges both). Persisted selfDialSub keeps the URL stable across re-pairs. dial-pair route: `viaRelay` branch in server.js; plugin: setSelfDialSub/selfDialSub in status. PROTOCOL-AWARE publish (2.184.0): frpPublish `_probeProto`s the backend — HTTP→routed `type=http` subdomain (relay terminates TLS server-side w/ a wildcard cert via a Caddy front → browser-trusted, ZERO cert on instances), HTTPS→`https://ip:port` passthrough (backend's own cert), raw-TCP→`tcp://ip:port` (a DB/VNC has no Host/SNI). Never blindly https2http. `proto` rides the publish result + `publicProto` on the forward record. Relay side (private runbook): Caddy :443 wildcard-cert termination → frps vhostHTTP :8080; acme.sh Cloudflare DNS-01 auto-renew.** Test: scripts/test-frp-plugin.mjs (live, against the real relay) **THIRD plugin OPENCODE-SERVE (2026-09-07, owner decision — the ONE switch for the OpenCode background service, DEFAULT OFF):** the keeper, resource guard and every serve FACT stay in the SHARED module src/opencode-serve.js; this manager is only the CONTROL SURFACE and owns exactly three bits of user intent in data/plugins.json — `enabled`, `desiredUp`, `promptedAt`. `defs()` gains the row; `status('opencode-serve')` = `_ocStatus()` (installed/configured = the `opencode` CLI resolved by cli-env, running/port/pid/source/version/cpuPct/rssMb/parkedKind straight off `facts().state()`, `enabled` overridden by the env force, `prompted`, and `reason` = the shared `reasonUnavailable()` so the panel and every user action quote the SAME sentence); `start()` = `_ocStart()` (sets enabled+desiredUp, refuses loudly when the CLI is missing or `VIBESPACE_OPENCODE_SERVE=0` forces it off, then `locator.start()` — which CLEARS a previous stop/park, an explicit user start being the deliberate retry — and DROPS the facts caches so the sidebar does not keep showing the 10s negative-cached "nothing"); `stop()`/`setEnabled(id,false)` = `_ocStop()` (desiredUp false + `locator.stop({killRecorded:true})` — "off" must mean the process is GONE, including a serve merely ADOPTED from data/opencode-serve.json; the process-exit path deliberately leaves an adopted one alone so the next boot reuses it); `setConfig` REFUSES (there is nothing to configure — it binds a free loopback port); `install()` cannot install anything (VibeSpace runs the user's own CLI) so it says how to get OpenCode instead of offering a dead button; boot replay = enabled+desiredUp ⇒ start with the server. NEW GENERIC MEMBERS used by the harness layer: `wantsServiceUp(id)` (the plugin half of `decideAutostart`), `serviceState(id)`/`services()` (the compact {enabled,desiredUp,prompted,installed,running,starting,parked,envForced,reason} row cli-env puts on the /api/home harness row when a descriptor declares `store.servicePlugin`), and `setPrompted(id)` behind POST /api/plugins/:id/prompted (the first-use dialog is asked ONCE **per instance** — the flag is store state that BROADCASTS, never per-browser localStorage). Every `plugins-updated` broadcast now carries `services` beside `plugins`. Test: scripts/test-opencode-plugin.mjs.

### accounts.js

  accounts.js          — **2.369.157 r4: the ledger rung is STABLE — the pool's own default rows on either side of `createdAt`: the last one before it (`to`), else — the ledger was recording (its oldest row predates the start) and no row of this pool precedes it (a pool older than the ledger) — the FIRST one after it (`from`), else the current default; `before.to !== after.from` (a re-point the ledger never saw) ⇒ `unknown`; `_heldPoolOrigin === 'no-start'` (boot-restore: a meta without createdAt) ⇒ `unknown`. r3 read only `before`, so a pre-ledger pool's legacy process flipped from `{A, ledger}` to `unknown` at the pool's first recorded move — the very row whose `from` names A — and a restarted server filed its wall on the pool's new member.** **2.369.157 r3: `poolMemberOfSession(poolId, session, sessKey)` = THE member a pool session's process speaks as → `{id, held, origin}`: a non-hot pool (`capsOf(backend).hotSwitch !== 'verified'`, local) holds its spawn stamp (`stamp`), else the slot-transition ledger's pool default at the session's `createdAt` (`ledger` — also when the ledger was recording at the start and the default never moved since), else `unknown` (id = the link, nothing may spend on it); every other pool session = its link / the default (`link`). Read by the engine (credit/reading/wall/fire), server.js `recordUsageAttribution` (the permanent ledger) and `sessionAuth` (the badge).** AccountManager (per-session billing-identity switching, backend-scoped via a `backend` field on each account — legacy records = 'claude'. THREE account types: (1) Claude API key — AES-256-GCM in data/accounts.json + .accounts-key, injected as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; (2) Claude SUBSCRIPTION (2.56.0) — a dir data/subs/<id>/ holding ONLY that account's .credentials.json, read by the CLI via CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR (relocates the SECRET store ONLY; projects/sessions/settings stay in ~/.claude so transcripts+discovery stay shared — verified vs claude 2.1.205: Wde()=env??sn(). Empty dir→loggedIn:false, dir-with-creds→that login, ~/.claude untouched. **CONSEQUENCE (2.244.2, forensically verified on 2.1.222): claude's /status Organization/Email reads the NON-relocated ~/.claude.json — a relocated/host-held spawn DISPLAYS the machine login's identity while the TOKEN (= billing) is the dir account's (proof: the spawn refreshes the dir's token, machine store untouched). Never treat /status identity as billing proof for relocated logins; the host-held Test toast explains this to users**); (3) Codex/ChatGPT SUBSCRIPTION (2.59.0) — a dir data/codex-subs/cxs-<id>/ = an isolated CODEX_HOME whose sessions/+config.toml SYMLINK the shared ~/.codex (threads/settings shared, unified discovery — VERIFIED codex 0.142.5: symlinks survive a run, rollout lands in the shared dir), auth.json real per-account; createCodexSubscription/readCodexSubAuth(parses auth_mode + id_token JWT→email/plan)/finalizeCodexSubscription; login = `codex login --device-auth`. resolveForSpawn(requested, backend) returns {kind, localEnv:{VAR:val}, secret?, remoteCreds?} — claude-api→ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, claude-sub→CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR, codex-sub→CODEX_HOME; all PROCESS-ENV only, never argv. Separate defaults per backend (defaultAccountId / defaultCodexAccountId). REMOTE (P3, 2.59.0): subscriptions ship their creds dir to a host via `remoteCreds` — ws-handler tars the whitelisted files (.credentials.json/.claude.json | auth.json), streams over ssh-stdin into 0700 ~/.vibespace/<subs|codex-subs>/<id>, symlinks shared subdirs, prefixes the env var; 2.59.1: NO rm -rf (concurrent same-account sessions), tar --keep-newer-files newest-wins (host-side refresh rotates the live token — don't clobber it) + poison-heal probe (remote creds file missing its validity marker is rm'd pre-extract). list() returns tail-8 for keys, email/plan/loggedIn for subs (read-only). importFromCli() captures a Console primaryApiKey. **remove() POOL HYGIENE (2.335.0, owner report: deleting the account a pool sat on broke the whole pool): deleting a claude subscription strips it from every pool's explicit member list, re-points the default symlink to a live member (or unlinks it — absent = honestly signed-out, a dangling link is a phantom login), and re-points/drops per-session links that billed to it (`_healPoolsAfterRemoval`); gated by test-pool-signed-out (17).** **Re-login identity guard (2.333.0, owner directive): `reloginResolve(id)` finalizes an on-this-machine re-login by COMPARING the fresh login's identity to the record — same ⇒ in-place; matches ANOTHER record ⇒ creds move there ('moved'); unknown ⇒ auto-SPLIT to a new entry named by the email while the original stays signed-out with history intact (a friend logging the wrong account can never rebrand/pollute a record); route POST /api/accounts/:id/relogin-finalize, watcher in manage-agents toasts all outcomes; matrix scripts/test-account-relogin.mjs (13).** Lets the user's OWN subscription logins coexist per backend, switchable per session — the CLI's own /login only keeps one active at a time, so VibeSpace remembers each separately (like signing in/out without losing the others). **§ban-safety (2.59.1, after a real Max ban+refund — see [[reference_multi_subscription]]):** NO background /api/oauth/usage polling with sub tokens (that off-CLI fixed-cadence automated call on idle accounts is the #1 bot-flag: ToS §3.7 + 2026-02-20 OAuth-clarification) — usage is now captured PASSIVELY by data/bin/vibespace-usage (STATIC file), a statusLine hook injected via --settings into LOCAL TERMINAL sessions only that harvests the CLI's OWN rate_limits into data/usage-cache/<key>.json (zero API calls; chat/stream-json has no statusline → last-known; server ingestPassiveUsage reads the dir, no network). Subscription creds shipping to REMOTE is OFF by default (setting accounts.shipSubscriptionToRemote; ws-handler remoteAccountEnv gate throws with guidance) — a sub token from a datacenter IP is an impossible-travel/abuse signal; default = "log in on the host"; API keys always ship (sanctioned programmatic path)) **list() POOLED-FIRST (2.369.18, P1 codex pool UI): the pooled branch is evaluated BEFORE the per-backend branches for every backend — the codex branch used to win, so a codex pool listed as a bare ChatGPT login with no `pooled/current/currentName/memberOptions/auto/hot` (no client surface could operate it AND the engine's `type==='pooled' && a.auto` tick enumeration never saw it). The pool row reads identity THROUGH the symlink with the member's own auth reader (readCodexSubAuth / readSubCreds) and carries `hotSupported` = capsOf(backend).hotSwitch==='verified' (src/backend-caps.js) so the UI hides the hot toggle where the engine ignores it (codex). Pinned in test-codex-pool.**

  **LOGIN-SESSION EXPIRY (2026-09-07, src/login-expiry.js):** `loginStateOf(id, now)` answers "when does this account's LOGIN end" through the harness descriptor's OPTIONAL `creds.loginState` — claude declares it, every other harness simply does not and gets 'unknown' (an absent reader is honest; a fabricated 'ok' is not). Every subscription row in `list()` carries `loginState`; a POOL's row carries `poolLoginState` = its members' WORST plus `worstId`/`worstName` (a pool has no login of its own). `_poolLoginCandidates` asks TWO questions, not one (round-2 verifier, reproduced against this instance's own store): an EXPLICIT `members: [...]` list is what the user NAMED, so a signed-out member of it IS the pool's finding and stays in the summary; an IMPLICIT pool (`members: null` — the default, and the shape of the only pool here) has its membership DEFINED as `poolMembers()`, so an account that is signed out was never a member of it. Round 1 used the over-broad set for both, and on a pool whose three routing members were all logged in it read `logged-out` forever, drew a permanent red chip offering to re-login an account dead 700 h that the pool never routes to, and — because worst-of ranks 'logged-out' above 'expiring' — MASKED the CURRENT target's login dying in 16 h. The current link target is always in the set even if its own login has since died: the pool is pointed AT it, so it is the pool's problem however it got there. `resolveForSpawn`'s pool self-heal now ORDERS the alive list by `loginRank` (an 'expired' member still parses as loggedIn, because the tokens are only blanked at the CLI's next failed refresh, so without this the heal happily re-points onto a login that fails the first turn) — an ordering, never a filter: every member being expired must still start the session and then say so. **SAME-SPELLING TRAP:** the `/relogin` + `/subscription/:id/finalize` routes also return `loginState`, a STRING ('error') about how the login TERMINAL run went. Different objects, different types; never join them (a comment at that route says so too).

Matrix: scripts/test-account-verdicts.mjs 45 asserts (incl. the 2.269.0 local-only-mac rung). **INTENDED-USAGE (official docs code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions, 2.253.1): setup-token/CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is Anthropic's DOCUMENTED path to run your subscription on remote/CI machines (generate locally → use as a secret on the runner) — cross-machine use is BY DESIGN. But the docs steer to an API key "for a secret shared across repositories … an OAuth token is tied to the subscription of the person who ran claude setup-token", so broad multi-context sharing is OUTSIDE the intended lane — the UI copy says "tied to your subscription, safer than shipping the login, use an API key for broadly-shared credentials", NOT "zero-risk anywhere". §ban-safety reality: oat removes refresh-rotation + shipping the interactive login, NOT the "subscription inference from a datacenter IP" signal (identical to shipping creds) — but it IS the sanctioned mechanism so the ToS posture is better. ### account-pool-auto.js

**THE PROJECTION (B-f69c ③, 2.369.163, owner ruling ut-1c6c15a2db ③ "1%/min 燃烧 40 分钟读一次不够").** The pool decides on the estimate of NOW; at a fast burn a bucket a few points above its line is across it before any scheduled reading lands. Three PURE pieces: `projectCacheAhead(cache, burn, nowSec, leadSec)` advances every bucket by its own burn (`burn` = the estimator's `burnRates`, utilization per minute, keys `fiveHour`/`sevenDay`/`scoped:<name>`; an absent key is no claim) — never a window that resets inside the lead (it refills; advancing a spent number past its own reset would invent a wall) and never an EMPTY window (B-8b12), returning the SAME object when nothing moved; `projectionCrossing(cache, burn, nowSec, {hot})` = the soonest bucket to reach its switch line (the hot bar on a hot pool, else the hard bar), strictly in the FUTURE — a bucket already under its line is the estimate's business — and never past its own reset; `PROJECTION_LEAD_SEC = 300` = the fast rung's own floor (the longest a reading the projection asked for can be withheld by pacing, so an early move covers exactly the stretch no fresh reading can). **The auto-cli rule:** `decideCliRefresh` is now one eligibility rule `cliRefreshWhy(a, now, opts)` → `'projection' | 'drift' | 'stale-active' | 'stale-idle' | null` + `nextScheduledReadMs` (the age rung, or the drift rung at the current burn `estBurnPtPerMin`); a `projCrossInMs` that lands BEFORE the next scheduled read asks the SAME rung now, ranked first (soonest crossing), under the SAME 5-min floor, failure backoff and one-per-tick serialization — event-driven by a projection, never a cadence, never a new vendor path. **ONE READING PER CROSSING (quota r1, the verifier's slow-approach simulation):** the floor paces a spawn but never limited the drift rung (it needs 4 pt of movement between reads), and the projection had no such self-limiter — after each reading the crossing was still ahead and still before the next scheduled read, so `projection` was answered again every time the floor cleared (0.05 %/min from 7 %: reads at min 5, 10, …, 35 = 7 where the pre-B-f69c rule took none before the line). The loop now carries `projReadCrossAt` = the crossing INSTANT its last SUCCESSFUL projection read was spent on (server.js `projBought`, stamped after `refreshViaCliPanel` answered ok — a failed read bought nothing, the failure backoff paces its retry); `cliRefreshWhy` answers `projection` for the same instant within `PROJECTION_MOVE_MS` (5 min, the estimate's own wobble) never again, a crossing that MOVED further (the burn changed) is a new question, and the drift/age/idle rungs ignore the memory. The same approach now reads once at min 5, then on the age rung. Not adopted from the verifier's sketch: a second arm "re-ask when the reading is older than the crossing is far" — on the same world it re-arms a halving sequence (min 22.5, 31, 36), i.e. the cadence again; the cold-conversation 300 s projected view covers the last stretch before the line. **THE WARM RULES STAND:** the engine hands a projected view only to a decision about a COLD conversation — a projection alone never moves a warm one (the .149 warm-cache hold and the .153 first-stop rule judge only real readings). Gates: test-pool-auto (the pure legs + a REAL-engine world with one cold and one warm conversation on a burning member, and two scratch-dir patched copies — the warm gate removed ⇒ the warm one moves too; the lead zeroed (master) ⇒ the cold one meets the line), test-auto-cli-refresh §8 (the owner's arithmetic, the drift-first case, floor, ranking, one pick, wiring pins), test-usage-estimator (burn). **THE MEMORY IS THE BUCKET, THE PASSIVE READING IS THE READING, AND THE PACING STATE OUTLIVES A RESTART (quota r2, the r2 verifier's three reproduced findings).** ① The r1 memory keyed on the crossing INSTANT, and the instant is the burn window's own noise: `burnRates` is a 10-min trailing window, so under Poisson arrivals at the SAME mean burn the projected crossing moved by more than `PROJECTION_MOVE_MS` on 47-65 % of ticks (median 13.6 min, p90 52 min at 1 request/min) and every wobble was bought again at the floor — 3-4 projection reads before one line where a constant burn took 1; a 10-member fleet 42 projection reads in its first hour instead of 9. The loop now remembers WHICH BUCKET of WHICH WINDOW bought a reading: `projReads = {label: {at, resetsAt, boughtAt}}` per account (PURE `projectionReadsAfter` stamps it after a SUCCESSFUL projection read, pruning expired records), `projectionCrossing` returns the crossing bucket's `resetsAt` (0 = unknown) and the engine's `projectionRereadFor` passes it through, and `cliRefreshWhy` answers `projection` never for a bucket `projectionBucketBought` says already bought — until its window resets (an unknown reset: `PROJECTION_MEMORY_MS`, 5 h, after the purchase). A second bucket is its own question (two families ⇒ two reads; alternation between them re-buys nothing); the r1 instant band stays as the secondary guard across buckets (`projReadCrossAt` = the last bought instant). Not adopted: a proportional band (max(5 min, 0.5×distance)) — the verifier measured it halving the re-buys (42 → 29), not ending them. ② The projection arm now also needs `age >= floorMs`: a passive (statusline) reading 30 s old IS the number the projection would buy — the verifier's passive-every-minute world spent 2 projection reads with a 30-s-old reading at each (worse than no passive readings: each rebase zeroes drift and pushes the drift rung's horizon out, so the projection is 'before the next scheduled read' more often). Because `fetchedAt` lives on disk this is also the rung's restart-proof floor. The drift/age/idle rungs are untouched. ③ `attempts`, `fails` and `projReads` were closure state in server.js, the first tick 60 s after boot: every restart re-bought the same bucket with no floor (a restart every 3 min: 11 spawns in 40 min; every 2 min: 15). The loop moved to **src/server/auto-cli-loop.js** (`createAutoCliLoop(deps)` → `{tick, start, state}`, clock/RNG injectable) and persists its pacing state in `data/auto-cli-state.json` (tmp + rename after every spawn — at most one write per tick, so nothing is left to flush on SIGTERM; an unreadable file starts empty, the `age >= floorMs` guard is the floor without it). Gates: test-auto-cli-refresh §9 drives the REAL loop with the REAL rule, projectionCrossing and burnRates over a synthetic ledger (constant and Poisson arrivals, three seeds → exactly ONE projection read each; two families → one per bucket; a passive reading every minute → zero spawns; crash loops every 3 and 2 min → the no-restart control's count; a 10-member fleet → at most one projection read per member, 17/15/17 spawns per hour in every arrival model), each fix with a scratch-dir patched copy as its negative control (the r1 instant band alone re-buys under Poisson; no age guard spends a read on a 30-s-old reading; an in-memory-only loop re-buys after a restart). **THE READ IS SPENT NEXT TO THE LINE; A RECORD THAT CANNOT BE A WINDOW IS NO MEMORY (quota r3, the r3 verifier's placement and state-file worlds).** ① One read per bucket was spent at the FIRST eligible tick — the moment the reading turned floor-old — i.e. as far from the line as the floor allowed: a 10 % / 0.05 %/min approach read at min 43 for a line at min 80, so the estimate the pool met the line with was 37 min old and `PROJECTION_LEAD_SEC`'s promise no longer held. The projection arm now also needs `cross <= projWindowMs` (`PROJECTION_WINDOW_MS` = the floor + the lead = 10 min): the read lands in the last window before the line (measured 71 min for that world, 8-10 min before the line on every slow world; the fleet's spawns per hour unchanged). ② A read of ANY rung that lands while the bucket's crossing is inside that window is the purchase too (the loop marks it): the two-family world used to buy Fable twice — the idle rung at min 42, a projection at min 47. ③ `projectionBucketBought` ignores a record whose `resetsAt` lies more than `PROJECTION_RECORD_MAX_MS` (8 d — no vendor window is longer than 7 d) past its purchase (a ms-shaped resetsAt silenced its bucket until year 58 700; `projectionReadsAfter` prunes it), and answers "not bought" when the crossing names a DIFFERENT known window than the record by more than `PROJECTION_MOVE_MS` (a panel-estimated reset corrected by an exact event, the next window) — a minute of disagreement or an unknown crossing window stays the same window. Gates: test-auto-cli-refresh §① (placement ≤ 10 min before the line on three worlds + a no-window patched copy reading 37 min early; each bucket bought once with a projection-only-buys patched copy re-buying) and §⑤ (the window/record pure legs, a ms-poisoned state file healing in the real loop).

server/auto-cli-loop.js — THE AUTO-CLI QUOTA REFRESH LOOP (2.329.0; moved out of server.js in quota r2): `createAutoCliLoop({serverSetting, accounts, autoCliReady, USAGE_CACHE_DIR, usageIdentityGroupsCached, usageEstimator, projectionRereadFor, lastMemberReadAt, usage, onMemberReadingFresh, dataDir, now?, rand?})` → `{tick, start, state}`; server.js only wires it. One `claude -p /usage` spawn per 60 s tick at most, through `usage.refreshViaCliPanel` (the owner-approved exception, §ban-safety), picked by account-pool-auto's `decideCliRefresh`; its pacing state (`attempts`, `fails`, `projReads`) persists in `data/auto-cli-state.json` (tmp + rename after every spawn; unreadable ⇒ empty) so a restart neither re-buys a bucket nor loses the floor/backoff. test-quota-model ⑩ names it (reads usage-cache, writes only its own state); since 2.369.164 (B-a5c0) its drift read is usage-estimator's `cliRefreshDrift` (a raw bucket whose `resetsAt` is past is no control for the LOGGED drift; `estDriftPct`/`activeBurn` = its `triggerDrift`/`moved`, unchanged) — so it touches no raw bucket and left ⑪'s table. Gate: test-auto-cli-refresh §8/§9 (the real loop, injected clock), test-new-member-wake (the attempt clock + the fresh-reading edge pins). **quota r3 (the r3 verifier's persistence findings, each red first):** ① **the order of a spawn** is stamp → `saveState` → `refreshViaCliPanel` → the backoff + the bought bucket → `saveState` → THEN `onMemberReadingFresh` in its OWN try (a throwing wake used to skip the bucket memory and the write, re-buying every floor) → the journal line — a restart while `claude -p /usage` is in flight (under KillMode=process the orphaned probe still spends its vendor call) sees the attempt and does not spawn again inside the floor; ② **the clock can step back** (VM restore, NTP step): `clampStamps` (at load and every tick) clamps an attempt stamp to `now` and DROPS a bought-bucket record from the future beyond a 60 s skew, with one warn line — before, a file stamped 720 h ahead pinned every rung off for the whole step and nothing ever rewrote it; ③ an unreadable file (corrupt JSON, an array, a number) starts empty with ONE `[auto-cli] pacing state unreadable` warn line (a missing file stays silent); ④ **one identity, one memory**: two account ids over one org-merged identity (`usageIdentityGroupsCached`) read the group's merged `projReads` (`mergedReads`), share the attempt floor (max over the ids) and a purchase is written under every id — they used to buy the same org's bucket twice; ⑤ a read of any rung inside the projection window marks its bucket (see account-pool-auto's projection essay); ⑥ `ok` = `!!refreshViaCliPanel()` — the producer's answer is now its WRITE (usage-routes). Gates: test-auto-cli-refresh §③ (future stamps ×3 vs a past-stamp control + a no-clamp copy silencing 4 h; the hung-spawn restart + a save-after-spawn copy re-spawning; the throwing wake + an r2-order copy; three unreadable shapes + a missing file), §⑤ (the two-ids-one-group world + a keyed-by-id copy; a producer answering false paced by the backoff vs one answering true spawning every floor).

The reset-credit ladder fork lives in src/reset-credit.js, not here (this module decides a MOVE; the verdict decides a SPEND).** **2.369.153 THE FIRST STOP: PURE `conversationInTurn({isStreaming, turnState})` = `isStreaming === true || turnState === 'running' || 'requires_action'` (a paused turn is not an ended one; a terminal-mode session with neither fact is NOT in a turn ⇒ it moves at once — ignorance never defers). `decidePoolSwitch`'s `warm` may carry `inTurn`: on a HOT pool the SOFT band (a bucket under its `hot` bar, none under `hard`, login alive) with a warm AND in-turn conversation answers `none('warm-soft-defer', {agoSec, ttlSec, wouldTo, wouldToName, band:'soft', softBucket:{label,kind,remaining,hot,hard}, fromRemaining, …bucket bands})` — the move owed at the first stop; cold or idle ⇒ `{…, reason:'exhausted', band:'soft'}` as before; every exhausted return now names its `band` ('hard' = a bucket under the hard bar or a dead login — moves at once, never deferred); `no-settleable` still wins when nothing can settle; the proactive 'edf' tier is unchanged (warm ⇒ 'warm-cache' whether or not in a turn — its verdict now also carries `wouldToName`, verifier INFO-a); `warm` without `inTurn` ⇒ byte-identical to 2.369.149.** **2.369.108 `quotaVerdict` also returns `deadBuckets` [{label,kind,remaining,line,resetsAt s}] + `until` {label,resetsAt s} = the bucket that sets blockedUntil (reporting only — no threshold reads them; empty shapes on usable/no-data so readers never branch on presence).** Pooled pseudo-account (B-6217, 2.251.0-2.252.0): account type 'pooled' — ONE switchable billing identity over the logged-in Claude subscriptions. Historical pre-2.256.0 events carry no pool tag (fine — they just don't appear in the pool lens). v2: `auto` = at claude turn end (maybePoolAutoSwitch in server.js), current target <5% remaining (MIN across 5h/7d/scoped-weekly; account-pool-auto.js pure decisions — reset-passed bucket = full, unknown member = 50, unknown CURRENT = never switch, 60s throttle) → re-point, re-record ledger attribution, and (cold) ask exactly ONE connected client to restart affected conversations via `pool-auto-switched` (headless = de-facto hot until a client appears). **v3 EDF RANKING (2.259.0, user-designed): quota is PERISHABLE — the target choice is earliest-WEEKLY-deadline-first, not most-remaining** (KEY FACT, user-confirmed + cache-verified ±1s: scoped weeklies like Fable are COMPONENTS of the same 7d window — same resetsAt — so each account has ONE weekly deadline and per-account EDF is optimal; the coupled-bucket objection collapses). 5h is EXCLUDED from ranking (burst limiter refilling ~33×/week — else every account's soonest reset is its 5h and the sort is noise) but stays in the <5% usability GATE. Same deadline ±60s → more remaining first (equal expiry ⇒ order can't change utilization; fewer switches); known-deadline members outrank unknown; fresh-after-reset (deadline unknowable from stale cache) ranks last. **HOT pools get a PROACTIVE tier** (`proactive: !!a.hot`): switch toward a strictly-sooner deadline (≥1h margin, never onto unknown data) BEFORE exhaustion — hot re-points are free; cold pools stay exhaustion-only (each switch restarts conversations).
