The row label is the file's BASENAME with the full path on the `title` (a 375px column cannot show a 120-char path AND the size; measured in `scripts/test-worktree-userchan-ui.mjs`).

**SendUserFile → the published-pages channel.** `src/server/stdout/claude-stream-json.js` publishes the files ONE call names through `publishContent` — session-owned, **private by default** (a VibeSpace login is the gate) — and broadcasts `user-file-published {sessionId, toolCallId, files:[{path, name, link?, pageId?, size?, error?}]}`. Fully async (a sent file can sit on a wedged mount — the never-block-the-event-loop law), bounded (8 MiB, 20 files), and **every failure rides the same broadcast onto the card**: a file the agent believes it delivered and the user never got is precisely the silent failure this product does not tolerate. `link` is **RELATIVE** (`/p/<id>`) — the 2.366.1 URL law: the server does not know how it is being reached, so the browser joins it with its own origin. **LOCAL sessions only**: a remote session's files are on another machine and are not ours to read, so the card renders with no link and says so — an honest absence, never a guessed URL. Paths resolve against the directory the CLI **itself** is in (`session._worktreePath` for a `--worktree` session, else `session.cwd`), because the tool's own describe says "absolute or relative to cwd".

**The channel has its OWN key namespace, and never re-asserts visibility (2026-09-07 round 3).** `srcKey` is published-pages' UPSERT IDENTITY, and `local:<abs>` is the key the user's own `publish()` mints AND the one `vibespace-page publish` uses (`<host|local>:<path>`). Publishing under it meant a file the agent sent silently **took over** the page the user had published from that path — same id, agent's bytes, re-attributed to this conversation — and the explicit `makePublic:false` flipped a page they had deliberately shared back to private, so the link they had handed out started redirecting to `/login`. It also collapsed two conversations naming the same stable path (`report.md`, `/tmp/out.png` — what agents actually write) into ONE record, and the older conversation's card lost its link entirely because `list({conversationId})` stopped matching it. So the key is `userfile:<conversationId|sessionId>:<abs>` — scoped to the CONVERSATION, so a re-send inside the same conversation still keeps ONE stable `/p/<id>` across resumes while a different conversation gets its own page — and **no visibility flag is passed at all**: a freshly minted record is already `public:false`, so private-by-default is preserved while an existing page's visibility is never overwritten (the same rule the agent publish route already follows). `publishContent` gained an optional DESCRIPTIVE `srcPath` for exactly this: a namespaced key must not be prefix-stripped into an invented `<conv>:/abs/path`.

**A FAILED call says so on the card.** These cards have no ✓/✗ column — the wrap label is the channel icon — so until 2026-09-07 a `SendUserFile` the CLI rejected, or a `SendUserMessage` the turn interrupted, rendered as an ordinary successful "File for you" about a file that was never delivered (the per-file `upload_error` was honoured; the CALL-level failure was dropped). `userChannelOutcome({toolStatus, status})` is the PURE rule — `error` | `pending` | `ok` — and it reads the MESSAGE-level fields first because the two producers disagree in shape: an `is_error` tool_result marks the block too, an INTERRUPTED call keeps its `tool_call` block and only the message says `error`. The record carries `outcome` plus `error` (the CLI's own failure text, which is exactly why `output` did not parse as JSON), the cards draw `.chat-userchan-failed` and take the red rule, and the delivery `note` is suppressed. `pending` is deliberately silent: this card is meant to be read the moment the agent writes it.

**Client re-hydration.** `ChatView._publishedUserFiles` is a bounded (500) `toolCallId → rows` map fed by the live broadcast AND by one `/api/pages?conversationId=` read on attach, so a RELOADED history shows the same links a live session does. That read matches pages to cards **by the page's own `srcPath`**, never by parsing a path back out of `srcKey`: the key is an UPSERT IDENTITY whose format is the publisher's business, and the hand-rolled `local:`-stripping drifted the moment the channel got its own namespace (round 3) — absolute paths, which is what the SendUserFile schema documents agents send, silently stopped resolving while relative ones kept working by accident through the basename fallback (round 4). The basename fallback stays for records that named a relative path: the publisher resolved it against the CLI's own cwd, which the client does not know and must not guess. `_rerenderToolCard` swaps the one card in place (no window/pin/scroll change) **through `ChatView._swapMessageEl`** — see the chat-view entry: a swap that skips that bookkeeping unregisters the message.

**Gates.** `scripts/test-stdout-registry.mjs` (real `tool_use` fixtures for both tools, the end-to-end publish against real `published-pages`, the remote rule, and the unrelated-tool negative control) + `scripts/test-worktree-userchan-ui.mjs` (the card measured at 375×667 in headless chrome, with a CSS negative control).

## src/backend-caps.js `worktree` + src/adapters/claude-code.js spawn flags (owner ruling 9 + 8(c))

**The caps row is the ONLY gate.** `capsOf(backend).worktree = {supported, flag, named, requiresGitRepo, hookEscape, landsIn, branchPrefix}` — the New Session checkbox, the Session Properties checkbox, the session-card badge and the ws refusal all read it (client mirror `worktreeCapsFor` in `src/lib/agent-meta.js`; `scripts/test-harness-contract.mjs` deep-compares the two, so a drifted mirror is a red test rather than a checkbox offering a flag the spawn will refuse). claude is the only harness with one — **gemini 0.33.2 does NOT have it** (0 hits in the package, correcting an earlier draft).

**The flag, dumped from `claude --help` on 2.1.257**: `-w, --worktree [name]` — "Create a new git worktree for this session (optionally specify a name)". We never send a name: the CLI mints a unique one, whereas a name of ours would collide with an existing worktree (two sessions in one tree) and would put a user string in argv for no gain. Measured layout (2.1.257 decompiled): `pCn(repo,name) = join(repo, '.claude', 'worktrees', name)` and the branch is `worktree-<name>` (`_de`), and the process **chdir's into it** during setup (`setup_worktree_ms` / `worktree_chdir:`), which is why the init frame's `cwd` is the worktree path.

**`--tmux` is NEVER emitted.** Its own help says "Create a tmux session for the worktree (requires --worktree)", and dtach is our persistence layer — a tmux inside our dtach session is a second multiplexer nobody attaches to. Owner ruling 9 spells this out; `test-remote-shell` and `test-harness-contract` both pin its absence.

**Three PURE rules, so no surface has to know the CLI's semantics:**
- `worktreeRefusal({backend, want, isGitRepo, hasWorktreeHook})` — the CLI exits 1 outside a git repo BEFORE the session exists ("Error: Can only use --worktree in a git repository, but `<dir>` is not a git repository. Configure a WorktreeCreate hook in settings.json to use --worktree with other VCS systems."), so ws-create refuses first, with `scope:'action'` (a session-scoped error flips live windows read-only — inc-mt2arppw). Both probes are **TRI-STATE**: `null` = "the probe could not answer" (unreachable host, timeout) and is NOT a refusal — the CLI speaks for itself. The CLI's real gate is `hook OR repo` (`if(!pX() && !await rh())`, `pX(){return fB("WorktreeCreate").length>0}`), so a definite hook RESCUES a definite non-repo; a preflight stricter than the CLI it protects is a false refusal. The asymmetry is deliberate: an UNKNOWN hook still refuses a KNOWN non-repo (there the alternative is the instantly-dead window this exists to prevent), and the message names the hook so a mis-detected hook user is told what to configure instead of hitting a dead end.
- `worktreeSpawnArgs({backend, want, resume, fork})` — **new ⇒ pass, fork ⇒ pass, plain resume ⇒ NEVER pass.** The CLI RECORDS the worktree on the conversation (`worktreeSession`) and re-enters it itself on `--resume` (reporting `worktree-gone` / "cannot resume into worktree …" when it cannot), while `--fork-session` explicitly STRIPS the binding (`eMe(se,{stripWorktreeSession:true})`). A second `--worktree` on a resume would create a SECOND tree.
- `worktreePick({saved, live})` + `worktreeLatchWrite({saved, live})` (round-2 verifier) — WHICH answer a surface gives to *"would the NEXT run of this conversation be isolated?"*. `saved` is **TRI-STATE**: `true` = the user asked for it, `false` = the user explicitly revoked it, `undefined` = **no pick on record**, which is the normal state right after a New Session tick (the conversation has no id yet when the box is ticked). An absent pick therefore defers to the LIVE run — which is exactly what the Session Properties checkbox has always displayed, so the checkbox and the fork now answer with one function instead of two paraphrases. `worktreeLatchWrite` is the ONE-WAY companion: only an ABSENT pick is ever written, and only to `true`. The client reaches both through `src/lib/agent-meta.js`, which re-exports the very same function objects (`test-harness-contract` asserts identity, not shape).

**The init frame is the ARBITER, in BOTH directions.** `src/server/stdout/claude-stream-json.js` reads the `system/init` record's own `cwd` — a typed record, never a path we compose from a naming rule we would have to keep in sync (and which a `WorktreeCreate` hook can put anywhere). Different from the launch dir ⇒ record `_worktreePath`. **The SAME** ⇒ the process is telling us it is NOT isolated (the CLI's own 'worktree-gone' path continues "in the current directory without worktree isolation. The worktree binding has been cleared.", and a resume can only re-enter a recorded worktree, never create one) ⇒ the live fact is retired, so the badge can never outlive it. Trailing slashes are cosmetic; nothing else is normalized, because a path we massaged is no longer the record the CLI gave us.

**Two fields, deliberately not one.** `session._worktree` = "THIS RUN is isolated" (server truth, arbitrated above, on the `active-sessions` payload and the `attached`/`created` payloads). The sidebar's per-session `cfg.worktree` = the standing PICK for this conversation, which a fork (and a restart from this config) asks for. `ChatView._latchWorktreePick` records the pick **ONE-WAY — it only latches ON, and only over an ABSENT pick**: letting a live fact the CLI corrected erase the preference would silently discard a user's choice because of a transient, and letting it overwrite an explicit `false` would overrule a decision with a fact. Session Properties shows both, apart.

**Round-2 verifier: the pick had no producer where it mattered most.** Three defects, all in the seam between those two fields:
- **A fork carried nothing.** `_doForkSession`'s `createSession({…})` had no `worktree` key at all, so `worktreeSpawnArgs`'s `fork ⇒ pass` branch was **unreachable in production** — the fork ran in the user's real working tree while Session Properties promised "Applies when a new session or a fork starts", and the suite pinned the branch with a call no site could make. It now resolves `worktreePick({saved: cfg.worktree, live: sessionInfo.worktree})` and passes it; `test-harness-contract` greps the FORK call site, not just the rule.
- **The pick could not express an untick.** `setSessionConfig`'s truthy whitelist dropped `worktree:false`, so unticking the box while the run WAS isolated re-checked it on the next render (an accept-and-ignore control, the 2.361.4 class) and a fork kept inheriting a revoked preference. It is now tri-state, like `autoResume`, and Session Properties writes the raw boolean.
- **The `worktree-path` client branch was a dead write.** It assigned `this._worktree` and nothing read it (`_applyLiveMeta` reassigns the field on the line above its only reader), while a grep pin asserted that assignment as "the saved pick LATCHES ON only". That branch is the FIRST moment a brand-new isolated session can record its pick — the box is ticked before the conversation has an id, the `created` payload arrives before the CLI has announced one, and the creator never gets an `attached` (2.368.4) — so it now runs the shared latch. Its body moved to the prototype (`ChatView._onWorktreePath`) precisely because a body inside the live-view constructor closure can be pinned by grep **and by nothing else**; `scripts/test-worktree-userchan-ui.mjs` drives it for real, with the pre-fix branch reproduced as a negative control.

**The preflight gates on the EMITTED decision, not on the tick.** `ws-create` used to run the git-repo probe whenever `data.worktree` was set, which refused spawns that would never have sent the flag: every resume/restart/resume-all of a conversation whose folder is not (or is no longer) a repo — including the B-7812 recreate-cwd path, which rebuilds the folder EMPTY — was refused for a flag `worktreeSpawnArgs` returns `resume-rebinds` for. That is the module's own comment turned against itself ("a preflight that is STRICTER than the CLI it protects is a false refusal"). The probe now runs iff `worktreeSpawnArgs({…}).pass`; the `unsupported` refusal stays UNCONDITIONAL, because asking a harness for a flag it does not have is a broken promise whatever the spawn kind. `test-harness-contract` drives the REAL handler (stub deps + a `buildSessionArgs` that throws a sentinel, so nothing is ever spawned) for all four cases and reproduces the pre-fix gate from the product source.

**Spawn flags (owner ruling 8(c), ALL default OFF, each mapped to ONE dumped flag).** `claude.brief` → `--brief` ("Enable SendUserMessage tool for agent-to-user communication"); the prompt-cache trio `claude.systemPromptSnapshot` → `--system-prompt-snapshot on|off`, `claude.excludeDynamicSystemPromptSections` → `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections`, `claude.autocompact` → `--autocompact auto|<100k–1M>` (compaction is what breaks the cached prefix — the CLI's own telemetry calls it `promptCacheBreak` / `isPostCompaction`). Each value is **validated against the CLI's own accepted vocabulary before it becomes an argv token**: a value the CLI would reject exits before the session exists, so an invalid/empty setting simply drops the flag. Spawn hygiene: these are switches and enums — nothing user-typed and no secret ever reaches argv.

**Claude Code's OWN auto-continue at a usage limit is spawned OFF (owner ruling 2026-09-22, 2.369.155; row `claude.autoContinueAtUsageLimit`, default false).** The 2.1.280 binary declares `autoContinueAtUsageLimit` in its settings schema (*"When a claude.ai usage limit stops your session, wait for the limit to reset and continue the task automatically. When off, the limit dialog offers the wait as a choice instead."*) and reads it through `D7(key)`, which walks `["policySettings","flagSettings","userSettings"]` — so the inline `--settings` JSON (flagSettings) IS a real layer for this key, a project/local settings file is NOT, and a managed policy value outranks us. Absent everywhere ⇒ ON (`SWt(e){return jmt()??e==="absent"}`) behind the GrowthBook flag `tengu_marble_heron` (`enabled`/`autoArm` default true when the flag is absent). There is NO env var and NO dedicated CLI flag — `--settings` is the only per-invocation door. **IT ONLY ARMS IN AN INTERACTIVE LAUNCH, SO WHAT THE SWITCH CHANGES IS PER MODE** (read by byte offset; a live wall is not reproducible under §ban-safety): both arm paths start `if(!ETe(t))return!1`, `ETe = ft() && billingType!=="usage_based" && sW(e) && lzr()`, `lzr = Wmt() && Dge()`, `Wmt = id() && !At() && !Ut()`, `id()` = `launchOptions.isInteractive()`, default false, set only by main from `Zrn(argv)` = `-p || --print || --init-only || --sdk-url || !process.stdout.isTTY` (@192668682). ① **CHAT**: every chat transport gives claude a pipe or a file for stdout (chat-wrapper `stdio:['pipe','pipe','pipe']`, the ssh keeper's fifo/file fds, the agentd pipe session) ⇒ non-interactive ⇒ the CLI's continue NEVER arms there, whatever the key says; src/server/auto-resume.js is the only producer and the flag is belt and braces against a later CLI. ② **TERMINAL**: pty-wrapper gives it a real pty ⇒ interactive ⇒ the CLI's continue WAS live — and it was the ONLY automatic continue there, because VibeSpace's auto-resume delivers through `sendChatInput` (server.js `sendToSession` returns false for `mode !== 'chat'`). OFF therefore leaves a terminal session STOPPED at a wall with the dialog offering the wait as a choice, and nobody continues it by itself. The owner's ruling keeps it off because the CLI's continue is a turn nobody typed that no spend ceiling bounds; the trade-off (off / scope to chat only / a VibeSpace-side terminal resume) is his to revisit through the row. So `buildSessionArgs` merges `autoContinueAtUsageLimit:false` into the ONE `--settings` flag on EVERY claude spawn (a flagSettings value also hides the CLI's own /config toggle) unless the row is ON (then nothing is passed); a missing settings bag counts as off; a user's own `--settings <file>` in extra args is never clobbered by this default and an explicit key in the user's inline JSON is kept. It rides every transport because it is in `args` (one `buildSessionArgs` call feeds local dtach/r6Argv and all five `buildRemoteExec` builders; both statusline injections merge). **NO DETECTION, BY DESIGN (2026-09-22 verifier):** the first cut journaled a `cli-auto-continue` spend event from `origin:{kind:"auto-continuation"}` — but 2.1.280 stamps that origin at TEN enqueue sites (plan-mode approval "Implement the following plan:", the ultraplan hand-off, `/goal` proposal approval, three dialog nextInput/shouldQuery enqueues, the reset-credit "You can continue now…" `vNe`) and only ONE is the quota continue `W()` (prompts `D` "Your claude.ai usage limit has reset…" / `F` "…usage is available again before the usage-limit reset…"), so every plan approval was journaled as "continued BY ITSELF after a usage limit"; and the stream consumers only see CHAT, the one mode where it cannot fire. It was removed rather than kept as visibility it could not deliver. A terminal-side carrier (a transcript scan of terminal sessions' JSONL for the `D`/`F` heads) is the open gap. Gates: test-fallback-policy §5 (argv legs, ON control, file/inline legs) + §5b (the per-mode PREMISE pinned: chat-wrapper piped, pty-wrapper a pty, sendToSession chat-only, the row's wording — each with a snippet control), test-remote-shell (every transport), test-harness-settings §3, test-stdout-registry + test-peer-command-card (the origin census over every source + plan/`/goal`/ultraplan shapes handed to nobody, a live-recorder control).

## src/msg-acl.js + src/server/conversation-deliver.js + data/bin/vibespace-msg (2.362.0 — Communication Channels v1)

**What.** Agent-to-agent messaging with Task-Group-scoped reach, built as the first channel of the owner's Communication Channels vision (external sources — Gmail/Lark/Slack — later feed the same ladder with their own `source` tags; every stash envelope already carries one).

**ACL (msg-acl.js, PURE).** Same group = mutual see+message (the default collaboration boundary). Outside: group `externalVisibility` (`none` default / `visible` / `messageable`, task-groups field + task-detail select) and a per-session `_msgReachability` override (schema-registered, meta-persisted, `POST /api/sessions/:id/msg-reachability`, widening ONLY). Levels rank none<visible<messageable; effective = max of grants; multi-group targets = union; ungrouped sessions are closed singletons. HONESTY: this is a coordination/attention boundary, NOT security — same-OS-user agents can always read transcripts and raw sockets; the native ListAgents/SendMessage tools still see the whole machine. Uniform not-found errors (no existence oracle).

**2.366.1 (published-pages.js) — the hosting layer.** `/p/<id>` is a SHELL (our own HTML on the real origin, no user content) that frames `/p/<id>/raw`, where the published HTML runs under the sandbox CSP (opaque origin; **never** `allow-same-origin`). Both routes share one `gate()`; the shell escapes the agent-chosen name. `/raw` injects a COMPAT PRELUDE (`COMPAT_PRELUDE`/`injectShim`, cached per snapshot): `crypto.randomUUID` polyfilled from `getRandomValues` — it is SECURE-CONTEXT-ONLY and VibeSpace is normally plain http on a hostname, which hung every canvas artboard forever (kb-bugfix-invariants: HOSTED PAGE NEEDED A SECURE CONTEXT) — plus in-memory `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` for the opaque origin; each only when genuinely missing. Share URLs: `urlFor(id, req)` = `agentd.publicUrl` → the ASKING request's Host → relative `/p/<id>`; nothing is remembered (the server cannot know about proxies/tunnels), agents get the path, and chat-renderers linkifies it against `location.origin`. **2.369.7 geo/storage bridge (B-74de, owner-directed via 生活方式助手's verified spec)**: the shell ships a per-request-nonce'd postMessage bridge (`script-src 'nonce-…'` added to the SHELL CSP only) forwarding a geolocation watch stream + `vp_<pageId>_`-namespaced localStorage into the sandboxed iframe. Protocol FROZEN (consumer pages ship it): `vibeBridge:'ready'{geo,store}` on iframe load / `vibeGeo:'start'|'stop'` → `'pos'{lat,lng,accuracy,heading,speed,ts}|'err'` / `vibeStore:'set'|'del'{k,v}`. Source verified (`e.source===iframe.contentWindow`), pages cannot read each other's keys, NO user content enters the shell (interpolations = ID_RE id + own nonce), and the red line stands verbatim — iframe never gains allow-same-origin, raw CSP untouched. Accepted trade-off: any published page may surface a geolocation PROMPT on this origin (browser still asks the user; per-page gating is the escalation path if that ever bites). Pins: test-published-pages (bridge presence, source-check+namespace, per-request nonce). **2.369.11 offline + blobs**: /p/sw.js service worker (location-capped scope /p/ — structurally cannot touch the app; network-first + 4s cache fallback, NOT cache-first — an online logged-out browser must never read a private page from cache) + vibeBlob protocol (IndexedDB vibespace-pages/blobs, `<pageId>:` keys, on-demand get — 10-30MB tile caches; vibeStore/localStorage stays for small values). Shell shows a 6s 'offline ready' badge when a cached copy exists.

**2.366.0 additions (published-pages.js).** `publishContent({html, name, srcKey, makePublic, sessionId, conversationId})` = the upload path (agent CLI / remote hosts; body in the request); upsert identity is `srcKey` (`local:<abs>` for file publishes, `<host>:<abs>` for uploads — legacy records get `local:`+srcPath on load); records carry `sessionId`/`conversationId` (`list({sessionId})`, `GET /api/pages?sessionId=`); `onPublished(page, {replaced})` is the ONE notify point (server.js broadcasts `page-published` to the session's clients) for dialog AND agent publishes; `noteBrowserOrigin(req)` (every management call) teaches the server the browser's origin (`x-forwarded-*` first) so `url` is absolute when `agentd.publicUrl` is unset — relative `/p/<id>` stays the honest fallback and the client joins it with `location.origin`.

**Delivery (conversation-deliver.js).** ONE ladder for jobs notifications AND agent messages (jobs-wiring's inline twin deleted — the 2.361.5 lesson: delivery topology must have one home): ① channel socket (experimental) ② local CLI inbox (peer-messaging findPeer/postToPeer — peer-messaging is now a SHARED-tier module, the daemon bundles it) ③ the OWNING machine's daemon via the `peer-post` agentd op (capability-gated three-touch; conversation-index.ownerHost names the machine — raw conversation uuids are the ONLY address, agents never learn topology) ④ durable stash `data/msg-stash.json` (cap 30/conversation, debounced atomic write) drained at the conversation's next context injection — machine-agnostic because remote sessions' hooks call back to the hub anyway. **2.368.26 rung ①.5 — registry lane `rpc-queue`** (between ② and ③, local only): when `capsOf(backend).peerDelivery === 'rpc-queue'` (codex; NEVER a backend-id branch — src/backend-caps.js is the registry) AND the wrapper's OWN sidecar adverts `caps.peerMessage` (2.361.1 law: gate on what the process wrote; negative verdicts never cached — stateless read per attempt), deliver writes a `peer-message` stdin frame to the live wrapper. The wrapper owns the app-server RPC connection: idle ⇒ `turn/start` (billed turn + reply, claude-inbox parity), busy ⇒ `thread/queue/add` (runs right after the current turn — upstream-test-pinned, codex 0.149 source). The frame carries `fromName`+`cardText` (P1, design-harness-plugins §1); the wrapper records the peer user message itself WITH a `webui_peer:{name,body}` marker (item notifications never carry `userMessage` ⇒ no double render; the codex normalizer renders that record as the LABELLED peer card live and on rebuild — marker-blind twin dedup, see codex-message-manager.js) so this rung does NOT emitPeerCard (an in-memory card on top would double-render live, and a stdin write is not yet a delivery); it reports `peer_message_result` both ways (ok:false echoes text+fromName) and ok:false makes session-stdout re-stash the echoed text with its label — a promised message is never lost. Old wrapper / claude session / no sidecar = honest miss falling to later rungs. Gate: scripts/test-peer-delivery.mjs (19 — functional real create() + sidecar + negative controls + the 2.355.0-class WIRING pins, incl. the recordCodexQuotaSignal dead-wiring fix this work uncovered). **2026-09-07 — THE FRAME CARRIES A TYPED ORIGIN, and it is the ladder's ONLY new job.** `deliverToConversation(cid, text, {kind})` resolves `kind` to `'notification'` (VibeSpace itself speaking: jobs.js `_deliverTo` stamps every owner/subscriber notification, and system notices join it) or `'peer'` (a person's message via `POST /api/agent/msg/send` — and the DEFAULT for absent/unknown, so an older caller can never silently change lane), puts it on the rung-1.5 stdin frame and echoes it in the result. It does NOT pick the lane: only the WRAPPER knows whether a turn is running right now, so the decision lives there (codex: busy notification ⇒ `turn/steer`, busy peer ⇒ `thread/queue/add`, idle ⇒ `turn/start`). The reason is an owner incident: a codex session had accumulated **20** "[VibeSpace Background Work] … done" items as 20 separate queued submissions = 20 billed turns waiting behind the one it was running ("系统通知默认应该是steering的" → "按照TUI实现吧"). WHICH lane a harness takes at all is DERIVED from its own capability row — `backend-caps notificationDelivery({peerDelivery, inputModes})` → `steer` (rpc-queue + a `steer` verb) / `queue` (rpc-queue without it) / `cli-inbox` (claude: its CLI queues a mid-turn delivery itself; that lane is the CLI's) / `stash` — the same derivation law that makes `inputModes.steer` a VIEW of `queueVerbs`, so "notifications steer" is never declared in a second place and never a backend-id branch. The client mirrors `peerDelivery` next to `inputModes` in BACKEND_META and derives through the SAME pure function (`notificationDeliveryFor`), which is what Session Properties → Background Work states in words. **jobs.js is UNCHANGED apart from the tag**: the 30s per-conversation flood floor and the `pendingNotifs` stash stay, and they are what makes a burst ONE frame — only the first distinct event is posted, the rest are stashed, and the stash is drained by the injection routes (agent-routes SessionStart + prompt-context) as ONE rendered block (`job-model renderNotifStash`) riding the conversation's next turn; it is never handed back to this ladder entry by entry, which is exactly how a batch would become N queued messages again. Gate: scripts/test-peer-delivery.mjs (44 — the derived lane table incl. a hypothetical rpc-queue-without-steer row, the client-mirror drift check, frame tagging + unknown/absent normalisation, and the wiring pins for jobs/msg-send/session-props/codex-events) + test-jobs-engine (the floor→stash→ONE-block drain leg) + test-codex-p2-wrapper ②f (the wrapper-side lanes against a real stub app-server).

**The old-wrapper skew (B-d963, 2.369.164 batch 7).** The rpc rung's notification lane is the HARNESS's (`notificationDelivery(capsOf(backend)) === 'steer'`), but the running wrapper may predate it: a codex wrapper started before 2.369.63 adverts `inputQueue` and NO `queueVerbs` list (the owner's sess-13 sidecar: `{peerMessage, frameFile, threadScoped, inputQueue, responseStyle}`), ignores the frame's `kind` and answers a notification with `thread/queue/add` — a BILLED turn after the running one (the owner saw two queued). The ladder now reads the process's OWN advert before the write — `wrapperCaps().notificationSteer` (an explicit verb table naming `steer`; the notification steer and the verb table shipped in the same release, so that table IS the proof — never a version number) — and, when a turn is running and the advert is missing, writes nothing and returns the TYPED miss `{ok:false, lane:'rpc-queue', refused:'wrapper-no-steer', reason}`; the hold goes back in the one `finally`. Every notification producer already stashes a miss, so this IS the stash rung: jobs types it `held.kind:'wrapper-no-steer'` (job-model `HELD_KINDS`; the panel says "restart this session"), channels and the browser handback `stashFor` it; the next prompt's injection drains it and the drain site renders its chat card (`emitPeerCard`). Unchanged on purpose: an IDLE old wrapper still gets the frame (it opens a turn either way, exactly as a new wrapper does), a person's `peer` message still queues (its own turn by design), and a wrapper that names `steer` is written and settled as before. Gate: test-peer-delivery (the sess-13 caps verbatim, busy/idle/peer/new-wrapper/no-sidecar, hold returned, `heldKind`, the panel sentence) + test-spend-paths' rpc fixtures now carry the current wrapper's caps (`CURRENT_WRAPPER_CAPS`).

**Routes/tool.** `/api/agent/msg/peers` + `/api/agent/msg/send` (vsst_; integration master switch gates; 30s per-pair floor + 10min dup dedupe + 16KB cap — a delivered message opens a BILLED turn on an idle receiver, the intro/manual/CLI all teach this). CLI `vibespace-msg list/send`; manual `docs/agent/msg-manual.md` (`vibespace-docs msg`). Incoming messages render via the existing peer-message card (origin.name → 2.361.6).

**Delivery-site card rendering (2.363.0).** Server-posted injections reach the CLI as an UNREGISTERED poster → the CLI records origin {kind:'peer',from:'unknown'} with no name/msg_id/body, so neither the JSONL rebuild nor result-mining can attribute or even display them. The ladder therefore renders the receiving chat window's peer card ITSELF on every ok lane (`emitPeerCard` dep from server.js → session normalizer `injectPeerCard`; opts.fromName/opts.cardText on deliverToConversation carry the label + raw body). Stash drains (agent-msg ×2 + job-notifications ×2 sites in agent-routes) emit the same card at injection time. injectPeerCard is deliberately containment-free — the delivery site posts once per fire, and same-body repeats are legitimate (the 2.362.2 review lesson).

**Agent groups (2.369.159, design §22).** `send <agent>` no longer hands the peer a turn: it posts into the pair's TWO-MEMBER group (found or created, symmetric) and each receiver's notify mode decides — the default is a report on its next USER turn at no cost; `--wake` / an @name is a billed wake through this same ladder. `vibespace-msg` grew `groups`, `read <group> [--before]`, `group create|invite|leave|kick|rename|archive|notify` and `send <group>`; the legacy direct delivery stays for a server without the groups engine. **The ladder now stamps `s._machineInputAt` on the live local session at every rung that hands it a frame (`machineTurn()` inside `spent()` and the predicted-free steer branch)** — auto-resume's continue stamps it too (server.js `sendToSession`), and ws `input`/`chat-input` stamp `_userInputAt` — so prompt-context can tell a machine-started turn from the owner's and hold the group reports for the latter (`turnIsUserInitiated`).

**The CLI, g2 (2.369.159 — data/bin/vibespace-msg + docs/agent/msg-manual.md).** Verbs: `list`, `group list` (= `groups`), `read <group> [--before <ts>] [--limit n]`, `send <group|agent> "…" [--wake]`, `group create|invite|leave|kick|rename|archive|notify`. **Every wake is ECHOED as a count** — `woke 2 agents = 2 billed turns: a, b` (create/invite: `invitees`), said at 0 too (`--quiet: woke 0 invitees = 0 billed turns`), a refused wake `(not billed)` with the authorizer's reason, the free next-turn receivers named. **Typed refusals**: `vibespace-msg: refused [<code>] — <server words>`, every `candidates` id on its own line, then `→ <remedy>` from the CLI's REMEDY-by-code table; exit 1 on any refusal (a non-2xx with no body included, a code-less 429 = `rate-floor`), 2 outside a session, 3 server unreachable. Names resolve SERVER-side; an ambiguous one is refused `ambiguous` WITH the candidates, never guessed. **The job fence**: under `VIBESPACE_JOB_TOKEN` (no session token) the CLI speaks as the job's OWNER conversation — list / group list / read / send only; a membership verb is refused LOCALLY with `job-token` before any request (the routes refuse it too). Dependency-free (ships to hosts). The manual's `## Groups` section is the owner's words (explicit groups, DM = the pair's group, notify modes and what each costs, invite context, `read --before` for history, the wake echo); the index line names groups. Gate: scripts/test-msg-cli-groups.mjs (fast, 82: the CLI against a stub + the routes over the REAL engine/store/ladder + the words, each with its control). r1: a floored wake prints as a refused wake `(not billed) — <name>: rate floor …` like the authorizer's; no CLI change was needed. **r2: `--yes`** (send / group create / invite ⇒ `yes:true`) confirms an act the server refused `confirm-wakes` (more than 5 wakes — the refusal prints the count and the REMEDY: nothing was sent, `--yes` only if worth that many billed turns, or drop `--wake` / add `--quiet`); the usage names the 5-wake confirmation and the 8-per-minute pace; the manual says both, the cut-line pointer and the named-only turn.

**Invariants.** Delivery topology stays in ONE module — any new notification-shaped feature consumes conversation-deliver, never scans registries itself; ACL changes stay in the PURE module with matrix tests (scripts/test-agent-msg.mjs, 41); the per-session override only WIDENS; stash envelopes always carry `source`; message VISIBILITY is owned by the party that has the information — when the transport strips attribution, the POSTER renders the card.

## src/otel-truth.js + src/server/otel-ingest.js (2.361.0, B-345b 终案 — the per-request billing-TRUTH stack)

**Why it exists.** Pool hot-switches do NOT take effect inside a RUNNING claude process — repointPoolSymlink's utimes trick invalidates the CLI's mtime-gated credential cache only for NEW processes / token expiry; a live CLI kept billing the OLD org ≥25 minutes after being switched away (forensic case: 79928a2b, 6 auto-switches in 35min, old org climbed 35%→95% and rate-limited FROM that session while attribution said three other orgs; 558 mid-session switches / $7.9k post-switch spend in 12 days). Link-intent attribution therefore mis-books storm spend in both directions, poisoning per-org odometers AND rate learning (the ≥10pt burst calibration residual of -30~-49% — six alternative mechanisms tested and REFUTED: walker gaps ($0 diff vs raw transcripts), reading lag (storm-level residual doesn't cancel), training censoring (73 big pairs in-set), output share, family mix, cw5/cw1 mix, per-request overhead, unresolved-host exclusion).

**The channel.** Transcript records, statusline payloads and rate_limit_event all carry quota VALUES but never identity (verified field inventory, CLI 2.1.235). The CLI's built-in OpenTelemetry export is the ONLY per-request source that NAMES the org: every `claude_code.api_request` log record carries organization.id + user.account_uuid/email + request_id (the ledger's rid) + model + all four token classes + cost_usd; prompt content is redacted upstream. Base endpoint + `/v1/logs` path semantics verified empirically.

**Data flow.** ws-create's r6Env IIFE injects OTEL_* env into LOCAL claude spawns (gate `!session.host && backend==='claude' && otelEnv()`; a user-set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT in the session spec wins; process-env channel — the PERSISTED token (data/usage-history/otel-token, 0600; per-boot would silently 403 sessions surviving a restart) rides OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS, never argv).   **A POOL IS NEVER A SPENDER IN THE ACCOUNT DIMENSION (2026-09-07 r3, reproduced).** `_acctAt`'s last resort is session-meta's `accountId`, which is the SPAWN identity — and for a pooled session `resolveForSpawn` returns the POOL's own id, so the fallback baked `acct:'pool-…', atype:'pooled'` onto ledger events: a pseudo-account that holds no credentials, double-counted against its own members, in the per-account totals. server.js states the invariant verbatim at the OTHER site that reaches this decision ("an unresolvable pool target falls to GLOBAL, never to the pool id itself"); `_nonPoolAcct` applies it here, on BOTH the ordinary scan and the r2 emptied-sid re-bake. Which MEMBER it was is deliberately not guessed — this fallback only runs for a conversation with no attribution entry at all, exactly the case the repair could not place from the transition ledger either, so global is the honest answer and the `pool` tag (now also derived from meta on the scan path) keeps the per-pool total correct. `_poolIdOf` has TWO legs on purpose: the injected `resolveAccount` maps `backend === 'codex'` to one type BEFORE `a.type` is read, so it reports a CODEX pool as `'codex-subscription'` and the type test alone misses every one — the minted id shape (`'pool-' + randomBytes(6).hex`, one call site in accounts.createPool) is primary, the type is the belt, and each leg has a test that fails without it.

### login-expiry.js / server/login-expiry-watch.js (2026-09-07 — the LOGIN SESSION's own deadline)

  src/login-expiry.js — PURE (imports nothing; the daemon and the browser bundle can both carry it). THE FACT, measured on this instance: a Claude subscription's `data/subs/<id>/.credentials.json` carries `claudeAiOauth.refreshTokenExpiresAt` = the ABSOLUTE end of the LOGIN SESSION, and it does NOT move when the access token refreshes (a member refreshed 30 min earlier still showed an expiry 17 h out while siblings showed 5 and 16 days). Past it the CLI's refresh gets `invalid_grant`, prints "Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed", and BLANKS accessToken/refreshToken/expiresAt while KEEPING refreshTokenExpiresAt + scopes — that wiped shape is what "logged out" looks like on disk (three members were in it when this shipped). `loginState(creds, now)` → `{state: 'ok'|'expiring'|'expired'|'logged-out'|'unknown', refreshExpiresAt, accessExpiresAt, msLeft}`: EXPIRING_MS = 24 h (the chip + the first warning), NEAR_MS = 30 min (a SWITCH TARGET must outlive the switch). **'unknown' means NO CLAIM and every consumer must treat it as "do not block"** — missing/garbage fields are unknown, NEVER 'ok' (claiming health we cannot read is how the old behaviour surprised people); an oauth record with no tokens AND no residue is also unknown, because `{}` is what a Console /login wipe writes and it is not evidence of an expiry. Predicates: `loginUsable` (dead = expired|logged-out), `loginSwitchTarget` (dead OR inside NEAR), `loginRank` (0 ok/unknown · 1 expiring · 2 near · 3 dead — the LAST tiebreak, never a reordering of what quota separates), `loginBlockReason`/`loginBucketLabel` (the SPEAK rule's named bucket), `loginBlockedPhrase`/`loginBlockedText` (round 2 — how a notice SAYS a blocked member: each one states its own fact, `A (login expired), B (signed out), C (login expires in 20 min)`, because round 1 wrote one sentence over a list mixing all three and reported a member with 20 min left as expired), `loginWallPhrase` (round 3 — how the CURRENT member's own dead login is said inside a sentence that has already named the account: a CLAUSE, `Member F's login session expired` / `Member F's login is signed out`, where `loginBucketLabel` is a LIST-ITEM label. It exists because round 2 had no output for that fact at all and put the label into `deadBuckets`, where the notice renders it as a spent quota bucket), `reviewWarnings(info, entry, now, opts)` = the once-per-member-per-threshold transition (a DIFFERENT refreshTokenExpiresAt is a re-login ⇒ the old ledger is dropped; a SKIPPED rung fires the most urgent one and marks the rest done — a stale "expires in 24 h" filed when 40 min are left is worse than silence). **ROUND 2 — the terminal rung had no staleness gate.** The ledger loads empty on a fresh install, so the FIRST sweep after the upgrade filed an `urgent` "For you" item for every login that had ever died: three on the instance this was measured on (dead 15 h, 116 h and 700 h, none of them a routing member), i.e. the feature opened on a red blinking badge about accounts abandoned weeks ago. `opts.watchingSince` (the ledger's own birth, persisted as `since`) makes a death that happened BEFORE we were watching AND is older than `STALE_GRACE_MS` (= EXPIRING_MS, one day) a PRE-EXISTING CONDITION: recorded as done, `suppressed: 'pre-existing'`, never spoken — its surface is the permanent red chip in Manage Agents, not an event inbox. BOTH clauses are load-bearing: a death inside the grace is still news on a fresh install, and a death AFTER `watchingSince` is one WE missed (server was off), which is the whole promise. The FUTURE rungs (24 h / 1 h) are untouched — a coming death is always news. A logged-out record with no readable deadline cannot be dated, so it is never suppressed (firing is the fail-safe direction). Omit `watchingSince` and the gate is inert (pinned with a control). **RECOVERY (2026-09-07): `reloggedIn(info, prevExp)` — did a REAL new login session start?** Three clauses, each load-bearing: the login must be ALIVE again ('ok'/'expiring'), because a wiped file KEEPS its deadline and that deadline can be in the FUTURE, so "the number went up" alone reads a signed-out account as recovered; there must be a readable deadline now (a live token with no deadline is 'unknown' = NO CLAIM, and no claim never overrides a warning filed from a fact); and the deadline must be DIFFERENT from the recorded one — a session's deadline is fixed for its whole life, so a change can only come from a new session, while a REWRITE that keeps it (an access-token refresh, a creds file copied between machines, an import) is the SAME session and nothing may be retracted. Deliberately NOT "strictly newer": an org with a short SSO policy hands back a deadline that can be EARLIER than the one we warned about (warned with 20 h left, the new session is 12 h long), and a `>` test leaves that now-false item open forever — the same defect one scenario over. Retraction cannot lose a deserved warning either way, because the ladder re-arms on the new deadline in the SAME sweep. `prevExp == null` with a live deadline now IS a re-login (the recorded row was the un-datable wiped shape). `SHORT_SESSION_MS` (36 h) + `shortSession(spanMs)` back the session-policy hint: a MEASURED login session under 36 h is not how Claude subscriptions normally behave (the deadlines here were 5, 9, 12 and 16 DAYS out) and looks like an org SSO policy — never true for a missing measurement.
  src/server/login-expiry-watch.js — the PASSIVE sweep (create(deps) factory; server.js starts it in ONE wiring line). Boot+5 min (the 1 h rung needs a cadence well under an hour — the oat sweep's 6 h would sail past it), reads the account roster + each subscription's credential file through `accounts.loginStateOf`, and files at most THREE "For you" inbox items per login: 24 h (normal) / 1 h (high) / expired (urgent), each naming the ACCOUNT and the EXPIRY TIME. **`itemTextFor` branches on the login's STATE, never on the RUNG (round 3).** `warnStageFor` maps BOTH 'expired' and 'logged-out' onto the terminal 'expired' rung — the rung answers "how urgent", the state answers "what happened". A WIPED credential file is produced by any unrecoverable refresh (a revoked or rotated session, an explicit logout in an isolated dir), not only by the deadline passing, and the CLI KEEPS `refreshTokenExpiresAt` when it blanks the tokens, so that deadline can still be in the FUTURE: round 2 filed an `urgent` item reading `Claude login for "Member F" expired 2026-09-27 20:01 UTC` — a past-tense claim about a date 20 days out — while `loginExpiryChipHtml`, which DOES branch on the state, said "login signed out — re-login" on the same row. Two surfaces, one record, opposite claims. (Every wiped dir on this instance happens to have a past deadline, which is why the fixtures never hit it — they inherited the local sample, not the shape.) The wiped shape now reads "is signed out — the CLI cleared its tokens", with `(its login session ended <t>)` appended only when the deadline really has passed; the `detail` carries the deadline beside `State: <state>`, in the tense the number earns ("ends" vs "ended"). Ledger `data/login-expiry.json` (atomic tmp+rename), carrying `since` = when this ledger started watching ⇒ a restart replays nothing, a re-login goes silent, and the upgrade day does not open on a screen of urgent items about logins that died before the feature existed (round 2; the grace is spent exactly once because `since` is persisted). A REFUSED inbox write (the 20-open-per-key cap) rolls the rung back so the next sweep retries — marking it sent would be the no-silent-failures violation this feature exists to fix. Items land in the `accounts` inbox bucket (like jobs' `jobs` bucket); user-todos-panel jumps them to Manage Agents. **§ban-safety: file reads only — no vendor call, no probe, no token ever touched.** **RECOVERY — a filed item is a CLAIM, and the thing that filed it must RETRACT it (2026-09-07, measured here).** Dropping the ledger row on a re-login only silences FUTURE filings: the owner re-logged two members (fresh tokens, a deadline 29 days out) and the "For you" panel still listed `Claude login for "Member F" is signed out — the CLI cleared its tokens…` as OPEN, forever, until someone ticked it off by hand — while the chip on the same row had already gone green. The member row now carries `items: [{id, text}]` (the ids of what THIS watch filed for THIS deadline, persisted — a server that restarts between the warning and the re-login must still be able to retract, or the bug is back with an extra step), and a `reloggedIn` transition resolves each of them through `userTodos.setStatus(id,'done','system')` — the store's OWN path, so it saves AND broadcasts and every open client updates live — then journals ONE line, `X: re-logged in — N warning(s) cleared`. Three things it must never do, each with a negative control: **reopen or re-resolve an item the USER already handled** (any item that is not `open` is dropped from the list untouched), **touch an item filed by anything else** (it only ever acts on ids from its own ledger, and re-checks `sessionKey` + text before writing — an agent's vibespace-ask item in another session is invisible to it), and **treat a credentials rewrite with the SAME deadline as a re-login**. `resolvedBy: 'system'` is neither 'user' nor 'agent'; the panel's resolved tail labels it `automatically`, because an item that vanishes on its own must say it vanished on its own. **THE IMMEDIATE SWEEP:** the poll is 5 min, which is a long time to keep staring at the item about the login you JUST fixed, so every login FINALIZE route (`/api/accounts/:id/relogin-finalize`, `/api/accounts/subscription/:id/finalize` — placed ABOVE the auto-merge branch's early return, so both exits sweep — and the codex device-auth finalize) sweeps when the login actually succeeded. server.js keeps the handle and passes it as `getLoginExpiryWatch`, a lazy getter like every other late singleton. **ROUND 2 — the gate has to be the answer the method actually gives, and a POLLED route may not carry an unbounded side effect.** (i) Round 1 gated the re-login route on `r.loggedIn`, a property `accounts.reloginResolve` returns on NONE of its four outcomes — it answers `{outcome:'pending'}`, `{outcome:'same'|'split', account}` or `{outcome:'moved', movedTo}`, so the captured login rides in a NESTED `account` and 'moved' has no account at all. The sweep was therefore DEAD on the exact route the inbox item and the login chip send the user to, and the suite was green only because its fixture invented that shape (the §5b fixtures are now CAPTURED from a real `reloginResolve` call against a temp store, so the method's shape cannot drift away from them). The gate is `!!r.account?.loggedIn || r.outcome === 'moved'`: 'moved' relocated a live login into ANOTHER record, whose ledger row is the one to retract; 'pending' stays silent. (ii) manage-agents polls `/relogin-finalize` every 3 s for up to 5 minutes and 'same' repeats, so a side effect hung on the answer runs ~100× (measured: 100 polls → 100 sweeps). The route sweeps only on the TRANSITION — `sweepOnLoginTransition` compares the answer's CREDENTIAL FINGERPRINT (outcome + record + identity + access-token expiry, all read off the answer the route already has, so it is NOT a second credential reader) with the last one it swept for. Deliberately not a boolean 'already swept this account' latch: re-logging a STILL-logged-in account answers 'same' from poll #1, minutes before the browser flow finishes, so a latch would skip exactly the sweep that matters. (iii) The Add-flow finalize sweeps AGAIN, right after a successful `accounts.mergeSubscription`. The sweep above `fin` runs while the fresh credentials are still in the THROWAWAY record's dir; the survivor — the record carrying the open warning — still has its dead file, so that sweep reads a stale deadline and retracts nothing. `mergeSubscription` is the moment the survivor's file changes. The pre-merge sweep stays because it is the only sweep on every non-merge exit, and because the sweep is idempotent (pinned). **ONE READER:** the sweep asks `accounts.loginStateOf`, which is exactly what the roster row's `loginState` — the chip — is built from, so the chip and the inbox cannot disagree about the same file and there is no second credential reader to drift; the failure is logged, never thrown (a login must not fail because a follow-up sweep did). **THE SESSION-POLICY HINT** on the 24 h / 1 h rungs: when this member's last login session was MEASURED under 36 h, the item adds `(its last login session lasted only ~24 h — this org's session policy may be short)`. The measurement is the load-bearing part. The naive predicate — deadline minus the credential file's mtime — reports a healthy 30-day login as a 20-hour one, because every access-token refresh rewrites that file while `refreshTokenExpiresAt` stays put; at the 24 h rung on an actively-used account it is < 36 h essentially always. So `measureLoginSpan` only trusts the mtime when the login was WITNESSED: an OBSERVATION LOG (`seen`, one row per subscription written every sweep, deliberately separate from the sparse warning ledger — a healthy member has no warning row, and that is precisely the member whose next login we need to have witnessed) confirmed this member ≤3 sweeps ago, the deadline has CHANGED since, and the file was written after that confirmation. That pins the login write to a window one sweep wide. Nothing witnessed ⇒ nothing said; and a recorded span shorter than what is still LEFT of the current deadline is stale, so `itemTextFor` drops it too. It says "may be": one session of one member is evidence about a policy, not a reading of it. `src/harnesses/claude.js` is the only place that touches the file, and it reports `writtenAt` = the mtime alongside the pure verdict. Gate: scripts/test-login-expiry.mjs (255, incl. a fake-clock ladder, restart survival, the re-login retraction end to end against the REAL UserTodoManager with every negative control, the routes factory driven with a stub express app so the lazy getter is proven to resolve at request time, §5b's fixtures captured from the real `reloginResolve`, the 100-poll transition measurement, and §5c which drives the REAL AccountManager + UserTodoManager + watch through the REAL routes and asserts the inbox EFFECT — a call count cannot tell you the sweep found anything, which is how round 1's merge leg stayed green — plus a REAL 375×667 headless-chrome measurement of the chip).

### user-todos.js

  user-todos.js        — **2.369.157 ACTION PAYLOAD (design-reset-credits §5): `add({…, action})` takes a producer's `{type, …flat facts}` validated by `normalizeAction` (kebab `type`, ≤ 12 flat fields of string ≤ 200 / finite number / boolean / null — never nested, never markup; the CLIENT maps `type` to a verb it owns, the payload only names WHICH session/account); a re-file merges a changed action. First producer: the reset-credit rung's ask mode (`type:'reset-credit'`); the agent route never forwards it.** UserTodoManager (2.65.0, the GLOBAL user-facing TODO list / "For you" inbox): discrete items an AGENT filed that need the USER (decision/input/review) — the inverse of the agent's own TodoWrite. One item = one owning session (sessionKey like session-status, webui:→backend rekey in the agent route); data/user-todos.json (session-status persistence pattern: debounced 500ms + content-compared + exit flush); add() idempotent BY TEXT across ALL statuses (open → refresh; resolved/dismissed → REOPEN the SAME id — review finding: fresh-id minting let an add→resolve loop or a dismissed-text re-file toast-spam every client despite the open cap); caps: 20 open/session (add throws with guidance), 1000 total (oldest RESOLVED pruned, open never); resolveByAgent by id or unique text substring (own session only); snapshot() = {open: urgency-then-newest sorted, resolved: last 15}; 'user-todos-updated' broadcast on every change. Client = src/lib/user-todos-panel.js. KNOWN LIMIT: webui:→backend rekey happens on the agent's NEXT call only (same as session-status) — in practice unreachable since vibespace-ask runs mid-turn when the backend id already exists. Client review fixes (do not regress): jump falls back to attachSession for a live session with NO open window (goToWindow is a no-op then); resync fetch on ws reconnect (items filed while offline stayed invisible); setStatus checks r.success (fetchJson never throws); knownIds includes the resolved tail (reopen must not self-toast). Panel detail+origin (2.69.1): item detail renders behind a collapsed `.ut-detail-exp` expander (open AND resolved rows — inline 2000-char details swamped the list); resolved rows carry the source session name (`.ut-sess`) and row-click jumps like open rows; clicks inside the expander are guarded from the row's jump-and-close. **WORDS AS STRUCTURE (a3 r4, 2026-09-21):** `add()` accepts `i18n = {text:{key,params}, detail?:[{key,params}…], source?:{key}}` (normalized: keys ≤ 400, params strings/numbers only, a bad shape throws by name; updated in place on a re-file like `detail`) beside the English `text`/`detail` — those stay the dedupe key and the agent CLI's contract; the CLIENT words `i18n` with its own t(). Producers: the channels engine's pointer / access request / unknown outcome / failure headline (`i18nKey(…)` literals the extractor censuses).

**KIND (2.369.118, owner: spend notices are DISTRACTING beside real asks).** An item carries `kind: 'action' | 'notice'` — `add()` validates it (`KINDS`), defaults to `action`, and updates it on a re-file; older items have no field and read as actions. It is a PRODUCER's declaration, never inferred from text: spend-guard's `fileInbox` says `notice`; `vibespace-ask --notice` reaches it through `POST /api/agent/user-todo add.kind`; login-expiry, channels and jobs stay actions (each needs a hand). The client splits on it (user-todos-layout `isNotice` / `splitNotices` / `badgeCounts`): notices sit in their own section under the asks with the same append-only slots, and never colour the badge (a grey count).

**EXPIRY (2.369.152, "SPEND NOTICES LIVED FOREVER AS ACTIONS").** An item may carry `expiresAt` (ms epoch). `add()` takes it through `validExpiry` — a finite number in the FUTURE, anything else (past, NaN, a string) is IGNORED as null, never a throw and never an item dead on arrival. A re-file into an OPEN item keeps the LATER end; an open item with NO `expiresAt` is lasting and a re-file never makes it expire; a re-file that REOPENS a resolved item is a new filing and takes the new end or none (the old one is past). `expireDue(now)` resolves every OPEN item whose `expiresAt <= now` — status `done`, `resolvedBy: 'expired'`, `resolvedAt: now`, the record kept — never an item without `expiresAt` (expiry is a producer's declaration, never inferred from age or text) and never an already-resolved one; ONE `_save()` + ONE broadcast per sweep, returns the count. The manager runs it at the END of construction (an item that expired while the server was down goes at boot) and on its OWN `setInterval(EXPIRY_SWEEP_MS = 5 min)`, `unref()`ed — server.js has no shared sweep cadence other stores hook into (each keeper runs its own); `stop()` clears it; `expirySweepMs: 0` builds a manager with no timer (a migration's private manager, suites). A user REOPEN (`setStatus('open')`) clears `expiresAt` — the user said it still matters. `reshapeItems(fn)` is the store's door for a one-shot reshaping: server.js hands the LIVE manager to migrations.js because it holds data/user-todos.json in memory and a second writer beside it would be overwritten by its next save. Panel: a notice row's meta says `expires in {n} min` / `{n} h`; a resolved row says `expired`. Gate: test-user-todos-expiry (every leg beside a patched-copy control).

**Round 3, A2 (2.369.166 — the app's exit closes the window, the outer ✕ is the app's own close; docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless.md §3.2):** three PURE decisions + one constant. `windowsLeftCount(rows)` = the windows a person could still see after the app process exited — mapped (`false` excludes, `null` = unknown counts), ≥ 16×16 (a WM's 5×5 helper, a 1×1 leader are not windows), on screen (xfwm4 parks its helper at -1000,-1000). `exitCloseVerdict(rec, {leased})` → `{close, why}` decided ONCE per window at the record's arrival in a terminal state: `failed` stays (its red sentence is the one place the error is said), an agent lease keeps it (`lease`), any stop closes (`stoppedBy` set ⇒ `stopped` — VibeSpace tore the display down on purpose, D2d), an exit closes unless the keeper's census found a window LEFT (`windowsAtExit` > 0 ⇒ `windows-left`: a forking launcher exited while its child still shows one; 0 / absent ⇒ `exited`). `outerCloseVerdict({state, stream, seat, connected, mainWid, leased, askedAt, now})` → `{act: 'close'|'ask-app'|'stop', why}`: not ready ⇒ close; a second ✕ within `OUTER_CLOSE_AGAIN_MS` (5000) of an ask ⇒ stop (even with no main window left — the app closed its window and kept running); the rfb rung (no per-window protocol), an agent lease, a blocked / Watch pane, no main window ⇒ close (today's pane-only close); otherwise ask-app. A clock that went back is not "again". Gate: test-desktop-apps §12 (the census table, 14 exit rows, 16 outer-✕ rows, wiring pins on the keeper / the window / WindowManager / every user close).


**B-bfe6 — A BROWSER AS A DESKTOP APP (2.369.166, owner 2026-09-23 "应用里面也可以加入一下浏览器"; docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md §7.7):** a desktop-app browser is a HUMAN'S browser — a registry exec (§5, never an agent's), on the xpra per-window rung like every app, with its OWN profile the app session owns; never an agent-browser profile (those live under data/browser-* and are driven over CDP by the Browser profiles keeper, design-agent-browser-v2 §3) and never the user's real ~/.config/chromium / ~/.mozilla. `BROWSER_KINDS` = the two families `chromium` (execs chromium → chromium-browser → google-chrome) and `firefox` (firefox → firefox-esr) with the label per binary ("Google Chrome", "Firefox ESR"); `BROWSER_BINS` their union (desktop-display probes THAT list). DEFAULT_REGISTRY's `chromium` / `firefox` rows carry `browser` + `execs` (the old rows were a bare `chromium` exec and `firefox --new-instance` with NO profile — the user's real default profile, or a hand-off to their running Firefox). `validateAppRow`: `browser` a known family, `execs` bare names on a browser row only, and a browser row may NOT carry a profile or automation flag (`isForbiddenBrowserArg`: --user-data-dir / -profile / -P / --remote-debugging-* / --remote-allow-* / --enable-automation / --headless / --marionette / --start-debugger-server / --load-extension …, refused `automation-flag`). `browserRowFor(row, bins)` → the first `execs` name `bins` has becomes the served `exec`/`path`/label, else `browser-absent` naming every candidate. `validateBrowserUrl(v)` (the dialog runs the SAME function): http/https only, no whitespace/control char, ≤ 2048, parsed to its href, else `bad-url` with the why. `profileDirVerdict(dir, {home, ownedRoot, confinement, exec})`: absolute and INSIDE `ownedRoot` (the keeper's data/desktop-apps — so an agent-browser dir or a `..` escape is `profile-not-owned`), not $HOME and not inside `REAL_BROWSER_ROOTS` (deb / snap / flatpak profile roots, `profile-is-users`), and for a SNAP binary inside $HOME under a non-hidden first segment (a snap sees a private /tmp and no ~/.hidden — `snap-profile-unreachable`). `browserArgv(row, {profileDir, url})` = the row's own args, THEN chromium `--user-data-dir=<dir> --no-first-run --no-default-browser-check --password-store=basic` / firefox `--new-instance -profile <dir>`, THEN the URL (one argv item; an http(s) href never starts with '-'). `firefoxUserJs()` = Firefox's first-run switch (it has no --no-first-run): user_pref lines the keeper writes into the profile. `validateLaunchRequest`: `url` / `keepProfile` (boolean) ride a BROWSER row's launch; on any other row or a typed command they are refused `not-a-browser`, never ignored; a bad URL `bad-url`. Gate: test-desktop-apps §11.


**HiDPI + the app's minimum (2.369.158, docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md §7.6; the owner's 2026-09-23 GNOME Calculator report on a devicePixelRatio-2 screen):** `APP_SCALES` [1, 1.5, 2]; `normalizeDpr` (a finite 1..3, else 1); `appScaleFor(setting, dpr)` (`desktop.appScale`: auto/unset = 2 from a DPR of 1.5 up, else 1 (r2 — never the text-only 1.5, below), an explicit '1'|'1.5'|'2' wins, anything else 1); `scaleKnobs(scale)` → `{scale, gdkScale, dpi, env, xresources}` — the MEASURED rule: GDK_SCALE = the integer part (doubles GTK3 AND GTK4 exactly), the display's font dpi = 96 × scale / GDK_SCALE (Xft.dpi MULTIPLIES with GDK_SCALE — 192 + GDK_SCALE=2 = 4× text), GDK_DPI_SCALE never (GTK4 ignores it, GTK3 would double-count the fraction), QT_ENABLE_HIGHDPI_SCALING=1 + QT_SCALE_FACTOR=<integer part> (unmeasured — no Qt app here), and at a scale > 1 `XTerm/UXTerm*faceName: Monospace` + `faceSize: 8 × GDK_SCALE` (xterm's bitmap default no dpi reaches). `validateLaunchRequest` carries `launch.dpr` and REFUSES a dpr outside 1..3 by name; `newRecord` stores `scale` (default 1) + `dpi` (default 96). Gate: test-desktop-apps §10.

**r2 (the verifier, measured): 1.5× IS TEXT ONLY FOR GTK.** X11 GTK has no fractional GDK_SCALE, so 1.5× = GDK_SCALE 1 + fonts at 144 dpi: GNOME Calculator's minimum is 360×616 device px at 1× AND at 1.5× (720×1232 at 2×) — on a DPR-1.5 screen that is a 240×411 CSS pane, keys at 0.67× their 1×-screen size. `auto` therefore picks 2 from a DPR of 1.5 up (widgets 1.33× on a 1.5 screen, 1.14× on 1.75) and 1 below (0.8× on 1.25) — the nearer integer scale in ratio; 1.5× stays an explicit choice, labelled t('1.5× (text only in GTK apps)'). Consequence, stated: an app with a tall minimum at 2× on a small 1.5 screen (a 1080p laptop at 150 %) does not fit and is shown scaled to fit with the badge — pick 1× there. Gate: test-desktop-apps §10 (the table + the pre-fix nearest-0.5 rule as the control).

**Round 3, A3 (2.369.166 — the scale DERIVED from VibeSpace's own scale, per window; docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless.md §3.4):** `effectiveScale(dpr, uiScale)` = dpr × the UI scale (the body zoom — the pane is counter-zoomed to net zoom 1, so before A3 a 125 % UI drew a 1.0× app beside 1.25× chrome, M4), clamped 1..`SCALE_MAX` 3. `appScaleFor('auto', dpr, uiScale)` answers the TEXT scale by the ratio rule: below √2 as is, √2..2 ⇒ 2, 2..2√2 as is, above ⇒ 3 — so a screen of 1.5 or more never gets the text-only 1.5 (r2's invariant, kept); an explicit 1 / 1.5 / 2 is returned as given. `scaleKnobs(s)` takes ANY 1..3 and spells it by the floor rule: GDK_SCALE = floor, the rest in the font dpi (96 × s / GDK_SCALE) — 2.5 ⇒ 2 + 120 dpi, 1.25 ⇒ 1 + 120, an explicit 1.5 ⇒ 1 + 144 (text only in GTK, as ever). `scalePick({setting, choice, dpr, uiScale})` → `{scale, origin: auto|setting|chosen, from}` (a relaunch's `choice` wins; its `auto` re-derives from the RELAUNCHING client). `validateLaunchRequest` carries `uiScale` (0.6..2 = the product's own `UI_SCALE_MIN/MAX`, else refused by name); `newRecord` keeps `scale` (1..3, two decimals), `scaleOrigin`, `scaleFrom`. The per-window relaunch: `SCALE_CHOICES` (auto, 1, 1.5, 2), `validateRelaunchRequest`, `relaunchVerdict` (ready + the xpra stream + not a browser, each refusal a code), `relaunchBodyOf` (a catalog row by id, a typed command as typed), `scaleMenuModel(rec, {dpr, uiScale, leased, seat})` (the rows, which one is current — not offered again unless auto would now derive something else — and one reason CODE disabling all: the relaunch verdict, `lease`, `seat`). `exitCloseVerdict` answers `relaunched` + `replacedBy` FIRST — a replaced record never closes its window. Gate: test-desktop-apps §13 (the design's table + the √2 / 2√2 boundaries, uiScale-absent = the .158 answers on DPR 1/1.5/2 as the regression control, the refusals, the menu model, wiring pins on the keeper / the route / the launcher / the window); §10's r2 auto table moved to the new thresholds with its invariant kept.

### src/server/desktop-app-keeper.js — THE DESKTOP-APP LIFECYCLE (§2 row 3)

**Round 3, A2 (2.369.166 — docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless.md §3.2): THE WINDOW CENSUS AT AN APP EXIT.** `onPartExit('app')` still flips the record to `exited` at once (`fail`), then ONE census while X is still up — `windowsLeftAtExit(rec)`: `enumerateWindows` on the record's OWN display (null on the shared singleton, with no display, or when the census fails or outlives `EXIT_CENSUS_MS` = 2000 — a warn names it) through `seamlessWindows` (xpra) or `M.appWindows` (the other rungs) into `M.windowsLeftCount` — stamped as `rec.windowsAtExit`, THEN the teardown, THEN the commit that broadcasts it. So every client decides "the app exited ⇒ close my window" from the same keeper fact (a blocked pane has no protocol windows to count). MEASURED (xpra 6.5.3): xpra keeps a managed app window inside a Corral wrapper that is MAPPED only while a client is connected — with no client the forking launcher's surviving xterm read viewable=false, so on the xpra rung the census counts the seamless rows' EXISTENCE (`mapped: null`), elsewhere X's viewability. A stop records no census (`stoppedBy` is the fact the window closes on). **KEEPALIVE + A NAMED CLOSE (2.369.118, userW inc-mu3lmd4s-dmwf).** `bridgeRfb` pings every `pingMs` (`PING_MS` = 20 s; `create({pingMs})` for tests), marks the peer dead after two silent rounds and terminates it with the reason `no pong for N ms`; it logs `bridge opened → 127.0.0.1:<port>` and ONE close line per bridge — `closed (<who>) after <s>s, <down> B to the browser, <up> B to the server` where who = the browser's code/reason, `the VNC server closed its socket`, a socket error, or the ping timeout. `stats()` unchanged. The singleton Desktop window (desktop-window.js) now passes `autoReconnect: true` like the app windows. Gate: test-desktop-stream-keepalive.

### src/routes/desktop-apps.js — THE DESKTOP ROUTE FAMILY (§2 row 5)

**B-bfe6 (2.369.166):** `POST /api/desktop/apps {appId, url?, keepProfile?}` — the keeper's browser refusals map to 400 (`bad-url`, `not-a-browser`, `automation-flag`, `profile-not-owned`, `profile-is-users`) and 409 (`browser-absent`, `snap-profile-unreachable`); a launch-request refusal now keeps the PURE verdict's own code instead of a blanket `bad-request`.


**HiDPI + the app's minimum (2.369.158, docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md §7.6; the owner's 2026-09-23 GNOME Calculator report on a devicePixelRatio-2 screen):** `POST /api/desktop/apps` passes the body through to the keeper unchanged — the new `dpr` field (the launching client's devicePixelRatio, 1..3) is validated by the PURE `validateLaunchRequest` (400 bad-request `dpr must be a number from 1 to 3`); the record view carries `scale` + `dpi`.

**x5 (2026-09-22):** `GET /api/desktop/apps/:id/viewers` (the `desktop-app-viewers` payload) + `POST /api/desktop/apps/:id/viewers/takeover {viewerId}` = RESUME HERE: the viewer's socket must be open (`stream.viewerAlive`, else 409 `no_viewer` in words); with an agent's lease on the window it is the ENGINE's human takeover (a hold by ANOTHER human moves with `holderAlive:false` — `decideTakeover` then grants without a handback, so nothing is announced and no turn is billed), then `keeper.takeoverViewer`; answers `{ok, already, viewers, lease}`. The P9b `POST …/takeover` also makes the taker the ACTIVE viewer (and answers `viewers`).


  **P9 (2026-09-21):** the keeper gained `x11EnvFor(id)` — the x11 env a process ADDRESSING a record's display gets (the same rule as the app's own: `x11Env` over the sanitised base, the per-app Xauthority for an owned display, the singleton's cookie file for a shared one; null before the display exists) — the window-targets engine's one way to point xdotool / the screenshot helper at a keeper display.

  **P8-2 chunk x1 (2026-09-21):** `GET /api/desktop/apps/:id/windows` → `keeper.windows(id)` (the on-demand window snapshot; 404 not-found). THE HOSTED UPSTREAM CLIENT (D21 (c) (a), the validation slice): `GET /api/desktop/:id/xpra-ui/` and `/xpra-ui/*` serve the installed xpra's html5 client (`keeper.xpraWww()`) behind the app-level cookie middleware every /api route sits behind (server.js mounts `auth.middleware()` before any router), through `express.static` with `index:false, redirect:false, dotfiles:'deny'` + `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` + `Cache-Control: no-store` on every answer, `..`/dotfiles/NUL refused before the static handler; the BARE dir REDIRECTS (302) to `index.html?path=/api/desktop/<id>/stream&sound=false&printing=false&file_transfer=false&remote_logging=false&autohide=true&reconnect=true` — the client concatenates `ws://<host>` + `path`, and its `getstrparam` FILTERS a value to `[0-9A-Za-z _+-:/]` (an id is `[a-z0-9-]` by construction; a query on the path would be stripped, which is why netem is remembered server-side); a record whose stream kind is not xpra answers 409 `not-xpra`, no www tree 503 `xpra-ui-unavailable`; `?netem=…` on the bare dir is handed to `stream.setNetem(id, spec)` and echoed in `X-VibeSpace-Netem` (`disabled` when the gate is off). Driven by the slice's driver against a worktree server (index 200 nosniff, `js/` 404, `../../../etc/passwd` 404) and by chunk x1's boot smoke.


  routes/desktop-apps.js — thin over the keeper: GET /api/desktop/apps (registry + availability per row, live sessions, the ladder with reasons, the cap, the idle default), POST /api/desktop/apps (`{appId}` | `{exec, args?, cwd?, label?}`), GET /api/desktop/apps/:id, POST …/:id/stop, POST …/:id/keep-alive, and the singleton's GET /api/vnc/status · POST /api/vnc/start (moved from server.js, answers unchanged). **P9b (2026-09-21): the user's side of a window lease** — `GET …/:id/lease` → `{id, origin, lease|null, idleMs}`, `POST …/:id/takeover {viewerId}` (the live view's own id — the one it put on its stream upgrade; 400 without it) → `{ok, already, lease}`, `POST …/:id/handback {viewerId?}` → `{ok, cause:'explicit', heldMs, byHolder, lease}`; decided by the window-targets engine (`setup({keeper, vnc, windowEngine})`; 503 `no-engine` without it), refusals typed at 409: `held` (another viewer drives), `not_taken` (nobody does), `no_lease` (no agent holds it — the user's input already reaches it). EVERY route takes `host` (query or body) and REFUSES a non-local one by name (400 `unsupported-host`) — `hostId` is a parameter, never a silent local fallback; every failure answers `{error, code}` with a status by code (404 not-found; 400 bad-request/exec-not-found/cwd-missing/needs-wayland; 409 cap/runaway-parked/no-backend/backend-not-wired). fetchJson never throws, so a 200-with-nothing would be a silent failure of a user action. **x3 (2026-09-22):** every route above driven on a real server with cookie auth (test-desktop-xpra); `PATCH /api/settings` takes `desktop.idleTimeoutMin` / `desktop.backendPrefs` live — both are read at launch (a running app keeps what it was born with). **2.369.156:** the hosted upstream page (`/api/desktop/:id/xpra-ui/`) is a read-only WATCH viewer — its socket names no viewer (the upstream page strips `?`/`=`/`&` from its `path`, so it cannot carry one) and an anonymous socket is never elected (LOW-3); the product's own window is the driving surface.

scripts/test-desktop-xpra.mjs — THE XPRA RUNG ON A REAL SERVER (P8-2 x3, 2026-09-22; heavy, ~50 s, no chrome — the chrome half is test-desktop-xpra-window): boots a worktree server with `VIBESPACE_PASSWORD` (so the relay's 401 is a real gate), starts the real xpra through `POST /api/desktop/apps`, and speaks xpra from node through the product's own bridge — the upstream `Protocol.js` framing (8-byte header, flags 16 = rencodeplus, raw chunks re-attached by index) over the INSTALLED client's `rencode.js` / `lz4.js` / `brotli_decode.js` loaded with `vm.runInThisContext` (ONE realm — a separate vm context would hand back foreign Uint8Arrays), the hello with compression declared OFF so packets arrive plain (the decoders stay wired).
