### clerk-auth.js

  clerk-auth.js        — ClerkAuth (2.103.0, env-gated: VIBESPACE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY = on-switch, frontend-API host + JWKS URL DERIVED from the key's base64 payload; VIBESPACE_CLERK_ALLOWED_EMAILS comma list, @domain = whole domain, EMPTY = reject all). verifyToken = pure node:crypto RS256 vs cached JWKS (1h TTL, unknown-kid rotation refetch, exp/nbf ±60s skew, iss check, alg pinned to RS256). REQUIRES an email claim in the token — Clerk dashboard: session-token custom claims {"email":"{{user.primary_email_address}}"} or a JWT template named 'vibespace' (login page tries template first). No Clerk SECRET key anywhere — the backend only reads JWKS

### agent-routes.js

  agent-routes.js      — setupAgentRoutes() (2.93.0 split): every agent-facing endpoint — vibespace-ask/status/task routes, task-context/prompt-context injection (incl. user preamble + per-turn extras), stop-check nudge arbiter. Injection ORDER + SIZE are load-bearing — read the renderContext notes before touching payloads. TEACHING ARCHITECTURE (2.111.22-25, user-driven): the injected tools section is a DISCOVERY layer — per tool one trigger sentence + one fenced COPY-READY complete invocation (status sample carries --reason+--detail+--urgency; progress/ask carry --detail) so the first copied call is already valid; syntax/edge cases live in each CLI's own no-args output; hard rules enforce at point of use (waiting-state reason+detail rejection, success-output reminders). Don't grow the upfront block back into a rules dump (2.68.0 oversize incident is the other guardrail). **GROUP UPDATES DELIVER AS DIFFS (2.113.0, user request):** a mid-session group change no longer re-injects the whole group context — the session keeps a per-group SNAPSHOT of what it last saw (`s._groupSnap`, set at every delivery next to `_groupSeenAt`/`_ctxSig`; in-memory, restart ⇒ full re-delivery like the seen markers) and prompt-context injects a `<vibespace-task-update>` DELTA block (tasks.renderContextDiff: renamed / objective / backlog PARKED-RESOLVED-DROPPED-CLAIMED-UNCLAIMED-reworded-REMOVED one-liners (2.122.0; since 2.123.0 matched by the stable item id — occurrence-indexed text pairing retired — and TARGETED: `sessionKey` filters events to items the session created or claimed, everyone else keeps only the count pointer) / contextDir files updated-new-removed via old-vs-new `_ctxSig` / new activity entries LAST; ~5KB hard cap with tail-first truncation + `show --full` pointers; EMPTY diff = a no-op edit ⇒ nothing injected, markers still advance — the old code re-sent everything for those too; checklist deltas REMOVED with the feature in 2.121.0). No snapshot / setting `agents.contextUpdateDiffs` off ⇒ the old full "was UPDATED" payload. Also: FIRST-TIME groups on one prompt get ONE layered renderMultiContext (the codex first-prompt path) instead of N full payloads each repeating the ~2.3KB tools section — but ONLY when they cover the WHOLE membership (renderMultiContext states absolute membership; a subset call told a 3-group session "belongs to 2" — partial sets render per-group, count-free). REVIEW-HARDENED invariants (10-finding adversarial pass, do not regress; the checklist occurrence-indexed-diff one retired with the feature in 2.121.0): contextDir set/changed/cleared ⇒ diff returns null ⇒ FULL fallback (structural — the file index + folder conventions must be taught, a one-line path left pre-existing files invisible); the TASK.md pointer renders for LOCAL sessions only (remote ctx rsync excludes `.vibespace/`); contextDirSignature escapes `%`/`|` in paths (raw `|` sheared parse entries → wrong-path reports); **N CHANGED GROUPS COLLAPSE INTO ONE COMBINED BLOCK (2.113.1, user directive twice-clarified — 穿插/layered, the 2.68.0 class):** stacked per-group `<vibespace-task-update>` blocks + the ~2KB persisted-preview truncation could hide the very FACT that a 2nd group changed — `renderContextDiffMulti` (fed by `diffChanges`, which returns {lines, bits} where bits = phrase summaries like '3 new activity') renders ONE block whose HEADER line enumerates EVERY changed group + its summary, then per-group `##` sections SMALLEST-FIRST, 6.5KB cap with tail-first truncation (details die, the enumeration never does); ANY multi-block delivery (diff block + full re-deliveries + new-group fulls) is manifest-headed — `<vibespace-delivery-note>` naming EVERY block by group + the persisted-output rescue, diff block first, fulls last; combined parts >8KB with no rescue line get one prepended; markers/snapshot advance at RENDER, so a harness-dropped delivery (hook 3s timeout) stays lost until `show --full`/restart — ACCEPTED, same class as the seen-bump loss window. Tests: scripts/test-context-diff.mjs (store) + scripts/test-prompt-context.mjs (route, fake express) **BACKLOG NUMBERS (2.369.154 r2): `backlogListingShown` (`${key}|${gid}` → the open ids GET task served, in order; in memory, 1000-entry bound) is what a numeric ref in task-backlog's `findIdx` resolves against (never the store order, `openOnly:false` widens only id/text matches; no listing yet ⇒ the live sortBacklog order; out of range / gone / already-resolved ⇒ refused by name); done/drop echo `item` by id; `liveClaimPredicate()` feeds every renderContext/renderMultiContext call (gate: test-backlog-priority §3b/§4b).** **`renderMsgStash` is PER-SOURCE (2026-09-16, the comm-panel P4 verifier): a `channel` / `channel-receipt` stash entry is a producer-budgeted §7.5 block rendered WHOLE (re-clipping it to 400 chars lost every hit after the first while the engine had already cleared them as "durably stashed"); the section is walked newest-first under `MSG_STASH_MAX_BYTES` (6144) / 6 entries and what does not fit is handed back as `rest` and RE-STASHED with its own ts for the next drain — never dropped; cards are emitted for the shown entries only; the hint names vibespace-channels for a channel entry. Exported for the gate: test-channels-engine ⑥ (f′).** **BACKLOG CLEANUP NUDGE (2.369.154): `POST /api/agent/task-backlog`'s add / edit / claim — the verbs that can grow what the caller holds; never done / drop / unclaim (they shrink it) or show (writes nothing) — compute `backlogNudge(updated.backlog, key, {threshold: nudgeThreshold(serverSetting('tasks.backlogNudgeAt'))})` AFTER the write and answer `nudge: {text, owned, stale, threshold}` beside the normal payload; `text` = `nudgeText` with the `--group <gid> ` prefix when the request named a group. Gate: test-backlog-nudge §2 (every-verb and never-reads-the-setting controls).** **EVERY TURN + ONE INLINE CAP (2.369.154 r2, verifier: the nudge rode only full context injections, and N per-group paragraphs pushed a 2-group CJK SessionStart to 10.8 KB — wrapped): prompt-context computes `tasks.backlogNudgeFor(ids, key, {multi, tools})` over the injected groups whose FULL context this prompt does NOT already carry (`fullCovered` = updatedFulls + the first-delivery groups — the codex first prompt carries it exactly once) and puts the ONE paragraph inside the per-turn `<vibespace-reminder>` body (after the tools line; the reminder is never suppressed by it) or, on a turn that already delivers something, as its own `<vibespace-reminder>` block; `tasks.backlogNudgeAt` 0 or the task tool off ⇒ nothing. `capInline(ctx, multi)` (module scope, `INLINE_CAP` 9600) is the ONE inline cap BOTH hook payloads pass — task-context had none, so a 3-group SessionStart with CJK backlog text was 12.8 KB. Gate: test-backlog-nudge §3b (pre-fix route + forgotten-coverage controls) / §3c (no-cap control).**

**Agent groups (2.369.159, design §22 D2).** prompt-context appends the NEXT-TURN GROUP REPORTS LAST — `groupsEngine().reportsForTurn(cid, {budget})` with the budget = `min(GROUP_REPORT_BUDGET 4096, INLINE_CAP − the bytes the rest of this delivery took − 64)`, so `capInline` never trims it — and ONLY when `turnIsUserInitiated(s)` (`_machineInputAt` not newer than `_userInputAt`; no stamps = a user turn); `commitReports` advances only the groups handed out. `/api/agent/msg/send` routes a group / an agent target through the groups engine (`resolveGroup` first, else `sendToAgent`), 10 min dedupe + one `wake` per target per 30 s; `/api/agent/msg/groups`, `/read`, `/group {op}` are the group verbs, the caller always its own conversation id. The tools intro's msg line teaches groups + the free default + `--wake`. **r1 (2.369.159):** the section is pushed — and its marks committed — only when it fits WHOLE (`used + 2 + section ≤ INLINE_CAP − 64`), else nothing is committed and it waits (a journal line says so); `send` resolves its target ONCE (`ge.resolveTarget`: a name that is a group AND a session ⇒ `ambiguous`), keys the 10-min dedupe by the RESOLVED target, and paces EVERY wake through `wakeFloorFor(myCid)` (one per (sender, member cid) per 30 s — @mentions, `--wake`, invites alike; floored wakes come back in `refused`, the message still posted; the old code-less 429 for `--wake` is gone); with a groups engine present a sender with no conversation id is refused 409 `bad-member` — the pre-groups direct lane runs only when there is no groups engine. **r2:** `wakeFloorFor(cid)` now RETURNS the groups engine's persisted `pacerFor(cid)` (the module-level `_wakeFloor` Map is gone — it forgot every floor on a restart, and a refused wake consumed its slot) — 30 s per pair + 8 per sender per minute; every send / create / invite also carries `consent: agentConsent(body.yes)` (`G.consentVerdict`: more than 5 wakes without `yes:true` ⇒ 409 `confirm-wakes` with `wakes`, nothing posted); `groupAnswer` passes `wakes` through.

**`msgCaller` (g2).** ONE caller resolution for every `/api/agent/msg/*` route: vsst_ = the session as its own conversation; jbt_ = the job's OWNER conversation (`job.owner.conversation.id`, its live session lending Task Groups to reach; unknown token 401 `auth`, jobs engine not ready 503 `unavailable`, no owner 409). A job may `peers`/`groups`/`read`/`send` — `send <agent>` with `sendToAgent({create: !who.job})`, i.e. only into an EXISTING pair — and every `POST /group` op is `403 job-token` (`JOB_NO_MEMBERSHIP` says what a job may do); the no-engine legacy lane refuses a job. `groupAnswer` carries `candidates` through; an `ambiguous` GROUP name returns before the session lookup (it would otherwise answer a misleading `unreachable`).

### server/usage-probe-log.js

server/usage-probe-log.js — THE RAW /usage PROBE LOG (2.369.109, owner 2026-09-17 "我建议你以后把最近一段时间的所有的/usage的raw返回结果和对应的parse结果保存起来方便debug"): `appendProbeLog(dataDir, rec)` / `readProbeLog(dataDir, {limit, key, rung})` / `machineOauthAccount(home)` over `data/usage-probe-log.ndjson` (rotates to `.1` at 8 MB — two files ≈ days at the auto-cli cadence; a panel is 1–3 KB, stdout clipped at 32 KB, stderr at 8 KB, always with a visible marker). ONE line per probe from the two allowlisted producers: the PANEL rung (usage-routes.js `refreshViaCliPanel`: `{rung:'panel', key, name, credsDir, argv, machineOrgBefore, machineOrgAfter, exitCode, ms, rawStdout, rawStderr, parsed, outcome: written|write-refused|no-buckets-parsed|spawn-failed|account-removed, why, window}` — `credsDir` is the function's ONE derivation, shared by the spawn and the log, test-readings-attribution §7) and the CONTROL rung (usage-pool-engine.js `probeUsageForAccountKey` / `probeUsageViaSession`: `{rung:'control', key, name, sessionId, sessionKey, raw (the verbatim control_response payload, stashed by the stdout consumer on the pending entry before it resolves and looked up through `_vsuRawOf`), parsed, outcome: written|refused-by-window-guard|timeout|unparsed, target, window}`). `machineOrgBefore/After` = `~/.claude.json` oauthAccount {email, orgUuid, orgName} read around the spawn — the ONE input the panel probe does not control and the mechanism of B-855a (the probe returns whichever org the last CLI process cached there; measured 2026-09-17: PandyMax 15 of 50 panel reads in 24 h carried another member's window, Natural Max 22 of 47, B-Stack 14 of 43 — the members the pool parks on), so a foreign panel is diagnosable from the log alone. Reader route `GET /api/usage/probe-log?key=&rung=&limit=` (read-only). Secrets never enter it (the panel text carries no token; env VALUES are not recorded). Gate: scripts/test-usage-probe-log.mjs (32: the ring, the panel rung through the REAL setupUsage with a fake claude, the control rung through the REAL engine, wiring pins). **B-855a c1 (2026-09-17): a panel record ALSO carries `configDir` (the isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR the spawn was given), `configOrgBefore/After` (that dir's oauthAccount around the spawn — the seeded value is OUR statement; only a CHANGE the CLI made to it is evidence), `identity: {org, phase, expected, panel, matched, apiWindow}` and `identityVerified`; `outcome:'write-refused'` with a `why` naming BOTH identities is the identity gate's refusal (the proof after c1: no `written` record carries a panel identity ≠ the account's own).**
server/usage-pool-engine.js — the pool/billing engine. **2.369.157 r5 — the round-4 verifier's medium + four lows (test-codex-pool §R15 r5/§R14c r5/§R17b r5/§R19c r5, each beside its pre-fix control):** ① **A RESTATED WALL IS DECIDED BEFORE ANYTHING IS WRITTEN** — `restatedResetWallTry(key, R)` = the identity's try with outcome `reset` inside the 10-min floor whose stated reset EQUALS the record's (0 = none on both sides); the `task_failed` branch asks it FIRST and returns with a `restated wall of the re-opened event` journal line: no `writeSnap` (the synthesized spent mark was newer than the open post-reset reading and re-marked A), no hold release, no ladder — a third conversation whose turn was in flight when the credit landed moved the pool off the account the credit had just re-opened and cold-restarted every follower, with or without the hold; the rung's own same-event check reads the same predicate (strict: a record stating a different reset, or one the try did not state, is a new wall). ② **A HELD MEMBER THE POOL NO LONGER LISTS IS NEVER CONTINUED** — codex has no login reader (no `creds.loginState`; `memberLoginState` is claude-only), so a narrowed-out / wiped held member read healthy at its reset and got one automatic continue; `quotaVerdictFor` now answers `usable:false, blockedUntil:0` for it (after the walled check — the arm keeps A's own reset until then). ③ **THE MANUAL USE THROUGH A CARRIER WHOSE COLD RESTART IS IN FLIGHT IS REFUSED BY NAME** — `restartPending` carries `inFlight:true` (a request went out, `restartInFlight`) ⇒ preview/POST `code:'restart_pending'` (409); `pending:true` (the pool moved, no client asked yet) ⇒ allowed; a not-in-flight carrier is preferred. **2.369.157 r4 — the round-3 verifier's major + two mediums + four lows, each reproduced with its recipe on this real engine first (test-codex-pool §R14c/§R14d/§R15 r4/§R17b/§R19b/§R19c, each beside its pre-fix control):** ① **THE HELD MEMBER IS JUDGED DIRECTLY** — `quotaVerdictFor` builds a held session's member list from `accounts.get(heldId)`, never `poolMembers` (a held member the pool no longer lists — narrowed, or its login file wiped while the process keeps its in-memory tokens — left an EMPTY set, `usable:null` "pool has no members", and the pre-fire gate let null through: a billed continue into the process still holding walled A); an empty held set is `usable:false`; the gate refuses a held verdict that is not a positive `true`; `sessionBillingMember` validates a held member with `validateHeldSlot` (a known subscription of the pool's harness — membership and login state are not asked) so the process's own wall DEMOTES it instead of `slot-not-a-member`. ② **THE VENDOR'S `reset` IS THE FACT UNTIL A READING SAYS OTHERWISE** — `holdForResetReading` PROBES the identity at once (`probeQuotaForKey`, the leader's own app-server) and again at 30 s, holding pool decisions until a reading ENDS it (`resetReadingEndsHold`: newer than the attempt AND the leader's own or one the verdict calls usable — a sibling's stale spent push is journaled and ignored), a new wall on that identity ends it (no force), or its 10-min ceiling (`RESET_HOLD_MAX_MS`) lifts it WITHOUT a forced decision (r3 forced a re-decide on the wall's pre-reset mark at 30 s and left the re-opened account); `claimColdRestarts` is the manual routes' twin (their response IS the request); census: one payload builder in the engine. ④ `poolMemberOfSessionFor` no longer memoizes `unknown` (one unreadable ledger read pinned a process unknown for life) and PERSISTS a ledger answer into the session-meta (`persistHeldStamp`: `heldPoolMember` + `heldPoolOrigin:'ledger'`). `requestHeldRestart(session)` (onWalledTurn's `finally`, after the pool eval) re-asks ONE client to cold-restart it onto the pool's member — at most once per 10 min per session, `_heldRestartAskedAt` stamped by EVERY `pool-auto-switched` send that actually went out (default switch, per-session switch, auth-failure evict) so a request in flight is never doubled (a double resumes the conversation twice); the wrapper now emits the re-read FIRST (the hold is the fallback for wrappers still running old code). ③ **ONE RULE FOR WHICH MEMBER A POOL PROCESS SPEAKS AS** — `heldPoolMemberFor` delegates to `accounts.poolMemberOfSession` through `poolMemberOfSessionFor` (a LEDGER answer is memoized onto the session as its stamp with `_heldPoolOrigin:'ledger'`; an `unknown` one is memoized too — both final); the default switch no longer re-attributes held followers (server.js's resolver reads the same rule). ④ **`held-unknown`** — `creditIdentityFor` → `{key, current, moved, unknown}`; the auto rung refuses an unknown holder by name and `resetCreditCarriers` skips it (no person's credit either). The rule is "any top-level object carrying `utilization`/`used_percentage` that is not five_hour/seven_day/extra_usage/seven_day_oauth_apps is a model cap" — which would MISFILE the credit-program keys the 2.1.280 envelope carries (`cinder_cove`, and `cedar_ember`/`juniper_tide` if they ever carry a utilization) as an exhausted model cap. **identityMismatch semantics (2.337.3, owner confusion report):** `_usageGlobalLink.email` comes from the GLOBAL ~/.claude.json oauthAccount — a field EVERY relocated dir login also stamps (CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR relocates only the secret store; the 2.244.2 consequence). After any Manage-Agents account login the config identity is therefore residue, NOT the machine login. The token-derived orgEmail/orgUuid is the truth and drives display + linking. The UI treats the mismatch as an informational note (residue explanation, "no action needed") — NEVER as a warning telling the user to /login (that advice would trigger a needless real global login switch).

### incident.js

  incident.js          — FREEZE THE SCENE for a panic-button capture (2.239.0, the admin's correction: users troubleshoot their own problems — ssh/resume/kill — and destroy the evidence before anyone looks). captureLocal: process table, dtach socket stats, VERBATIM copies of session-meta + wrapper-meta (clobbered by every create/kill), claude lock files (deleted on CLI exit), and per referenced conversation the transcript IDENTITY (size+mtime+**sha256**+frozen 512KB tail — a later manual `--resume` double-write/fork becomes provable). captureRemote: one bounded probe per machine over hosts._hostShell (ssh AND dial) — remote process table, locks, keeper/agentd state, transcript stat+sha256+last timestamps, project dirs, disk, CLI versions. ALL read-only + bounded (child processes with timeouts — never node fs on a possibly-hung mount, §2.108.3; ≤6 hosts, ≤12 conversations, size-capped copies) and per-step try/caught so a dead host degrades the bundle instead of failing it. Runs ASYNC after the id is returned; `env.json.pending` marks a cut-off freeze. Test: scripts/test-incident.mjs (16 asserts incl. frozen-copy-survives-clobber). **B-8ebb (last row, codex rollouts in the freeze):** the transcript-identity loop no longer knows only claude's project dirs — after the claude scan it iterates the HARNESS REGISTRY (`require('./harnesses').list()`, lazy) and asks each `store.locate(cid)` where its conversation lives: codex rollouts (`rollout-*-<tid>.jsonl` / `.jsonl.zst`, the local tree or the remote-jsonl cache) get the same size+mtime+sha256 identity + frozen tail (`<cid>__<dir>.tail.jsonl[.zst]`, `harness:'codex'`, `compressed:true` for a .zst whose raw tail bytes are the evidence, not lines); claude's locate dedups against the scan. The remote probe is generated the same way — `buildRemoteTranscriptProbe(cids)` emits one `find <root> <findExpr> | probe_transcript` line per (conversation × harness) from each descriptor's `store.remoteFind(id)` (claude's expression byte-identical to before, codex's `$HOME/.codex/sessions … rollout-*<id>.jsonl(.zst)` added; `probe_transcript` is one shell function; `lastts` greps with -a for compressed bytes) and the versions line asks codex too. Never a backend id branch in incident.js — a third harness freezes by registering a store. Test: scripts/test-incident.mjs (+8: a codex rollout in the cache is fingerprinted + tail-frozen + tagged, the claude conversation still freezes once, remote probe lines per harness, no id branch).

**TERMINAL TAILS (2.369.118, userW's login-terminal report froze the wrapper sidecar only).** `captureLocal(dir, {dataDir, cids, terminalIds})` copies the LAST 64 KB (`TERMINAL_TAIL`, `copyTail`) of every named terminal-mode session's raw PTY buffer to `frozen/buffers/<id>.tail` and records `{bytes, truncatedFrom}` under `local.terminalTails`; ids are validated twice (the wiring's `idOk` and the freeze's own filter — a buffer id is a file name). `_incidentTargets` (incident-wiring) collects them from live terminal-mode sessions and from the reporter's terminal windows; `_incidentServerState` adds `desktop` (singleton facts, `keeper.listApps()`, `stream.stats()`) through the late-bound `getDesktop` dep. Gate: test-incident.

**SESSION-META FROZEN AS DATA (2.369.160, inc-mudv05ja-n5rv).** The 64 KiB byte cap (`copyCapped`, which keeps the TAIL bytes) froze every session-meta carrying `taskRecords` (2.369.140; the owner's own was 96 877 B) into an unparseable half — exactly the sessions with workflows, which is what a workflow incident needs. Session-meta AND wrapper-meta are now copied by `copyJsonWhole(src, dest, ceiling)` (exported with `META_COPY_MAX` = 2 MiB): WHOLE up to the ceiling; above it a VALID JSON trimmed as data — the largest top-level array keeps its NEWEST records (halving until it fits), then the next field; a non-array field too big is dropped whole; `_frozenTrimmed: {originalBytes, ceiling, dropped: [{field, from, kept} | {field, bytes, whole}]}` names every touch; a file that does not parse (or is over `META_PARSE_MAX` 16 MiB — never a sync parse that big on the server loop) freezes as `{_frozenTrimmed: {unparseable: true, …}, rawTail}`. A trimmed/failed copy is noted on `env.local.sessionMetas[f].frozen`. `copyCapped` remains only for the transcript tail (bytes ARE the evidence there). 不变量=a frozen file is truncated as DATA, never as bytes. Test: scripts/test-incident.mjs (+5: a 98 KB meta with 40 taskRecords freezes whole, a 3 MB one freezes ≤ 2 MiB with the marker and the newest record, the copier's three branches).

### routes/persistence.js

  routes/persistence.js — …also **LAYOUT ROLLBACK POINTS (2.296.0, after a bug flattened a user's whole desktop layout)**: `writeLayouts` is the ONE choke point every layout write passes through, so it snapshots the PREVIOUS state into `data/layout-history/` whenever the desktop→window SHAPE changes (per-desktop sorted window ids; geometry drags and z-order churn deliberately ignored or one drag would evict every useful restore point). A destructive write therefore always leaves the last good shape on disk — the thing the incident lacked, where two EMPTIED desktops made even the pre-damage mapping unrecoverable. Bounded 40; **filenames carry a sequence suffix — a bare ISO stamp has ms resolution and a mass-resume burst lands inside one millisecond, silently overwriting the older entry i.e. destroying the pre-damage state exactly when it matters (caught by the bounded-history assertion)**. Legacy top-level `autoSave` counted too (instances without virtual desktops otherwise read "0 windows"). Routes GET /api/layout-history + POST /api/layout-history/:id/restore (id regex-validated; restoring writes through the same path so it is ITSELF undoable). UI: ⚙ → Restore a previous layout… (setup-flows `_showLayoutHistory`). Test: scripts/test-layout-history.mjs (11). **USER-STATE CARRIES EVERY KEY (2026-09-14):** `normalizeUserState` rebuilds only the session-ref keys it migrates (`USER_STATE_DEFAULT`'s set) and carries every OTHER top-level key through verbatim — it used to return a literal of exactly the session keys, so any per-feature preference PATCHed here was dropped on the very write that carried it (measured in headless chrome: `PATCH {desktopAppAdvancedOpen:true}` ⇒ GET never carried it; the desktop-app launcher's `desktopAppRecents` never survived a reload since 2.369.96). The merge-only PATCH (B-b87b) is now real for any key; a full-document POST from a stale tab still replaces the whole document (the documented residual).

  lib/incident-recorder.js — "Report a problem" panic button (2.238.0, the timezone-gap fix): ALWAYS-ON client ring buffers (clicks/coarse keys — typed TEXT never recorded, only a per-burst marker; ws message TYPES both directions, never payloads; console errors/warns) + on-demand full client snapshot → POST /api/incident → server adds its own scene (activeSessions digest, 30-min sysinfo history, in-memory server console ring (600 lines, wraps console.* in server.js), hosts digest, resume-breaker table + remote-discovery cache digest — the two conversation-disappeared-class facts that survive nowhere else, 2.238.1) → data/incidents/<inc-id>/bundle.json (+followup.json auto-appended 2min later; newest 30 kept). **snapshot.chatTraces (2.264.0, B-21bc user request): each open chat window's SCROLL TRACER ring tail ships automatically** — chat-view's `_trace()` is an always-on capped ring again (the 2.111.8 removal stubbed it AND the documented Ctrl+Shift+J dump, leaving viewport-jump reports blind): paging/trim/jump/runsRestore breadcrumbs + a coarse scroll sampler (>400px moves w/ pin state + wheelAgo — user-scroll vs programmatic-yank discriminator) + an unpin breadcrumb; positions/op tags only, never content. User relays the short id; admin reads the bundle. Entry: ⚙ → Report a problem…; GET /api/incidents lists. **SEMANTIC OP BREADCRUMBS (2.296.0): `window.__vsOp(name, data)` pushes into a 4th ring (`op`, cap 300) — for ops that RELOCATE OR REPLACE a window/session, the class where "what did the app just do to my layout" is the whole question. The pool-collapse incident left NO trace of its desktop reassignments (the action ring has clicks, the ws ring has message types; neither answers 'what moved these windows'), so the sequence had to be reconstructed by reading code. Wired at desktop-move / pool-cold-restart / resume-place. Names+ids only — the privacy rule is unchanged. The server bundle also carries the LAYOUT TABLE (window→desktop+sid) and the layout-history index, which is what turns a flattened layout from JSON surgery into one click.** PRIVACY: the note is the only free text — keep it that way. Test: scripts/test-incident.mjs

### resume-continuity.js (PURE, B-6b6d)

  src/resume-continuity.js — **THE RESUME LADDER**: `resumeSpawnPick({explicit, conversation, instanceDefault, resume, hasSource})` → `{value, origin}` with `origin ∈ chosen|conversation|instance|harness`, plus `continuityLogLine`. The owner's 2026-09-07 ruling in one function: **a conversation's OWN model/effort wins on resume/fork/restart; the instance default is a NEW-session default; an explicit per-session pick beats both.** TWO callers, one law — the CLIENT (session-lifecycle `createSession`, `hasSource:false` = only the server can read a conversation's records ⇒ a continuation sends NOTHING) and the SERVER (ws-create, immediately before `buildSessionArgs`, with the harness descriptor's `store.lastTurn<Knob>` reader wired in). `hasSource` is DERIVED from that hook's presence — never a parallel caps boolean. **`''` is a STATED choice, `undefined` is silence, and the difference only survives on a NEW session** (round 2): the New Session dialog's first option IS `''` ("Auto (model default)"), so collapsing it made an explicit Auto resolve to the instance default; on a non-continuation `''` wins as `{value:'', origin:'chosen'}` and the client sends the resolved value verbatim so it survives the wire. On a CONTINUATION the create message carries `model: sessionModel || undefined`, so there an explicit Auto and an absent field really are identical bytes and both mean "take the conversation's own value". A knob with NO source sends nothing on a resume rather than the default (an unconditional default there IS the defect); a source that came up EMPTY falls back to the default and the caller LOGS it. **`applyOriginHint(origin, hint)` (round 3)** — the wire's other half. On a NEW session the CLIENT resolves `<prefix>.default*` (it needs the value for its own chip, and it owns the legacy `session.defaultEffort` key + `settings.isModified`, which the server cannot see) and sends it VERBATIM, so the server saw a bare string it could only read as a pick: `_modelOrigin`/`_effortOrigin` were ALWAYS `'chosen'` for a new session, `'instance'`/`'harness'` were unreachable there, and Session Properties called `<prefix>.defaultModel` “your choice for this session” on every create path that shows no picker (openShellTerminal, the toolbar, setup-flows, manage-agents). The client now also sends the origin it computed (`spawnOriginHint`) and this reconciles: it may ONLY downgrade the server's own `'chosen'` to `'instance'`/`'harness'`, never upgrade or re-point a rung the server decided from facts the client never had, and it never touches the VALUE; a `'conversation'`/`'chosen'`/garbage hint is ignored, and an older client that sends none keeps master's answer. Gate: scripts/test-codex-effort-meta.mjs legs ⑪ / ⑫ / ⑫ c.

### sidebar-mounts.js

    sidebar-mounts.js  — Remote tab: machines (ssh hosts) + storage (mounts) rendering (installSidebarMounts mixin, ~1000 lines; 2.152.0: "Pair a device" action + _showDevicePairDialog — dial-out device pairing, mints via POST /api/agentd/dial-pair and renders the full installer command incl BOTH --dial-token and --host-token; the host token is what the daemon verifies OUR mux hello against — omit it and the device dials in but rejects every command). **KEY IMPORT (2.246.0): `_askPrivateKey({text,error,showPass})` is the reusable, PREFILLABLE "Private key" sub-dialog** — resolves {privateKey, keyPassphrase} or null; the Add-machine POST wraps it in a RETRY LOOP (a KEY_ERR_CODES failure re-opens it with the key still pasted + the localized reason, so a wrong passphrase is never a dead end). **TWO ORDERING TRAPS, both real: (1) `createModalShell`'s close() fires onClose on EVERY path, so the submit handler must `resolve(value)` BEFORE `ctx.close()` — close-then-resolve lets the cancel-resolver win and "Use this key" behaves exactly like Cancel (the entire paste-a-key flow was dead; idempotency alone does NOT save you, the FIRST settle wins; caught only by the headless dialog test). (2) sub-dialogs REUSE the overlay id `mounts-dialog-overlay`, and createModalShell REMOVES the existing one — so from the first sub-dialog onward the Add-machine dialog is DETACHED and _mountsDialog's inline error element renders into nothing; the submit callback takes `err` and toasts when `!err.isConnected`.** Passphrase + key text are read RAW from the elements (a passphrase may legitimately have leading/trailing whitespace — verified ssh-keygen accepts `'p@ss w/ spaces '`), deliberately bypassing _mountsDialog's trimming field reader. Detection reveals affordances but NEVER blocks submit (server is authoritative; an always-available "Key has a passphrase?" toggle covers a misjudged format), and the passphrase row uses `style.display`, not a `hidden` class (no global `.hidden` rule in this project)

**2.369.165 (integrations chunk 1, D1 of docs/design-integrations-per-account.zh.md) — THE DIALOG COMPONENT MOVED OUT.** `_mountsDialog`'s field renderer, `oauthLinkRow`, `_wireOAuthConnect`'s consent block and the throwing fetch wrapper `api` live in src/lib/mounts-dialog.js (imported here); `_mountsDialog` / `_wireOAuthConnect` stay as thin delegates so every storage caller is unchanged, and `_lastMountsDialog` is still stamped HERE (only this mixin's callers read it). The move is pixel-identical (scripts/test-mounts-dialog-extract.mjs) and kept single (scripts/test-oauth-field-parity.mjs): never re-grow a local copy of any of the four, and a storage-dialog field spelling the channel dialogs share is renamed on BOTH sides. **Chunk 3: `_showDriveReauthDialog` is a CALLER of the shared `reauthDialog`** (its three storage routes and its drive-token save are the parameters; the dialog's DOM is byte- and pixel-identical — test-mounts-dialog-extract's `reauth-drive` scenario); the channel account's Re-authorize is the same dialog with the OAuth client select on top.

**Chunk 4a — D2: SWITCHING A STORAGE RECORD'S OAUTH CLIENT IS A RE-AUTHORIZATION** (the channel accounts' rule, adopted by the storage side in its own commit; docs/design-integrations-per-account.zh.md §6 D2). `_showEditMountDialog`'s Save asks `_mountClientSwitch(cfg, cur, presets)` whether the client the record RESOLVES to changes — the server's own resolution (`MountManager._driveClient` / gmail-sync `_client`): a custom id wins (Gmail: id + secret), else the preset key, else the resolver's fallback (the only preset, else `default`, else rclone's built-in), so `''` → the only preset is NOT a switch; the SECRET is not the identity (a rotated secret of the same client keeps its tokens and saves directly). On a switch (Drive / Gmail top-level records only, a token pasted by hand = the user brought their own ⇒ a plain save) Save PATCHes every OTHER changed field, closes, and opens `_showClientSwitchReauthDialog` — the shared `reauthDialog` (the SAME skeleton as `_showDriveReauthDialog`, only the hint differs: it names the new client and says the connection keeps its current client and sign-in until the switch finishes) whose consent starts under the NEW client (the add flow's `gdrive-auth/start` / `gmail-auth/start` body, never `mountId`) and whose token lands WITH it (Drive: `drive-token {token, client}`; Gmail: one PATCH `{clientPreset, token}`). A custom client without its secret is refused inline before any save or consent. The Edit dialog DRAWS exactly what it drew (test-mounts-dialog-extract §3: outerHTML + 0 differing pixels against a patched copy with the decision neutered — the same copy is the control that still saves silently).

### src/lib/mounts-dialog.js — THE MOUNTS DIALOG COMPONENT, shared by storage and channel accounts (2.369.165, integrations chunk 1)

ONE field renderer + ONE consent block + ONE cross-browser link row for every "connect a thing with a login" dialog (design-integrations-per-account §8.1 #12, D1: "two dialogs = one component"). Exports, all moved VERBATIM from sidebar-mounts.js at 2.369.160: `mountsDialog(title, fields, submitLabel, onSubmit, opts)` → `{close, inputs, body, applyConds}` — the field-spec array `{key, label, type: text|password|select|textarea, options, value, placeholder, when(values), hint, advanced, autocomplete}` becomes label / control / `.mounts-field-hint` line / the collapsed `details.mounts-advanced` / `.cfg-err` / `.btn-create`, `when:` re-evaluated on every input/change; the overlay id is `mounts-dialog-overlay` (a sub-dialog REPLACES the one below it — the two ordering traps in the sidebar-mounts essay hold for every caller); `opts.onClose` is REQUIRED by a caller that awaits a Promise from the dialog. `oauthLinkRow(url)` — the 2.226.2 cross-browser affordance (the consent URL as a copyable read-only input, "Account signed in on ANOTHER browser?"). `wireOAuthConnect(ctx, {tokenKey, backend, label, clientIdKey, clientSecretKey, endpoints})` — the in-dialog consent block placed before the token field (visibility follows the field through a MutationObserver): button → status → link row → paste-back box → 1.5 s status poll → the token lands in the field, the button reads Reconnect. `endpoints` (`{start, status, callback}`, default `MOUNT_OAUTH_ENDPOINTS` = the `/api/mounts/gdrive-auth/*` routes) is the ONE parameter the move added, so the channel side can run the same block against its own consent routes. `api(url, opts)` — the fetch wrapper that THROWS on HTTP errors / `{error}` bodies and carries the server's `code`. Remove… in Edit on both sides and never a storage row icon; D8's auth-death sentence (the storage one in src/mounts.js, same head + tail); §8 the design's §4 i18n key list PARSED OUT OF docs/design-integrations-per-account.zh.md (`designI18nKeys`: 共用键 / 新键 / 删除键) — every key has a `DESIGN_I18N` row, drawn where it belongs AS BUILT (the channel side includes the adapters' `i18nKey` option labels) and carried by zh + ja; a key built under another spelling or not drawn names why (`Duplicate…`, the health line in three parts, `Include query`, Lark's include-groups option — not declared); the deleted `Add account…` is drawn by no channel file. §5: one patched in-memory control per rule (a control counts only against a rule green on the tree). A design edit that adds a key, a side that renames a shared spelling, a re-ordered Edit — each reddens here.

### src/lib/channel-account-dialogs.js — THE CHANNEL ACCOUNT DIALOGS on the storage component (2.369.165, integrations chunk 3)

Connect an account / Re-authorize / Edit / Duplicate / Remove for a Lark or Gmail ACCOUNT, each the storage dialog (docs/design-integrations-per-account.zh.md r4 §2.2 / §2.5 / §3 / §8.1 #2–#5, #11–#12; D1 / D3 / D4 / D5). It holds field SPECS only — `mountsDialog` / `wireOAuthConnect` / `reauthDialog` from src/lib/mounts-dialog.js draw them (scripts/test-oauth-field-parity.mjs §6: the imports, the calls, the channel consent routes, no renderer spelling written here, the retired wizard gone). **The OAuth client field** (`clientFieldSpecs`): `Preset: {label}` per preset the digest carries (`presets` `{key,label}`, the one env reader), `Custom (own client id/secret)`, no Built-in; presets[0] preselected, `custom` when there is none; a preset the account names that the cluster no longer provides stays listed BY NAME ("(no longer provided)"); the registry's `clientHint` as the hint (Edit / Re-authorize / Duplicate word their own); `Custom {registry label}` inputs (`clientFields` — the registry's labels, placeholders and help) on `when: custom`; a type with a console setup (Lark) adds the `copy` row with the callback URL and one hint per prerequisite. The route body is `choiceBody` (`clientPreset:'<k>'` | `clientPreset:'custom'` + `clientId` + `clientSecret`). **Names:** `providerOf` = the TYPE's label off the registry row (`integration`), never an account's own label (a copy named "Gmail (copy)" is still Gmail) — the Re-authorize button, the health tag, the toasts; `signinOf` = the row's `signinName` (Gmail → Google) else the product — `{provider} authorization`, `Connect {provider}`, `Sign in with {provider}`. **Connect** (`showConnectAccountDialog(app, kinds)`): Type first, every other field `when:` its type (suffixed keys, one consent block per type, the others hidden), the consent through `CHANNEL_OAUTH_ENDPOINTS` (`/api/channels/oauth/{start,status,callback}`, the flow id is the "token" the block writes), Connect → `POST /adapters/<kind>/connect {flowId, name, options, choice}`; before a sign-in it is refused in `.cfg-err` and nothing exists. **Re-authorize** (`showReauthAccountDialog(app, a, {kinds, preselect})`): `reauthDialog` + the client select (a custom client prefilled from `GET /adapters/:id/config`, D3); start = `POST /adapters/:id/reauthorize {choice}` (another client = the server's rebind); its end is watched on the `channels-updated` broadcast (`authWatcher`: `lastAuthAt` moved + `auth.state` connected, or `lastAuthError`) — no poll route; the paste-back = `POST /adapters/:id/auth/finish`. **Edit** (`showEditAccountDialog`): the config route's values prefilled INCLUDING the custom secret as plain text (D3, the storage 2.108.8 rule), the sign-in facts (`note`), the declared options, the push claim, the sender line; buttons Re-authorize {product}… · Duplicate… · Remove… · Save (Save sends only what changed: `PUT {label, options, push, senderHonestyLine, credential(same id)}`); `switchesClient` ⇒ Save opens Re-authorize with the new client preselected (never a silent re-point). **Duplicate** (`showDuplicateAccountDialog`): `{label} (copy)`, the type read-only, client / first option / push claim copied and changeable, the copied / not-copied note, its OWN consent block whose `start` first creates the copy (`POST /adapters/:id/duplicate`, then a changed option / claim PUT) and then re-authorizes it under the dialog's client; dismissed before its sign-in landed ⇒ the copy is DELETEd again. **Remove** (`removeAccount`): confirm → `DELETE /adapters/:id`; `409 account-referenced` ⇒ `showRemoveRefusedDialog` (`#chan-remove-refused`) naming each reference (`assignment: {conv} → {who}`, `reach: {who} may see the whole account`, `outbox: {n} proposal(s) awaiting approval`, once) with the Disconnect sentence and Open Outbox. XSS: every account name, preset label, app id and principal reaches the DOM through the component's textContent or `el()`; nothing here writes innerHTML. Gates: test-oauth-field-parity (fast) + test-integrations-ui ⑩ (heavy, the whole flow in chrome against scripts/fixtures/channels-vendor-stub.cjs) + test-channels-i18n (the six dialogs under zh + ja).

### picture-shell.js — THE PICTURE SHELL (P8-2 x2, 2026-09-22)

**Round 3, A1 (2.369.166, docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless.md §3.1 — the owner: "why does a copy inside the app need a click to reach my clipboard?"):** `clipboardDelivery({secure, canWrite, gestureAge})` has THREE answers — `api` (a secure page with the API, unchanged), `gesture` (no API, and the view's copy-chord stamp is `0 ≤ age < GESTURE_WINDOW_MS` = 5000, Chrome's transient activation — MEASURED on a plain-http hostname page: an asynchronous `execCommand('copy')` succeeds 0…4800 ms after a trusted Ctrl+C and fails from 5200 ms, whatever the keydown's `preventDefault`), `chip` (anything else: no stamp, a stale one, a non-number). `deliverCopy(text, {secure, clipboard, toast, gestureAge})` returns the route taken; on `gesture` it runs `copyViaSelection` (the hidden textarea) with NO click and toasts — the browser's own `false` is the second gate and falls to the chip. THE ONE-TIME HTTPS HINT: the first chip shown BECAUSE the page is plain http (never an API refusal on https) on a device reveals `.desktop-copy-hint` beside it — "Enable HTTPS for seamless copy", a "How to enable HTTPS" link to `HTTPS_DOCS_URL` (docs/getting-started.md "## HTTPS for seamless copy": the Chrome flag / `tailscale serve` / a Caddy reverse proxy; the product serves no TLS), an SVG dismiss — and writes `localStorage['vibespace.desktopCopyHintShown']` (`COPY_HINT_KEY`; PURE `copyHintDue({secure, storage})`, an unreadable storage ⇒ not due). The RFB rung passes no stamp, so it keeps the chip (noVNC owns its canvas's keys). Gate: test-xpra-client §1 (the age table incl. 4999/5000, the hint predicate, the docs anchor exists, the xpra-proto twin gone) + §3c. **A r1 (2.369.166) — THE FOCUS GOES BACK.** `copyViaSelection` remembers `document.activeElement` (unless it is `<body>`) before `ta.select()` — which FOCUSES the temporary textarea — and after `ta.remove()` (which drops the focus to `<body>`) hands it back with `{preventScroll:true}`, on a refused and on a throwing `execCommand` too. Before r1 every key after a gesture copy went to `<body>`: the verifier's real-rung probe typed 1234, Ctrl+C (the token landed) and then `5` + Ctrl+C produced nothing, the calculator still at 1234, no sign anywhere (the heavy suite masked it by calling `view.focus()` before every typing step). Gate: test-vnc-view §8 (a focus-tracking fake document: restored to the IME with preventScroll, nothing focused from `<body>`, the refused/throwing writes) + heavy test-desktop-xpra-window §9 (the IME holds the focus after each gesture copy — `activeElement` TEXTAREA — and the `5` typed with NO script refocus reaches the calculator: the second copy reads `12345`, token 30 ms after the chord).

    picture-shell.js     — `createPictureShell(host, {labels, autoReconnect, onStatus, background, focus})` → `{container, bar, mount, status, pasteBtn, reBtn, copyChip, labels, setStatus, addControl, emit, scheduleRetry(connect), resetLadder, want, unwant, close, pasteFromClipboard, openPasteBox, closePasteBox, deliverCopy, showCopied, hideCopied, state, wanted, closed, pasteOpen, copiedText}` + the PURE `clipboardDelivery` / `pageIsSecure` / `copyViaSelection`. THE CLIPBOARD CHROME lives here for every rung: `pasteFromClipboard({connected, notConnected, send, clipboard})` refuses a dead view, sends a readable clipboard, else opens the `.vnc-paste-box` (reason sentence + textarea + Send/Cancel, under the bar — its native paste works on plain http and on a touch screen; Esc/Cancel refocus the view); `deliverCopy(text, {secure, clipboard, toast, gestureAge})` = the API on a secure context that has it, the no-click `execCommand` inside the user's gesture window on plain http (Round 3, A1 above; A r1: the focus goes back to the pane), else — and on a refusal — the `.desktop-copied-chip` (appended AFTER Reconnect so `addControl` keeps its slots) whose click copies through `copyViaSelection` (execCommand, the user gesture) and goes away. It is also what vnc-view.js and xpra-view.js share and nothing a protocol knows — the counter-zoomed container (`COUNTER_ZOOM`, net zoom 1; the retired cssText literal verbatim, a view may recolour the background), the ONE `.desktop-bar` (status chip / Paste / hidden Reconnect — test-xpra-client §4 censuses that no other file builds it), the mount, and the BOUNDED reconnect ladder keyed on `wanted` (never on a transport's clean flag). A view decides what a connect is and hands `scheduleRetry` its own connect. `streamUrl` and `RECONNECT_LADDER` live here (re-exported by vnc-view.js for its callers).

### xpra-proto.js — THE XPRA WORDS, PURE (P8-2 x2, 2026-09-22; D21 (c) (b))

**HiDPI + the app's minimum (2.369.158, docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md §7.6; the owner's 2026-09-23 GNOME Calculator report on a devicePixelRatio-2 screen):** THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE CROPPED KEYPAD: `METADATA_SUPPORTED` carried xpra-html5 v21's `size-hints` (the pre-4 name) and not `size-constraints` (6.x's), and the server only sends the keys a client lists — no window ever carried its minimum, the fit belt ran blind, a pane shorter than GNOME Calculator's 616 px was asked for, X clamped it and the pane cropped it (measured: the calculator's new-window carried has-alpha,title,class-instance,window-type,decorations). `size-constraints` is listed now. New: `pixelRatioOf`, `devicePane({width,height}, ratio)` (CSS × ratio, rounded DOWN since r2 — below), `minPaneCss(constraints, ratio)` (minimum-size, else base-size per ICCCM, ÷ ratio rounded UP so `devicePane(minPaneCss(h,r),r)` is never below the minimum; no hints ⇒ null). `fitGeometry` already raises to the minimum — the fit never asks below it. Gate: test-xpra-client §6 (incl. the old-list control and a 9-ratio × 4-minimum sweep).

**r2 — A FRACTIONAL RATIO IS 1:1 (the verifier, DPR 1.25/1.5/1.75: a 0.9995 stage transform, the badge on a pane that holds the app, 4.18 % of the pixels off):** `devicePane` rounds DOWN (`floor(css × r + 1e-6)` — the epsilon absorbs 700 × 1.15 = 804.99…) so the device pane's CSS box never exceeds the pane (733 × 1.5 was 1100 ⇒ 733.33 CSS). And `gridStep(r)` / `backingSize(n, r)`: Chrome paints a canvas into its box snapped to WHOLE CSS px (MEASURED — a 1:1 copy only when the box is a whole CSS px): a box of 1346 / 1.5 = 897.33… CSS (1.5 % of a calculator's pixels off) and even 1395 / 2 = 697.5 CSS (an xterm 1395 device px wide at DPR 2: 18.6 % off, every glyph edge softened; padded to 1396 ⇒ 698 CSS: 1 pixel off of 1.19 M) are resampled. `gridStep` = the smallest device step k ≤ 16 whose CSS size k / r is a WHOLE CSS px (2 ⇒ 2, 1.5 ⇒ 3, 1.25 ⇒ 5, 1.75 ⇒ 7, 1.1 ⇒ 11, 1 ⇒ 1, none ⇒ 1); `backingSize` = n rounded UP to it — the view's canvas backing. Gate: test-xpra-client §6b (every pane width 200..1400 × 10 ratios; every size 1..2000 × 9 ratios; the old rounding's 733.33 / 898.4 and the unpadded 897.33 / 697.5 boxes as controls).

    xpra-proto.js        — imports nothing; bundled + imported by the node suite. `helloCaps` (the html5 v21 hello trimmed to what the window does: windows/keyboard/pointer/clipboard/cursors; rencodeplus+lz4+brotli; `share:true` for N viewers; NO rgb encodings — their in-packet lz4 lives in the worker), every packet the client sends in xpra-html5 v21's forms (read from its Client.js on this box: `key-action`, `button-action`, `pointer-position`, `map-window`, `configure-window`, `damage-sequence`, `clipboard-token/-contents/-none`, `focus`, `ping_echo`), `displayPacket` (6.5.3's `display-configure` — `configure-display` its legacy alias — else `desktop_size`), `keyboardConfigPacket` (`keyboard-config` else `keymap-changed`), the WHEEL as button 4–7 clicks accumulated per 120 units (`WheelAccumulator` — xtest has no precise wheel and `wheel-motion` trips its assert), `fitGeometry` (the pane under min/max/increment/base hints, snapped DOWN to the cell grid), `placeInside` (dialogs nudged inside), `windowKind` (popup / dialog / main), `clipboardShortcut` (Ctrl/⌘+V is the browser's — the paste event carries the text on plain http; Ctrl+C/X go to the app AND the browser); the delivery rule `clipboardDelivery` lives ONLY in picture-shell.js (every rung shares it; the unused copy that still sat here was removed in Round 3, A1 — test-xpra-client §1 asserts it is gone). **THE KEYMAP IS NATIVE (measured on 6.5.3: a client sending only `keycodes` — xpra-html5's shape — is TRANSLATED onto the server's `us` keymap, so `é`, let alone `中`, can never be typed; a client sending `x11_keycodes` + `query_struct` has the X keymap PROGRAMMED from its own map):** `X11_KEYMAP` (every keycode with its shifted level, the modifiers on their own keycodes, sent as a Map so the keycodes stay integers — a plain object would stringify them), `NAME_TO_KEYCODE` (a key-action's keycode is the one carrying its keysym: KP_Enter on 108, right-hand modifiers on the left name — one JS keyCode, Meta = Super/mod4, AltGraph = ISO_Level3_Shift/mod5), `nativeKey`, and `ImeKeymap.plan(text)` — a character outside the keymap gets a rolling keycode row (226–255, `U<hex>` / Latin-1 names) PUBLISHED by a `keyboard-config` before its press (the server reprograms the X keymap, once per new character). The file header records why the npm `xpra-html5-client` is not used (README says MPL-2.0 derived from upstream while package.json says Apache-2.0; frozen 2022-05, 4.x era; 10.7 MB / 2.37 MB ESM with node-forge+lodash-es; a whole client, not a protocol layer) and that the transport is the upstream html5 v21 Protocol.js worker served unmodified from the installed package behind our auth. Gate: test-xpra-client §1.

### xpra-client.js — THE XPRA SESSION, DOM-FREE (P8-2 x2, 2026-09-22)

**Round 3, A2 (2.369.166):** `closeMain()` = the OUTER ✕'s ask — ONE `close-window` naming the MAIN window (xpra's WM_DELETE_WINDOW: the app may answer with its own "save?" dialog, and nothing closes then); never a dialog's wid (the app's own ✕ on a dialog is the app's business), never from Watch / view-only, nothing before a main window exists or after it is lost — `false` = nothing sent (the window then closes its pane as before). Gate: test-xpra-client §2c. **A r1 (2.369.166, measured):** what the app DOES with WM_DELETE_WINDOW is the app's business — xterm (no client-side decorations) answers it by HANGING UP its child (SIGHUP) and exits when the child does: an interactive bash ends on the first ✕ (both windows gone 375–418 ms after it, two runs); a child that survives SIGHUP keeps xterm running — the verifier's plain `xterm` ran $SHELL = zsh in a HOME with no .zshrc, whose first-run menu (zsh-newuser-install) survives the hangup (by hand on Xvfb: the same xterm exits once that HOME has an empty .zshrc) — and then the second ✕ within 5 s (the toast names it) is the Stop. Never an automatic Stop: an app answering with its own "save?" dialog looks the same from outside. Gate: heavy test-desktop-xpra-window §10 (3b).

**2.369.165 r1 — a late worker message never acts on a torn-down worker:** `finish()` nulls `worker` before `terminate()`, and a Worker can still deliver a message it queued before that; the `onmessage` closure is bound to its own instance (`const w = worker`) and returns when `worker !== w`. test-xpra-client §late pins it with a pre-fix patched copy as the control.

**HiDPI + the app's minimum (2.369.158, docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md §7.6; the owner's 2026-09-23 GNOME Calculator report on a devicePixelRatio-2 screen):** the session speaks DEVICE px: `screen` and `resize(w,h)` take CSS px, `ratio` (a number or a function read at every resize) turns them into the device pane (`devicePane`) for the hello's desktop size, every display-configure and every fit/configure-window; windows, draws and pointer coordinates are device px. `dpi` is the DISPLAY's font dpi (the record's) — never 96 × ratio: xpra rewrites Xft.dpi to a client's dpi when it changes (measured 96 → 144), which would quadruple a GDK_SCALE=2 app's text. `on.constraints(hints|null)` announces the MAIN window's size constraints on every change (new main, a size-constraints metadata change, the main lost ⇒ null); getters `cssPane`, `ratio`, `dpi`, `mainConstraints`. Gate: test-xpra-client §6 (a patched copy with the ratio pinned to 1 as the control).

**r2 — THE DISPLAY CONTAINS THE WINDOW IT PLACES (the verifier on a 320×568 phone @2: the display was the pane, 640×982, under the calculator fitted to its 740×1232 minimum; X clamped the pointer at row 981, so '0', the lower rows and the '=' column could not be clicked — `7894564564`).** `displayFor()` = max(the pane, the main window's fit) is the ONE display rule and `syncDisplay(force)` the ONE sender (only when it differs from what this client last asked, `sentDisplay` — the hello's desktop size first): the server hello (the pane of now), `resize`, leaving Watch (forced — the watched viewer set the display), `refit` (BEFORE the configure-window, so a larger minimum grows the display first), a new main (before its map-window) and the main lost (back to the pane). Getter `display`. Measured after: display 720×1232 ⊇ the window, all ten digits land, `xdotool` reads the app's bottom-right corner. Gate: test-xpra-client §6b (grown before the map; pane-sized again when the pane holds the app / the main is gone; the pane-only r1 rule as the patched-copy control) + test-desktop-xpra-window §7 (b).

**x5 (2026-09-22):** `watch` (an agent drives the window): NO geometry at all — windows are drawn where the SERVER has them (no fit at map, the map-window carries the server's geometry), the belt and `refit` return, `resize()` only remembers the pane (the verifier's LOW); leaving watch sends `display-configure` for the pane then re-fits the main + keeps dialogs inside. `dormant` (the pane is BLOCKED: the bridge holds its hello and relays nothing): the hello timeout is suspended (`armHello`) — the server's hello arrives the moment the pane becomes active; a hello answered for a pane that changed size since (`helloPane`) is followed by `display-configure` for the pane of NOW. test-xpra-client §5 (a patched copy without the Watch guards as the control; the non-dormant client timing out as the dormant one's control).


    xpra-client.js       — `createXpraClient({url, workerUrl, screen, dpi, layout, on, Worker, decode, now, log, helloTimeoutMs, pasteKeyDelayMs, beltGapMs, beltFightMs, beltMaxFights})` → `{connect, close, send, resize, keyDown, keyUp, typeText, pointerMove, pointerButton, wheel, pasteText, focusWindow, windowAt, beltState, state, closedReason, windows, mainWid, focusedWid, pane, serverCaps, packetTypes, viewOnly, lastPaste, lastReceived}`; `on.status/window/paint/title/icon/clipboard/cursor/ready`. The transport is the upstream Protocol.js WORKER (`{c:'r'}` ready → `{c:'o',u}` open → `{c:'p',p}` packets / `{c:'s',p}` sends; it frames, rencodeplus-codes and inflates off the main thread). Invariants: the FIRST top-level window is mapped at 0,0 with the pane's fitted size (the app never appears small in a corner) and `resize` re-fits it — `display-configure` first (the virtual screen follows the pane) then `configure-window`; every OTHER non-popup window (a dialog, a SECOND top-level — xpra clamps one at +2000+1500 to 20x20 px visible) keeps its size and is placed inside the pane at map, when X moves it and when the pane shrinks; THE BELT (2026-09-22): a server geometry packet (`window-move-resize` / `window-resized` — the app resized or moved ITSELF, GNOME Calculator's mode switch fell to 40 % of the pane) is checked against the fit (the main within one size increment at 0,0, a secondary inside) and answered with ONE corrective `configure-window`, at most one per window per `BELT_GAP_MS` 500 (a packet inside the gap after our own configure is re-checked when the gap ends — it may be the confirmation or X's snap), and an app that undoes the fit `BELT_MAX_FIGHTS` 3 times in a row, each within `BELT_FIGHT_MS` 2000, wins until the pane or its hints change (said once — bounded, never a ping-pong, two viewers of different panes included); a popup is drawn where X put it and never moved; draws are PAINTED IN ORDER per window (a promise chain — a later png may decode first) and EVERY draw is acked (`damage-sequence`, decode ms or -1 + the reason: an unsupported coding, an unknown window) or the server stops sending; a text `clipboard-token` on CLIPBOARD is surfaced ONCE (deduped against the last paste and the last receipt); a `clipboard-request` is answered with the last pasted text (`-none` before any); `pasteText` sends the token then the app's own Ctrl+V after 60 ms (the token must land first); a key the published keymap lacks goes publish-then-press from keyDown (its keyUp is swallowed); `typeText` (IME) publishes the rows BEFORE the presses; `viewOnly` drops every input at the source (Ctrl+V still answers `paste` so the browser keeps working); a `disconnect` names its reason, a hello that never comes closes with a deadline, a worker that cannot start (the html5 package missing on a host) closes by name; nothing is sent after the close. Gate: test-xpra-client §2 (a fake worker + an out-of-order fake decoder) + §2b (the belt and the placement as packets, with the within-one-increment CONTROL) + test-desktop-xpra-window §4 (the real rung: xterm resizing / moving ITSELF fitted back and X agreeing, a second top-level at +2000+1500 placed inside, GNOME Calculator's Ctrl+Alt+A/B mode switch keeping 100 % of the pane — the pre-fix client, run as the control, measured 78.0 % then 41.2 %).

### xpra-view.js — THE XPRA PICTURE VIEW (P8-2 x2, 2026-09-22; §4.4: the window is OURS)

**Round 3, A2 (2.369.166):** `closeApp()` = `client.closeMain()` (false with no client) — the desktop-app window's outer ✕ asks through it.


**Round 3, A1 (2.369.166 — the copy without a click on plain http):** THE GESTURE STAMP. The IME textarea's keydown stamps `copyGestureAt = clock()` when `client.keyDown` answers `'copy'` (Ctrl/⌘+C or +X FORWARDED to the app — a view-only / Watch pane forwards nothing, so it never stamps) AND the event is the user's own (`isTrusted === true`, not an auto-`repeat`); `onClipboard` hands the shell `gestureAge = clock() − copyGestureAt` and SPENDS the stamp on every delivery — one chord, at most one write, so a later copy nobody made on this page (an agent through P9, an app on a timer, another client) meets no stamp and keeps the chip. `clock` = the injectable `now` (else `performance.now`). A token the client DEDUPES (the same text as the last one) is no delivery and spends nothing. Measured on the real rung (test-desktop-xpra-window §9, GNOME Calculator on a hostname page): the calculator's token arrives ~30 ms after the trusted Ctrl+C and lands in the browser clipboard with no click; xclip's token 5.5 s after a chord ⇒ the chip; a copy 0.1 s after a plain digit key (the page HAS activation, no chord) ⇒ the chip. New getters `hintShown`, `copyHint`. Gate: test-xpra-client §3c (+ the WIRING PIN in §4) + test-desktop-xpra-window §9.

**HiDPI + the app's minimum (2.369.158, docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md §7.6; the owner's 2026-09-23 GNOME Calculator report on a devicePixelRatio-2 screen):** options `dpi` (number or function — the record's) and `pixelRatio` (() => devicePixelRatio, injectable). Each window's box is its device geometry ÷ the ratio and its canvas keeps the DEVICE pixels (r2: the backing is `backingSize(win, r)` and its CSS box backing ÷ r — see below) — 1:1 on a 2× screen, crisp; the pointer maps pane CSS → the stage's own coordinates (offset and scale undone) → device px; a devicePixelRatio change (a `(resolution: Ndppx)` media query, re-armed at each ratio) relayouts every box and the minimum. The stage's contain-fit is no longer Watch-only: an ACTIVE picture whose app is larger than the pane (its minimum on a phone / a narrow cell) is scaled to fit and centred — never cropped — with the `.xpra-fit-badge` t('Scaled to fit — the app needs at least {w}×{h}'); unscaled it stays at 0,0 as before (the increment leftover right/bottom). `onMinSize({w,h}|null)` hands the window the smallest pane (`minPaneCss(the main's constraints, ratio)`); getters `fitBadge`, `ratio`, `minSize`. The cursor PNG is device px: at a ratio ≠ 1 it is re-declared as `image-set(url() Nx)` with the hotspot ÷ ratio after the plain url() (kept when a browser rejects the form). Gate: test-xpra-client §6 + test-desktop-xpra-window §6 (real rung, DPR 2).

**r2 (the verifier's findings on this view):** ① ACTIVE SCALES ONLY IN THE MINIMUM CASE — the contain-fit of an ACTIVE pane reads the MAIN window only and only when the app has a minimum (`minSize`): exactly the badge's condition, so an active scale is never silent, and a dialog larger than the pane no longer zooms the whole picture mid-session (Watch still contains every non-popup window). ② `FIT_SLACK_CSS` = 1: an overflow under one CSS px is not an overflow (a fractional ratio's rounding) — a sub-1 transform resamples the 1:1 picture. ③ THE DEVICE-PIXEL GRID: `gridNudge` moves the stage right/down by < 1 device px so its origin lands on a device pixel (a pane at CSS 65 is device 97.5 at DPR 1.5), re-read at every fit, on `pointerenter` and through `resnap()` (the window's `onMoved`); ④ each canvas backing is `backingSize(win, r)` with an explicit CSS box of backing ÷ r (a WHOLE CSS px — Chrome snaps a canvas's paint box to whole CSS px, so even an odd width at DPR 2, 697.5 CSS, was resampled: an xterm 18.6 % off), the < k-px transparent margin clipped by the window's own box. Measured after (a full screenshot vs the canvas, only pixels stable across the capture): DPR 1.5 — 9 / 12 / 229 of ~1.7 M pixels off at three window sizes (before: a 0.9995 transform + the badge, 4.18 %; with the transform gone but no grid/backing, 1.3–1.9 %); 1.25 and 1.75 likewise; DPR 2 unchanged. Gate: test-xpra-client §6b (the 1.5 fit identity + the canvas box 898×734 px; the oversized dialog; each with an r1 patched-copy control) + test-desktop-xpra-window §7 (a).

**x5 (2026-09-22):** the windows ride a STAGE (`.xpra-stage`, the pane now `isolation: isolate` so the blocked overlay sits above every window): identity while active, `scale(s)` in WATCH with s = min(pane / the non-popup windows' bounding box) — contain, never cropped (`stageScale`). `setMode(m)` sets the client's `viewOnly` / `watch` / `dormant` and, going active, hands the pane's size in once. A CUT (the Protocol.js close reason `4001: '<reason>'`) clears the windows and reconnects AT ONCE as a dormant viewer — never the ladder's 1 s, so the pane stays seated for re-election. **2.369.156 (the product's default, INFO b):** the Watch scale is CAPPED AT 1 and the stage CENTRED (`translate(ox, oy) scale(s)`, whole-pixel offsets; `stageOffset`) — a pane larger than the app shows it crisp at 1:1, never blown up (test-xpra-client §5 with the uncapped factor printed as the control; test-desktop-xpra-window §5 on a 1080×700 page). The vnc rung's picture is noVNC's `scaleViewport` (unchanged).


    xpra-view.js         — `createXpraView(host, {url, workerUrl, before, labels, autoReconnect, onStatus, onTitle, onIcon, Worker, decode, secure, clipboardApi, log})` → the shell's handles + `{pane, ime, chip, setViewOnly, windows(), client, chipText}`. On the shared shell (background `var(--bg-primary)`), a `.xpra-pane` (THEME colour — no root, no black; test-xpra-client §4 censuses no `#000` in the xpra files) holding ONE `.xpra-win` canvas per xpra window placed where the session says (a resize keeps the painted pixels until the server repaints), draws applied in order (image → drawImage at its rect, closed after; scroll → the canvas copied onto itself by each move), pointer from the PANE's own rect (viewport px == layout px at net zoom 1 — never mixed; capture on down; wheel prevented; contextmenu prevented), the keyboard through a hidden `.xpra-ime` textarea (focused on every pointerdown; keydown/keyup forwarded and prevented ONLY when sent — Ctrl+V is left to the browser so its `paste` event fires; `compositionend` and an `insertText` input event deliver IME text through `typeText`), a debounced (150 ms) ResizeObserver ⇒ `client.resize`, the app's title/icon (PNG bytes → `pngDataUrl`, a validated base64 data URL) handed to the caller, cursor packets as a `url()` cursor. CLIPBOARD (owner acceptance 2): the `paste` event's text ⇒ `pasteText` (works on plain http); the Paste chip is the SHELL's flow (a secure context reads the async API; plain http / a refusal / an empty clipboard opens the shell's paste box, then Send ⇒ `pasteText`, the focus back on the app — measured with REAL pastes on a hostname page); a copy inside the app ⇒ `shell.deliverCopy` (the API on a secure context with a toast; on plain http a token inside the user's own copy-chord gesture window is written with no click (Round 3, A1 above); else — and when the API refuses — the shell's "Copied in the app — click to copy" chip; a refused execCommand keeps the chip and says so). Status: "Waiting for the application window…" after the hello, "Connected" at the first window, "The application closed its window" when the last goes, "Connection lost: <the server's reason>" in red + the shell's ladder. Gate: test-xpra-client §3 (the fake DOM, both clipboard branches) + test-desktop-xpra-window (heavy, the real rung).

### desktop-window.js — THE SINGLETON DESKTOP WINDOW, ON THE SHARED COMPONENT

    desktop-window.js    — the in-container desktop window (noVNC through the cookie-authed ws bridge — since 2026-09-13 the singleton id on src/server/desktop-stream.js, url `streamUrl('/api/vnc')`). Decides only WHAT to show and gates the connect on POST /api/vnc/start (`{ok:false, error: st?.error || null}` ⇒ the server's own text in the chip, e.g. "no VNC server installed (Xtigervnc/Xvnc not on PATH)"); the picture, the counter-zoom, the bar, clipboard and the status transitions are vnc-view.js. Singleton per client (`_isDesktop`). `registerWindowType({type:'desktop', singleton:true, action:'openDesktop'})` unchanged. Behaviour is byte-for-byte the pre-extraction window — test-vnc-view §2 proves it against the retired file.

### desktop-app-window.js — THE `desktop-app` WINDOW (§2 row 7)

**Round 3, A2 (2.369.166 — the app's exit closes this window; the outer ✕ is the app's own close; docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless.md §3.2, the owner: "我关闭内部窗口之后外部窗口还要额外关闭一次").** `decideExit(r)` runs on every record this window applies (the broadcast, the stop's answer, a reconnect's re-read, the FIRST GET) and decides ONCE (`exitDecided` — a lease dropping later never re-decides): PURE `exitCloseVerdict(r, {leased: !!lease})`; close ⇒ `showToast(exitToastText(r, name))` — "Calculator exited" / "… stopped" / "… stopped after N min without input" / "… stopped: <why>" (textContent: the name is the app's own title) — then `app.wm.closeWindow` (programmatic, never vetoed; every client closes its own copy from its own broadcast, the layout autosave then carries the removal); keep ⇒ the ended sentence as before. `closed` makes every late answer a no-op. THE FIRST GET: a `not-found` answer (the keeper pruned the record) closes with "This desktop app no longer exists"; an exited record closes before the window ever paints — the window is born `desktop-app-pending` (style.css: opacity 0, no pointer; a 3 s timer reveals it if the GET never answers), so a layout replay of a dead record opens NO window. THE OUTER ✕: `winInfo.onCloseRequest` (WindowManager.requestClose asks it on every USER close) → PURE `outerCloseVerdict` over the record, `seatState()`, the lease, the view's connection and `client.mainWid`: `ask-app` ⇒ `view.closeApp()` + the toast "Asked {app} to close — press ✕ again within 5 s to stop it" and the window stays (a packet the socket refused ⇒ the pane closes as before); `stop` ⇒ the existing Stop (`stopApp`, shared with the bar's button); `close` ⇒ true. Measured on the real rung (test-desktop-xpra-window §10, two clients): the calculator's OWN ✕ ⇒ the window gone on both pages 1028–1033 ms after the click (two runs), toast "Calculator exited" on each; the outer ✕ ⇒ `close-window` ⇒ the calculator process gone 257–775 ms and both windows 231–750 ms after the click; a Tk app answering WM_DELETE_WINDOW with its own "Save?" dialog keeps everything (the dialog closing is not the app exiting), the second ✕ 1.5–1.8 s later ⇒ stopped, both windows gone 416–738 ms; a blocked pane's ✕ never asks the app; a dead record replayed from the layout: created pending, never revealed, closed with its toast. CONTROL: a copy whose close line is pulled back leaves the dead picture ("Exited: application exited (code 0)") — M3c's measurement before A2. **A r1:** an app that ignores the ask needs the second ✕ — measured with xterm (§10 (3b)): an interactive bash ends on the first ✕ (both windows gone 375–418 ms, two runs), a child that ignores SIGHUP keeps it (still ready 2 s after the first ✕, the second ✕ 3.0 s later ⇒ Stop, both windows gone 846–847 ms); the toast already names the second ✕, so the window never looks dead.


**HiDPI + the app's minimum (2.369.158, docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md §7.6; the owner's 2026-09-23 GNOME Calculator report on a devicePixelRatio-2 screen):** the xpra view gets `dpi: () => rec.dpi` and `onMinSize: applyMinSize` — the minimum pane + this window's own chrome (outer rect − pane rect, VIEWPORT px) → `windowMinForPane(…, uiScale())` (layout px) → `app.wm.setMinSize(winInfo.id, min)`; a window that is not rendered (another desktop, minimized, a background tab) is re-measured when it is laid out again (r2 — the ResizeObserver below; the r1 bounded 500 ms × 40 retry gave up after 20 s); `winInfo._desktopMinPane` is the suites' raw handle. `scaleChipText(rec)` + the `.desktop-app-chip-scale` chip (`2×` on an xpra record, `flex-shrink: 0` so it never ellipsises at the minimum width; tooltip: a change takes effect at the next launch); the backend chip's tooltip on the xpra stream adds t('xpra streams each app window as pixels; text stays crisp at your screen’s scale'). Gate: test-window-minsize §3 pins + test-desktop-xpra-window §6.

**r2 (the verifier's low finding: the minimum was a one-time snapshot of the chrome):** `applyMinNow` is re-run (rAF-coalesced `scheduleMin`) by ONE ResizeObserver on the window element, the title bar, the view's status strip and the pane — a chrome height change (the UI font scale, a wrapping strip) and a window laid out again after display:none both resize something observed — and by the `vs:ui-scale` window event (utils.applyUiPrefs announces a CHANGE; layout px = viewport ÷ the scale), bound to the window's AbortController signal; the observer is disconnected on close. `winInfo.onMoved = () => view.resnap()` puts a moved window's picture back on the device-pixel grid. The window's minimum is CAPPED AT THE WORKSPACE by window.js (see there): a DPR-1 client taking over a 2× app gets a window that fits the screen and the picture scaled to fit with the badge.

**x5 (2026-09-22) — ONE ACTIVE VIEWER** (docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md §7 P8-2 / §7.5 "x5 多客户端 = 单活跃 viewer", the owner's ruling "直接block掉非active客户端的app界面…" + "仿照terminal…可以手动take over"): the pane's state = PURE `paneState` over the lease + the `desktop-app-viewers` broadcast (one GET `…/viewers` at open and on every ws reconnect; `winInfo._desktopSeats` is the suites' raw handle). The pane names itself with a stable PUBLIC `pane` key (`pn-…`, `?pane=` on every upgrade beside the per-socket secret viewer id; `winInfo._desktopPaneKey`). BLOCKED ⇒ the `.desktop-app-blocked` overlay (house `.term-blocked-*` classes — the terminal's Resume here): the app's title as TEXT (peer-controlled), t('Active on another client'), a `Resume here` button; the mount's other children hidden (`desktop-app-is-blocked`), the view in `setMode('blocked')`. RESUME HERE flips the pane LOCALLY first (`optimistic`, ≤ 8 s) — never waiting for the broadcast echo — then POSTs `…/viewers/takeover`; the answer (or the broadcast) corrects it, a refusal toasts and restores. WATCH (an agent drives) ⇒ the picture scaled to fit with the existing badge; a click there is still the hint toast (only in watch — the overlay's own button never toasts). `renderSeat()` is the ONE place the state reaches the view; a cut pane that is still wanted reconnects from there too.


**r-fix (2026-09-21):** `viewerId` is re-minted per connect through the url function and never leaves the pane except on its own upgrade/takeover/handback bodies; `myTag` = the tag my takeover answer carried, cleared on my handback; every mode read compares tags.

    **P9b (2026-09-21) — THE `window-live` FORM.** The same window grows the browser live view's three modes when an agent holds a lease on the app: the badge (`browser-live-mode`, the exact three phrases through PURE `windowModeBadge`), Take over / Hand back (the desktop routes, this pane's `viewerId` — `newViewerId()`, put on the stream upgrade as `?viewer=` AND on the takeover so the lease names the viewer and the bridge hands back when that socket closes), the §6.6 class marker chip "VibeSpace-started window" (the other class never appears here; the tooltip says the user's own desktop is never listed), the holder chip "Agent: <name>" ("Agent gone: <name>" for an orphaned lease), the title "<label> — agent window"; noVNC `rfb.viewOnly` = `windowLiveMode({lease, viewerId}).viewOnly` (Watch, or somebody else driving) re-applied on connect and on every lease change — the client MIRRORS the server's verdict, it never enforces it (the bridge drops the input regardless); a pointerdown on the picture in Watch is a throttled hint toast. The lease arrives on `window-leases-updated` (a GET at open + on every ws reconnect); toasts by PURE `leaseTransition` (took-over / handed-back / lapsed / other-took). A window nobody leases shows none of it and behaves exactly as before (never view-only). Gate: the PURE half in test-window-target §1; the chrome leg is owed to test-desktop-app-window.

    desktop-app-window.js — `openDesktopApp(app, id, {syncId})`: one window per app session (`win._desktopAppId`; a second call focuses), `registerWindowType({type:'desktop-app', action:'openDesktopApp'})` with openSpec `{action:'openDesktopApp', id}` — so layout sync replays it on every other client and on reload (N viewers on one `-shared` display), it can enter a tab group like any window, and test-window-types pins the kind + action + owner. The picture is `createVncView` on `/api/desktop/<id>/stream` with `before` = the record gate (launching ⇒ "Starting application…"; exited/failed ⇒ `endedText`), `autoReconnect: true`. The bar adds: the backend chip `backendChipText` = `vnc-display (xpra not on PATH)` (the user must know whether this is one window or a whole display — §3), `liveChipText` CPU/RSS and `idleChipText` the countdown — both READ from the `desktop-apps-updated` broadcast (one GET at open; the countdown ticks locally from `lastInputAt + idleTimeoutMs`), Keep running (POST keep-alive) and Stop (POST stop; a terminal record disconnects the view and shows `Stopped` / `Exited (code N)` / `Failed: why`). `applyRecord` connects whenever the record is READY and the picture is not up (state not connected/connecting/starting), and the window re-reads its record on every main-ws reconnect — a server restart ADOPTS the session before any client reconnects, so the adoption broadcast reaches nobody; measured in the heavy suite: the SAME open window comes back with zero clicks. Labels reach the title through `setTitle` (textContent) and every list through escHtml. No iframe remains.** **x4 (2026-09-22): `fitChipText(rec)` + the `.desktop-app-chip-fit` chip — ONLY a record whose `fitMode` is 'fixed' prints (`fixed 1280x800 (Xvfb) — install tigervnc for a window that follows`, the geometry from the keeper's measured `fb`, the binary from `via`'s first group member; zh+ja; the title explains the scale) — a display that follows (Xvnc, xpra) shows nothing: the picture is the app and it follows. The stream url carries `&prev=<pane>` — the pane key this TAB's previous window of the app had (sessionStorage `vibespace.desktopPane.<id>`), the keeper's grace successor on a page reload.

**Round 3, A3 (2.369.166 — the scale, derived and per window; docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless.md §3.4, the owner: "内部app的dpi也应该是可调的，最好是能从vibespace自身的dpi自动推导").** The chip prints the value AND its origin (`scaleChipText`: "2.5× · auto" / "1.5× · chosen" / "2× · Settings"; a pre-A3 record the number alone) and its tooltip the numbers (`scaleChipTitle`: dpr × UI scale for auto, widgets = GDK_SCALE, text dpi). A pick asks first (showConfirmDialog: "The app restarts at the new scale; unsaved work in it is lost." / Relaunch) and POSTs `…/relaunch {scale, dpr, uiScale}`; the answer's `app.id` RETARGETS the window at once (never waiting for the echo): `retarget(nextId)` disposes the view, resets every per-record fact (rec, exit decision, the ✕ ask, seats, lease, the minimum), swaps `id` / `_desktopAppId` / `_openSpec` (+ `wm._notify()` so the layout carries it), re-claims the pane hint and re-reads the record — same window, same place, the picture reconnects. `followReplacement` runs FIRST on every applied record and on the first GET: a record naming `replacedBy` retargets (every other client from its broadcast; a layout replay of a replaced id follows the chain); a window already showing the successor closes this one quietly (no duplicate).
