### jobs-layout.js

    jobs-layout.js       — PURE (imports nothing, DOM-free) the Background Work panel's TRIAGE arithmetic (docs/design-background-work.md §13, 2026-09-14; the user-todos-layout.js precedent — every decision the panel used to make inline, twice, lives here once): `attentionOf(job)` → awaiting | unacked-failure | acked-failure | null (a parked SERVICE can never be acknowledged — it needs a start — so it stays an unacked failure); `badgeCounts(jobs)` / `badgeText` = the ONE counter the rail badge and both panel summaries read (red = awaiting-user + UNACKNOWLEDGED failed|missed|unverified, grey = "N seen"); `familyOf(name)` = the name-family rule (a trailing ` run`, `-r<n>`, `-v<n>`, `-<n>` and version-like tails stripped until the name is stable; table-tested); `foldTasks(tasks, {expanded, sessionNames})` = owner session (sidebar display name > short id > "created by you") → family → rows, `defaultExpanded` only when the group holds a running / awaiting-user / unacknowledged row, the persisted folds applied AFTER the defaults; `pruneFolds(folds, layout)` = the user-state `jobsPanelFolds` map minus every key no live group holds (a stale fold would grow user state without bound); `heldText(digest, {t, cid})` = the held-notification sentence from the server's STRUCTURE (`{total, byConversation}`), words by the device's own t() — the server cannot say them, the digest is broadcast to every client while the language is per device. Invariants: the client READS `job.ack` and never derives acknowledgement (the server computes it over the full record; the snapshot's journal is truncated); one counter, one fold rule, both surfaces. Gated by test-job-model (137) + test-jobs-panel.

### stage-manager.js

    stage-manager.js   — StageManager (2.112.0 dynamic desktop 'Stage', default OFF via desktop.dynamicEnabled — docs/design-dynamic-desktop.md is the blueprint+progress anchor. VIEW model: one window two geometries (home gridBounds vs shared slot); materialization intercepts wm.focusWindow (_stageBypass prevents recursion; createWindow's tail focus flows through it too); per-hero aux workspaces = {openSpec, stageBounds, extras(scroll walker)} in SyncStore 'stage' (slot/ws:<key>/lru), heroKey RE-DERIVED AT RECORD TIME (backendSessionId arrives late); placeholder is a REAL wm window type 'stage-placeholder' — onWindowCreated MUST check the TYPE, the _isStagePlaceholder flag lands after createWindow's tail hook (smoke-caught: placeholder got swept as transient); incoming hero z-stacks at BOTTOM (moved slot must not cover a recorded workspace); LRU evicts hidden AUX only — session windows are NEVER closed by the stage (userW's killed-session lesson); desktop autosave is SUPPRESSED while staged (layout.js gate) — stage state never leaks into desktop records; userW's four defenses ported: serialized latest-wins switches, keyed replay dedup 15s, programmatic-switch guard, separate _hiddenByStage flag. RESTORATION MATRIX (2.112.1-2, design §4b, all 17 openSpec actions): durable=file/info-probed then replayed; derived=archive-entry temps carry via:{archive,entry} recipe and RE-EXTRACT on replay (the zip-PDF case); volatile=blob/data pages+recipe-less temps+DIRTY EDITORS (winInfo._editorDirty(), CodeEditor.modified exposed 2.112.2) are NEVER LRU-evicted and skip+one-toast when dead at replay; deleted task groups + 404 workflows pre-checked. INIT-ORDER GOTCHA (2.112.3, real 'placeholder never moves' report): stage.init() MUST run after initStateSync — StateSync.set() SILENTLY DROPS writes for unregistered stores, so the slot never persisted while dragging worked fine; _sync() lazily registers the store on any access as the guard. Any new SyncStore consumer needs the same care. **2.112.4 field fixes (4 user reports, CDP-smoke-verified — do not regress):** ① leave()/_deactivateHero HAND THE HERO BACK to the desktop system — restore _stageHomeBounds→gridBounds, clear _isStageHero/_onStage (off-stage moves edit HOME bounds, not the slot), then dm._hideWin/target-show like a normal desktop window (bare _hideStage left it invisible on its home desktop AND at slot size — the reported bug); enter() re-borrows via the still-set _heroWinId with a FRESH home snapshot; STAGE_ID-created heroes have no home and stay stage-hidden; _materializeInner clears stale _hiddenByDesktop. ② stage grid persists via stage-store key 'grid' — the interception lives at the TOP of scheduleAutoSave (NOT _doAutoSave: the _restoring gates dropped the call before the stage gate ran, smoke-caught); enter() applies it. ③ stage↔desktop window drags blocked BOTH directions (user directive superseding the design-§4 unbind+move): stage.dragToDesktopBlocked(win) gates window.js preview hover + dm.moveWindowToDesktop (covers the right-click menu too); placeholder additionally healStray()-recaptured + excluded from captureState (real report: escaped placeholder stuck on a desktop). ④ desktop.dynamicEnabled applies LIVE (init() settings listener → render kick / leave-if-disabled); same class fixed in sidebar for sessionCard.* card-build-time settings — a liveApply:true schema flag is a CLAIM, every render-time-read setting needs a change listener that re-renders its surface. **2.112.5 MULTI-CLIENT (real cross-client window-loss report — do not regress):** materializing a session with NO local window used to mint a stage-owned hero under a FRESH winId; leaving to the desktop holding that session per OTHER clients' records captured a state missing the recorded winId → the broadcast CLOSED the window on every client. Fix = IDENTITY ADOPTION: `_adoptDesktopIdentity` scans dm._savedStates for the session and converges (wm.rekeyWindow onto the recorded winId — chain-less windows only — + home desktop/gridBounds/isMaximized), retried at leave/_deactivateHero for late ids (resume fills openSpec async). Structural gotchas: createWindow's TAIL focus runs materialization BEFORE app.js's desktop-tag wrapper assigns _desktopId (adoption gate accepts !win._desktopId; the wrapper must not clobber an id set during creation); maximized heroes un-maximize onto the slot and hand-back applies home element geometry BEFORE re-maximizing (toggleMaximize must record HOME px as prevBounds). Live sync: init() subscribes 'stage'/'*' (StateSync fires for REMOTE ops only) — slot → re-apply to occupant, grid → setGrid, ws:<activeHeroKey> → debounced _reconcileWorkspace (restore + close-absent aux, dirty editors exempt); _scheduleRecord(500ms) on aux create/move keeps records live. **Hero is SHARED across clients (2.112.6, user directive — 挂机/walk-over): 'hero' store key {key, openSpec}; _publishHero at materialize (skip while _applyingRemoteHero), _followRemoteHero on remote ops (pointer-down deferred) + at enter (shared hero WINS over the tab's stale hero); hero close → clear → placeholder everywhere; only staged-or-not stays per-tab. closeWindow auto-focus-next (and applyLayout/overlap filters) must skip _hiddenByStage — a stage-hidden previous hero got auto-focused on hero close and re-materialized fleet-wide (harness-caught).** **2.151.0 preview fixes (2nd ghost report — do not regress):** ① the 2.134.0 home-bounds substitution in dm._renderSwitcher read `_stageHomeBounds?.gridBounds` but _stageHomeBounds IS the flat bounds object → always undefined → hero ghost-painted at the SLOT position on its home preview for 17 releases (shape-mismatch no-op; now reads the flat shape); ② the preview render DIGEST must cover every field the render filters on — _hiddenByDesktop/_hiddenByStage/_onStage were missing, so leave()'s intermediate setGrid-triggered render (target windows still hidden) cached a BLANK preview and the post-show render early-returned (preview stayed white until visiting another desktop); leave() also mirrors switchTo's +400/+1300ms refreshSwitcher retries. COMMITTED smoke: scripts/test-stage-preview.mjs (throwaway git-worktree server + headless-chrome raw CDP, 9 assertions through the REAL materialize/leave paths — replaces the ephemeral harnesses). Verified: 2-CDP-client harness 10/10 + single-client 11/11 — harness needs --disable-background-timer-throttling + real per-client input for _userDirty. **2.209.0 pile-at-slot rootfix (userW's 超级重叠 — Stage↔desktop round trip stacked every stage-born session at the slot, accumulating per trip; repro'd 16/16 then fixed, scripts/test-stage-overlap.mjs): ① enter() re-shows ONLY the live workspace (remembered hero + aux bound to _heroKey/'__pending__') — the blanket every-_hiddenByStage re-show resurrected every slot-PARKED ex-hero; ② _borrowHero ALWAYS creates a home snapshot BEFORE applying the slot (a window born while staged has no gridBounds at the synchronous creation-tail borrow → pixel _captureGridBounds first — safe, stage flags not yet set — else _cascadeHome(); slot-near bounds never become home) and _handBackHero has a cascade belt for pre-fix degenerated field state — without this the slot was the window's ONLY geometry forever; ③ dm.switchTo routes through stage.leave()/enter() while staged and treats '__stage__' as never-a-target — a raw switchTo (add-desktop +, command-mode d/D, moveSessionWindow, _onRemoteDesktopUpdated) captured the stage's window set under desktops['__stage__'] (lazy-replayed later as REAL windows at slot bounds) and left stage._active desynced; client boot + server layout-sync both refuse-and-scrub the poisoned record; ④ _onRemoteDesktopUpdated exempts STAGE_ID windows from deleted-desktop reassignment (any remote desktop meta change used to retag the whole stage onto a normal desktop) and never force-switches a staged client; ⑤ _materializeInner aborts when !_active (queued materialize firing post-leave); ⑥ leave() validates the target desktop still exists (remote-deleted _prevDesktopId). KNOWN MINOR (parked): stale shared-hero follow — _publishHero early-returns on null _heroKey with no retry at id adoption, so multi-client walk-over can follow an outdated hero record.**

### session-palette.js

    session-palette.js — Ctrl+K session palette (fuzzy session switcher; installSessionPalette, desktop only). **SEARCH IS TOKENISED (2.249.1, userW inc-msjro90z-n6y3 — never regress to whole-query matching):** the query splits on whitespace with AND semantics; NAME hits (1000-pos) outrank path/host/id hits (300) outrank a fuzzy subsequence (100) CONFINED TO THE NAME. Matching the query as ONE literal string meant a space could never substring-hit a CamelCase/hyphenated name ("best ever" vs "BestEver-ToB-signing"), so EVERY multi-word query fell through to a subsequence over the whole haystack (name + cwd + 3 UUIDs) — a shared cwd prefix supplies almost any letter sequence, so unrelated sessions all tied at the same low score. Compounding it, the live bonus was `+1000` on that tie, sorting every live session above every stopped one, and `slice(0,12)` cut the list before the wanted STOPPED session could appear. Ranking is now `sc*1000 + (live?500:0)` — match quality dominates, live only breaks ties among equally-good matches. Fuzzy-matching against a UUID is pure noise; never re-add it. Test: scripts/test-session-palette-search.mjs (11 asserts on the real reported data).

### collab-row.js (PURE, B-7473)

  src/collab-row.js — the label/HTML builder for codex multi-agent collab rows. PURE tier, **zero requires** (CJS pulled into the bundle like ssh-key-format.js): the escaper, the translator and the icon set are INJECTED. That is not ceremony — it makes the XSS rule *verifiable*: scripts/test-codex-subagents ① passes a MARKER escaper and asserts that nothing outside the markers is model-controlled, then repeats with the real `escHtml` semantics. `collabRowParts` splits a row into `{pre, name, post}` so the plain-text label (which lands in the message's `tool_result` output → search previews, fold summaries, the minimap) and the HTML row can never drift; `collabRowsHtml` renders one row or the coalesced summary + one clickable chip per agent; `collabRowTitle` is the hover envelope and says *payload encrypted upstream* when the body was withheld. A row NEVER carries an encrypted blob. The default translator substitutes `{n}` so server-side text is complete without a client `t()`. **LIVE PROGRESS READOUT (2026-09-07, owner: “这种互聊如果连续发生是不是应该界面里展示下连续数量，这样我好知道对话没卡住”):** dozens of ENCRYPTED one-line rows over minutes with no assistant text between them are indistinguishable from a wedged turn, so the module gained the composers every progress surface reads — `collabTrafficStats` (count / distinct agents / first+last row `ts` / `messagesOnly`, i.e. every row is mail vs a mixed set that must say “sub-agent events”), `collabAgeText` (1s granularity under a minute, whole FLOORED minutes above — “is it moving”, not a stopwatch), `collabSpanText` (“4 min 12 s”), `collabCountParts` (REAL singular keys — never “1 messages”), `collabHeadText`, `collabRunPart` (the run-label segment) and `subAgentStreamLabel` (the spinner line). NOTHING is stored and nothing is counted into a field: every number is derived from the rows the normalizer already stamped, so a second client renders identical text off the same message state. LIVE and FROZEN differ ONLY in the last segment — a ticking `last {age} ago` while the turn runs, the absolute `over {span}` once it stops — and a row with no usable `ts` DROPS the segment rather than inventing a clock (never “over 0 s”). `collabRowsHtml` puts the head in its OWN `.chat-collab-head` element so the view's single ticker rewrites just that text (re-rendering the card would drop the fold state the user opened), and a LONE row still renders its full `agent · TYPE` label — summarising one event only loses information, and the owner's ask is about CONTINUOUS chatter, which is the coalesced shape by construction. `collabSummaryText` (the stored `tool_result` output that search previews and the minimap read) is the SAME composer in its frozen form, so the words on screen and the words in the index cannot drift. `collabRowTitle` now leads with `Time: <clock> (record timestamp|arrival time)`: the normalizer's `_stampRowTime` takes the RECORD's own timestamp when it has one (`recordTs`, which returns null instead of `toTs`'s silent `Date.now()`) and the arrival time otherwise — saying WHICH is the point, or a burst replayed from a rebuild would read as “just now”. **THREE SURFACES = THREE SCOPES (2026-09-07 r2, and they are MEANT to differ):** `collabHeadText` counts ONE coalesced card, `collabRunPart` the folded RUN, `subAgentStreamLabel` the whole TURN — a card that stopped growing at 4 events sits inside a run of 5 while the spinner counts the turn's 5, so all three are honest and only the one that floats FREE of the thing it counts has to say which scope it means (“Sub-agents working — 5 sub-agent events **this turn**, last 4s ago”); the other two are read inside their own container. Do not "fix" the divergence by making the card head turn-scoped — two cards would then both claim the turn's total. Gate: scripts/test-collab-live-counter.mjs ①②.

### chat-view.js
  chat-view.js — ChatView controller (virtual scroll, op dispatch, lifecycle; gap-seek mixin in chat-view-seek.js). FOLD KINDS (2.369.33; chat.collapseKinds, semantic, one set for every backend): thinking/bash/read/write/memory/mcp/skill/agent/search/image — memberKind() maps claude tool names (Bash→bash, Read→read, Write/Edit/Patch→write, Grep/Glob/LS→read, WebSearch/WebFetch→search, Read of an image file→image (2.369.34), ToolSearch→mcp, Skill→skill, Agent/Task→agent, mcp__*→mcp) while codex/ACP cards arrive with `collapseKind` stamped by their normalizer (codex web_search/web_fetch→search, view_image→image; ACP kind search→search). The run header's byKind counter must list EVERY kind the classifier returns — an unlisted kind counts NaN and vanishes from the summary (2.369.34). INVARIANT: a tool card whose kind resolves to null is not merely unfolded — it BREAKS the run around it (the 42-WebSearch session had nothing folded); every new tool name needs a kind. Users who customised the kinds list must tick a new kind themselves (sparse settings keep their explicit list). **MSG-META POPUP (2026-09-06, codex per-message meta):** `_showMsgMeta` is backend-neutral — additive rows only when the meta carries them: 'Reasoning tokens' (`usage.reasoning_output_tokens`), 'Effort' (`meta.effort`), the cache-write row falls back to codex's `usage.cache_write_input_tokens` when there is no claude `cache_creation` TTL split (claude usage never has that field ⇒ unchanged), and the id labels follow the normalizer's kind markers — `requestIdKind:'ledger'` ⇒ 'Ledger request key' (the cx synthetic key is never dressed as a vendor request id), `msgIdKind:'response'` ⇒ 'Response ID'; claude meta has no kinds ⇒ old labels. Users who customised the kinds list must tick a new kind themselves (sparse settings keep their explicit list). **RUN CHROME (2.369.37, expanded-run legibility — see kb-features Chat Mode for the DOM shape):** `_updateRuns` rebuilds `this._runs` = `[{header, members, footer, label, open}]` every pass; `_setRunOpen(run, open)` is the ONE writer of `.chat-run-collapsed` / `.chat-run-member` / `-first` / `-last` and of the `.chat-run-footer` (inserted after the last member only while open); header AND footer are non-`.chat-msg` list children that every pass removes (`:scope > .chat-run-header, :scope > .chat-run-footer`) — so `_withViewportAnchor` and the seek gap anchor SKIP them as anchor candidates (a run-chrome anchor is dead after any pass inside fn → estimate-skewed delta fallback; members are only class-toggled and stay stable). The floating `.chat-run-bar` (lazily created on the `.chat-view` container, never in the list) is updated by `_updateRunBar(scrollTop)` from the scroll handler's rAF — placed BEFORE the `_programmaticScroll` early return, with the frame's already-read scrollTop, header/footer offsets read in the same layout pass; `_scheduleRunBar` (rAF-coalesced) re-runs it after each pass / setRunOpen / resume; `setSuspended(true)` hides it; dispose cancels the rAF. Bar/footer collapse = `_collapseRunTo` → `_setRunOpen(false)` + `_landOnHeader` (absolute `scrollTop = header.offsetTop` under a 400ms `_programmaticScroll` mute via `_jumpGuardTimer`, `_lastStructuralAt` stamped with dir null, pin re-derived from the landing). **Toggling a run OUTSIDE a pass is itself a childList mutation (the footer) and must be hidden from the observer exactly the way a pass drains its own records** (2026-09-06 adversarial review, measured in headless chrome: on a PINNED view with 2+ runs, clicking any header except the last opened the run and re-collapsed it ~180ms later). A user click is not a pass, so the footer record scheduled one, and that pass's PINNED AUTO-REFOLD (`built.slice(0, -1)` — while `_pinned`, only the LAST run keeps an open flag, so a run expanded to watch the live tail re-folds once the tail moves past it, 2.227.x “一部分没折叠”) closed the run the click had just opened: every non-last header was a no-op while pinned. `_setRunOpen` now sets `_runsMutating` around the footer insert/remove when called outside a pass and calls `takeRecords()` only if it REALLY mutated (never swallow an unrelated pending record), and a deliberate toggle on a NON-LAST run marks its members in `_runStickyOpen` — a WeakSet keyed by member element like `_runExpanded`, because run records are rebuilt every pass; the auto-refold skips marked runs and nothing else, collapsing (header/footer/bar) clears the mark, and an INHERITED open flag still re-folds. The anchor restore is unaffected (it anchors on the first non-chrome visible element). Overlay hygiene: the floating bar shares the list's top edge with `.chat-pos-indicator` AND the history-load pill `.chat-history-status` — both are positioned by chat.css (the load pill lost its inline `top`, which no selector could have overridden) and both drop to `top:34px` (42px ≤768px) under `.chat-view.chat-run-bar-on`, the transient overlap being paging up INSIDE an open run. **Fixture law learned here: a browser fixture with ONE run cannot reach the multi-run branches** — 51 asserts were green over a broken interaction; test-fold-ux now builds two runs (the long tool run + a short mcp run after a text turn) and pins first-run-stays-open at t+600ms and across an explicit pass, the last run's unchanged behaviour, and the inherited-flag negative control. Rules that must hold: the bar never calls `_extendTop/_extendBottom/_trim*` or writes `_pinned` (test-fold-ux greps its body); no Esc binding (data-popover protocol); the footer never counts toward the rendered window (trims select `.chat-msg:not(.chat-gap-msg)`). **SHORT-VIEW RESCUE after attach (2.369.43)**: content that doesn't fill the viewport has no scrollable range, so the scroll handler never runs and touch has no wheel-up path — a fold-dominated slab (50 cards collapsed into two run headers) is a dead end with thousands of unreachable messages above. `_shortViewNeedsFill(list)` is the decision (more history above, no scrollable range, not suspended/disposed/teleported, and `rendered + 50 <= 150` so the extra page can never trip a trim onto the live tail) and `_scheduleAttachFill()` takes TWO readings 700ms/1600ms after loadHistory, extending only if both agree and `_lastStructuralAt` didn't move between them — the collapsed-geometry artifact that motivated the 2.369.36 hardening is transient and cannot survive the second reading. The 2.369.36 form (`rendered < 30`) was UNSATISFIABLE — every attach ships tail(50) and folding hides members without removing them, so the rescue was dead code; both timers clear in dispose(). Because chat-view.js is DOM-free at import, the predicate + schedule are FUNCTIONALLY tested against fake geometry in scripts/test-chat-trim-guard.mjs. A Read is 'image' only when its RESULT carried image blocks (`content[0].images`) — EVIDENCE, never the extension (image-card review round 2: 12/12 real `Read *.svg` results in the fleet are numbered TEXT, and an extension rule both mis-counted them and let them escape the fold); codex/ACP arrive with `collapseKind` stamped. **THE IMAGE MEMBER IS EXEMPT FROM THE FOLD, NOT THE RUN (2.369.43 → image-card review round 2):** 'image' ships ON in the default kinds and the "any tool card folds, even a lone one" rule applied to it too, so every media card landed inside "1 image read" — `display:none`, invisible until clicked, and its `loading="lazy"` thumbnail never even fetched (the owner asked to SEE the image). The first cut exempted whole runs made ONLY of image views, which is the RARE shape — in real sessions the card sits BETWEEN foldable cards (Bash → Read(png) → Bash) and stayed hidden. So `flush()` computes `run.inline` = the image-kind members: they stay members of the run for every other purpose (rail, first/last, sticky mark, the floating bar's span, the summary's "N image reads") but `_setRunOpen` never gives them `.chat-run-collapsed`, so the fold closes AROUND them. A run with nothing left to fold (every member an image) gets no header at all — a fold control that hides nothing is a dead control. Pinned by test-image-cards ⑦ + the test-fold-ux browser fixture (bash|image|bash: the media card's computed display is not 'none' and its `<img>` really loads, while the Bash cards fold under the header). MEDIA THUMBNAILS: the list carries a CAPTURE-phase `error` delegate (img error does not bubble) that flags a broken `.chat-tool-img`'s `.chat-media` as `.chat-media-broken` (CSS swaps the img for the honest line) — rendered HTML never carries inline handlers; the fold's `display:none` is what keeps `loading="lazy"` thumbnails of a collapsed run from fetching. **COLLAB CLICK-THROUGH (B-7473):** a message carrying `collab` renders through chat-renderers `_renderCollabMsg` (report card / compact rows, src/collab-row.js does the escaping); the agent NAME (`.chat-collab-name`, data-agent-path + data-thread-id) is delegated in the messageList click handler to `_openCollabAgent`, which opens the child's rollout in the EXISTING sub-agent viewer when the thread id is known (0.153.4 always knows it — SubAgentActivity.agent_thread_id) and otherwise asks `GET /api/subagents?backend=codex&threadId=<root>` and TOASTS when the child is not on this machine (never a silent no-op). The run header gains `{n} sub-agent messages` (counting `collab.rows[].dir === 'in'`) and a `{n} sub-agents: …` chip list built from the run's rows — those chips get their OWN onclick with `stopPropagation()`, because the header's click toggles the fold, and they de-duplicate on `row.agentPath`, which the normalizer normalises to an ABSOLUTE path for every direction (round-5 fix: outbound rows keyed the bare `task_name` and one agent drew two chips). **The two B-7473 summary lines live in the PURE module like every other line (integration 2026-09-06 + round-5 rebase):** `'report'` — a sub-agent's written answer — is a REAL fold kind in `RUN_KINDS`/`SUMMARY_ORDER` (offered in `chat.collapseKinds` but shipping UNCHECKED, because a report is the content the window was opened to read; the one-line rows stay `'agent'`, which IS default-on), and the inbound-message count is `SUMMARY_EXTRAS = ['subAgentIn']` — a count the CALLER assigns into `byKind` (never produced by `messageKind`, never zero-filled, so an unset one renders nothing and can never go NaN) whose position in the label is decided by the same single `SUMMARY_ORDER`. chat-view NEVER keeps a second kind table. **THE QUEUE CHIP'S CAPABILITY ARRIVES AFTER THE PIXELS (2026-09-06, round-3 review):** the chip on a user bubble is built by `renderUserMsg`, which asks the view (`getQueueCaps` → `_queueCaps()` = harness `inputModes` ∧ the RUNNING wrapper's `_queueSupported`) and hands `applyQueueChip` a null handler when the answer is no — which renders it `disabled`. `_queueSupported` starts FALSE and BOTH of its sources land AFTER the bubbles: `loadHistory` renders every message and calls `_applyLiveMeta` (the attach payload's `queueSupported`) at the END, and a live wrapper's baseline `queue_changed` (`_onMeta` subtype 'queue', `supported:true`) arrives frames after the first messages. So after ANY history load the chip was permanently dead. `_setQueueSupported` is therefore the ONE writer of the flag and a change in EITHER direction schedules `_refreshQueueChips()` — rAF-coalesced, ONE pass over `_elements`, re-running `ChatRenderers.applyQueueChip` for every rendered message that carries a `queueState` (false→true makes them live, true→false makes them inert; the pending frame is cancelled in dispose()). The queue STRIP never had this bug because `_setQueue` re-renders it — the chips live inside bubbles nobody rebuilds. Gate: test-queue-steer ⑦ (render-then-deliver for both messengers + the reverse flip + a one-writer pin). **AUTO-SCROLL IS AUTOMATIC REPOSITIONING, AND IT MUST LOSE TO THE READER (B-9702, round 5 of the desktop-resume campaign):** `_forceScrollToBottom` writes `scrollTop = scrollHeight` for up to 10 frames (~166 ms) under the `_programmaticScroll` mute — the pinned view's auto-follow AND what every resume re-tail rung calls. It now carries an EPOCH: `_cancelForcedScroll(via)` bumps it and is called from `_notePositioning` and `_noteUserNav` (never from `_noteUserInput` — a click moves nothing), so every frame already queued is orphaned instead of writing scrollTop once more, while a later `_forceScrollToBottom` starts a fresh epoch so a cancel can never kill auto-follow. The mute is released ONE FRAME after the final write, guarded on `_fsbActive`: a scroll event is delivered after the callback that wrote it, so clearing the flag in the write's own frame handed our displacement to the boundary decision as if a reader had produced it. Without both, a re-tail rung armed at resume+1240 ms was still writing when the reader wheeled up at +1400 ms, its last frame landed 3 ms after their scroll, the pin re-engaged off our own write (`repin st:1760 … fsb:-1 posAgo:3` — ordinary geometry, `collapsedGeomSkip` never fired) and `_extendTop`'s pinned-tail invariant re-asserted the bottom: 5 of 20 real wheel-ups undone, 0 of 20 after. The `repin` trace (the twin of `unpin`) is what named it and stays. Gates: scripts/test-chat-trim-guard.mjs (DOM-free chain semantics against a fake rAF queue, including the "auto-follow survives a cancel" and "the mute is never permanent" controls) + the two +1400 ms wheel legs in scripts/test-desktop-resume-paging.mjs (the second arms a chain by hand for determinism, with `_cancelForcedScroll` neutered on the instance as its control). **LIVE SUB-AGENT TRAFFIC (2026-09-07, the same owner ask):** three surfaces read the ONE composer over three SCOPES — card / run / turn (they can legitimately show different numbers at the same instant; see collab-row.js, where the free-floating one names its scope). (i) the coalesced card's head — the renderer asks the view `isCollabLive(msg)` → `_liveCollabId()`, which is the LAST message and only while `_typingSince` is set (a view-only window has no live turn, so a stopped transcript is always frozen; the moment anything else arrives the burst is over and the card freezes). (ii) the run header / footer / floating bar — `flush()` computes `collabStats` over the run's `collab.rows` and captures `mkLabel({now, live})`, a CLOSURE over that run's own counts, so the per-second repaint re-asks the ONE composer (`runSummaryLabel` gained a PRE-COMPOSED `collabPart` string — words from src/collab-row.js, POSITION from chat-run-summary.js, which still imports nothing) instead of rebuilding a second kind table; the “{n} sub-agents” text moved OUT of `chat-run-agents` into the label so the floating bar and the footer carry it too and the header never says it twice, leaving only the clickable chips there — with an explicit ` · ` in front of them (r2: dropping the old “{n} sub-agents:” colon glued the count to the names, “2 sub-agent events water_research” read as one phrase). (iii) the spinner line — `_noteRecordKind` (called from `_onOp` AFTER the message is applied, so a coalescing edit carries the grown rows) records whether the newest typed record was collab traffic, and `_applyStreamLabel` shows `subAgentStreamLabel(_liveCollabStats())` — TURN-scoped, because a report card between two coalesced cards would restart a per-card count mid-burst. THE SERVER STAYS THE LABEL AUTHORITY: `_onServerStreamLabel` is the one place that remembers the broadcast label/kind (all three call sites — the `streaming-label` frame, the attach meta, the reattach reply — go through it), and the override yields back ONLY what it took (`_collabLabelShown`); re-asserting the remembered label on every op would fight the label ChatInput sets locally on send and a stale “running Bash” from the previous turn would win. THE TICKER: ONE `setInterval(1000)` per ChatView, created lazily on the first collab record, bound to `winInfo._listenerCtl.signal` ('abort' → `_stopCollabTick`) and cleared in `dispose()` — a per-message interval over a fifty-row burst is fifty timers nobody cancels. It is a NO-OP while `_suspended` (a hidden window's ages are unread; `setSuspended(false)` runs one tick so the first frame back is right), it writes ONLY `textContent` into the head / header / footer / bar (never `_extendTop`/`_trim*`/`_pinned`/`scrollTop` — the suite greps its body), and it FREEZES every card the traffic has moved past exactly once (`_freezeStaleHeads(liveId, now)`). `_hideTyping` → `_freezeCollab()`: turn end stops the ticker and repaints every surface in its absolute-span form, because a ticking age on a finished turn reads as progress. **THE FREEZE MUST NOT DEPEND ON THE TICKER HAVING PAINTED (r2 MAJOR, reproduced 2/2):** the first cut repainted only the card the TICKER had last touched, and a burst that starts AND ends while the window is hidden (desktop switch — start an orchestration, switch desktop, come back) never ticks at all, while the RENDERER keeps painting each coalescing edit with a live age; the card then read “last 0s ago” on a turn that had ended minutes ago, contradicting the run header beside it (whose liveness IS captured in the fold pass, which runs while hidden). So the authority is a SET: `_noteCollabHeadPainted` (the renderer's `isCollabLive` hook returns its answer through it, and every `_paintCollabHead` keeps it honest — a card trimmed out of the window just leaves) and `_freezeStaleHeads(liveId|null, now)` walks it, from the tick AND from the freeze. ARMING: `_startCollabTick` is gated on `_liveCollabId()` (a claude session must not carry an interval at all) and paints ONCE immediately — `loadHistory` renders every card BEFORE `_showTyping` runs, so a window attached mid-burst would otherwise sit on the frozen span; `_onServerStreamLabel` is the event that finally makes liveness answerable, so it arms the ticker too (attaching to a STALLED turn is precisely the case the readout exists for). Gate: scripts/test-collab-live-counter.mjs (node composers + wiring pins, then a REAL codex rollout opened read-only and a LIVE codex chat session driven by a stub app-server through the real wrapper → real normalizer → real ws push; the stub is a reminder that a faithful fixture matters twice over — its blobs must differ inside the normalizer's 32-char fernet discriminator or the dedup silently collapses the burst, and a `commandExecution` needs its `item/started` or the wrapper records only an OUTPUT and the card falls to the unknown-tool 'mcp' kind). **THE STEER CHORD'S VIEW HALF (2026-09-07 + round-2 verifier):** `_canSteerComposer()`/`steerComposerText()` are what the contributed command `chat.steerNow` runs (see contributions.js), and `_steerAfterSend(msgId)` is its second half — a steer NAMES A QUEUED ITEM, so the chord sends on the ordinary path and this parks the msgId in a MAP until `_setQueue` drains it into the SAME `queue-op` frame the strip and the chip send. Its 8s timeout is the no-silent-failure half, and the guard that keeps it from CRYING WOLF is a TURN IDENTITY, not a flag: `_showTyping` stamps `_turnEpoch` on the same null→armed transition that sets `_typingSince`, `_steerAfterSend` captures it, and the timeout speaks only if that SAME epoch is still running. Testing `_typingSince` for truthiness (the shipped first cut) was false exactly where it mattered — the only shape that lets the timer fire is a NOT-busy wrapper running the message as its own `turn/start`, which re-arms the flag — so the window apologised for a message the agent was visibly running. `_typingSince` is a TIME and a time is not an identity (two turns can arm in the same millisecond); the epoch advances only where the flag arms, so a relabelled turn is still the same turn. Gate: test-queue-steer ⑨c drives the real `_hideTyping()`→`_showTyping()` sequence (a hand-set `_typingSince: null` fixture cannot occur on that path) with the old predicate's value asserted as the negative control. **2.369.112 the HIDDEN-REASON SET (inc-mu6bfv1t-4drq): `setHidden(reason, on)` — mobile / tab / minimized / desktop compose, `_suspended` is DERIVED (`_applySuspend` holds the pin snapshot + settle + re-tail), `setSuspended(on)` = the desktop reason (desktop-manager / stage-manager untouched); a hider never writes the flag. `_applyElementMarks` ①b: a compaction summary user record (`isCompactSummaryText`) resolves the "Prompt is too long" cards before it in time (inc-mu6btbfr-uaxg). The per-message hover buttons are `display:none` ≤768px (chat.css; measured 18/18 sat on the text at 390 px). `onSearch` for the status-bar magnifier is `readOnly ? null : () => this._search.open()` — a read-only viewer builds no ChatSearch (Ctrl+F does nothing there), so it shows no chip either.** **2.369.129 (inc-mub8xwrb-z57x): `_extendTop` folds BEFORE the trim decision and GROWS BY HEIGHT (`FOLD_GROW_PASSES` slabs until two viewports); both trims skip entirely below THREE viewports (`FOLD_DOM_CEILING` = the only bound) — the 2.368.29 residual seen in the field; gate test-chat-paging §4b + test-chat-trim-guard.** **THE RING NAMES THE AUTHOR OF EVERY MOVE (inc-mubvu3a4-x8sb, 2026-09-21, g1 evidence):** `_traceExpect(by)` is the ONE scrollTop-write author stamp (`_lastStWriteAt`/`_lastStWriteBy`) every programmatic write calls first (anchor restores, both delta fallbacks, `_forceScrollToBottom`'s frames, `jumpToIndex`, `runsRestore`, `_landOnHeader`, and every write in chat-view-seek.js), and the coarse `scroll` sample carries `writeAgo`/`by` beside `wheelAgo` — a move with both ages large is native anchoring or content growth, never ours. `trimBottom`/`trimTop` trace their DECISION INPUTS (`n`, `sh` at the gate, `sh2` after, `ch`, `st`) so a trim that undoes a landing is visible; `extendTop:done` carries `pass`/`ch`; `repin` carries `we`/`total` (a pin engaged with `we < total` is a pin in the MIDDLE of history, not the live tail); `wheelTop`/`wheelBottom`/`pageUp`/`pageDown` name the TRIGGER of every extend; `anchorLost {why}` says why `_withViewportAnchor` fell back. Ring 600→400 (recorder ships 300). Rule: a new scrollTop write anywhere calls `_traceExpect(by)` before it. **THE TRIMS ARE BY HEIGHT (inc-mubvu3a4-x8sb, g2 — supersedes the 2.369.129 three-viewport gate above):** `_trimEdge(side)` is the ONE trim (`_trimBottom`/`_trimTop` call it); it removes rendered cards only outside the KEEP ZONE (`_keepZone()` = the viewport ± `TRIM_KEEP_VIEWPORTS` (1) viewports), `TRIM_SOFT_CARDS` (150) is a target a zone may exceed, `FOLD_DOM_CEILING` the only hard bound (removes past the zone — folded cards cost no pixels); `_cardPositions(els)` gives every card a span, a folded (display:none) card taking its run header's. Order: `_extendTop` = anchored {prepend → `_reserveFreshHeights(fresh)` → `_updateRuns`} → carry → trim (AFTER the landing, reading the restored scrollTop) → re-fold; `_extendBottom` = append → reserve → fold → trim → re-fold → carry. Both grow by the content in the paging direction (`above = scrollTop < ch` / `below < ch`, `FOLD_GROW_PASSES` max). `_atLiveTail(st, sh, ch)` (not teleported ∧ `windowEnd ≥ total` ∧ DOM bottom) is the ONE pin predicate — the scroll handler, `_landOnHeader`, the read-only scroll button; the DOM edge pages, never pins. `_reserveFreshHeights` = a fresh slab rendered once at insert (`contentVisibility: visible` for two frames) so landings and the zone read measured heights — a MITIGATION, not an invariant (r1: Δsh keeps drifting a few hundred px after a landing; the anchor absorbs it, §4c prints the max); the gap loaders reserve the same way. `_withViewportAnchor` never anchors on the seek sentinel (skip = run chrome ∨ `_isSeekSentinel`) — at the top edge the anchor is the first visible card with its delta. THE NOTCH IS NOT LOST (r1: the OVERSHOOT is carried): the wheel handler carries the part of a notch the browser cannot deliver (`px − room` — a notch that CROSSES the edge, not only one that starts there) through ONE accounting: `_addWheelCarry(dir, px)` (≤ one viewport, a reversal clears), `_applyWheelCarry(dir, by)` = the ONE consumer at all four landings (both extends, both gap slabs), `_clearWheelCarry(why)` at every chosen destination (`_noteUserNav`, `_resetGapAfterJump`, `_seekTeleport`) — bounded to one viewport PER LANDING; a notch eaten by the lock marks `_wheelPending` and traces `{eaten:1}` first; `_liftLoadLock()` re-arms the extend for it, re-checked at the edge. A GAP SLAB LIVES ONLY DIRECTLY ABOVE MESSAGE 0 (r1): `_extendTop` prepends before the first NON-gap card, and `_trimEdge('top')` calls `_dropGapSlab(why, zone)` inside its anchored removal when a non-teleported window leaves windowStart 0 (sentinel cursor/anchor reset, `_gapEpoch` bumped so an in-flight slab lands `gapUp:stale`, the slab's stable-heights regime ended with `_setStableHeights(false, {recenter:false})`; refused with `gapDrop:skip` if a gap card still touches the zone). `_trace` stamps a monotonic `seq` on every entry (the ring splices 600→400 — an index mark goes blind; readers slice by seq). Traces: `trimBottom`/`trimTop {removed, n, anchored, sh, sh2, ch, st, st2, zone}`, `trimSkipZone`, `foldCeiling {side, forced}`, `extendTop:done {st = the history above}`, `extendBottom {below, pass}`, `extendBottom:grown`, `wheelTop`/`wheelBottom {carry | eaten}`, `wheelCarry {dir, px, by}`, `wheelCarry:clear {why}`, `wheelPending`, `gapDrop {why, n}` / `gapDrop:skip`. Gates: test-chat-trim-guard (the zone executed against injected geometry), test-chat-paging §1c/§4c/§4d, scripts/dbg-huge-paging.mjs. **2.369.144: the message list is born `aria-hidden` when `accessibility.exposeChat` is false (app.js `applyAxExposure` flips every live list on change) — the lever that keeps transcripts out of the accessibility tree.** **THE READER'S BAND (design-accessibility-tree §3 row 1 / §8, chunk a1): `_syncAxExposure` is ONE derivation with ONE layout read (`_cardPositions`) — every rendered card (gap cards too) farther than `AX_BAND_VIEWPORTS` (2) viewports from the viewport is `aria-hidden`, everything inside the band plus the focused card, `_lastJumpTargetEl` and the search reveal's card (ChatSearch `onReveal`) is exposed. `_scheduleAxSync(why)` coalesces (150 ms → rAF) every landing at its END (extendTop / extendBottom / trim / gapUp / gapDown / trimGap / teleport / the fold pass — never inside an anchored section), the scroll events (programmatic ones too), the resume from any hidden reason and the setting's flip (app.js `applyAxExposure` walks EVERY `.chat-message-list` on both flips and reaches its view through the list's `_axView` backref — a sub-agent viewer is not in `app.sessions`, so the earlier sessions loop left its band un-derived on the ON flip), plus ONE settle pass 1.2 s later (heights keep resolving after a landing; superseded by any newer schedule); NEVER mid-gesture — a pass whose wheel/touch input is younger than the debounce re-arms (edge notches fire no scroll event); a suspended view skips; teardown removes nothing. The jump / reveal exemption lapses once the reader scrolls after it (`_lastUserScrollAt > _lastJumpAt / _axRevealAt`); `_axBand` records each pass's why / counts / geometry. FOCUS IS EXPOSED IN ITS OWN TASK (verifier finding on a1): a `focusin` on the list removes the landing card's aria-hidden synchronously (no layout read) and schedules a 'focus' pass that keeps it through the activeElement exemption — the pass alone ran ≥ 150 ms after the focus (and never, for a `.focus()` without a scroll); `_axCardOf(el)` = the list's direct `.chat-msg` child holding el, the ONE rule both the handler and the pass's exemptions key on (the element the band writes).
