The ingest engine (`create(deps)`): the per-adapter loop with its single
flight, the pass that appends to the durable log BEFORE it advances an anchor,
the ONE broadcast per pass, the digest the panel and every `channels-updated`
carry, and the store's serialized index owner — of which the engine is the only
writer. **The lane is ASKED, never read off `caps`**: the tick's cadence is
`laneState(...).pollCadence` and the scan source is `scanState(...)`, so a
demoted or dead push lane gets the fast cadence back immediately with nothing
else in the tree deciding it a second time. Filtering, assignment and the wake
decision arrived in P2; the outbox, policy and reach in P3 (below).
The routes take `host` everywhere and refuse another machine BY NAME. The
wiring is one `create(deps)` factory called once from server.js, whose channel
flush rides the existing SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown.

**THE ACCOUNT MODEL (2026-09-22, owner: "为啥不能和mount那种类似，管理的是账号，
每个账号添加的时候可以选oauth client？").** The panel manages ACCOUNTS the way
the storage mounts do — a Gmail mount stores only the preset KEY of the OAuth
client it was authorized under — and the engine had ONE record per kind whose
credential was "the integration row's current pick", so a refresh token minted
under client A was refreshed with client B the moment the pick changed (Google
answers `invalid_client`; the model itself broke §14.2's "never a silent
swap"). Invariants, one sentence each: N adapter records per kind, the FIRST
keeping `id === kind` (every existing record, conversation, reach entry and
filter valid untouched) and every further one `<kind>:<8 hex>` from
`mintAdapterId`; every record carries `credentialKey` (`cluster:<presetKey>` |
`own`), stamped at CONNECT from the wizard's choice — validated against
`offeredCredentials` and refused `400 unknown-credential` BY NAME otherwise,
the row's own pick (`defaultCredentialKey`) when omitted — and never re-picked
by the row afterwards; `adapterFor` hands the key down in `adapterDeps` and
the adapter also reads it LIVE off the record (so the migration's stamp lands
on an adapter built before it); `connect(kind, {credentialKey, newAccount})`
mints only with `newAccount` or on a kind with no record, else it is the P1a
per-kind path re-authorizing the FIRST account (its `credentialKey` handed
there); `reauthorize(adapterId, {credentialKey})` is BY ID, never by kind —
a key RE-BINDS a TOKEN-LESS record (never authenticated / disconnected:
nothing is minted under its key; the live adapter is dropped so `adapterFor`
rebuilds it under the new key, exactly as an options change does — measured:
the stamp alone left the consent URL on the old client) and is refused
`400 credential-bound` BY NAME on a record HOLDING a token bound elsewhere
(its stamp, else what the token itself names), never dropped (verifier r1);
a legacy record's missing key is stamped by `credentialKeyEvidence`; a FURTHER account's
`disconnect` REMOVES its record, live entry, wake windows and index rows —
only its own, through the two serialized doors — while the first account's
keeps the record (P1a unchanged); `adapterView` carries `credentialKey`,
`credentialLabel` (a preset's env label; `own` is worded by the client),
`credential` (the facts FOR THAT KEY), `credentials` (the offered list, the
"Add account" step's input), `credentialDefault` (the row's CURRENT pick = what
a further account is bound to unless the wizard says otherwise — never this
account's own key; c2), `auth.credentialKey` and `auth.tokenHeld` (does the
record HOLD a token — the client's Connect verb re-binds only a token-less
account); `available[]` carries `credentials` and `credentialDefault` too;
`stampCredentialKeys()` is the migration's verb, through
`credentialKeyEvidence(rec, mod)`: the client the record's OWN TOKEN names
wins when this instance still offers it (a Gmail token carries the
`clusterKey` it was exchanged under, null = `own`; `evidence:'token'`), else
the row's current pick (`evidence:'row-pick'` — what refreshed it until now;
a Lark token names nothing), every stamped row naming its evidence and the
token's key; the live records mutated synchronously, the write queued through
`saveAdapters`, a record whose token names nothing offered and whose
integration resolves to nothing left unstamped (verifier r1: stamping the pick
alone re-bound an org1-minted token to the channels client whenever the pick
had flipped before the upgrade — the case the model exists for). Gate:
scripts/test-channels-accounts.mjs (77) — incl. a patched-copy PRE-FIX
control (both the hand-down and the record stamp removed) that reproduces
the silent swap, ⑤ bound-vs-token-less; scripts/test-migrations.mjs (82) —
the token-evidence legs.

**A ROUTE MAY NOT MINT AN INDEX ROW (r2).** `POST /track` and `POST /read` on
ANY adapter/conversation id wrote a permanent, invisible row into `index.json`
— a file read on every render and deep-cloned by `digest()` on every broadcast
— while the track route's own `404 No such conversation` was UNREACHABLE dead
code, because `setTracked` set `found = true` unconditionally. `known()` now
resolves the adapter from the records and the conversation from the index
snapshot BEFORE anything is mutated, both mutators take the `{create:false}`
entry, and `POST /read` answers 404 too. A `tracked:true` orphan would resume
ingesting the day its adapter id was reused.

**`markRead` DOES NOT BROADCAST A NO-OP, AND ITS DEFAULT INSTANT IS THE NEWEST
RECORD'S (r2).** Both halves are load-bearing, and together they are what
broke a self-feeding loop between this engine and an open window. (1) "Read"
means "I have seen everything this conversation holds", and a vendor is free
to stamp a record ahead of our clock (the fake adapter spreads a day over the
whole current UTC day, so future-dated records are ALWAYS present; a real
vendor's clock skew does the same) — with `now()` those stay unread for ever,
`unread` never reaches 0 and nothing watching it can settle. Taking the newest
record is also strictly MORE honest in the other direction: a record arriving
between it and this instant stays unread instead of being silently marked
read. (2) Every broadcast recomputes the digest (deep-cloning the index),
re-renders every panel and re-reads every open window's tail, so notifying
when nothing moved turned ONE open window into ~490 requests a second, for
ever, with the user touching nothing — rewriting `readAt` ~500 times a second,
i.e. destroying the mark it was setting. The cache-invalidation law is one
DIRTY signal, one computation; an unchanged value is not a dirty signal.

**THE DIGEST CARRIES NO HUMAN SENTENCE (r2)** — see src/channel-caps.js: this
payload is broadcast to every client at once while the language is per DEVICE,
so a sentence composed here is English for everybody by construction.

**THE INGEST IS GATED ON THE RESOLVER (r3, high).** The r2 engine asked
`scanState()` for the CHIP and then called `adapter.history()` regardless,
while `scan.hostFacts` had NO producer anywhere in the product (`scanHost`
had zero callers; the seed wrote `hostFacts: null` and nothing replaced it), so
the resolver could only ever answer `host-facts-stale` — and the fake adapter
re-derived its own source. Measured on the shipped seam: 11 records ingested,
anchor advanced, unread badged, chip "not scanning" — the honesty contract
publishing the opposite of what happened. Three things changed, each with
its own control: (1) `pass()` PRODUCES the facts — `scan.hostFacts` trigger
③ of the three the design names (§4 / §5 invariant 7): unconditionally before
a scan pass that would advance the anchor, the store analogue of "re-resolve
at approval time". ① (the connect wizard) is P1's and ② (the first panel
render past the TTL) is subsumed, because a render has no side effects — the
r2 loop lesson — and every scan pass refreshes anyway. The round trip spends
one request and the facts land on the LIVE row through the serialized door.
(2) `ingest()` asks `laneOrScan()` BEFORE a byte is fetched and refuses a scan
lane with no source (`complete:false`, the anchor stays, `why` carried) — a
refused lane is NOT a failed pass, which is what tells it apart from the
registry's own refusal. (3) The resolved source is HANDED to `history()` as
`opts.source`, and the lane label written on the entry is the RESOLVED lane.
`laneOrScan` now asks `laneState` and follows its `via` (r2 read `caps.receive`
there AND in the ingest label). The pre-fix control wires three patched copies
— engine, registry, fake — to each other, and reproduces the r2 numbers.

**"READ" IS THE NEWEST RECORD'S FOR PAST-STAMPED RECORDS TOO (r3).** r2
spelled the default `Math.max(now(), newest.at)` — right for the fake adapter,
whose records are always future-dated (and whose suite ASSERTED so), and
`now()` for every adapter whose records are stamped in the PAST, i.e. every
real one. There a message stamped before the mark but fetched after it (the
routine shape: the poll interval is 30-300 s) was SILENTLY MARKED READ and
never badged, and `changed` was true on every call, so the no-op-broadcast
rule was structurally inert. The stamp is now the newest record's, or the
existing mark when there is no record (nothing to have seen). The leg drives a
real-vendor-shaped adapter with a growing world and a backdated arrival; the
control is the r2 spelling.

**TRACKING BROADCASTS BEFORE THE PASS IT KICKS (r3).** `setTracked(true)`'s
only notification was the pass it kicked, and a pass the request budget could
not afford returned before `notify()` — so the flag was on disk, the route had
answered `{ok:true}`, and NO client learned, including the one that clicked
(the panel repaints only on the broadcast). Measured: 26 of 30 tracks silent (the verifier measured 19 — the count follows the budget clock)
under the 20/min budget with a 30-conversation adapter (the design measures
~50 for a real account). `setTracked` now notifies on BOTH branches, after the
convCaps refresh and before the pass; the pass adds its own broadcast when it
ingests something. The digest also hands `enabled` to `freshnessClaim`, so a
row on a disabled adapter and an untracked row are published `off`.

P1a (2026-09-16), the real adapters wired: `REAL_ADAPTERS` (lark, gmail) is
the ONE list the engine reads for what is connectable and what each row
declares; the adapter's OWN token is `auth.tokenEnc` on the record, encrypted

integrations layer's, §13), decrypted only for the adapter that owns it and
never in `adapterView`; the engine registers each row's Test runner on the
integrations store (the consumer owns the runner, the store dispatches);
`connect(kind)` asks the credential facts BEFORE any record exists and refuses
with a typed `auth-expired {needsCredentials}` — the route answers `409
needs-credentials` — when the row resolves to none, so a refused connect mints
NO adapter row (measured on a fresh worktree boot: it used to leave a
permanent row behind and the PUT/disconnect 404s answered 200 about it); on
a fresh record the row is persisted only after `auth.begin()` returned, and a
begin that throws drops the live instance;
`finishAuth` is paste-back through the adapter's own `auth.finish`;
`onAuthDone` re-asks auth, kicks a pass on success and SAYS a failure on the
record (`lastAuthError`); `disconnect` clears the token and retracts any
failure item; a never-authenticated record is `not-connected` and passes
nothing, while a dead token fails with the vendor's typed refusal and SPEAKS
(fence 8: ONE "For you" item after `FAILURES_BEFORE_LOUD`, naming adapter /
code / vendor words / remedy, retracted by the SAME producer on the first
passing pass — only its own still-open item); discovery pages the adapter's
cursor up to `DISCOVERY_PAGES`; `setOptions` refuses undeclared keys and
values outside `choices` by name and rebuilds the live adapter for a
`rebuild:true` option. The digest carries `available` (connectable kinds not
yet connected, with the credential facts for the wizard's three copy paths)
and each adapter row's `connectable`/`integration`/`credential`/`flow`
(never the flow's `state` secret)/`lastAuthError`/`failureItem`/`options`/
`optionsSchema`. Routes: `POST /api/channels/adapters/:kind/connect`,
`POST …/:id/auth/finish` `{url}`, `POST …/:id/auth/cancel`,
`POST …/:id/disconnect`, `PUT …/:id` `{enabled?, options?}`. Gates:
test-channels-lark-shape + test-channels-gmail-shape (the engine verbs over
the real engine) + test-channels-engine.

**P1b (2026-09-16), the push lanes wired.** `syncPushLanes()` (every tick +
the mutations that change the answer) arms a lane when `pushWanted` — a push
adapter with a live half, enabled, its switch on (an opt-in lane needs an
explicit `true`), a `connected` auth — and stops it when not; every callback
is keyed on the arm token, so a superseded lane reaches nothing. `onPushEvent`
IS FENCE 11: the record lands in the durable log FIRST and the function
RETURNS (= the ack) before the index moves or a client is told; the index
update + broadcast are coalesced per batch (`PUSH_NOTIFY_DEBOUNCE_MS`, one
broadcast never one per message); vendor event ids are remembered
(`PUSH_EVENT_DEDUP_MAX`) so an at-least-once replay is acked and absorbed.
Content rides only while `laneState().carryContent` and the conversation is
TRACKED (invariant 6); otherwise the event is a cursor KICK — one kick-origin
pass per `KICK_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` per adapter, respecting the backoff, a kick
arriving mid-pass runs after it. THE MEASUREMENT: `ingest()` samples only
while push carries content, only on an already-anchored conversation (a first
walk is a backlog), only records stamped after `push.contentSince`; a TIMER
pass finding a new record is a miss, a KICK pass finding one is push doing
its job; in kick mode NOTHING is sampled (no ratchet). `checkDemotion` writes
`demotedAt`/`demotedWhy`/`demoted{missed,total,rate}`, logs one line and
broadcasts; the connection stays up (demoted, not stopped). `setPush(id,
{enabled?, claimedExclusive?})` is the ONE way back: a re-declaration zeroes
the counters, clears the demotion and retries the lane ONCE with a fresh arm;
`pushView` publishes the public half (never the raw sample batches), `null`
on an adapter without a push lane. A heartbeat only refreshes `lastEventAt`
in memory; a state TRANSITION persists and broadcasts (`adapters.update`
writes bytes every call). Route: `PUT /api/channels/adapters/:id {push}`
(`400 no-push-lane` / a claim outside the closed set refused by name). Gate:
test-channels-push (65).

**P2 — assign, filter, wake (design §7; fences 2 + 12).** Invariants, one
sentence each:

- THE FUNNEL: every lane calls `onFresh(rec, convId, fresh, {lane, origin})`
  with exactly the records that became durable (`appendRecords` now returns
  `fresh`), from `ingest()` after the index step and from `onPushEvent`'s
  content branch (never awaited there — the ack is that function's return);
  after that nothing knows the lane.
- The coalescing window (`coalesceSeconds()` = `channels.pushCoalesceSeconds`,
  default 60, fractional honoured, 0 = wake per message) opens ONLY while
  `laneState().carryContent` holds and `notify:'wake'` — a poll or scan pass
  is already a batch — gated on the RESOLVED lane, never `caps.receive`.
- Hits that must wait are PENDING ON THE INDEX (`en.pending`, bounded to
  `PENDING_CAP` with `pendingElided`), persisted BEFORE the timer exists, so a
  restart delivers them (`scheduleBootPending` → one digest per conversation
  after `BOOT_PENDING_DELAY_MS`); `stop()` only clears timers.
- A hold is a delay, never a drop: a later direct wake CARRIES the entry's
  pending hits along and only the NEW hits are re-held on a refusal.
- `wake()` resolves the target (`liveSessions()`; a group rotates over its
  live members with the cursor in `ix.rotations`, none ⇒ held with a named
  reason), asks `paceVerdict` (held, never dropped), renders the block, and
  calls `deliver.deliverToConversation(cid, text, {kind:'notification',
  spendReason:'channel-message', fromName, cardText})` — the ladder authorizes,
  charges the slot it authorized and releases its hold; the engine adds
  NOTHING beside it (fence 2; test-spend-paths lists the site as an allowed
  forward with its reason); a refusal is `deliver.stashFor(cid, …)` — the
  ladder's own durable stash, drained at the agent's next injection.
- The two derived ledgers (`stats.msgs`/`stats.hits`) are written through a
  non-fatal `ledger()` — a failed write costs one stale number and is SAID,
  never the wake that follows.
- `setAssignment` writes ONE `reachEntries` row `{principal, scope, level:
  'visible', origin:'assignment'}` and `null` removes ONLY rows with that
  origin (a user's grant on the same pair is byte-identical after); both are
  audited. `setFilter` keeps one filter per conversation in `ix.filters`
  (`f-<adapter>/<conv>`), refuses to clear one a filtered assignment still
  names (`filter-in-use`). `estimateFilter` reads `ESTIMATE_CAP` (5000)
  records off the log and passes `capHit` as the estimator's honesty input.
- The digest carries `assignment` (via `assignmentView`: `authority` clamped
  by `authorityCapsFor`, `authorityStored`/`authorityClamped`/`authorityWhy`),
  `filter`, `stats` (`statsView`), `authorityCaps` and `wakeLatency`
  (`wakeLatencyFor`: push = window + ack budget, poll = `pollInterval.hot`
  which the tick itself now uses for an adapter with an assigned row, scan =
  `scanLatency[source]`, reconcile = `RECONCILE_SECONDS`).
- Decision 9 as shipped: `policyRequiresReview` defaults to true (every v1
  adapter is external) until P3's policy store writes `entry.policy.mode`.

Routes (src/routes/channels.js): `PUT …/:adapterId/:convId/assignment`
`{assignment|null, estimateAtSet?}` (404 not-found · 400 bad-assignment /
no-such-filter · 409 authority-capped), `PUT …/filter` `{filter|null,
estimate?}` (400 bad-filter / filter-in-use), `POST …/estimate` `{filter}`.
Wiring: server.js hands `deliver`, `serverSetting` and `liveSessions` (cid +
name + task-group ids per live session) to channels-wiring. Gate:
test-channels-engine ⑥ (125) + test-channels-lane-parity (33) +
test-spend-paths (262).

**P3 — OUTBOX · POLICY · REACH (design §8, §9, §11).** Invariants, one sentence
each: `propose` refuses with the typed `send-not-available` and creates
NOTHING when no identity is offered (refreshing `convCaps` once when the
cached answer is `unknown`/`stale`); a proposal's authority is the user's
`send` or the assignment's EFFECTIVE (clamped) authority, else `draft`;
`decideOutbound` runs with the guards read from settings
(`channels.guardLinksReview` / `guardAttachmentsReview` / `offHoursTz` /
`offHoursStart` / `offHoursEnd`); `direct` sends at once, `review` lands in
`awaiting-approval`. `approve` RE-RESOLVES `convCaps` UNCONDITIONALLY before
the send and a "not offered" answer stops with `send-not-available` + the
adapter's reason, the proposal `failed`, the receipt carrying that reason.
`sendNow` writes the audit ATTEMPT line before the request and the OUTCOME
line after (a crash between them is the state `reconcile` exists for); a
typed refusal is `failed`, a throw is `unknown` and `unknown` is never retried
— the USER gets a For-you item instead. The per-conversation "For you" POINTER
has a count-free text (dedupe-by-text is the idempotence), the count + latest
body in `detail`, its id persisted as `pendingTodoId` on the conversation row,
retracted by this producer alone when the last proposal leaves
`awaiting-approval`, and an inbox throw (the open cap) DEGRADES to the rail
badge + the Outbox window. The RECEIPT rides the ladder with `noWake` (spend
reason `channel-receipt`) unless the assignment's `receiptWake` opted in, a
refusal stashed through the ladder's own stash. Every outbox audit line carries
`draftedBy` / `approvedBy` / `sentAs` / `identityMarking` and none of it reaches
the message body. Policy reads own > adapter `policyDefault` > review. Reach:
`setReach` writes/removes only the USER-origin row; `request` files ONE For-you
item and `decideRequest` approves into EXACTLY ONE visible grant; the agent
reads (`listFor` / `readFor` / `statusFor`) resolve reach FIRST and answer the
uniform not-found. The TTL sweep (24 h) runs from the tick once a minute. The
store gained `outbox.json` (single-owner door, bounded at `OUTBOX_KEEP` = 500
terminal proposals) and `auditTail()`.

P4 (§9.4/§9.5) — EXACTLY ONCE OR HONESTLY UNKNOWN: `sendNow` stamps
`attemptAt` + the WIRE text (`wire`) on the proposal BEFORE the request (what a
reconcile compares against), hands a two-phase adapter's handle to the store the
moment `onHandle` fires (`sendHandle`), and reads a transport failure AFTER the
request left (`detail.lost`) as `unknown` — never `failed`; the OUTCOME audit
line says `lost`. `reconcile(id)` is the ONLY way out of `unknown`, asked by a
PERSON (the card's Check outcome / the route), gated by `canReconcile` on the
adapter's declared idempotency (`none` ⇒ typed `reconcile-not-available`,
audited as `reconcile-refused`); the adapter is asked with the SAME key, the
attempt instant, the wire text and the handle; landed ⇒ `sent` by actor
`reconcile` with the receipt owed now and the unknown-outcome item retracted by
this producer; not-landed ⇒ `failed`; else still unknown with `reconcile.n`
counted — nothing is ever re-sent by the engine. `sweepSending()` runs from
`start()`: a `sending` corpse becomes `unknown` by actor `boot` (`lost-at-boot`).
THE SENDER HONESTY LINE is OFF by default (`channels.senderHonestyLine`; the
adapter record's `senderHonestyLine` true/false/null overrides it via
`setSenderHonesty`, audited) and appended at send time ONLY for an agent-drafted
proposal — `proposalView.honestyLine` says so BEFORE the approval and the
recorded fact after. A send's `observed` sender_type is recorded on the adapter
row as `identityObserved` (the digest carries it) and LOGGED with the flip it
licenses while the declaration is still `unknown`. Gates: test-channel-outbox
(107), test-channel-acl (38), test-channels-identity (55),
test-channels-agent-cli (19), test-channels-e2e (heavy).

**WAKES ON ONE CONVERSATION ARE SERIALIZED (2026-09-16, the P4 verifier):**
`wake()` and `flushPending()` queue on a per-key promise chain (`serialWake`)
and only `wakeNow` delivers, so the boot flush (5 s) and the first tick's
direct wake (5 s) cannot both carry the same held hits (two billed turns);
a wake clears from `pending` ONLY the record ids it carried (`heldIds`) — the
old `pending = []` also dropped a hit that went pending DURING the RPC through
a window's keepPending; a direct wake that carries a window's hits clears that
window's timer (the window's delivery is this wake). Gate: test-channels-engine
⑥ (i)/(j), 140.

**g3 — THE OWNER'S OWN MESSAGE (2.369.159, design §22.2 ①: "an IM, not a feed").** `propose(ctx, a, c, {…, direct:true})` from the USER (`POST /api/channels/:adapterId/:convId/send` — the composer's Send) skips the policy and its guards: the decision is `{mode:'direct', reasons:[], detail:{ownMessage:true}}` and the send is AS THE USER; it still rides the whole outbox machinery (the record, the audit propose → attempt → outcome, the lost answer's `unknown` that is never re-sent, the receipt path). Only `sendAs:'user'` qualifies — a conversation offering only the bot identity answers `send-not-available` WITH the send-as-user reason (`sendIdentityFor` returns `userWhy`), because a bot message is not the owner speaking; an AGENT's `direct` is ignored (agent drafts are what the policy exists for). The digest's conversation row carries `lastText` (the ingest tracks the newest APPENDED record's text + instant apart from `lastAt` — discovery may already have set `lastAt` from the vendor's listing to that very instant — and the push batch does the same). Gate: test-channels-groups-ui §2 (the link that would force review does not hold the owner's own words; the same text without `direct` is review — the control) + test-channels-e2e ⑩b.

**r3 — THE SIDE DOORS, THE FIRST SCREEN, A BLOCKED STORE (2.369.159, 2026-09-23 verifier, each leg RED on the pre-fix tree).** ① `propose(ctx, a, c, input, guards)` and `approve(id, {text, by, consent, mayWake})` pass a send that STARTS A TURN (`sendStartsTurn(rec)` = the adapter module's declaration) through `wakeGate(convId, n, guards)`: `n` = 1 when it goes out now (a direct decision / an approve) else 0; `consent(n)` first — `wake-count-mismatch` `{wakes}` with nothing created (an approve's proposal stays awaiting) — then `mayWake(convId)` — `rate-floor` with nothing created / the proposal still awaiting; a granted slot is refunded when the send ended anything but `sent`/`unknown` (`wakeRefundIfUnsent`). `routes/channels.js` `wakeGuards(body)` = `{consent: ownerConsent(body), mayWake: auth off ? groups.pacerFor('user') : null}` — THE SAME persisted ledger as the group routes (keyed `user|<conversation>`, so a target the group route just woke is floored on the side door too); no groups engine with auth off ⇒ a pacer that refuses by name. `answer3`: `wake-count-mismatch` 409, `rate-floor` 429. test-architecture §49 censuses every `router.post/put` in this file that reaches `engine().propose/approve` or `ge.post/create/invite`: it must hand consent AND the pacer (a planted door is the control). The agent route `/api/agent/channels/reply` hands the agent's own `wakeFloorFor(cid)` (429 `rate-floor` in `chanAnswer`). ② `groupReply` passes the refusal's `group` view on a `wake-count-mismatch` (the panel repaints before its next click). ③ `digest()` carries `quarantined` `[{file, to, why, at, blocked}]` (the first screen names a set-aside store; the For-you item alone left a real instance's vanished accounts unexplained), and the boot inbox item for a BLOCKED entry says it could NOT be set aside (its own i18n key) instead of "set aside as <its own name>". ④ A blocked family's refusal is `{code:'store-blocked', status:503}` from the store; `fail()` answers it as `{error, code}` (it was 500 with `code:null`). Gate: test-channel-groups §2c · §3j; test-channel-store §r3; test-architecture §49.

**r4 — A THROW AFTER THE GRANT GIVES THE SLOT BACK (2.369.159, 2026-09-23 verifier, the leg RED on the pre-fix tree).** `propose` and `approve` wrap everything after a granted `wakeGate` in try/catch: a throw (a blocked store's 503 `store-blocked` from the door, an EACCES / ENOSPC write after the door ran) calls `wakeRefundIfUnsent(gate, guards, convId, id, {threw:true})` and rethrows. The refund reads WHERE the act died: `sent`/`unknown` keep the slot; a proposal whose adapter send was CALLED (`sendLeft` — the id set right before `adapter.send`, cleared when `sendNow` returns, so an entry that survives is a sendNow that threw after the request may have left) keeps the slot; anything else returns the PAIR and the sender's minute (`mayWake.refund(convId, {attempted:false})` — nothing reached the authorizer, so it was not an attempt). Without a throw the r3 rule stands (a refusal returns the pair, keeps the attempt). Before: the grant outlived the throw, so the retry once the store was back was a 429 blaming "a wake less than 30 s ago" that never happened, and eight such errors floored an unrelated group wake for a minute. Gate: test-channel-groups §3j (① /send, door refused → 503, ledger byte-equal, retry SENT · ② /propose, EACCES after fn ran → same · ③ approve, transition refused → 503, ledger equal, still awaiting, re-approve SENT · ④ CONTROL: delivered then the outcome write refused ⇒ the floor stays, retry 429).

### src/lib/channels-panel.js + src/lib/channel-window.js (CLIENT)

**r4 CHUNK 3 (2.369.165, docs/design-integrations-per-account.zh.md §2.5 / §8.1 #1–#7/#10/#11, D6/D8) — THE ACCOUNT CARD. SUPERSEDES the P1a connect wizard, its three copy paths, the flow dialog, the credential step and "Add account…" described below.** A section whose adapter is `connectable` (a Lark / Gmail ACCOUNT) is drawn by `accountCard` in the storage row's grammar, credential-first: head = chevron · type glyph · `accountName` · the client chip (`clientChipText`: `Preset: {label}` / `Custom client`) · the dot (`accountDot(a, trackedN)`: connected → ok, the sign-in dead (`auth.state` expired) → bad, `needs-credentials` → warn, never signed in / disabled / connected-but-tracking-nothing → idle, a consent running → attn, ≥ 3 failed passes → warn) · tracked/total · ✎ (`mounts-icon-btn`, Edit) · ⋯. `accountLines` draws UNDER the head: the HEALTH line `.chan-sec-health` = `[.mounts-typetag product] Connected · <the first declared free-text option's value> · last poll <ago> · push: <claim>` (the storage detail line), or the storage `.mounts-errline` "Couldn’t connect: <the mounts' auth-death sentence, its nouns the channel's> (<auth.why>)" + the primary `.mounts-reauth-btn` `Re-authorize {product}…` (D8) for a dead sign-in, the same line with the store's credential why for a missing client, "Not connected — …" + Connect for a record never signed in, a running consent + Cancel, the re-authorize countdown, the last connect failure, failing passes, a withdrawn push claim. Its CHILDREN are the tracked conversations only, as `row(conv, {child:true})` = `.chan-row-tracked` with the storage `.mounts-child-arrow` ↳; an untracked one is reached through Track… (`showTrackPicker`, today's checklist). Connected and tracking nothing ⇒ the credential-only register "Login only — …" + Track…. The `channel-adapter` ⋯ for an account is the storage row's order (D6, registration `group`/`order` — scripts/test-oauth-field-parity.mjs `accountMenuOrder` reads it off the source): Open conversation window (the most recent tracked conversation) · Track… · Options · Push… ‖ Re-authorize / Connect · Duplicate… · Disconnect · Remove… ‖ Disable; the sender-line rows stay for a SOURCE only (an account's lives in Edit). A SOURCE (the built-in watcher, a scan-only fixture) keeps the `section` renderer and `adapterNotes` below unchanged. ONE `Connect an account ({types})` button (`data-connect-account`) at the bottom of the Accounts part replaces the per-kind buttons. Every dialog — connect, re-authorize, edit, duplicate, remove refused — is src/lib/channel-account-dialogs.js on the shared storage component; THIS file holds no field renderer (the parity census). Repaint stays in place from the digest; channel-window.js is unchanged by r4 (the ⋯ "Open conversation window" calls `app.openChannel`). The CSS is the storage row's (`.mounts-errline` / `-typetag` / `-reauth-btn` / `-child-arrow` / `-icon-btn`, so a phone draws what a storage row draws) plus three rules below the mockup's marker: `.chan-sec-health`, `.chan-row.chan-row-tracked`, `.chan-sec .mounts-errline` (the indent).

P1a (2026-09-16), the adapter's own controls, all on its section and all
read from the digest (no fetch on repaint): the connect wizard's three copy
paths by `credential.source` (`none` ⇒ "Set up <label> credentials…" opens the
Integrations card FIRST — never a consent page that will fail there; `cluster`
⇒ "Provided by the cluster · <label>" beside the button; `user` ⇒ nothing
more; the route's own `409 needs-credentials` opens that card too); the flow
dialog = the consent page as a LINK the user clicks (a window opened after an
await is popup-blocked), the named `port-busy` refusal in the user's words,
PASTE-BACK + Cancel, and it follows the adapter's broadcast so a loopback
completion closes it by itself; the auth line is the four-valued state with
`reauthEta(expiresAt, now)` beside a connected row that states an expiry and
a verb chosen by the STATE (Re-authorize / Open Integrations / Connect); the
last connect failure and a filed "For you" item are SAID on the section; the
tracked picker is a checkbox per discovered conversation (tracked is opt-in,
each tick a `/track` POST that is refused loudly and reverted); the options
editor renders the adapter's DECLARED `optionsSchema` (a select for
`choices`, `''` restores the default) and PUTs `{options}`; Disconnect is
confirmed; Enable/Disable PUTs `{enabled}`. Invariants, one sentence each:
nothing here branches on an adapter's kind; every string that a vendor, a
peer or the server composed renders through textContent; the "next phase"
empty text is retired — an instance with no adapter shows the connect rows.

**THE ACCOUNT MODEL (2026-09-22, the owner's mounts analogy — c2, the wizard
and the panel; the server half is channels-engine's).** One sentence per
invariant: every Connect / "Add account…" entry lands in `startConnect(app,
spec)` and MINTS (`newAccount: true`) — the P1a per-kind re-point of the first
record is never issued by this client; the wizard's spec (`wizardSpec`) is read
off the digest alone — `credentials` (what the integration offers a NEW
account right now), `credentialDefault` (the row's own pick, pre-picked never
forced) — from an `available[]` entry or an existing account's row, the same
three fields; the CREDENTIAL step (`showCredentialStep`, stepper index 0) is
drawn ONLY when more than one credential is offered — exactly one ⇒ that key
rides the connect body and the step is skipped silently (no empty step, no
extra click), none ⇒ the body carries no key and the server stamps the row's
pick; the step is a radio per offered credential (a preset by its env LABEL —
data, rendered through textContent, never translated — `own` worded here as
"Own client"), Cancel there mints nothing, Continue posts `{credentialKey,
newAccount:true}` and `showFlowDialog(…, shell)` moves the SAME dialog on to
the consent step; an existing account re-authorizes ITSELF — the status-line
verb and the ⋯ menu's Re-authorize / Connect post `/adapters/:id/reauthorize`
by id, never the kind; a TOKEN-LESS account (`auth.tokenHeld` false: never
authenticated, or disconnected) runs the credential step FIRST when more than
one is offered — its OWN key pre-picked, never the row's default over it —
through `showCredentialStep(app, spec, {submit})` posting `{credentialKey}`
to ITS `/reauthorize` (a re-bind; exactly one offered rides the body
silently, as for a new account), while a HELD token posts `{}` — the server
refuses another key by name (`credential-bound`, worded in channel-words:
disconnect first, or add another account); "Add account…" (⋯ menu, `3_auth` order 15, gated on
`connectable`) opens the wizard for another account of that kind; a section is
NAMED BY ITS ACCOUNT (`accountName`: the token's user when the auth carries one,
else the kind's label, NUMBERED "Gmail account 2" in record order only when
the kind holds more than one — a lone account keeps its plain name; the head's
tooltip keeps the kind beside the account); the credential chip
(`.chan-cred-chip`, the preset's label / "Own client") is drawn only where it
disambiguates — the kind holds several accounts OR the integration offers
several credentials — and never for a legacy record with no key; every section
carries `data-adapter=<id>`. Gate: test-integrations-ui ⑩ (two offered ⇒ the
step with the chosen key in the body; "Add account…" ⇒ two sections with
distinct names + chips; Connect on a token-less account = the credential step
with its OWN key pre-picked, the chosen key posted to ITS /reauthorize and
re-bound server-side, the second section's to ITS id; one offered ⇒ skipped;
the withdrawn preset said by name on the account it minted).

The rail panel (adapters as sections, a freshness chip on every row, the
`channel-row` menu and the ⚙ row as CONTRIBUTIONS registered by the module
that owns them — gear-menu.js never learns the row's name; since 2.369.124 the
row files itself under the Communication ▸ head with `parent:'comm'`, order 10) and the conversation window (a registered window type; plain text through
textContent on every path; a composer ONLY where `offers()` allows one, and a
named reason where it does not). The panel repaints from the digest the engine
broadcasts rather than re-fetching; the window re-reads its own tail when its
id is named (§10.4).

**MARKING READ IS A USER ACTION, NOT A REPAINT SIDE EFFECT (r2).** The POST
lived at the end of `render()`, which the broadcast handler calls — so the
engine's notify re-rendered the window, the render POSTed /read, the POST
notified, and the cycle ran at ~490 requests a second for ever (measured in
headless chrome on the shipped fake adapter's own data: 5,482 broadcasts and
5,479 /read POSTs over ten IDLE seconds with ONE window open). It is now
issued when the window OPENS and when the user touches it, and only while the
last drawn summary says there is something unread.

**THE PAGE BOUNDARY IS A RECORD, NOT AN INSTANT (r2)** — the window sends
`before` AND `beforeId` (the store's `(at, vendorId)` total order).

**THE FRESHNESS SENTENCE IS COMPOSED HERE (r2)** — both files import the PURE
`src/channel-caps.js` directly and render `freshnessText` / `identityWarningText`
with their own `t`, because the digest is broadcast to every client while the
language is per DEVICE.

**THE MANAGER OWNS TITLES (r3).** `winInfo.setTitle?.(c.title || convId)` was
a PERMANENT no-op — the winInfo literal (src/lib/window.js) has no such member
and none is ever assigned, `setTitle(id, t)` is a WindowManager method — so
every channel window's title bar, taskbar entry and tab label read "Channel"
and two open conversations were indistinguishable. The same
silent-optional-call shape as the `off?.()` r2 removed; jobs-panel.js had the
identical call. Both now call `app.wm.setTitle(winInfo.id, …)`, the e2e leg
reads the title off the window, and test-window-types censuses the idiom
across src/lib. The panel's section header also says `disabled` for a
disabled adapter, beside its rows' "not polling" chips.

**THE ws HANDLER IS REMOVED BY NAME (r2).** `ws.onGlobal()` returned undefined,
so `off?.()` in both teardowns was a silent no-op: a CLOSED channel window kept
re-rendering, kept fetching and kept POSTing /read over the user's mark (3,689
POSTs in six seconds from three closed windows, and the mark itself
overwritten), holding its whole detached DOM subtree alive. `onGlobal` now
RETURNS its own unsubscribe — that is the load-bearing half, MEASURED:
reverting it alone reddens the contract pin while reverting the two teardowns
alone is ALL PASS — and the named-const teardown is a belt that does not depend
on a return value nobody asserts.


**g3 — THE PANEL IS AN IM (2.369.159; design §22, the owner's clarification of 2026-09-22 "the first screen is the group list, a simple IM").** One sentence per invariant:
the FIRST SCREEN is ONE list (`.chan-groups`, rows `.chan-grow` — distinct classes from the account rows `.chan-row`, so nothing that counts or measures the account rows ever sees a group row) of every agent group and every TRACKED conversation of a non-built-in source, sorted by last activity (`groupListRows`); a row is glyph · name · time / source chip (`Agents` / `Direct` / the account's label) · last line · unread, carrying `data-grow` (the key), `data-group` (a group) and `data-at` (the instant it is ordered by); archived groups fold apart under "Archived groups (n)" (per page session); an UNTRACKED external conversation is NOT in it (nothing fetched, no history — its Track verb stays in the account's section) and neither are the built-in agents SOURCES; the accounts (every non-built-in adapter's section + the Connect block) and the **Message watcher** (the built-in section, found by its `builtin` FACT — the pre-g3 `kind === 'agents' || id === 'agents'` spelling is gone) are SECONDARY `.chan-part`s below, each folded by the user, the fold PATCHed to user state as `channelsPanelFolds` (merge-only, only the known parts, only a literal true — `foldsFrom`), loaded once per page and followed from other clients through `user-state-updated` (every live panel repaints; a panel no longer in the document is pruned at the next dispatch); the panel draws from TWO broadcasts, each carrying its own recomputed half — `channels-updated` the digest, `channel-groups-updated` the owner's group list (with `unread`) — and neither repaint fetches (test-channels-groups-e2e ⑥ counts both routes; test-channels-e2e ⑬ still counts `/api/channels`); the bar's house button **New group** (plus glyph + label, the label hidden only under 160 px) opens `showGroupMembersDialog`; a group row's context menu is the group's own verbs (Open / Members & notifications… / Invite… / Rename… / Archive), a channel row keeps the `channel-row` contributions.
THE COMPOSER IS DECIDED BY `composerMode`, NEVER AN ADAPTER ID: an external conversation offering `sendAsUser` ⇒ **Send** (`data-channel-direct`, `POST …/send` — the owner's own words out at once, as the owner; the note says the outbox holds only agent drafts; the toast words `sent` / `failed` / `unknown` by state); only `sendAsBot` ⇒ **Propose** (`data-channel-propose`, `POST …/propose`) with "Sending as you is not offered here (<the send-as-user reason>)" before the policy sentence; nothing offered ⇒ the untracked footer or the named read-only reason, NO composer element (P0's exit condition unchanged); the inline outbox cards stay for agent drafts.
AN AGENT GROUP IS THE SAME `channel` WINDOW TYPE (`openSpec {action:'openChannel', adapterId: GROUP_ADAPTER_ID, convId: <groupId>}` — layout restore, sync, tabs, taskbar unchanged, `isGroupConv` routes it to `openGroupWindow`): the log from `/api/channel-groups/:id/messages` (paged upward by `before`), a system record (create / invite / leave / kick / rename / archive) worded HERE by kind in the device's language (`groupSysText`; the record's own `text` is the agent-facing English, the fallback), the invite's context under its record (`.chanmsg-ctx`), the owner's messages drawn as "You"; the bar = the name + a members chip (`data-group-members`) + ⋯ (the group's verbs) + a meta line (Agent group / Direct conversation · You (observer) · member names · Archived); THE COMPOSER SENDS DIRECTLY AS YOU (`data-group-composer`, `data-group-send` → `POST /api/channel-groups/:id/post`, never `/propose`): `@` opens an autocomplete over the member names (`mentionQuery`/`mentionCandidates`/`insertMention`; ↑/↓/Enter/Tab/Esc, Esc stops at the popup), a PREVIEW under the box names who THIS text would wake — "Will wake alpha, beta — 2 billed turn(s)" in amber, else "nobody is woken" (`wakePreview` = the model's own `mentionsIn` + the D2 table; test-channels-groups-ui proves it equals the engine's `wakeVerdict` over notify³ × five texts) — and the send answers with its record (drawn at once, deduplicated by `vendorId` against the broadcast's `messages`) and the wake echo in the toast (`wakeEchoText`: woke N = N billed turns, said at 0; refused wakes "not billed"; who reads it next turn); an archived group has no composer; the window marks the group READ on open and on touch while it has unread (`POST …/read`, a user act, never a repaint); the broadcast updates the bar from the list and appends the new records — no full re-render per event.
XSS: every group name, member name, invite context, last line and message body reaches the DOM through textContent (`el()`, `.textContent`, createModalShell's title, showContextMenu's plain `label`) — test-channels-groups-ui's census over the five client files has ZERO innerHTML writes, with a planted `title.innerHTML = r.title` as its control, and test-channels-groups-e2e renders a hostile `<img onerror>` name as text in the row, the bar and the window title.
THE NARROW-RAIL THRESHOLD IS 160 px (was 180, MEASURED): the taller IM panel scrolls at the default 260 px sidebar and the list's own 15 px scrollbar dropped the content box from 187 to 172 px — under 180, so the DEFAULT width drew the narrow layout whenever the list scrolled (latent on any long list before g3; test-channels-e2e ⑫(a) went red on exactly that). Gate: test-channels-groups-ui (fast) + test-channels-groups-e2e (heavy) + test-channels-e2e ⑩b/⑫/⑬.

**r3 (agent groups, 2026-09-23):** the conversation composer reads the adapter row's `sendStartsTurn` (from `GET /api/channels/:a/:c`'s `adapter`): the note says "it wakes this agent: 1 billed turn" (amber) and the Send carries `expectWakes: 1` (0 elsewhere). The GROUP composer posts through `fetchJson` itself (not `groupPost`) so a `409 wake-count-mismatch` that carries the server's `group` view REPAINTS the bar, the preview and the @-autocomplete before the toast — a member renamed since the window drew it no longer makes every click a 409 (the server also re-announces renamed members: groups-engine `noteRoster`). The panel draws one `chan-quarantine-note` warning line per `digest.quarantined` entry above the group list (adapters.json: "your accounts were reset, reconnect them"; blocked: "could NOT be set aside — changes are refused"), zh + ja.

### src/lib/channel-groups-view.js (PURE)

THE IM-FIRST PANEL'S ARITHMETIC (g3): DOM-free and word-free — every function returns STRUCTURE and the panel / window say the words with the device's `t`; its only import is the PURE group model (`GROUP_ADAPTER_ID`, `NOTIFY_MODES`, `DEFAULT_NOTIFY`, `OWNER`, `mentionsIn` — spelled once there; test-architecture's EXCEPTIONS row names the edge). `groupListRows({groups, conversations, adapters})` → `{rows, archived}` (groups + TRACKED non-built-in conversations, newest activity first, order a property of the data); `composerMode({group}|{conv})` → group | archived | direct | propose (+ the send-as-user `why`) | untracked | readonly (+ `why`); `mentionQuery(text, caret)` (an `@` at the start or after whitespace/an opening bracket, read up to the CARET; `x@y` is an address) / `mentionCandidates(members, q)` (prefix first, then substring, never the owner) / `insertMention`; `memberRows(group)` (the owner FIRST as the observer, an unknown stored mode reads as the default); `pickerSections(sessions, tasks, {exclude})` (one section per Task Group by title, each session ONCE, no-group last, members DISABLED, nothing pre-selected — D1); `wakePreview(group, text)` (who a draft sent as You would wake — mute never, an @ yes, `always` yes); `wakeCount(answer)`; `foldsFrom(userState)` + `PANEL_PARTS`. Gate: test-channels-groups-ui §1 (incl. the wake-preview PARITY with the engine's `wakeVerdict` and a mute-blind preview as its control).

### src/lib/channel-group-dialogs.js (CLIENT)

THE AGENT-GROUP DIALOGS (g3, design §22.5): `showGroupMembersDialog(app, {group?})` = New group (name + members + opening context + "Wake now", default ON) or Invite… (the same dialog minus the name, existing members drawn disabled "already a member"): the members come from `GET /api/channel-groups/roster` titled by the sidebar's Task Groups (`groupTitle`), ONE checkbox per session and none per group (D1), the echo under Wake now says the cost BEFORE the click ("will wake N agent(s) (N billed turn(s))" / "nobody is woken — they read it on their next turn"), Create is disabled until a name and two agents (Invite: one) are picked, the answer's wake echo is the toast and a created group's window opens at once (never waiting for the broadcast); `showGroupDetail(app, group)` = the member list (the owner first as "You (observer)" — "sees everything, never woken"; every member's notify mode as a select the OWNER may change for anyone, reverted with a toast on refusal; creator chip; "not running" for a member whose session is not live; Remove, confirmed, a pair's removal saying the direct conversation will be archived) + Invite… (not on a pair) / Rename… / Archive (danger), repainted IN PLACE from `channel-groups-updated` (skipped while a select is mid-choice); `renameGroup` / `archiveGroup` via showInputDialog / showConfirmDialog; `groupPost` toasts every refusal by its CODE (`groupErrorText`). Every agent-controlled string is textContent. Gate: test-channels-groups-ui §3 + test-channels-groups-e2e ①④.

## Index essays (moved VERBATIM from the CLAUDE.md index on 2026-09-15 — CLAUDE.md keeps the head of each entry; this section is the full text)

### src/plugin-manifest.js

src/plugin-manifest.js — PURE plugin manifest validator (Plugin Ph2, 2.369.24): id=<publisher>.<name>=folder, semver, engines.vibespace min, client tier, server flag, contributes windows/agentTools/routes, declared capabilities; 2.369.43-.44 hardening = cleanText() on every free-text field (it reaches generated code), fs paths COLLAPSED **and their `*` wildcard MODELLED as the string prefix node matches** before the forbidden-root test (`/*` / `<parent>/*` used to pass; B-7638: the two rules meet at `~/.*` — collapsing the dot emitted `<home>*` = the whole home dir + every sibling home, so a `.` segment before `*` is refused), agentTools ⇒ needsConsent

### src/server/plugin-loader.js

src/server/plugin-loader.js — PLUGIN LOADER (Ph2): data/plugins/<id>/ manifests → sandboxed iframe assets at /plugins/<id>/ (opaque-origin CSP), forked server.js processes (IPC v1: route/tool/shutdown, crash backoff, parked after 5/10min), /api/plugins/<id>/x/* proxy (nosniff + sandbox CSP, no document content-type from an untrusted plugin), generated agent-tool shims data/bin/vibespace-tool-<id>-<name> → /api/agent/plugin-tool/ (bearer-validated; manifest text enters them ONLY through jsLiteral), data/plugin-registry.json (consent is per PACKAGE: contentHash+source, a different package under a trusted id is disabled + re-prompted — gated on the REGISTRY record, never on a folder having been replaced: 2.369.44, consent outlives a hand-deleted plugin dir), broadcasts plugins-manifests-updated. Example: docs/examples/hello-plugin

### src/channel-record.js

src/channel-record.js — PURE (imports nothing) THE ONE normalized message record every channel adapter produces (docs/design-communication-panel.zh.md §4): {id, convId, adapterId, vendorId, at, author, text, mentions, attachments, replyTo, threadKey, raw}. THREE rules: **`vendorId` IS THE DEDUP KEY** (a replayed page must be a no-op — Lark's anchor semantics guarantee one at every boundary; a screen-scraping source DECLARES a minted key with `raw.synthetic`, because the invariant wants A key, not a vendor-issued one, while an UNDECLARED minted key turns every re-scan into a batch of duplicates); **`@_user_N` are PER-MESSAGE ORDINALS, not identities** (resolved against that message's own `mentions`, and an ordinal with nothing behind it is left VERBATIM — inventing a name is the mis-attribution the rule exists to stop); **an external body may not carry OUR OWN frame syntax** (`<system-reminder>`/`<vibespace-*>`/`<task-notification>`/`<persisted-output>`/`<local-command-stdout>`/`<command-name>`/`<command-args>` are neutered at NORMALIZATION, because the record is the one shape every consumer reads). **r2: the neutering runs over EVERY peer-controlled field, not just `text`** — `author.name`, `mentions[].name` and `attachments[].name` came out with LIVE frames, which made that claim false at SOURCE while §7.5's agent block renders `from <author>`; `peerText()` is the ONE door, attributes are matched too, and the fixed half of the pattern is held by a grep-derived FRAME CENSUS (every hyphenated tag the tree writes must be neutered or classified as prose) because a hand-written list is the tool this class defeats. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### src/channel-caps.js

src/channel-caps.js — PURE (imports nothing) THE ONE place that answers "does this control exist" and "which lane is carrying this row RIGHT NOW" (design §4/§6.4/§12.5). Two axes MODELLED not flattened: how messages arrive (push|poll|scan + the per-PLATFORM `scanSources`/`scanLatency`/`historyBySource`) and what may be sent as whom (`sendAs`, narrowed per conversation by `convCaps`). **`laneState` = DEMOTED > LIVE > CLAIM** and `unknown` (the default) never carries content; liveness needs POSITIVE evidence and a demoted or dead push lane answers `via:'poll'` because that is where the records come from — the fact used to live in three stores with nothing saying which won (the `opencode-events` round-4 lesson: a lane that lies about being active is worse than no lane, because it turns the fallback OFF). **`scanState` = FACTS FRESH > PLATFORM > CLIENT PRESENT > READ GRANT > `'ui'`**, with ONE deliberate exception: a REFUSED read is the NAMED `tcc-denied` with `source:null` and never a silent fall back, because swapping a 15-second lane for a 5-minute one turns the latency on the row — this class's whole honesty contract — into a lie. `convCaps`/`scan.hostFacts` are CACHES (vendor round trips, not re-derivable) and pay for it with a 6h TTL + an honest degrade. `offers` needs BOTH halves and renders `unknown` as "not offered + a reason"; `freshnessClaim` takes its clock as an argument because it answers "how long ago". **r2: THE RESOLVERS RETURN STRUCTURE AND THE CLIENT SAYS THE WORDS** — `freshnessClaim` answers `{kind, state, seconds}` and `freshnessText(claim,{t})` renders it (the engine called the old composing form with no translator, so nine human-visible strings shipped English-only to a zh/ja UI, invisible to the build's i18n scan because they left the server as DATA; and the server structurally cannot take a translator — the digest is broadcast to every client while the language is per DEVICE). `state` exists because `kind` alone collapses "not scanning" with "not scanned yet"; `identityWarning` keeps only the adapter's OWN `verbatim` sentence on the wire. **`authState(record, now)`** is the same discipline for "is this adapter authenticated": the LAST PASS's `auth-expired` outranks a stamped expiry that has not arrived (a revoked credential carries a perfectly future one), a passed expiry is `expired`, and NO credential is `unknown` — never the stub whose two ternary branches were both `'connected'`. **r3: `freshnessClaim(caps, lane, entry, now, {enabled})` answers `state:'off'` + `why` (`untracked` / `adapter-disabled` / the scan resolver's own reason) for a row nothing will ever fetch** — untracked is the DEFAULT state of every discovered row and "within 5m" there was a promise about a fetch that would never happen; `tracked` is read STRICTLY, and `freshnessText` renders `off` as "not polling" / "not scanning" by lane. **P1b: `pushSamplesAdd`/`pushMissRate`/`pushDemotionVerdict` = the exclusivity MEASUREMENT over a ROLLING window (24 h or the last 200 records, whichever is larger; 2 % over ≥ 20; never true for a lane already demoted), `pushLaneText` = the adapter row's sentence WITH the numbers, `caps.pushOptIn` = the poll lane until `push.enabled === true`.** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### src/quota-model.js

src/quota-model.js — PURE (imports nothing; CJS so the bundle and the shipped statusline carry it) THE TYPED LIMIT SET (2026-09-09): an account key holds a LIST of limits — {limitId, name, scope plan|model|credits|overage, windows[{kind,minutes,usedPct,resetsAt,state running|empty|unknown,measuredAt}], flags, provenance} — because the vendors send several at once (B-9213: codex pushed `codex` + `GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark` + `premium` in ONE conversation, all collapsed last-writer-wins into one file with the plan limit GONE) and because a window that has not started reports `resetsAt = now + duration` on every read (B-8b12: a sliding reset became a precise panel time, an EDF deadline and an auto-resume arm). `limitFor` = the ONE accessor, `remaining`/`deadline` ignore empty windows, `mergeLimitSets` merges per limitId. Also `windowRefutes`/`wallAttribution` = whose wall is this (inc-mttbrtc0-6049): a running window's reset cannot move before it ends, so a contradicting reset REFUTES a member but identifies nobody — the slot ledger identifies, the window corroborates, and only their agreement moves a byte. **r2: `refutationStrength(kind)` says how much that refutation is worth — WEEKLY (7d/scoped) `decisive` (0 self-contradictions in 9998 judged readings here), FIVE-HOUR `corroborating` only (73.72 % of its refutations are true positives, but 13/1706 of its own producer's readings contradict its own stamp — B-9213 inside the plan bucket), anything unmeasured `none`; refusing a wall is money too, so a 5h disagreement nothing corroborates leaves the pin and SAYS so.** **r3: a bucket that makes a CLAIM must keep counting — `windowState` tests the stated spend BEFORE the reset (a deadline says whether a window STARTED, never whether it is spent), a stored `state` may not survive a producer re-stating the numbers (producers drop it at the restate, `fromLegacy` keeps the clock-free `usedPct > 0` belt for files older builds wrote — but a `status`-only event leaves it, or a genuinely empty window flips to running), and `toLegacyView(set,{nowSec})`'s `fiveHour` is THE BINDING BURST CONSTRAINT — ranked by `windowRemaining` on the accessor's own clock (a passed reset means the window ROLLED OVER and is full; ranking on raw `usedPct` re-created the very defect, accessor 50 % vs pool 90 %) with the plan window SEEDED so it wins every tie — so the projection can never be more optimistic than `remaining()`.** **r6: `markScopedEnumeration`/`scopedEnumeration`/`authoritativeScopesOf` = DID THIS READ SEE THE WHOLE SET — the ONE rule the enumerating producers ask before they may RETIRE a limit, marked on the parse result as a NON-ENUMERABLE, SYMBOL-KEYED property so a spread / a JSON round trip / a preserve-merge all lose it (no authority = the safe direction) and no stored file can forge it.** **B-9f4b: the r5 half counts only a model cap the parse NAMED (`scopedNamedCount` — a display name, a `seven_day_<model>` key, a panel line; a codename bucket never), and `toLegacyView` never projects the limit promoted into the plan slot a second time as a `scopedWeekly` row.** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **THE MODEL-CAP LANE (inc-mubu23bd-5vxi, 2026-09-21):** `MODEL_CAP_PLACEHOLDER` = {limitId 'model:cap', name 'Model cap'} — scope model, family null: it counts for the account-level min (the conservative direction), governs no named family, and is NEVER the plan; `scopedLimitId(name)` is the ONE id spelling (fromLegacy, the harness builder and the naming rule ask it; 'Model cap' round-trips to model:cap); `nameModelCapLane({limits, scoped, resetsAt, hint, jitterSec})` is the PURE ladder — the sidecar family with this reset → an existing model limit with this reset (±WINDOW_JITTER_SEC) → the hint family among several → else the placeholder; a window with NO reset is named only by a hint matching a cap the account has SHOWN; `foldPlaceholderCap`, run by every `mergeLimitSets`, is the ONE permitted collapse: the placeholder folds into the single NAMED model limit sharing its weekly reset (the newer window wins), stays put on a different or absent reset or an ambiguous pair, and two NAMED limits still never collapse (test-quota-model ⑲). The legacy projection is untouched: a plan-less set still projects its only window-bearing limit (⑭, codex's rule), so a claude file whose first reading is an un-windowed bucket event shows it as `sevenDay` until the first 5h/7d event lands — bounded, documented, never the case on 2.1.274 where every record states the plan windows.

### src/usage-cache-write.js

src/usage-cache-write.js — THE ONE WRITE PATH for data/usage-cache/*.json (design-account-hardening §4.2): validates the typed set, merges per limit, stamps source/fetchedAt per LIMIT, writes the legacy buckets as a DERIVED VIEW beside `limits`, owns the `.window-`/`.slot-` sidecars, and composes (never forks) the slot/window guards. A grep-derived standing sweep fails any other writer; the reader census fails any unclassified raw-bucket reader. **r2: a CLAUDE array with no `plan` limit takes its plan limit from the legacy view — the shipped statusline (the one allowlisted whole-object writer) now spreads the stored object instead of enumerating what to keep, and DROPS the single limit it can measure so this rung rebuilds it with that object's own source/clock; every other limit keeps the provenance of the producer that measured it.** **r5: the LIFT is the other half — a legacy object is ONE reading spread over a carry-forward, so `carryUnmeasuredLimits` (lift-only, WINDOW granularity, never applied to a typed set) keeps the previous reading's `source`/`fetchedAt`/`measuredAt` for any claim (`quotaModel.limitClaimKey` — the numbers, never the clock or the derived state) the write did not move, and `authoritativeScopes` lets ONLY a producer whose own parse enumerated a scope retire a limit it no longer names. A file's `source` and a limit's `source` are different questions and may disagree.** **r6: the right to retire is asked of the PARSE (`quotaModel.authoritativeScopesOf`), which each producer marks only when it dropped nothing — the three claude parsers disagreed on one vendor state, so six of the seven sites retired a spent cap they could never have seen; and the retirement line now NAMES the claim it drops (`model:opus (100% 7d, running)`), because removing a limit removes a constraint the pool reads.** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **The lift rung restores a MODEL cap too (inc-mubu23bd-5vxi):** a claude object whose `limits` array lacks the limit a legacy `scopedWeekly` entry names is that entry's reading — the statusline drops the `model:<name>` limit it measured exactly as it drops the plan one (2.1.274 ships `rate_limits.model_scoped[]`) — restored with the object's own provenance; every write-path write projects the array INTO `scopedWeekly`, so an entry only outlives its limit through the producer that cannot construct one (test-quota-model ⑲ LIFT).

### server.js

server.js — BOOTSTRAP + WIRING ONLY (~1910 lines since the 2.325.0 拆分; the arch suite RATCHETS it ≤2100). **One HOT PATH still lives here and it is named: `refreshWebuiPids()`** — it runs IN-BAND on every kill (ws-handler, before the broadcast) and 3 s after every create, so it asks `cli-identity.readChildPids` and starts NO child process per session (the `pgrep -P` it replaces blocked the loop 9,180.6 ms for 61 sessions at 1,560 MB RSS for the identical 244 pids). server.js is in BOTH halves of the test-architecture §45 spawn census — half (b) finds it by looking up where `refreshWebuiPids` is DEFINED — and its four surviving spawns (auto-update `git pull`/`npm install`/`npm run build`, `resolveCmd`'s `/usr/bin/which`) each carry a BOOT-ONLY reason. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### scripts/ci.mjs

scripts/ci.mjs — THE RELEASE GATE, TWO TIERS (B-4c5a, 2026-09-07): the tier table `{name, tier:'fast'|'heavy', why}` + EXCLUDED-with-a-reason, both runners, the detached `--heavy-launch`, the push-blocking `--check-heavy`, `--status`, `--census`, and (round 2) the MACHINE lock that keeps one heavy tier per box + `machineGlobalFixtures` (PURE: a suite claiming a literal port it binds or a fixed `/tmp` path it creates — banned in the fast tier, asserted over every fast row). Exit codes: 0 green · 1 red · 2 refused (dirty tree / bad `--only`) · 3 did not run (never got the lock) · 4 ABORTED (superseded / lock taken / terminated) — 0 and 1 are the only VERDICTS and no no-verdict path may ever exit 0. `killedFromOutside` is an ALLOWLIST of SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP (round 4): a crash signal is a fact about the code under test. `fastGate` also takes `--isolate --sha=<x>` (round 5): the hook runs the FAST tier in a scratch worktree AT a pushed ref's tip when that tip is not the commit you have checked out, writes NO green marker for it, and NAMES its subject in the closing line. `runSuite` SKIPS (never fails) a suite the gated commit does not contain (round 6 — the table is this gate's, the sources are that commit's; both tiers count them, the heavy marker carries `absent`, and a run where every suite was absent claims nothing). Imported (never re-run) by test-architecture §43 so the census rides in `npm run build`. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **2.369.104 THE SCRATCH-ORPHAN REAPER (owner 2026-09-16 "系统变得异常缓慢，进程树里有大量vibespace相关进程", the KVM went blank): every worktree server a gate suite boots spawns a DETACHED `vibespace-device` daemon (setsid, by design — production's must outlive a server restart) plus wrapper/child node processes, and a suite's teardown kills only the server it spawned. Measured: 504 device daemons (34.8 GB RSS, up to 76 h old) + 552 node processes under /tmp/vs-* + 2,137 orphaned `dtach -a` bridge clients, 86 GB used, load 15. `scratchOrphans({procRoot, now, staleMs, self})` is PURE over a proc root (test-ci-gate §8 drives a fake one): a candidate is a KNOWN executable (`REAP_NAMES` + `vibespace-device*` + `chrome*`) whose cwd / HOME / VIBESPACE_DEVICE_ROOT / VIBESPACE_AGENTD_ROOT lies under a `/tmp/vs-<name>-<random>` scratch dir (`SCRATCH_ROOT_RE` — the shape scripts/scratch.mjs mints; production is rooted in a checkout), grouped by that root; a group is reaped when the dir is GONE (the suite cleaned up and left the process) or when EVERY member is unowned (walking parents through fellow members reaches systemd/init or a vanished pid — never a live process outside the group) AND older than the 10-min fixture stale floor; a ci.mjs runner is never a candidate (the isolated heavy tier lives in /tmp/vs-ci-heavy-* for its whole run) and this process + its ancestors are skipped. `reapScratchOrphans` SIGTERMs then SIGKILLs after 3 s; it runs after EVERY `runSuite` (the fast tier's sync runner), after every suite on every LANE of the heavy tier (`reapScratchOrphansAsync`, 2026-09-16 — the sync twin's `Atomics.wait` grace would freeze the other lanes; the heavy tier never calls `runSuite`, so master's wiring alone reaped nothing between heavy suites), at the start of every `heavyLaunch`, and by hand as `node scripts/ci.mjs --reap`. 不变量=a process a suite starts is the suite's to end, and when the suite cannot (a detached daemon) the gate owns the standing sweep — evidence-based (root + ownership + age), never a name heuristic, never production.** **P8-2 x3 (2026-09-22):** heavy row `test-desktop-xpra` (a real server with auth + the real xpra rung driven from node, ~50 s, SKIPs with evidence without xpra / xauth / Xvfb / an X app). **B-3ccf ALREADY GREEN (2.369.164 batch 2):** `heavyLaunch` does not start a tier whose verdict is already on disk — PURE `heavyAlreadyGreen({markers, sha, full, commitTimeMs, scope, range, now})` (exported; heavyLaunch feeds it the markers with their file mtimes and `git show -s --format=%ct`) skips only for a GREEN for exactly that sha (short sha via its full one), not partial, whose mtime is newer than the commit time, FULL — or AFFECTED over the SAME range when this launch is affected too; then `heavy already GREEN for <sha> (<age>), not relaunching`, exit 0, no child. RED (or a red at least as new), partial, stale, narrower ⇒ relaunch; no commit time ⇒ never skip. Asked AFTER the supersession loop (an ancestor's run is still stopped). Gate: test-ci-heavy-launch §8 (fast; 129). ⇒ kb-bugfix-invariants.md

### scripts/mutant-copy.mjs (B-0220 generalized, batch r1)

scripts/mutant-copy.mjs — THE ONE place a negative control's PATCHED COPY of a product module is written (NOT a test-*.mjs, like scratch.mjs — no tier). `mutantCopies(name, repo)` → `{dir, files, write, load, pathFor}`: `dir` = `scratch('<name>-mut')` (per pid, removed on 'exit'); `write(origRel, src, tag?, {esm?, name?})` → the copy's absolute path — CJS (`.cjs`, so CommonJS whatever package.json says) gets `var require = require('node:module').createRequire(<real path>), __filename = <real path>, __dirname = <real dir>;` inserted on the original's FIRST-STATEMENT line (after a shebang and after a `'use strict'` directive — a statement before the directive would silently drop strict mode; never inside a leading comment), so `./x`/`../x` reach the very files AND require-cache entries a sibling reached and every line number is the original's; ESM (`.mjs`; chosen by the source's own syntax — top-level import/export, no `require(`/`module.exports` — or `esm:true`) gets every relative specifier (`from`, bare `import '…'`, `import('…')`) and `import.meta.url` rewritten to the real file's URL (`rebaseEsm`); `name` + `pathFor(name, ext)` let a CLOSED WORLD of copies require/import EACH OTHER by absolute path (quota-model ⑯/⑰, fable-cap-pool-storm's stdout chain, channels-engine's registry+fake+engine trio, xpra-client's proto/client/view trio); `load` = `write` + require (CJS only). `copiesCensus(files, dir, repo, {minCopies, match})` → two rows for the suite's own `ok`: git's view of `src/` INCLUDING ignored files narrowed to this pid (or `match`, for names with no pid) is empty, and every copy exists outside the checkout in `dir` — taken WHILE the copies exist (after exit it passes on the pre-fix placement too). `sweepLegacy(repo, dirs, re)` removes what a PRE-FIX run stranded, dead PIDs only. Used by 27 suites; test-architecture §51 is the census (no `scripts/*.mjs` write into `src/`, no wildcard `.js` ignore under `src/`, the helper's CJS/ESM contract driven). A copy that is loaded INTO a worktree (restore-liveness' e2e boot) is installed from the raw patched text, never from the rebound copy (whose require points at THIS checkout).

### scripts/test-new-member-wake.mjs + test-auto-resume-loop.mjs

scripts/test-new-member-wake.mjs + test-auto-resume-loop.mjs — THE PAIR (B-0220): every patched copy test-new-member-wake loads goes through `loadCopy(origRel, src)` (since batch r1 a thin delegate to scripts/mutant-copy.mjs, the one helper every suite uses) — written to `scratch('wake-mut')` as `.cjs`, its `require` re-bound on line 1 to `createRequire(<the real module's path>)` (relative requires and the require cache exactly as a sibling's; line numbers unchanged), NEVER a sibling in `src/` (a 2026-09-22 integration: test-auto-resume-loop's §5 `noteRecovered` census walked `src/` while the other suite's mutant engine sat there — 3 red, green alone; the old names were gitignored, which hid them from git only). §10 = the tree census taken WHILE the copies exist (`git status --porcelain --ignored --untracked-files=all -- src`) + the helper's ledger outside the checkout. `VS_WAKE_HOLD=<path>` = HOLD MODE: the suite writes `<path>.ready` (the copy paths) after §10 and waits for `<path>.go` (or its parent's death, or 5 min). test-auto-resume-loop starts such a held child FIRST, runs its whole self inside the hold, then releases it and asserts it green (heavy, ~14 s) — the concurrency held open deterministically, not raced for. Counts: new-member-wake 121 (fast), auto-resume-loop 221 (heavy).

### scripts/scratch.mjs `withoutVendorKeys` + the real-CLI legs (B-5f0b)

scripts/scratch.mjs `withoutVendorKeys(env)` / `VENDOR_KEY_ENV` — THE REAL-CLI LEG RULES (B-5f0b, 2.369.164 batch 3; the 2.369.69 red: a real `codex app-server` leg asserted before the server's own idle drain died on its 401, only under load). Every leg that runs a REAL claude / codex / opencode obeys two rules. ① **Its spawn env has no ambient vendor key**: `withoutVendorKeys()` drops OPENAI_API_KEY, CODEX_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN (a fake HOME / CODEX_HOME removes the LOGIN, never an env key — a leaked key would bill the drained turn, and the two Anthropic names outrank the oat test-chat-e2e seeds; `agentEnv()` passes them through on purpose, it is the user's choice in production). test-architecture §50 is the census: a `scripts/test-*.mjs` / `probe-*.mjs` that resolves a real CLI BY NAME (`command -v claude|codex|opencode`, `spawn('codex'…`, `OPENCODE_CMD || 'opencode'`) imports and calls it, or declares `// real-cli-env: <reason ≥10 chars>` (env built from nothing, or a binary that is only read / asked `--version`: test-design-kit, test-init-frame, test-permission-rules, test-stdout-registry). ② **It judges only after the child's TERMINAL signal, bounded**: `exit` for one-shots, the reply to its own request, `turn/completed` / `error` / a 401 for a server-started turn (test-queue-steer ⑩), `result` for a claude turn — scripts/probe-claude-stdout.mjs reports `sawResult`/`resultSubtype` and test-stdout-registry's `wireVerdict` SKIPs a capture that never reached its result (a budget expiry or a mid-turn death), control = the fake CLI's `FAKE_CLI_NO_RESULT` cut; test-vendor-whitelist's strace re-measurement reports a timeout-killed trace as `timedOut` (SKIP with evidence), never as a zero-connect measurement; test-opencode-s9 polls the live lane's `connected` and the second process's `external` row instead of one fixed sleep. Stub-only suites (test-codex-p2-wrapper, test-opencode-plugin, test-acp-harness) have no real-binary leg. Local pitfall: `NODE_OPTIONS=--preserve-symlinks` breaks the nvm `codex` shim and those legs SKIP — run them with NODE_OPTIONS unset to see them execute.

### scripts/test-ax-budget.mjs

### scripts/test-ax-paint.mjs

scripts/test-ax-paint.mjs — THE PAINT-ONLY CENSUS (fast; design-accessibility-tree §3 rows 2 + 3 in their §8 lean form, chunk a2): from the SOURCE, every paint-only element is marked before it is born and the marking never took a control's only name. ① icons.js `_s()` emits `aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"` on the `<svg>`, asserted FUNCTIONALLY over every exported FILE_ICONS / UI_ICONS value (the two raw strings that bypass the helper — `python`, `alert` — are covered because the values are what ships); ② the icon-only `<button>` census over every src/lib template (an `${UI_ICONS.…}` / backend-icon interpolation / inline `<svg>` / entity with no letters beside it ⇒ `title=` or `aria-label=` required; the same rule over DOM-built `x = document.createElement('button')` … `x.innerHTML = <rhs>;` whose right-hand side, its icon references / tags / entities taken out, has no letter or digit left — the template branch's own test, so `UI_ICONS.k`, `UI_ICONS.k + ' '` and `` `${UI_ICONS.k}` `` are icon-only and `UI_ICONS.inbox + segs` carries text), the classifier negative-controlled on a fixture string AND the whole census over a scratch copy of src/lib with a nameless `nb.innerHTML = UI_ICONS.copy + ' ';` planted in chat-input.js (must flag exactly that button; verifier LOW-1 — the exact-statement classifier `x.innerHTML = UI_ICONS.k;` passed that form green); ③ every `.chat-code-ln` gutter, `.chat-diff-prefix`, `.chat-run-arrow`, spinner creation site (a census over `chat-spinner` / `upload-active-spinner`, 10 sites), the 8 resize handles, the `.chat-minimap` strip and the tab strip's `.tab-split-glyph` (2.369.162 — the split mark became an element when the CSS `⫿` glyph was deleted, so ④'s named-family list dropped `⫿`) carry the attribute, and the TOC button is a SIBLING of the strip (appended to the container, never inside the hidden subtree); ④ the CSS glyph census over chat/style/viewers/theme-editor.css — a `content:` string that is a GLYPH (an escape or a non-ASCII character and no letters) carries the alt-text form `content: '…' / ""` as the LAST content declaration of its rule (the plain declaration stays first as the fallback for a parser without the slash syntax) and no TEXT string carries it (`'Collapse'`, the customize-mode sentence — a first cut's "non-ASCII ⇒ glyph" rule caught the em-dash sentence, which is why the classifier refuses letters); ⑤ ci.mjs carries the suite. 不变量=an aria-hidden icon is no longer a name, so the census that hides icons is the census that checks every icon-only button still has one; a generated glyph is alt-text "" and a generated sentence never is.

### The paint-only layer (a2, 2.369.150 — design-accessibility-tree §3 row 2 + row 3 lean)

icons.js — `_s()`, the ONE helper every UI/file icon goes through, emits `aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"` on the `<svg>` (the `python` / `alert` raw strings carry the same two attributes by hand): an icon is paint, never a name or a tab stop; every icon-only button names itself with `title=` / `aria-label=` (test-ax-paint ② census, 7 buttons today, 0 unnamed). Gate: test-ax-paint ①②.
highlight.js — the `.chat-code-ln` gutter span (both template sites, the truncation row too) is `aria-hidden`: a line number is paint; the text of the line stays exposed once. Gate: test-ax-paint ③.
chat-renderers.js — the `.chat-diff-prefix` span (both diff renderers) and the three tool-card spinners are `aria-hidden`; the copy path reads the prefix by `textContent` and is unaffected. Gate: test-ax-paint ③; test-owner-batch-2369-32's `</span>${mediaHtml}<details` seam untouched.

**THE LIVE WORKFLOW CARD'S TWO FRAGMENTS + THE CLI's AGENT WORDS (inc-mudv05ja-n5rv, 2.369.160).** The Workflow branch of `renderToolResult` draws the lifecycle chip through `renderTaskChip(ti)` and the live tree through `renderWorkflowLive(ti)` — the SAME two methods ChatView's in-place patch (`_patchWorkflowCard`) renders from, so a patched card and a fresh render can never draw two trees; phases carry `data-phase`, chips `data-agent-key` (`a:<agentId>` else `i:<index>`), the dot is `aria-hidden`. PURE exported `workflowAgentState(raw)` is the ONE vocabulary mapping: the CLI's working words `start` / `progress` (and the fixture's `running`) draw as `running` — production has never said `running` (8 buffers: 161 progress / 26 start / 253 done / 56 error), so chat.css's `[data-state="running"]` pulse and the tally's "N running" were dead until this; the chip's `data-state` AND the tally counts read it. `drawsWorkflowCard(msg)` answers whether renderToolMsg draws the Workflow RESULT card (not collab, a `tool_result`, not an error, toolName Workflow — mirrors the branch order) — the patch's gate. Gate: test-task-lifecycle (the vocabulary table + the end-to-end legs), test-fold-ux F2 (chrome, fed the real words: the dot pulses).
chat-view.js / chat-input.js / app.js / setup-flows.js / file-explorer-uploads.js — the `.chat-run-arrow` spans and every spinner (`chat-spinner`, `upload-active-spinner`) carry `aria-hidden` at creation; the label beside a spinner stays the live text. Gate: test-ax-paint ③ (a census over creation sites, not a list).
chat-minimap.js — the `.chat-minimap` strip is `aria-hidden` before it is appended (one marker div per user turn of the WHOLE conversation, uncapped — the one subtree that grew with the conversation's length, not the rendered window; a0 measured 201 nodes for 199 markers, a2 measures 0 — the strip's own node leaves the tree); the TOC button (`title` "Your messages (outline)") stays the accessible path to the same turns and is a SIBLING appended to the container, never inside the strip. Gate: test-ax-paint ③ + test-ax-budget ①b/④e (with the in-page control).
public/chat.css / style.css / viewers.css — every generated GLYPH (`\25B8` / `\25BE` / `\25B4` disclosure arrows, `\00B7` chip dots, the `\200e` LRM marks on paths, `†`, the role-indicator `\1F464` / `\2699` beside their font-size-0 text labels, the gear/context-menu `▸` / `\25C2`) is written twice — `content: '…'; content: '…' / "";` — so a parser with the alt-text syntax exposes nothing and one without keeps the glyph (the cascade takes the last VALID declaration); a generated SENTENCE (`'Collapse'`, `'Extra row — drag elements here'`) is never given the empty alt. Gate: test-ax-paint ④ (31 rules since 2.369.162 deleted the split tab's `⫿` — the split mark is the aria-hidden `.tab-split-glyph` element, ③; classifier negative-controlled).
MEASURED (test-ax-budget, Chrome 153, the §1c fixture): the 50-card baseline 1001 → 733 TOTAL / 516 → 260 NON-IGNORED, the window 724 → 462; after four page-ups 3214 → 2769; the 1,310-card slab window 5,448 → 4,576 TOTAL / 916 → 516 NON-IGNORED (now under the design's 5,000); the neutered-band control 20,158 → 14,871 — the paint-only layer is worth ≈ 16–36 % of a window on top of the band, and the strip's 201 nodes per window are gone.
