The account key is the credential LINK resolved per write (`VIBESPACE_ACCOUNT_LINK`, not the spawn-fixed key) and it lags the link by ONE REQUEST (2026-09-07 r3): `rate_limits` is the CLI's last API response, made with the PREVIOUS credentials, so a `.slot-<session_id>` sidecar (no `.json` — every usage-cache scanner filters on it) holds the last OBSERVED payload's fingerprint and the reading is not re-filed while the link moved but the numbers did not. **2026-09-08: that clause is now the LAST rung of ONE rule shared with the server — the sidecar records `{key, fp, win, at}` and asks the verbatim MIRROR of src/reading-lag.js (sentinel-delimited, parity-pinned), so it can also answer the case r3 could not: a payload whose WINDOW is the previous slot's even though the numbers moved. The established window (stamped only by the panel refresh) is how it knows a slot's window, and since r2 it is read from `.window-<key>` beside the cache — this file REBUILDS the cache object on every write, so a window kept in that object was deleted by one ordinary render.** **r3 two more, both reproduced: (a) the age it hands the shared rule is the RE-POINT's, read off `lstat(VIBESPACE_ACCOUNT_LINK).mtimeMs` (the pool re-MINTS that symlink), never `st.at` — that dates the last OBSERVATION, is systematically older, and one render of an idle pooled terminal therefore expired a shadow that had not started; (b) this producer now runs the WINDOW GUARD as well (re-file on the one matching account, else refuse + `.window-refused.ndjson`), because at 8 renders a minute it was the highest-frequency writer on the instance and the only one with no guard at all.** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **MODEL-SCOPED WINDOWS (claude 2.1.274, measured in the binary's statusline schema — inc-mubu23bd-5vxi):** `rate_limits.model_scoped[]` = {display_name, utilization = the server row's PERCENT (the binary's `Yde` projection puts `s.percent` there; ÷100 unconditionally, never by magnitude — 2.369.99), resets_at ISO} beside the older `seven_day_<model>` fields; `scopedFromRateLimits` writes each as the scoped bucket of that NAME (the lane is decided by what names it — never into `seven_day`), an empty list states nothing (the previous entries survive: the 2.70.0 rule), and the limits this render measured (the plan + the named model caps, matched by NAME never by re-spelling the id) are dropped so the reader reconstructs them with this producer's provenance. The statusline never carries `seven_day_overage_included` (census ⑩); the reading-lag mirror block is byte-identical still. test-quota-model ⑲ TOOL drives the real file (percent, ISO reset, an un-named Opus keeps its age, an empty list retires nothing, a top-level `seven_day_opus` names its lane the same way).

### spend-authorizer.js

spend-authorizer.js — PURE (imports nothing) THE ONE CEILING ON EVERY TURN NOBODY TYPED (design-account-hardening §4.4c / P9 / D3 / D6, 2026-09-08): the closed `SPEND_REASONS` set, `budgetLimits` (the four D6 numbers as settings; an explicit 0 is a CHOICE), rolling hour/day `spendCounts`, `authorizeUnattendedSpend` (fail closed on: an identity it cannot name · an undeclared reason · a credential that cannot serve · **paid overage in use** · each cap — while IGNORANCE never blocks, P6), `noteUnattendedSpend` (two-phase: authorize answers, note charges) with the 80% notice once per axis per window, and `overageState`/`overageText` = THE ONE READER of `cache.overage`/`cache.spend` (captured since 2.289.0, read by NOBODY until now — with overage ON utilization stays under 1 while every token is billed, so `accountRemaining()` ranked the account spending real money as the one with the most headroom). **r2: `CAP_MAX`/`stampCap` make the enforceable range equal the schema's offered range (a flat 800-stamp ledger silently never fired any cap above it), and `overageState` now DATES the claim that blocks — a record whose own `resetsAt` has passed, or whose `asOf` is older than `OVERAGE_STALE_MS` (7 d), answers 'unknown' while keeping `stated`/`evidence`; only `inUse:'yes'` is bounded, because it is the only answer that refuses anything.** **r5 adds the RESERVATION half** — `RESERVE_TTL_MS`/`pendingCounts`/`reservePending`/`releasePending`/`expirePending` and a `pending` input to `authorizeUnattendedSpend`, so an authorization that has not yet become a charge still binds the ceiling (five concurrent deliveries on one slot spent 5 turns against a cap of 2), plus `LOAD_RETENTION` = the retention a reader that cannot yet know the limits must use (the boot prune ran with the DEFAULTS and forgave 236 turns per restart). **r4 adds `spendControlState`/`spendControlText` = THE ONE READER of codex's `cache.spendControlReached` (the THIRD field the design's §1.4 row named and the one r3 marked CLOSED with zero readers): three-state, dated on the SAME `OVERAGE_STALE_MS` (imported, never re-declared — a second window for one physical fact is how twins are born), refusing under its own name in the `identity-cannot-serve` class rather than the money one, so `spend.allowOverageTurns` deliberately does NOT unlock it — that setting consents to spending money, not to being refused by the vendor. And every verdict CARRIES the identity it resolved (`identity` on both the ok and the refusal path) precisely so the charge can name the same slot.** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **B-ad05 (2026-09-17, USAGE CREDITS VISIBLE BEFORE THEY ARE SPENT): `overageState().mode` = `inUse` | `allowed` (overage present, `inUse:false`, no `status:'rejected'`/`disabledReason`) | `disabled` | `unknown`, and `overageAllowed(cache)` is that one question — an org-level configuration, so NOT date-bounded like `inUse:'no'`; it changes NO spend verdict (the guard refuses only once overage is IN USE — pinned in test-spend-paths §7c with a credits-allowed world whose continue fires).** **FINAL VERIFIER (2026-09-17): `mode:'allowed'` needs POSITIVE evidence — a vendor `status` that is not `rejected`, or a DATED `inUse:true` whose period ended or went stale; `{inUse:false}` with no status (the vendor omits `overageStatus` on ~a third of events, and the pre-fix merge wiped stored ones — two members on this instance carry exactly that shape, one of them overage-DISABLED) is `unknown`, never a last-resort rank or a "billing pay-per-use" sentence.**

### server/spend-guard.js

server/spend-guard.js — the ORCH half (persisted ledger data/spend-budget.json, journal line per (reason,identity,why) per 5min, ONE "For you" item per (identity,why) per 6h, telemetry, the Stop nudge's PERSISTED cooldown). CONSTRUCTED INSIDE usage-pool-engine (every input it needs is resolved there: the identity is the engine's own `fireIdentityFor`, never a second derivation — design §2), re-exported through server.js to auto-resume, the delivery ladder and the Stop nudge — while the engine's OWN producer (the codex reset credit) asks the module-local object directly, since a gate that depended on an injected dep server.js never passed was dead in production (r2). `credentialStateOf` is the ACCOUNT reader (`accountCredentialState` → `accountLoginState`), never the slot one: an oat-only subscription spawns and serves turns with NO credential file, and the slot reader called it dead for ever. **r5: `authorize()` HOLDS what it authorized** (`v.hold`, in-memory only — a restart kills the deliveries the holds stand for), `note()` converts it, `release()` gives it back, an unsettled one expires at `RESERVE_TTL_MS` and is COUNTED (`holdsOpen`/`holdsExpired`, the same kind of production census as `chargesUnhinted`); `authorize({hold:false})` is a PROBE, which is what auto-resume's pre-gate question must be. The boot load prunes with `A.LOAD_RETENTION`, never with `budgetLimits(serverSetting)` — at construction time that reader answers `undefined` for every key. **CHARGE WHAT YOU AUTHORIZED (r4): `authorize()` may resolve the slot, `note()` may not** — a charge that arrives with a session and no identity re-asks a question our own handlers are free to have moved (the ladder deferred its charge by up to 120 s and debited an account nobody asked), so it still charges (a dropped charge is the money-unsafe direction) but increments `chargesUnhinted`, journals once per 5 min and emits `spend-charge-unhinted`; `spendControlFor` is the ORCH half of the §1.4 row's third field. Gate: scripts/test-spend-paths.mjs (215) — a grep-derived census that PRINTS what it walked, PER SITE since r3 (a new producer beside a gated one in the same file used to inherit its verdict), with a synthetic producer, a mixed gated/ungated file and a JSDoc-only "gate" as its negative controls. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

**EVERY INBOX ITEM DIES WITH ITS WINDOW (2.369.152).** `fileInbox(text, detail, urgency, expiresAt)` stamps each item by what it is ABOUT (`noticeExpiry(about, now)` over `NOTICE_TTL_MS`): the hour-window 80 % warning (`r.warn.scope === 'hour'`) → now + 60 min; the day-window warnings (`'day'` per identity and `'instance'`) → now + 24 h; the refusal notice → now + 6 h (`REFUSE_INBOX_MS`, its own re-file cadence). `kind: 'notice'` stays; the store (user-todos.js `expireDue`) resolves them `expired`. ### login-state.js

login-state.js — THE credential-state reader (2026-09-07, SHARED, fs-only): `loginState(credsPath)` → live|expired|wiped|missing|unreadable + `since` = the instant the login stopped being able to produce a reading. `parseAuth`'s boolean collapses four states; two matter — WIPED is a file that stays with empty tokens (its mtime is the last-known-good MARKER the repair migration proves foreignness with), and a doubly-expired login still reports loggedIn:true, the satisfiable gap `poolMembers()` never closed. **2026-09-07 r2 adds the ACCOUNT-level twin `accountLoginState(credsPath, {oatMintedAt})`** — a wiped dir + a valid long-lived token (B-211a) is a supported, spawnable, reading-PRODUCING account, so the panels (/api/usage `logins`) and the repair migration ask THAT one, while the pool's slot validation deliberately keeps the FILE one (a token rides spawn ENV; re-pointing a symlink can never hand it to a running CLI). `OAT_TTL_MS` lives here and AccountManager reads it. INTEGRATION (2026-09-07, both branches landed): `login-expiry.js` (PURE) and this module are TWO QUESTIONS, not a twin — login-expiry reads the LOGIN SESSION's absolute deadline off a parsed credential object (ok/expiring/expired/logged-out/unknown), this one reads the FILE and answers whether it can produce a reading RIGHT NOW plus WHEN it stopped (live/expired/wiped/missing/unreadable + `since`). The pool gates on BOTH (a member is unusable if either says so); the panels/repair ask `accountLoginState`. Collapsing them into one exported `loginState` is an OPEN follow-up, not done here — the two suites pin different state vocabularies. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### reading-lag.js

reading-lag.js — PURE (imports nothing) WHOSE NUMBERS ARE THESE (inc-mts8a8mr-ulmm, 2026-09-08): ① `decideLagShadow` = a reading arriving after a re-point, carrying the PREVIOUS slot's window, is the previous slot's (the response to a request made 39s earlier with the old token — two false pool switches in 98s); the first reading matching the NEW slot ENDS the shadow and it stays ended; neither window decisive ⇒ the r3 statusline clause; BOUNDED 10min ② `decideReadingTarget` = the WINDOW IDENTITY GUARD (contradicts the target ⇒ re-file on the ONE matching account, else ARCHIVE with the reason; no evidence ⇒ write). `weeklyPhase`/`weeklyNear` compare by PHASE so a roll (exactly one week) is not a disagreement and the ±60s panel-vs-event wobble is not either. **r2: the WEEKLY half is the ONLY identity evidence** — the five-hour window names a TIME (measured: 7.2%/7.4% same-account drift from its own still-future stamped value, 47 reset values shared across identities because they snap to the clock, 50 real moments where the retired rung would have re-filed a legitimate reading onto a stranger), so it is recorded and never asked WHO; a reading with no weekly component answers 'unknown' and is written as asked. Identity needs no clock. **r2 also moved the established window OUT of the usage-cache snapshot into `windowSidecarName(key)`** — one ordinary statusline render used to delete it (that object is rebuilt whole by every reading producer). **r3: the clock bound moved BELOW the two window rungs** (it used to short-circuit first, which made the whole rule only as good as its caller's ESTIMATE of the age — see data/bin/vibespace-usage), and `repointAgeMs == null` is UNKNOWN and does not expire. `decideReadingTarget` moved INSIDE the sentinels: the statusline runs it too. The block between the `>>> reading-lag mirror` sentinels is mirrored VERBATIM into data/bin/vibespace-usage (a checkout-less host cannot require src/) — byte- and behaviour-pinned by test-readings-attribution §13. **B-855a c1: `apiWindowSidecarName(key)` = `.apiwin-<key>` (OUTSIDE the mirror block — the statusline stays byte-identical), the SECOND identity witness beside the established window: the panel is the very producer B-855a showed can answer for somebody else, so it cannot be its own proof; the weekly window the account's OWN slot-verified API events state is, and the engine writes it (`noteApiDerivedWindow`, only a `sevenDay`/`scoped` event, never a 5h one) while `refreshViaCliPanel` compares against it before it may write.** **c2: the `.window-` sidecar carries `source:'api'|'on-demand'` + `verifiedAt`/`verifiedBy` — a panel may stamp it only once verified, the API (the engine's K-RUN on an absent or contradicted one; the standing repair on a contradicting one) is the anchor of last resort, and `scopedRule:'same-phase-as-7d'` spells the measured rule every scoped bucket is judged by. FINAL VERIFIER (2026-09-17): `.apiwin-<key>` holds a RING of eligible candidates (`ring[]`, 8 kept) and its `sevenDay`/`scoped` witness is (re)written only when the newest `API_WITNESS_K` = 3 agree on one phase — ONE slot-verified reading is a candidate, never a witness (a response in flight across a re-point onto a FRESH member is slotOk by construction and carries the OLD member's window; the base stamped both sidecars with it and the new member's own readings were refused for good); the same run MOVES an established window (K consecutive readings the guard archived/refiled in one NEW phase re-anchor `.window-` + `.apiwin-`, the old sidecar archived as `window-sidecar/moved`, journal 'window moved', telemetry `usage-window-moved`); a candidate must pass `apiWitnessEligibility` (slot validated, not shadowed, no re-point of the conversation inside SHADOW_MS, the turn pin not older than the last re-point — `lastRepointRow(session, {minAt})` — OTel not disagreeing), and the guard's archive rows carry that `witness` verdict for the repair. ### reading-repair.js

reading-repair.js — the readings-by-slot DATA REPAIR (2026-09-07, run by migration `2026-09-reattribute-readings-by-slot`): re-attributes or archives-with-a-reason the provably-foreign entries in usage-cache / usage-anchors / attribution.ndjson, rebuilds each foreign cache from the newest anchor predating the wipe, voids the pairs it broke, drops rates.json so the estimator re-learns, and clears .attrib-rebake-v1 so the ledger re-bakes from the cleaned walk. **r2: a conversation whose LAST entry is archived is NAMED in .attrib-emptied.json (the re-bake deliberately skips a sid with no attribution entries and would otherwise keep the refuted account forever), and a member with a valid long-lived token is never marked dead just because its local credential dir is wiped (accountLoginState — such an account spawns and produces readings under its own key).** **r3: the two stores are keyed in DIFFERENT NAMESPACES (ledger = webui `sess-*`, attribution = claude conversation UUID) so the r2 lookup could never match a session row and every plan-C conversation silently got the POOL DEFAULT's answer written into the live store — `_sessionKeyMap(dataDir)` joins them through session-meta filenames, and only a session-scoped row may re-attribute; anything else is ARCHIVED with a reason naming the missing evidence.** Idempotent. Measured on a COPY of this instance: 3 caches / 248 anchors / 44 attribution entries. **ALSO the readings-by-WINDOW repair (`repairByWindow`, migration `2026-09-refile-readings-by-window`): each identity establishes its own weekly phases (7d AND every model-scoped bucket) from its OWN on-demand rows (≥5, ≥90 % after merging the ±60 s wobble), only the CURRENT roster may RECEIVE, and every anchor is judged PER BUCKET (r4) — the `{5h,7d}` primary half decides where the record goes, it carries only the buckets that agree with where it lands, every other bucket is archived with its own reason (the line keeps the original whole record), a record with no agreeing bucket is archived, a cache whose 7d agrees but whose scoped bucket does not is stripped in place, the rebuild picks only wholly-agreeing records and preserve-merges the previous scoped bucket rather than deleting the model cap the pool reads, and each roster account's window sidecar is SEEDED (scoped phases included) so the live guard is armed on the upgrade boot. Deciding on the 7d ALONE moved 443 of this instance's 476 re-files carrying a Fable bucket the destination contradicts — the 2.305.0 scoped-bucket class, created by the repair. Measured on a COPY: 476 re-filed (32 whole / 444 partial), 444 buckets archived, 0 records archived, 41 pairs voided, 7 sidecars seeded, 1 cache rebuilt, census 0 contradicting buckets anywhere, idempotent, 52 ms.** **r5: an identity can hold MORE THAN ONE cache file — the cache half is keyed on the FILES the product accepts (`usageIdentityGroups`' own predicate; `__models__`/`host-*`/a removed account's zombie/a pool all named and skipped) and each is resolved with the product's own `identityKeyFor` (so the migration now gets the roster RECORDS, not just ids), the `acct:` LAST RESORT being the only rung that may ask the streams (one match, else left alone and said; a pseudo key never — `__global__` and `__global_codex__` are both recorded with a null accountId). Keying on the stream's DOMINANT accountId left `usage-cache/__global__.json` — same org, same identity, 47 rows in that stream — unrepaired AND unseeded, so the live guard (keyed by CACHE FILE NAME) was inert on it and one `sweepUsageAnchors` (freshest cache of a group) re-poisoned the just-cleaned stream. Also `_primaryDrops`: a primary bucket the record STATES but the window cannot date is archived with its own line instead of vanishing, the move counts PARTIAL, and the refile reason is the verdict of the bucket that decided it, never the `'window'` placeholder. Measured on a COPY: 476 re-filed (32 whole / 444 partial), 444 buckets archived, 0 records archived, 42 pairs voided, **8 cache keys in an identity, 8 sidecars seeded, 0 without one, 0 contradicting buckets anywhere, 7106 rows in and out**, idempotent, 64 ms.** **④ THE IDENTITY ANCHOR IS DERIVED FROM THE API (B-855a c2, 2026-09-17, `repairSidecarsByApiPhase` — STANDING: every boot after the one-shots via the engine's `repairIdentityAnchors('boot')`, the human-triggered `POST /api/usage/repair-identity`, and once as migration `2026-09-repair-sidecars-by-api-phase`).** The panel is the producer B-855a showed can answer for another account, so it cannot be the identity anchor; the API phase of each roster claude subscription is derived from three witnesses — anchors whose 7d MOVED on a `rate-limit-event` (a 5h-only event re-anchors the file's carried-forward 7d: 6 of 12 on the polluted member, so a plain `source` filter is blind), the slot-verified readings the guard archived to readings-window-mismatch.ndjson (`entry.slot.slotOk`), and c1's `.apiwin-` — ≥3 rows, ≥60 % of the histogram (±120 s merged), else 'no-evidence' and the account is left alone. The API phase WINS: a contradicting `.window-` sidecar is archived (store `window-sidecar`, reason naming both phases) and re-stamped `{source:'api', verifiedAt, verifiedBy:'rate-limit-events', scopedRule:'same-phase-as-7d', n, of}` (an agreeing on-demand one is CONFIRMED to api; an api one is kept byte-identical), `.apiwin-` is written when absent; a cache whose 7d contradicts is archived (readings-foreign-usage-cache.ndjson, action replaced/emptied) and rebuilt via `_cacheFromAnchor` from the newest anchor that agrees WHOLLY (every scoped bucket judged on the 7d phase — the r4 measured same-phase rule; the r4 preserve source is only a dated, in-phase bucket, never an undated one riding a foreign record) or EMPTIED with `emptiedReason`; a cache whose only fault is a scoped bucket is stripped in place; then the last 24 h of archived own readings newer than the file are written back through `captureRateLimitEvent` in time order (idempotent by `fetchedAt`). MEASURED on a copy of this instance 2026-09-17: 10 identities with evidence (each ≥95 % on one phase), 3 sidecars re-stamped (each carried a fourth member's phase — four members shared ONE phase), 7 confirmed, 3 caches replaced, 128 readings re-admitted, second run all kept / 0 re-admitted, 90 ms; the member the owner felt rebuilt onto its OWN window (2026-09-24T09:00Z) with its own Fable 55 %, never the foreign 98 %. Gate: test-readings-attribution §20 (the fixture shaped like these stores + the untouched, confirmed, thin-evidence and emptied controls, idempotency) + test-migrations 42.** **FINAL VERIFIER (2026-09-17): `ORG_FIELDS` (`overage`, `spend`) are org-level billing facts, not readings — carried through `_cacheFromAnchor` and every emptied remnant (a rebuild that dropped them flipped the spend authorizer's only overage refusal from REFUSE to ALLOW and re-opened B-ad05 on the very boot that shipped it); `apiPhaseFor` no longer counts `.apiwin-` as evidence (it is the witness being judged — one poisoned live entry voted for itself) and skips an archived row the live path marked `witness.ok:false`; the repair also runs HOURLY (server.js, quiet unless it changed something). ### ledger-slot-backfill.js

ledger-slot-backfill.js — the one-shot RE-KEY of the permanent ledger rows the OTel-observed org attributed (B-f69c ②, 2.369.163, owner decision ut-1c6c15a2db ②; migration `2026-09-backfill-ledger-by-slot`). **What it repairs:** from 2.361.0 until the 2026-09-07 attribution law two OTel paths chose a row's ACCOUNT — `truthLookup(rid)` overrode the bake, and corrective attribution entries (`recordAttribution({sid, acct: observed, pool, ts: Math.max(rec.ts, lastTs + 1)})`) taught every later bake the spawn-time org; the readings-by-slot repair only reached entries a DEAD member could date, so the rows kept the account each hot-switched conversation STARTED on. **Candidates by evidence only:** a local claude row billed THROUGH A POOL (a session with no pool reads one credential dir for its whole life, so its observed org IS its slot by construction — the refuted mechanism needs a re-point to lie) whose rid the OTel stash (`usage-history/otel-truth.ndjson`) names with a KNOWN org whose account IS the row's account, or whose governing attribution entry is CORRECTIVE and names it; a corrective entry is recognised by its writer's own spelling (same sid + account as a stash observation, `ts` = the observation's ts or the previous entry + 1 ms — `recordUsageAttribution` stamps `Date.now()`). Codex, remote-host and every other disagreeing row is UNTOUCHED (not this migration's evidence). **Which slot:** ① the slot-transition ledger, session-scoped only, through reading-repair's session-meta join (a pool-default answer is not evidence about a conversation that may have had its own link); ② the conversation's own attribution walk with the corrective entries set aside (the rule every row baked since 2026-09-07 follows). **Refusals from the reading-window rules:** `decideLagShadow` — inside SHADOW_MS of a re-point the request may have carried the previous slot's token and a row states no window, so `no-evidence` ⇒ unprovable; `deathMarkers`/`isForeign` — a slot whose login was already dead cannot have answered. **The slot-ledger rung's previous slot is read by the row's `why`, never by `from`'s truthiness (quota r1, reproduced):** the ledger spells "no earlier slot" and "the machine login / a member whose record is gone" alike (`from: null` — `poolCurrentFor` answers null when the previous target's record vanished), and a spawn records `from` = the pool DEFAULT read before its link existed. `FIRST_LINK_WHYS` (`spawn`, `session-link`) ⇒ prevSlot undefined (a brand-new process has no in-flight request on any earlier token, so no shadow); every other why is a re-point ⇒ prevSlot = `from ?? null`, null = the machine login (`__global__` in the shadow rule) — exactly what the walk rung's predecessor entry says. Before, a row 3 s after a `from:null` per-session switch was re-keyed (the verifier measured 4.10 USD of rows under sub-b's re-learned rate vs 3.08 on the oracle ledger — that one row) and a row 3 s after a spawn off the default was archived as a lag shadow that cannot exist. **Outcomes:** confirmed (the slot record names the row's own account) ⇒ untouched, decided BEFORE any refusal — a row that already says its slot was not mis-attributed, and the shadow question belongs to every row of the ledger, not to this migration; proven ⇒ re-keyed in place (tokens kept, `atype`/`aname` from the roster, `slotRekeyedBy` + `slotRekeyedFrom`, the original archived VERBATIM with the rung that proved it); unprovable ⇒ ARCHIVED with a per-row reason class (`lag-shadow` / `no-slot-record` / `dead-slot` / `pool-target-unresolved`) and removed from the live ledger — never a guess; the corrective entries themselves are archived out of attribution.ndjson. All to `data/archive/ledger-by-slot-<date>.ndjson`, archive BEFORE each atomic rewrite (an archive failure throws ⇒ the run fails and retries). **The estimator:** every identity whose anchor stream names an account that lost or gained a row is re-learned through the estimator's own `ratesFor` over the repaired ledger (pair costs recompute from the live ledger, so no `costSince` is voided); the previous `rates.json` entries are archived first. **Report:** `{rows, candidates, rekeyed, archived, untouched, confirmed, byRung, archivedWhy, stash, corrective, shards, identities, relearned, ms}` — ONE `[migrate] ledger-by-slot:` line, the counts in the ledger's report row, one info notice when anything moved. Idempotent by itself (a second run finds nothing: re-keyed rows are skipped, archived ones and correctives are gone). **Scale:** the transition ledger is indexed once (`indexTransitions` / `ownLedgerRow` = `slotAt`'s session-scoped half by binary search) — measured on a synthetic 300 000-row ledger with 20 000 transitions and 20 000 attribution entries: 1.6 s, 1.1 GB peak RSS. **Honest limits:** a stash row trimmed by the 30-day/12 MB boot trim leaves its row unidentifiable (untouched); a corrective entry written for an observation with no timestamp (`ts` 0 ⇒ `Date.now()` at ingest) is not recognisable and stays in the walk. Gate: test-migrations (the synthetic ledger + transitions fixture: 3 re-keyed on both rungs, 3 archived with reasons, confirmed rows (one inside a re-point's shadow) and out-of-scope rows (codex, remote, no pool) untouched — the pooled scope and the confirm-first order each with a patched-copy control, the two corrective spellings, the relearn, the re-bake guard, a byte-identical second run; quota r1: a `from:null` per-session re-point 3 s before a row ⇒ archived `lag-shadow`, the same re-point 20 min before ⇒ re-keyed, a row 3 s after a SPAWN whose `from` names the pool default ⇒ re-keyed — both red on quota 3). **A PASS IS RESUMABLE (quota r2, the r2 verifier's crash probe — a real SIGKILL at three kill points on the production-shaped copy):** the runner retries a migration that never recorded itself, and the retry used to (A, killed after a shard's archive append, before its rename) archive every row of that shard AGAIN — 75,646 archive lines with 32,837 duplicates instead of 42,821 — and report/notify only the remainder (28,285 / 4,540 of 37,399 / 5,337, which is what `migrations.json` `reports` kept); (B, killed after every shard, before the attribution rename) re-archive the 84 corrective entries and report 0 / 0 with NO notice at all; and (B and C, killed inside the relearn) never re-learn the estimator — the retry found nothing left to touch, so the rates stayed learned from the OTel-attributed ledger (the verifier's third kill point looked clean on the ledger; its rates were not). Now `readPriorArchive(archiveDir, id)` reads every `ledger-by-slot-*.ndjson` line this migration id wrote: `_appendArchive` skips a line whose identity (`_archKey`: store + file + rid + mid + ts + sid for a row, sid + ts + acct for an attribution entry, the entry for the rates line) an EARLIER pass already wrote — never within the pass, because two identical rows the ledger genuinely holds (12 on the production copy) are two rows leaving it; archive lines carry `action: 'rekeyed' | 'archived'` (+ `slot`); a pass that finishes appends a `store: 'pass'` marker, and lines after the last marker are an OPEN (crashed) pass whose counts (per key max(earlier, this pass)) and touched accounts (its archived rows' accounts + the rows it already re-keyed, `slotRekeyedBy === id`) are this pass's too. `report.total` = the whole repair, `report.resumed`; the migration's notice and its ledger report row state `total` (+ `thisPass` when resumed). Measured on the production-shaped copy at all three kill points: live ledger byte-identical to the uninterrupted run, zero extra archive lines (only the marker), totals 37,399 / 5,337 / 84, relearned 5. **ONE KEY PER ANCHORS FILE (quota r2, low):** five anchor files hold two spellings of one identity (`org:<uuid>` and the file-name form `org_<uuid>`); both resolve to the same file, so the relearn minted five phantom `rates.json` entries under the `_` spelling and reported "relearned 10" for 5 identities. The relearn now groups the collected keys by `anchorSlug` and keeps the spelling the sanitiser CHANGES (the one readers look up), naming the others in `report.anchorKeySpellings` for a separate cleanup. Gates: test-migrations (+15: the three kill points in a child process retried through the runner, the uninterrupted reference, a no-memory patched copy as the negative control, a genuinely duplicated row, the two-spelling anchors file). **quota r3 (two lows, red first):** ① **a FINISHED pass the runner never recorded** (killed between the pass marker and the runner's migrations.json rename) used to retry into a pass that found every row already re-keyed and nothing open — 0 / 0, no notice, the 37,399-row repair recorded as nothing. `readPriorArchive` now also returns `lastComplete` (the newest marker; markers carry `relearned` since r3) and a pass with no work of its own and nothing open states that marker's totals (`resumed: true`, `recovered: true`) without writing a second marker. ② **a torn archive tail** (ENOSPC / a short write left a fragment with no newline) swallowed the first line of the retry's append — one archived original with no readable archive line. Every append (`_appendLines`, the marker too) now checks the file's last byte and closes a fragment with a newline first; `readPriorArchive` counts unparseable lines (`report.archiveUnparseable`, one warn line). Gates: test-migrations (D) the marker-before-ledger SIGKILL + a no-recovery copy, (E) the torn tail + an append-straight-after copy.

### weekly-lanes-unfold.js

weekly-lanes-unfold.js — the one-shot REPAIR of the plan weekly lane (inc-mubu23bd-5vxi, 2026-09-21, migration `2026-09-weekly-lanes-unfold` through src/migration-runner.js): since 2.361.2 the rate_limit_event parse wrote the overage-included weekly type — 2.1.274's own PER-MODEL bucket, about twice the plan week — into the plan 7d, so every capped account's plan week held the bucket's number until its next panel. **Candidates = claude caches whose PLAN limit's `source` is `rate-limit-event`** — the only producer that states ONE plan window; a panel, the statusline and get_usage state both windows and would already have corrected the week, so a plan week they wrote is NEVER touched (`kept`). **Evidence = the newest NON-rejected event carrying `unifiedWindows` in the live session buffers linked to that credential slot** (session-meta `accountId` → the per-session pool link `pool-links/<pool>/<sess>`, else the pool default link, else the subscription itself; a remote or codex session is never evidence; the last 512 KiB of each `.buf`), **judged by the account's own established window** (`.window-<key>` plan reset ±120 s, `weeklyNear`; no sidecar or a foreign reset ⇒ `left` with the reason). The rewrite archives the pre-repair object under `data/archive/weekly-lanes-unfold-<day>/` (+ `_migration.json` naming the keys) and writes the event's WEEKLY lanes through `captureRateLimitEvent` — the plan 7d, the model cap named by the sidecar's family, the fold rule — with the 5-hour lane deliberately left out (a tail line has no clock of its own and the 5h was never the bucket's victim). **THE CLOCK never regresses the file's `fetchedAt`** (max of the buffer's mtime, the replaced window's `measuredAt` + 1, the file's `fetchedAt` + 1): the anchors sweep dedups on `fetchedAt <= seen` and both newest-wins merges (`__global__` ↔ usage-cache.json, global ↔ named account) rank on it, so a regressed stamp would lose to the number it corrected. Content-idempotent (`already` when the plan week equals the event's window); the report carries a verb per key (rederived / already / left / kept) and the registry logs it and files ONE server notice only when something was rewritten. The poisoned anchors of the bad period are NOT rewritten here — a same-source pair with a ≥5-point jump and no corroborating cost is tainted by the estimator's own rule. Censuses: test-quota-model ⑩ names it (its cache writes go through the write path; its own `writeFileSync` is the archive copy) and ⑪ classifies it `migrated`; test-rate-limit-capture ⑩ requires it to describe the type without spelling it. Gates: test-migrations (the incident fixture verbatim on disk — pool default + per-session link, an older windowed event and a rejection in the same tail, a panel-sourced neighbour, an orphan candidate, a foreign-window candidate, a codex session that must not count; the archive, the notice, idempotency, the ledger belt, and the in-process `/api/usage` payload) + test-restore-smoke (the same fixture seeded into a worktree server's own data/, the FIRST `/api/usage` of that boot reads sevenDay 0.43 · fiveHour 0.09 · Fable 0.87 and the ledger records the run). **r2 (2026-09-21): a repair the module itself could not perform — the archive unwritable, the write path refusing — is a `refused` key (never `left`), a cache dir that exists but cannot be listed is `unreadable` (a MISSING dir is a fresh instance: nothing to repair, a success), and the migration THROWS on either so the runner logs it and retries next boot instead of recording a refusal as applied; the keys already re-derived are `already` on the retry (test-migrations r2).**

### usage-walker.js

usage-walker.js — THE ledger walk, ONE module (2.297.0 twin-killer): UsageHistory.scan() consumes it IN-PROCESS (cursors injected, onEvent enrichment orchestrator-side), the daemon runs it as the usage-scan op child, and data/bin/vibespace-usage-scan mirrors it for checkout-less ssh hosts (parity-pinned). **ORIGIN (2026-09-10): every event says WHICH KIND of transcript produced it — `origin` 'main'|'subagent'|'workflow' stamped on ALL of them (never "missing means main": the backfill must be able to answer 'unknown'), plus `wf`/`agent`; an agent event's `cwd` is the PARENT PROJECT's and its own directory rides along as `wcwd` ONLY when it differs, so a worktree agent stops being its own row in "By project" (272 of this instance's 3,155 agent transcripts). A codex rollout is 'main' by RULE (the store merges a sub-agent's rollout into the parent thread). `makeProjectCwdReader` is the EXPORTED ladder — a conversation's cwd is not constant (3 of 782 top-level transcripts state more than one, and one of them is this instance's biggest spender: a rename left its FIRST record on `…/claude-code-webui` while its latest records and its project dir say `…/vibespace`, so "the first cwd" filed $7,828 of one conversation's agent spend in a SECOND project row), so a candidate is VERIFIED by encoding it forward to the project directory name (§5's deterministic direction) → the tail window → the conversation's MOST RECENT cwd → a sibling transcript; bounded 128 KiB windows, memoized. The backfill migration REQUIRES that export rather than keeping a third copy.** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### login-expiry.js

login-expiry.js — PURE (零依赖) 登录会话寿命判定 (2026-09-07): `claudeAiOauth.refreshTokenExpiresAt` 是登录会话的**绝对**截止时间, 刷新 access token 不会推迟它(实测: 30 分钟前刷新过的成员仍然只剩 17 小时); 过期后 CLI 刷新拿到 invalid_grant 并把 accessToken/refreshToken/expiresAt **清空**却保留截止时间与 scopes = 磁盘上"已登出"的形状. loginState(creds, now) → ok/expiring(<24h)/expired/logged-out/**unknown**(缺字段一律 unknown, 永不 'ok' — 读不出来是无知不是健康, 每个消费者都必须把 unknown 当作"不要拦"); NEAR_MS=30min 是"切换目标必须活过这次切换"的线(**r2: 那是关于自愿移动的规则 — 当前成员已经死透时, 20 分钟的登录仍然胜过零, 逃生要能落到它上面**); loginBlockedPhrase/loginBlockedText = 每个被拦成员**各说各的事实**(已过期/已登出/还剩 <t>), 绝不用一句话覆盖一张混着三种事实的名单; **r3 增 loginWallPhrase = 当前成员自己那条死登录的从句形式 — 它是 `fromLogin` 这个具名输出, 绝不能塞进 `deadBuckets` 假装成一个花光了的配额桶(桶会随窗口自愈, 登录不会; 那条每小时重复一次的通知因此开出了配额药方"等窗口重置", 而唯一要用户动手的那个账号是它唯一说不出名字的)**; reviewWarnings = 每成员每档只说一次的纯状态转移(换了截止时间=重新登录⇒旧账本作废; 跳过的档只发最紧急那条, 绝不补发已成历史的提醒; **r2 增可选 watchingSince: 在本账本诞生之前就死掉、且已不新鲜(>STALE_GRACE_MS=24h)的登录是既有状况, 记为已发但不发声 — 它的面是 Manage Agents 里那枚常驻红芯片, 不是事件收件箱**); **2026-09-07 增 `reloggedIn(info, prevExp)` = 真的开了新会话吗(三条各自承重: 必须重新**活着**('ok'/'expiring') — 被清空的文件保留截止时间且那个时间可以在未来, 只看"数字变大"会把已登出读成已恢复; 必须**现在有**可读截止时间('unknown'=无主张, 无主张永不推翻按事实发出的警告); 截止时间必须**变了** — 一个会话的截止时间终生固定, 变了只能来自新会话, 而保持不变的凭据重写(token 刷新/跨机拷贝/导入)是同一个会话, 什么都没修好也就什么都不能撤回; 刻意**不是**"变大": 短 SSO 策略给回来的截止时间可以比我们警告的那个**更早**(还剩 20h 时警告, 新会话只有 12h), 用 `>` 判会把那条已经不成立的条目永远留着; 而撤回也不会丢掉仍然成立的警告——同一轮里阶梯就按新截止时间重新武装) 与 `SHORT_SESSION_MS`(36h)+`shortSession(spanMs)` = 会话时长短到值得提一句 org SSO 策略(本机实测的截止时间是 5/9/12/16 **天**), 没测到就永远为假. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### server/login-expiry-watch.js

server/login-expiry-watch.js — 被动巡检(boot+5min, 只读文件, §ban-safety 零 vendor 调用): 每个登录最多三条"For you"收件箱条目(24h/1h/已过期), 点名账号与到期时刻, 账本 data/login-expiry.json 原子落盘(含 `since`=本账本开始盯梢的时刻) ⇒ 重启不重发、重新登录即静默、升级当天不会为几周前就死掉的账号刷一屏 urgent(r2: 实测该实例首次巡检发了 3 条, 全是非路由成员); 收件箱拒收就回滚该档下次重试(标成已发=静默失败); **r3: 条目文案按 `state` 分支而不是按档 — warnStageFor 把 'expired' 与 'logged-out' 收进同一个终端档, 档回答"多紧急", 状态回答"发生了什么"; CLI 清空 token 时**保留**截止时间, 所以被清空的记录可以带一个**未来**的截止时间(任何不可恢复的刷新都会产生这个形状: 会话被吊销/轮换, 或在隔离目录里显式登出), 于是条目对着 20 天后的时间戳说"已过期", 而同一行上的芯片(它是按 state 分支的)说"已登出" — 一条记录两个面互相矛盾.** **2026-09-07 恢复: 已经发出去的条目是一个断言, 发它的人必须撤回它** — 掉账本只让**将来**不再发, 而 owner 重新登录了两个成员(新 token, 截止时间 29 天后)之后, 收件箱里那条 `Claude login for "Member F" is signed out…` 仍然 open, 旁边同一行的芯片却早就变绿了; 现在成员行带 `items:[{id,text}]`(本 watch 为**这个**截止时间发过的条目 id, **落盘** — 警告与重新登录之间重启一次也必须还能撤回, 否则只是把同一个 bug 推后一步), `reloggedIn` 成立即逐条走 store 自己的 `setStatus(id,'done','system')`(落盘+广播 ⇒ 所有客户端实时更新)并只记一行 `X: re-logged in — N warning(s) cleared`; 三条禁令各配负控: **用户已处理的绝不重开也不重标**(非 open 一律原样丢出列表)、**别人发的绝不碰**(只认自己账本里的 id, 写之前还要复核 sessionKey 与文案 — agent 在别的会话发的 vibespace-ask 对它不可见)、**保持同一截止时间的凭据重写不算重新登录**; `resolvedBy:'system'` 既不是 user 也不是 agent, 面板已解决区标 `automatically`(自己消失的条目必须自己说明是自己消失的). **登录成功即立刻巡检**: 5 分钟的轮询意味着盯着自己刚修好的那条看很久, 所以每条 finalize 路由(relogin-finalize / subscription finalize——放在自动合并那条**提前 return** 之上, 两个出口都巡检 / codex device-auth)在登录确实成功时巡检; server.js 留住句柄并以 `getLoginExpiryWatch` 惰性 getter 下发; **r2 三条**: ①门要读那个方法**真给的答案** — r1 门在 `r.loggedIn` 上, 而 `accounts.reloginResolve` 的四种回答里**没有一种**带顶层 `loggedIn`(`{outcome:'pending'}` / `{outcome:'same'|'split', account}` / `{outcome:'moved', movedTo}`, 抓到的登录在**嵌套**的 account 里, 'moved' 干脆没有 account), 于是这个功能恰恰死在收件箱条目与登录芯片把用户送去的那条路上, 而套件绿只因它的 fixture **编了**那个形状(现在 §5b 的 fixture 由真 `reloginResolve` 对着临时 store 的一次真调用**捕获**而来); 门=`!!r.account?.loggedIn || r.outcome === 'moved'`('moved' 把活登录搬进了**另一条**记录, 要撤回的是那条的账本行; 'pending' 保持沉默) ②**被轮询的路由不许带无界副作用**: manage-agents 每 3s 打一次 relogin-finalize 打满 5 分钟且 'same' 会重复(实测 100 次轮询=100 次巡检) ⇒ 只在**变化**时巡检(`sweepOnLoginTransition` 比对答案自己的**凭据指纹**: outcome+记录+身份+access token 到期, 全部取自路由已经拿在手里的那个答案, **不是**第二个凭据读者); 刻意**不是**"这个账号已经扫过了"的布尔闩——重新登录一个**仍然登录着**的账号从第 1 次轮询起就答 'same'(离用户真正完成浏览器流程还有几分钟), 布尔闩会恰好跳过唯一重要的那次 ③自动合并那条要在 `mergeSubscription` **之后**再巡检一次: `fin` 之上那次跑的时候新凭据还在**丢弃记录**的目录里, 而带着 open 警告的是幸存记录, 它读到的是陈旧截止时间, 什么都撤不回; 合并前那次保留(它是所有非合并出口上唯一的一次), 因为巡检是幂等的(已钉); **只有一个读者**: 巡检问 `accounts.loginStateOf`, 正是芯片(roster 行的 `loginState`)的来源 ⇒ 两个面不可能对同一个文件各说各话, 失败只记日志绝不抛回登录路由. **24h/1h 条目的组织策略提示**: 实测该成员上一次登录会话不足 36h 才加 `(its last login session lasted only ~24 h — this org's session policy may be short)`; 承重的是"实测"——朴素判据(截止时间减凭据文件 mtime)会把健康的 30 天登录报成 20 小时(每次 access token 刷新都重写该文件而截止时间不动), 所以 `measureLoginSpan` 只在**目击**到登录时才信 mtime(**观察日志** `seen`——每个订阅每轮都写, 与稀疏的警告账本刻意分开: 健康成员没有警告行, 而它恰恰就是下次登录需要被目击的那个——≤3 轮前确认过、截止时间此后变了、文件写在那次确认之后), 把登录那次写入钉在一轮宽的窗口里; 没目击就什么都不说, 记下的 span 比当前剩余时间还短就是陈旧值同样不说; 用词是 "may be"(一个成员的一次会话是关于策略的证据, 不是对策略的读数); 摸文件的只有 `src/harnesses/claude.js`, 它在纯判定旁附上 `writtenAt`. 此前 VibeSpace 只在**一轮已经死掉之后**才反应(池的 auth-failure 驱逐), 用户看见一次失败、然后它"又好了", 从没有人被告知要重新登录. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### auto-resume-signal.js

auto-resume-signal.js — PURE (imports nothing, 2026-09-08): does a NORMALIZED quota reading say the wall a conversation is WAITING on is gone? `windowOpened` needs THREE facts and each was a real way to spend a billed turn into a wall — the limit **LANE** matches (`snapshot.limitId`; a codex login reports `codex` and `codex_bengalfox` minute by minute and the spark lane read 0% through the whole 32h stall), the reading **STATES THE BUCKET** the wait is about and reports it not spent (a `rate_limit_event` names exactly ONE bucket, so a healthy 7d reading says nothing about a 5h wall), and no SIBLING bucket of that lane is spent (the c1206711 rule); an arm that does not know its own wall (the pool's +45s near-arm) is never opened this way. `why` is contract, not prose — 'we cannot tell' (other-lane/other-bucket/unknown-bucket/no-reading) may never be spelled like 'yes'. `bucketSpent` is deliberately NOT the pool's 3-5% candidate gate: that one picks between accounts, this one authorises an unattended turn. PURE because both producers ask it (claude rate_limit_event, codex rate_limits_updated) — and NOT the weekly-phase fingerprint (reading-lag.js), which is an ACCOUNT identity rule and would answer 'differ' about the very reading that proves recovery (codex's weekly window is not phase-stable: the incident's two windows are 152320s apart).

### resume-continuity.js

resume-continuity.js — PURE **resume ladder** (B-6b6d, owner ruling 2026-09-07): `resumeSpawnPick({explicit, conversation, instanceDefault, resume, hasSource})` → `{value, origin: chosen|conversation|instance|harness}` — 一个对话在 resume/fork/restart 时保留**它自己的** model/effort, 实例默认值只对**新建**会话生效, 显式 per-session 选择仍然压过两者. 两个调用者一条法则: 客户端 session-lifecycle(`hasSource:false` — 只有服务端读得到对话自己的记录 ⇒ 续跑时什么都不发)与服务端 ws-create(在 buildSessionArgs **之前**, 经 harness descriptor 的 `store.lastTurn<Knob>` 读回). `hasSource` 由那个 hook 的**存在**推导, 绝不另立 caps 布尔; 没有来源的旋钮在 resume 时发**空**而不是默认值(无条件兜底本身就是这个缺陷); 有来源但为空(还没跑过 turn)才回落实例默认并**记日志**. **r2(2026-09-07)**: ①**claude 两个旋钮都没有来源** — 全量语料 2650 份转录里 `message.model` 从不带 `[1m]` 变体(而 CLI 自己的 `model_refusal_fallback` 证明会话就跑在 `claude-fable-5[1m]` 上), 且分类器改道记录写在**它描述的那条 assistant 之后** 2-10 行(r1 的 20 行向后窗口 139 次只命中 1 次, 16.8% 的主线程 assistant 记录落在改道区间内) ⇒ 读回来的 id 结构上不可命令, **删掉来源**而不是再加一层守卫, claude resume 两个旋钮都不发, 由 CLI 自己的会话记录(变体精确)决定 ②**opencode 有来源就给它**(`serve.facts().sessionModel`, 与 discover 共用同一份 v1 列表缓存, 服务关着就是 `''`⇒实例默认并记日志) ③`''` 是**明确选择**(新建会话对话框第一项 "Auto (model default)")只有 `undefined` 才是沉默 — 只在**新建**这一侧成立(续跑的线路是 `model || undefined`, 两者同字节), 客户端在新建时原样发送让空串活过线路. **r3 增 `applyOriginHint(origin, hint)`**: 新建会话由**客户端**解析实例默认值(它要给自己的芯片用, 且它独占 legacy `session.defaultEffort` 与 `settings.isModified` 这两个服务端看不到的事实)并原样上线 ⇒ 服务端看到的只是一个裸字串, 只能读成显式选择, 于是新建会话的 origin **永远**是 `'chosen'`, `'instance'`/`'harness'` 结构上不可达, 而那些**根本不显示选择器**的创建路径(openShellTerminal/工具栏/setup-flows/manage-agents)在会话属性里被写成"你为本会话的选择"; 客户端现在把它算出来又丢掉的那个 origin 一并发出(`spawnOriginHint`), 本函数只允许把服务端自己的 `'chosen'` **降级**成 `'instance'`/`'harness'`, 绝不上调、绝不改动**值**、绝不重指服务端独有的事实(`'conversation'`/`'chosen'`/垃圾一律忽略, 旧客户端不发就保持 master 的答案). ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### permission-rules.js

permission-rules.js — PURE model + DOM-free tree renderer for the READ-ONLY "where does this rule come from" view (2026-09-07, owner ruling 10 / §2.14): the ONE typed record every harness produces (layers → rules, `kind` allow|deny|ask|value), claude's settings hierarchy in the CLI's OWN vocabulary (2.1.257 binary), codex `config/read` layers+origins (incl. the file-less `sessionFlags` layer), opencode's origin-less resolved config, the closed `UNAVAILABLE_REASONS` code set (an unavailable record NEVER carries layers), and `renderRuleTree` with esc/t/icons INJECTED so the XSS rule is unit-provable. allow/deny/ask are the harness's own words and are never translated. **2026-09-07 r4: codex keys `origins` by LEAF PATH for a TABLE-valued key (measured on 0.153.4 — `sandbox_workspace_write` itself is NEVER in `origins`, and a `-c …network_access=true` session flag lands on the LEAF as `sessionFlags`), so a key with no top-level origin is resolved from its leaves (all-agree ⇒ the key; split ⇒ ONE RULE PER LEAF under the layer that won it) — asking only the top level filed the user's own config under a forged "packaged defaults" layer noted "not set in any layer" and left the sessionFlags layer empty; the "nobody set it" bucket never forges codex's `packagedDefaults` variant (its schema REQUIRES a `file`), a layer may carry `fileNote` so "no file" ≠ "no path to show", and `originsDropped` (the producer's byte cap ate the map) files rules under an explicit unknown-source layer with `CODEX_CAPPED_NOTE`, never `CODEX_DEFAULT_NOTE`.** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### channel-store.js

channel-store.js — SHARED (fs+path only) persistence primitives for data/channels/ (design §5): adapters.json · index.json · msgs/<adapterId>/<convId>.ndjson (APPEND-ONLY) · audit.ndjson rolled by DATE into archive/ (the day comes from the file's OWN last record, never mtime; the shard is APPENDED to, never overwritten). **§5.1: `index.update(fn)` is the ONE mutation door** — a promise chain, so overlapping adapter passes QUEUE rather than race, and there is deliberately NO "write the whole index back" export: `writeJsonAtomic` is atomic at the fs layer only and the read-modify-write AROUND it is the round-4 codex-zst lost update, worse here because a clobbered ANCHOR makes the next pass SKIP. Cursor advances only after a COMPLETE pass; retention = 90d or 5,000 records whichever is SMALLER with a 7-DAY FLOOR; a derived value is cached for render speed and always re-derivable. **r2 three rules: the DEDUP SET remembers a vendorId only after its bytes are durable** (it was written inside the selection loop, so one failed append turned the batch into permanent "duplicates" and the anchor advanced past messages nobody wrote), **`readTail` pages on the TOTAL ORDER `(at, vendorId)`** and sorts by the order it pages by (a timestamp is not unique and a strict `<` stranded one record per group for ever), **and `adapters.json` gets the same single owner as the index** — `adapters.live()` + `adapters.update(fn)`, no `writeAdapters(obj)` for anyone to hand a private copy to, because the read-modify-write around it wiped a failing adapter's health whenever a healthy one passed second. `index.entry(a,c,{create:false})` is the LOOKUP form. **r3 two more: the log SEALS a partial last line before it grows** (an append is not atomic — a fragment plus the re-offered batch glued onto it swallowed exactly one record for ever, because the readers skip the unparseable line and the durable set then remembered its id; `appendRecords` preads the last byte, writes `\n` if it is not one, and the writer LOOPS) **and `readTail` SEEKS backward one 2 MiB window at a time** (reading the last window once left everything older unreachable while retention kept it — 3,000 lines, 2.28 MiB, 375 stranded — and made the dedup set forget them too; straddling bytes are carried as bytes, never decoded alone). **r4: a FAILED append DROPS the cached dedup set** — r2's "leaves no trace at all" was backwards: the write that threw may have landed a PREFIX, and a prefix that stopped on a record BOUNDARY (after `}` or after `\n`, the two cuts the seal cannot see) is a complete record the log holds while the LIVE set still calls it absent, so the same process re-offered the batch and served that record twice for ever (measured: `v1,v2,v3,v4,v4,v5`, `countSince` 6 for five records; a restart was already right, which pins it to the live set); now the retry re-derives the set from the log, byte-identical to the restart, while a throw BEFORE the write (`mkdirSync`) lands nothing and the set stays — r2 is what the set may CLAIM, r4 what it must FORGET, each with its own control. **r5: the dedup REBUILD refuses a log it cannot read** — `readTail` answered EMFILE/EIO/EACCES with an EMPTY read and the rebuild CACHED that empty set, so the post-restart first pass of every tracked conversation could write a replayed boundary page twice for ever (measured: `v1..v5,v5,v6`, `countSince` 7 for six records); `readTail(…, {strict:true})` at the ONE reader whose answer writes bytes — ENOENT is "no log yet", anything else throws out of `appendRecords` (pass fails, anchor stays, nothing cached), every other reader stays lenient because a derived number self-heals and `countSince` is asked inside `index.update()` after the anchor moved. **2.369.159: `groups.json` (agent groups, design §22.5) is the third single-owner file — `groups.update(fn)` / `live()` / `snapshot()`, no whole-file write for anyone else; a group's log is an ordinary `msgs/groups/<id>.ndjson`.** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **g3: `appendRecords` answers `lastText` (the newest appended record's text) for the index's last-line cache; the groups file carries `ownerRead` beside `groups`, same door.** **r2: an unreadable/unparseable store file (index / adapters / outbox / groups / wake-pace) is SET ASIDE as `<name>.corrupt-<ts>` (never unlinked, one named log line, `store.quarantined`) and only then started empty — a rename failure BLOCKS that family's writes; `pace` = the groups' persisted wake-pace ledger.** **r3: a BLOCKED index rejects `update()` too; every blocked door rejects `{code:'store-blocked', status:503}`; every refused flush is logged; a blocked wake-pace.json is never overwritten.**

### channel-groups.js

channel-groups.js — PURE (imports only channel-record) THE AGENT-GROUP MODEL (design §22, owner D1/D2, 2.369.159): the record + `validateGroup`/`newGroupId`/`pairKey` (symmetric), membership as PURE transitions `{group, event}` | `{code}` from the closed `ERROR_CODES` (g2 added the engine's `ambiguous` and the routes' `job-token` — every code the CLI's REMEDY table words) (duplicate invite = a no-op with a word; a pair takes no third member and is archived when a side leaves; kick = creator/owner; own notify only, the owner sets anyone's), `mentionsIn`, `wakeVerdict` (= the D2 table: next-turn|mention|always|mute × @ × invite × --quiet), `reportFor` (post-join, context first, newest kept under 2 KiB, the `read --before` pointer). r1: `reportFor`'s budget is the WHOLE text (three forms, else `fits:false` — never `null`, never over); `mentionsIn` ends a name at a script boundary (`@测试请看`). **r2: a line cut short is POINTED to (`read <gid> --before <cut+1> --limit <n>`); the PURE pace (`paceVerdict`/`paceGrant`/`paceRefund`/`prunePace`: 30 s per pair + 8 per sender per minute) and consent (`consentVerdict`: `confirm-wakes` over 5 without `--yes`, `wake-count-mismatch` for the owner's echo; `wakesPlanned`).** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **r3: `PACE_SKEW_MS` 5 s — a stamp further ahead is dropped by `prunePace`, ignored by `paceVerdict`, counted by `paceFuture`; `paceRefund(…, {keepSender})`.**

### server/groups-engine.js

server/groups-engine.js — ORCH the agent-groups engine (2.369.159): reach = msg-acl over the live roster (messageable, from the inviter, uniform refusal, atomic), every mutation inside channel-store's `groups.update` door with its log record (log first), `channel-groups-updated` on every change; a WAKE = the member's report down THE ladder under `peer-message` (its ONE ladder site), a refusal journaled + never stashed; `reportsForTurn`/`commitReports` for prompt-context; `sendToAgent` = the pair group (g2: `create:false` = post only into an EXISTING pair — `findPair` — else `job-token`). g2: `resolveMember`/`resolveGroup` refuse a shared name `ambiguous` WITH `candidates` (`{name, conversationId}` among sessions the actor may MESSAGE / `{name, groupId}` among its own groups — no oracle), never a guess. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **g3: the OWNER's read mark (`ownerRead`, moved only by `markRead` = the window opened/touched or the owner's own verb; `list()` adds the derived `unread`; a no-op mark broadcasts nothing) + `liveRoster()` for the New group / Invite dialogs.** **r1: `mayWake` asked of EVERY wake (the route's per-(sender, resolved member) 30 s floor; floored = `refused:'rate-floor'`); `resolveTarget` (a name that is a group AND a session ⇒ `ambiguous`); `memberRef` (kick/notify by a shared name ⇒ `ambiguous`); `reportsForTurn` ≤ budget WHOLE (≤ 3 waiting named, a report taken back until it fits).** **r2: `pacerFor(sender)` = THE pace (persisted in `store.pace`, a grant reserves, a wake that did not go out refunds), `consent` asked inside the door before any write, the unread count memoised against `(since, lastAt)` and moved by `appendIn` (no log re-read per broadcast), a turn with no room still NAMES its waiting groups.** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **r3: a `wake-count-mismatch` refusal carries `group: view(g)`; `noteRoster()` (from broadcastActiveSessions) re-announces the groups whose member names/liveness moved; the pacer drops future stamps (one log line) and refunds only the PAIR of a refused wake (`keepSender`).**

### channels/index.js + channels/fake.js

channels/index.js + channels/fake.js — ORCH: the adapter REGISTRY and its CONTRACT (design §4) — a declared capability must be implemented, an UNDECLARED one THROWS, every failure is a typed {code, retryable} from a closed set, `history()` returns nothing unasked-for and ADVANCES NOTHING, `convCaps` is never WIDER than `caps`, and on `sendAs: []` `send()` does not FAIL — it does not exist. Plus the FAKE adapter that talks to nothing and really runs all three receive modes (`fake-poll` sendable · `fake-push` a live lane AND read-only · `fake-scan` both sources, `'ui'` minting a DECLARED synthetic key so a re-scan is a no-op by construction), registered always and instantiated only under `VIBESPACE_CHANNELS_FAKE=1`. **r3: a scan adapter's `history()` takes the RESOLVED source as `opts.source` and the registry REFUSES a scan page that carries none** — the fake kept a `source()` closure falling back to `caps.scanSources[process.platform]`, a SECOND resolver two lines under a comment saying there was none, which is how the engine ingested through a lane `scanState` had just called unavailable; the contract suite censuses that no adapter module reads `scanSources[` or `process.platform` outside `scanHost`. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### server/channels-engine.js + server/channels-wiring.js + routes/channels.js

**2.369.165 (integrations chunk 2): the account's own client (`custom`), the transient consent, re-authorize = rebind, duplicate over `DUPLICATE_FIELDS`, remove refused by reference, disconnect keeps every record, the legacy own → custom copy — full text under the (ORCH) heading above.**

**a3 r4 (2026-09-21):** every "For you" item this engine files (the per-conversation pointer, an agent's access request, an unknown outcome, the failure headline) carries `i18n` = the same sentences as STRUCTURE (`i18nKey(…)` keys + params, `source: Channels`) beside its English `text`/`detail` — the client says the words, the English stays the dedupe key and the CLI's contract; `adapterView` passes an adapter's own `auth.whyCode/whyParams` through `authState` so a fake (self-resolving) adapter's needs-credentials line is worded by code too.

server/channels-engine.js + server/channels-wiring.js + routes/channels.js — ORCH: the per-adapter ingest loop with its single flight, the pass that appends to the durable log BEFORE it advances an anchor, ONE broadcast per pass carrying the recomputed digest, and the store's serialized index owner (the engine is its only writer). The lane is ASKED (`laneState`/`scanState`), never read off `caps`. Routes take `host` everywhere and refuse another machine BY NAME (v1 = this machine). Filter/assign/wake/outbox are LATER PHASES and are absent rather than stubbed. **r2: a route may not MINT an index row** (`known()` resolves both halves before anything is mutated; `POST /track` and `/read` 404 on an id nobody discovered — the track route's own 404 was unreachable dead code), **`markRead` broadcasts only when something CHANGED and its default instant is the NEWEST RECORD's** (an unchanged value is not a dirty signal, and `now()` left a future-dated vendor record unread for ever, which is what an open window re-POSTed on ~490 times a second), **and the digest carries NO composed sentence** (broadcast to every client, language per device). **r3: THE INGEST IS GATED ON THE RESOLVER** — `pass()` produces `scan.hostFacts` UNCONDITIONALLY before every scan pass (trigger ③; the field had no producer at all, so `scanState` could only answer `host-facts-stale` while records were ingested anyway), `ingest()` refuses a scan lane with no source and hands the resolved one to `history()`, and `laneOrScan` follows `laneState`'s `via` rather than reading `caps.receive`; **`markRead`'s stamp is the newest record's for PAST-stamped records too** (r2's `Math.max(now(), …)` was `now()` for every real adapter, silently marking a backdated arrival read and making the no-op rule inert); **`setTracked` broadcasts on both branches** (a pass over budget returned before `notify`, so a persisted flag reached no client); and the digest hands the claim `enabled` so an untracked or disabled row is published `off`. **P1a (2026-09-16): the REAL adapters register the same way as the fakes and nothing downstream learns their names — `REAL_ADAPTERS` is the ONE list the engine reads for `connectable`/`integration`/`OPTIONS`/`label`; each row's Test runner is registered on the integrations store BY THE ENGINE (the consumer owns it); the adapter's OWN token lives on the record as `auth.tokenEnc` through secret-box on `data/.channels-key` (a second store from the integrations layer's — a user's consent, not an admin's credential) and `adapterView` never carries it; connect/re-authorize/paste-back/cancel/disconnect/enable/options are engine verbs behind the new routes, `connect` refusing with a typed `409 needs-credentials` when the row resolves to none (the wizard opens THAT card first, §10.1); a never-authenticated record passes NOTHING and is `not-connected`, while a DEAD token fails the pass with the vendor's typed refusal and SPEAKS; discovery PAGES the adapter's cursor (`DISCOVERY_PAGES`); a failing adapter files ONE "For you" item after `FAILURES_BEFORE_LOUD` passes naming the adapter, the code, the vendor's words and the remedy, and the SAME producer retracts it on the first passing pass or on disconnect (fence 8, only its own still-open item); `setOptions` refuses an undeclared key or a value outside `choices` by name and REBUILDS the live adapter when the option is one it read at construction (`rebuild:true`).** **P1b: the push lanes — `syncPushLanes` arms/stops off the resolver's answer (every tick + every mutation that changes it), `onPushEvent` IS fence 11 (durable log → return = the ack → coalesced index + ONE broadcast per batch; event ids remembered for the vendor's replays; content only while `carryContent` AND tracked, else a cursor KICK coalesced per `KICK_MIN_INTERVAL_MS`), the measurement is sampled ONLY in content mode (timer pass = a miss, kick pass = push's own; a first walk and pre-`contentSince` records never judged; kick mode adds nothing), `checkDemotion` says why with the numbers and keeps the connection up, `setPush` is the ONE way back (re-declare ⇒ zero + one fresh arm), `pushView` publishes the public half (`null` = no lane).** **P2 (design §7, fences 2 + 12): THE FUNNEL — every lane hands `onFresh` exactly the records that became durable (`appendRecords` returns them), after which nothing knows the lane: the same matcher, the same pacing cap, the same ladder. The ONE lane-dependent step is the coalescing window, opened only while `laneState().carryContent` (a poll/scan pass is already a batch), `channels.pushCoalesceSeconds` default 60; hits that must wait (a digest window, the window, a group with no live member, the pacing cap) are PENDING on the index — persisted, bounded, delivered as one after a restart — and a later direct wake carries them along (a hold is a delay, never a drop). `wake()` goes through the delivery ladder with `spendReason:'channel-message'` and adds NOTHING beside it (the authorizer inside charges the slot it authorized); a refusal is stashed through the ladder's own stash. Assignment IMPLIES REACH as one `origin:'assignment'` grant and unassign removes only that row. Verbs: `setAssignment` / `setFilter` / `estimateFilter` (server-side over the stored log), the digest carries `assignment` (authority CLAMPED with the reason), `filter`, `stats` (hits7d / msgs7d / wakes / lastWake / pending / lastRefusal), `authorityCaps`, `wakeLatency` (the honest per-lane claim: push = window + ack budget, poll = the hot cadence the tick itself uses, scan = the source's latency, reconcile = 15 min).** **P4:** `sendNow` stamps attemptAt + the WIRE text BEFORE the request, persists a two-phase handle the moment it exists, reads `detail.lost` as `unknown`; `reconcile()` (a PERSON, never a timer) is the only way out of unknown; `sweepSending()` at boot ⇒ unknown by actor `boot`; the sender honesty line OFF by default (`channels.senderHonestyLine`, per-adapter `setSenderHonesty`); `identityObserved` on the row. **THE ACCOUNT MODEL (2026-09-22):** N records per kind (`<kind>:<8 hex>` after the first), `credentialKey` stamped at connect from the wizard's choice (validated against `offeredCredentials`, `400 unknown-credential` by name), handed to the adapter AND read live off the record, `connect(kind,{credentialKey,newAccount})` / `reauthorize(id)` by id / a further account's `disconnect` removes only its own record + index rows / `stampCredentialKeys()` for the migration; the view carries `credentialKey`, `credentialLabel`, `credential` (for that key), `credentials`, `auth.credentialKey`. **2.369.159 agent groups: the wiring builds `groups-engine` over `channels.store` + THE ladder + `groupSetting` and returns it as `groups`; the routes add the owner side under a DISTINCT prefix `/api/channel-groups` (list / messages / create / post / invite / kick / rename / archive / notify — `post` is the owner's own words, direct).** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **g3: the OWNER'S OWN MESSAGE — `propose(user, …, {direct:true})` = `POST /api/channels/:a/:c/send`: no policy, no guard, as the user only (a bot-only conversation refuses with the send-as-user reason; an agent's `direct` is ignored), still the full outbox record/audit/unknown; the digest carries `lastText`; routes add `/api/channel-groups/roster` and the owner's `/api/channel-groups/:id/read`.**

**r2 of agent groups (2.369.159):** the engine files ONE high-urgency "For you" item per `store.quarantined` entry at boot (a store file set aside as `<name>.corrupt-<ts>`, words as i18n structure); the wiring takes `authEnabled` (server.js: `() => auth.enabled`) and hands it to the routes; `routes/channels.js` — `ownerConsent(body)` = `consentVerdict(n, {expect: body.expectWakes})` on the owner's post / create / invite (409 `wake-count-mismatch` with `wakes`), `ownerPacer(ge)` = the engine's `pacerFor('user')` when auth is OFF (local-open routes — the owner cannot be told apart from a local agent; a missing switch counts as off), none when a cookie proved the owner.

### rewind-ops.js

rewind-ops.js — PURE 撤回语义(B3 §2.10/§3.2): claude `tombstone`(上游原话"渲染或持久化本流的消费者应当移除被指名的消息", 而我们两样都做⇒半截消息永远留着) 与 codex `thread_rolled_back{num_turns}`(ThreadRolledBackEvent 只有一个字段, 0.153.4 serde dump; 从 TUI 做的回溯在这里彻底隐形, 幽灵 turn 一直挂着) 落到**同一个** `rewound` meta op {harness,toMessageId,numTurns,ids,kind,ts}(恒发两个键, null 是陈述不是缺席). **标记, 绝不 splice**: 删条目会移动 slice(offset,limit) 的每个下标并改 total, 那正是三次分页事故的机器. kind 决定处置: superseded(claude)=隐藏(照它自己的指令, 规范副本就在旁边), rollback(codex)=原地划掉+"rewound"标签(藏起来等于悄悄改写别人读过的东西). codex 的一个 turn 按**user 消息**数, 不按我们的 turnIndex(那个计数器 task_started 与压缩也会加, 真 rollout 上 24 条 user 记录压着 30 个 turnIndex 组); 连续两次回溯各取 N 个**活**turn; num_turns 超过我们渲染过的量就两个数都说. 两个 normalizer 的 turnMap 都跳过 rewound(minimap 不许指向幽灵). ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### server/conversation-deliver.js

server/conversation-deliver.js — THE conversation delivery ladder (2.362.0): channel socket→local inbox→owning machine's agentd peer-post op→durable stash drained at injection; jobs通知与agent消息同一实现; 2.363.0投递点即渲染peer卡片(emitPeerCard→normalizer.injectPeerCard — server-posted在CLI侧是body-less origin, 只有poster能渲染); 2.368.26 rung1.5=capsOf(backend).peerDelivery=='rpc-queue'经wrapper stdin帧活投递codex(idle=turn/start计费turn, busy=thread/queue/add, wrapper自录user消息故此路不发卡片; ok:false重新入stash); **2026-09-07帧带typed origin `kind`**(notification=VibeSpace自己说话即jobs通知/系统通知, peer=别的会话里的人, 缺失或未知一律按peer这条保守道): 梯子只**打标**不选道(只有wrapper知道此刻有没有turn在跑), codex忙时把notification经turn/steer插进正在跑的那一轮(只携带自己, 队列一动不动), 人发的照旧queue/add; jobs的30s洪泛地板与stash不变, 排空时由注入路由渲染成**一整块**(renderNotifStash)绝不逐条重回梯子; **2026-09-09 花钱这一半: 一次投递只有在真的会开一个 turn 时才计费** — `notificationDelivery(capsOf(backend))==='steer'` 且 `kind:'notification'` 且此刻有 turn 在跑, 这一条(且仅这一条)结构上不开 turn, 于是**扣款被扣住而不是免掉**, 由 wrapper 自己的 `peer_message_result{mode}` 经 `settleRpcDelivery` 结算(steered⇒丢弃, queued/turn⇒此时才计费, ok:false⇒不计费, 调用方重新入 stash); claude 的 cli-inbox 与 codex 的 `thread/queue/add` 在忙时是**延后**不是免费, 照旧计费. 判据取自 caps 行, 绝不按 backend id. **r5: 授权会 HOLD 住它授权的那个名额** — 梯子在 await 之前同步授权、之后才计费, 于是一次同步派发的五条投递读到同一份未计费计数(实测 cap 2 花掉 5 个 turn); 现在 `charged` 携带 `v.hold`, 而**唯一**一个 `finally` 负责归还(九个出口加两个 catch, 逐个枚举正是它要消除的脆弱), 被扣住的 rpc 帧在 wrapper 确认 steer 时归还、说它开了 turn 时计费、被判定 stranded 时归还. **2.369.159: every rung that hands a live LOCAL session a frame stamps `s._machineInputAt` (`machineTurn()`), so prompt-context holds the next-turn group reports for a turn a person started.** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### server/stdout/

server/session-brain.js — SESSION-BRAIN CORE (decomposition #8): the dark parity comparator + `sbSeenFirst` (first-writer-wins record gate) + `claudeSideEffects` (the side-effect families, ONE implementation fed by the parse's registration and the device stream). **design-unknown-records (2026-09-21): FOUR named record→side-effect consumers live here and are called by BOTH feeds** — `noteHarnessNotification` (claude `system/notification` with priority immediate/high → the existing `serverNotice` toast, key `hn:<sid>:<key>:<turn>` so a re-asserted key in the same turn dedupes at serverNotice; the card is the normalizer's), `noteApiErrorAuth` (`system/api_error` status 401/403 on the LIVE feed → the SAME `notePoolAuthFailure` the live api_retry twin drives — and the engine's own classifier still gates what is forwarded: a lone 401 needs attempt ≥ 2, 403 always; 529/429 never; test-stdout-registry drives the REAL claude classifier over the forwarded info, attempt 1 vs 2. **HONESTY (r3 2026-09-21): the binary declares api_error on the stream union but the census of 35 live buffers saw it ONLY in transcripts (the stream carries api_retry) — on every instance where that holds this consumer is FORWARD-COMPAT and never fires; the transcript rows are deliberately NOT fed (no resume/attach preflight scan): a days-old 401 would evict TODAY's member (`notePoolAuthFailure` marks the session's CURRENT slot, not the one that failed) and the live twin fires on the first request of any resume if the login is still dead**), `noteVcsState` (`system/vcs_state_changed` → `session._vcs {kind, branch, cwd, at}` persisted to session-meta, the `session-vcs` push to EVERY client (`broadcastAll` — an explorer-only client is not attached to the session), an active-sessions broadcast, a `sessionStatus.noteEvent` timeline row — card-less), `notePublishedChange` (`system/code_change_published` → `session._prLinks[]` keyed by url, ≤20, persisted; the url is http(s)-only and never fetched). Deps are lazy/optional (`getServerNotice`, `broadcastAll`, `broadcastActiveSessions`, `getSessionMetaStore`, `getSessionStatus`, `sessionStatusKey`, engine.notePoolAuthFailure) so the dark-parity harness that passes none keeps working. The parse reaches them through `brainRef` (an `mk()` lazy proxy — PROPERTY-accessed, never called; session-brain is created after session-stdout). test-stdout-registry pins both feeds: the parse hands each record to its consumer, and `claudeSideEffects` on a real instance with stub deps produces the toast / the auth-failure call / the vcs fact + push + meta + timeline / the prLinks row. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md
server/stdout/ — HARNESS STDOUT consumer registry (S5; **2026-09-07: the lazy deps are PROPERTY-ACCESSED, never called** — `mk()` Proxies over a plain `{}` are truthy but NOT callable, so `ref?.()` threw and silently dropped every permission-rule answer and every failed-peer re-stash; `ref?.method?.(…)` IS the null check, every degrade catch logs verbatim, drift-guarded by test-permission-rules; B3: claude-stream-json 消费 `session_state_changed`(权威驱动 `_isStreaming`, 经 PURE turn-state.js)/**`system/status`**(压缩阶段: `{status:'compacting'}`→阶段中的 `hook_started`→`{status:null,compact_result|compact_error}`, 与 2.284.2 api_retry 同通道一律 card-less; 这是真实压缩在我们 stdout 上的**唯一**通道, 且是唯一看得见 **AUTO 压缩**的地方——ws-handler 的 /compact 发送点结构上看不见它; 同 subtype 的权限模式回声 `{status:null,permissionMode}` 必须不被读成压缩结束)/`set_in_progress_tool_use_ids` 与 `compact_progress`(两者都**从不到达我们的 stdout**——CLI 分别交给 `onInProgressToolUseIDs` 与 `onCompactEvent` 两个宿主回调, 保留为休眠/形状对等代码, 注释点名那个回调)): index.js maps the descriptor's caps.streamProtocol → ONE consumer module (claude-stream-json.js / codex-events.js / acp-events.js = the former setupSessionPty inline branches, moved verbatim; each = create(deps) → {protocol, attach(session,id,pty,helpers)}); session-stdout only looks up + attaches; unknown/missing protocol = loud console.error + telemetry + RAW passthrough (never stream-json); consumers stay ORCH (engine/hosts/ledger deps) so the descriptor carries NO protocol twin. Gates: test-stdout-registry + test-harness-contract. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md (HARNESS STDOUT) **B5 ruling 9 的远端腿(2026-09-07 残留)**: 判定「这个目录是不是 linked worktree」的那段 shell 原来直接比较 `git rev-parse --git-dir` 与 `--git-common-dir` 的**原始字符串**, 而 git 不用同一种形式回答 —— 从一个**普通检出的子目录**里问, 前者是绝对路径后者是相对路径(实测 git 2.51: `/repo/.git` vs `../.git`) ⇒ 每一个在子目录里起的远端会话都被读成「跑在自己的 worktree 里」; 本机那条腿从来没有这个缺陷, 因为它先把两个答案都 resolve 到目录上再比. 改成向 git 要**一种**形式(`--path-format=absolute`, git ≥ 2.31), 并且 git 找到之后**空答案一律 UNKNOWN 而不是 NO**(拒绝该 flag 的旧 git 什么都不该退役; "不是仓库"仍然从 `cd`/退出码那条路给出 NO). 回归是把 consumer **真正发出的那段脚本**跑在真仓库上(普通检出子目录 / 真 linked worktree 子目录), 外加逐字的修前脚本当负控. **2.369.112 the TURN-START peer card (inc-mu6bfv1t-4drq): `command_lifecycle started`'s `command_uuid` IS the JSONL uuid of the user record the CLI wrote — `peerCommandCard` (per-attach closure, local sessions only) reads the transcript tail (`findSessionJsonlPath`, ≤512 KB, retries 0/150/600/2000 ms) and injects through `feedPeerCard` with `msgId` so the result rung dedups; typed / task-notification / body-less server-posted records stop the lookup; `server.js` lists the type as handled. Gate: test-peer-command-card (24).** **design-unknown-records (2026-09-21): claude-stream-json takes `brainRef` (the lazy session-brain proxy) and hands `system/notification`, `api_error`, `vcs_state_changed`, `code_change_published` to the FOUR named consumers in src/server/session-brain.js — never an inline twin (the routing-table law); the device feed runs the same four through `claudeSideEffects`. test-stdout-registry's unknown-records section pins both feeds + the deps-list source pins name `brainRef`.**

### desktop-display.js

desktop-display.js — SHARED (node builtins + cli-identity) machine FACTS for desktop apps (§2 row 2): `binOnPath` (YES remembered for good, NO re-checked at 60 s), `hostFacts` (`hostId` a parameter — non-local REFUSED by name in v1), `x11Env` (strips WAYLAND_DISPLAY, pins DISPLAY/XAUTHORITY/XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11/GDK_BACKEND/QT_QPA_PLATFORM — x11vnc 0.9.17 EXITS under a Wayland env, measured), `writeXauthority` (the binary Xauthority format written directly, mode 0600 — the server loads the cookie under a placeholder `:0` entry BEFORE it knows its number, clients look their display up), `startXServer` (Xvfb or Xvnc through `-displayfd 3`, detached), `startX11vnc`/`startWindowManager`/`startApp`, `rfbBanner`/`waitForRfb` (a READ probe — x11vnc answers a silent client after ~320 ms), `sameProcess` (pid AND starttime via cli-identity.procSample), `enumerateWindows` (ONE `xwininfo -root -tree` + ONE `xdotool search --onlyvisible` — two spawns whatever N; the P9 window-target shape; its halves `windowTree`/`viewableWindows` exported for the keeper's belt), `environCensus` (ONE /proc walk over verbatim `KEY=value` needles — `markerCensus` is it with the marker; the keeper adds the per-app XAUTHORITY), `applyWindowPlan` (bare X: xdotool; a WM-framed client: `wmctrl` maximise, measured on xfwm4 4.18), `xpraVersion`. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **r2: `spawnDetached` (awaited, permanent `error` listener), `assertExecutable`/`forgetBin` (re-stat at spawn), the frozen `RECIPES` + `X_SERVER_ARGS` tables, `listenerInode`/`listenerHeldBy` (who holds the 127.0.0.1 LISTEN socket — measured: x11vnc keeps a taken port's number on `[::1]`), `sessionMembers`/`sessionCensus`/`sessionSample`/`environHas`.** **r3: `sameProcess` is FALSE for a null/undefined starttime or an unreadable /proc (no evidence is not a yes); `sessionSample` sums own + REAPED ticks (each unit of work once; boundary: an init-reaped, group-killed child is invisible to any /proc reader); `markerCensus` (ONE environ walk, ~45 ms, only the ids asked) + `refreshSessions`.**

### server/desktop-app-keeper.js

server/desktop-app-keeper.js — ORCH the LIFECYCLE of every desktop-app session (§2 row 3): `create({dataDir, env: agentEnv, broadcast, serverSetting, getTelemetry, singleton, limits, registryRows})` → launch/stop/keepAlive/noteInput/get/list/streamTarget/adoptAll/start/shutdown; data/desktop-apps.json (writeJsonAtomic, FACTS: display/port/pids+starts/backend+via+fallbackWhy/state/lastError/idleTimeoutMs/lastInputAt) + data/desktop-apps/<id>/{app.log,Xauthority}; the vnc-display rung in BOTH spellings (Xvnc when present, else Xvfb + x11vnc -localhost -rfbport -forever -shared, + xfwm4/openbox when present); adopt-or-reap at boot by pid+starttime+banner (a dead part ⇒ exited/failed with lastError KEPT, leftovers reaped, a recycled pid is never signalled); the 5 s tick = liveness (adopted sessions have no child handles) + idle (DA3, `desktop.idleTimeoutMin`, 0 = never; keep-alive is one explicit action) + the runaway sample every GUARD_SAMPLE_MS (stop + park the registry row for RUNAWAY_COOLDOWN_MS + telemetry `desktop-app-runaway`); `shutdown()` = timers only — the apps SURVIVE the restart by design. The xpra rung is refused BY NAME at bring-up (`backend-not-wired`) until P8-2. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **r2: bring-up = `display.RECIPES[M.recipeFor(backend, via)]` (no rung named here; `no-recipe` refused by name), `onPart` commits each pid the moment it exists, ready only after `listenerHeldBy` proves the port, stop = `killSessionVerified` per part (group + session members read FRESH, the env marker when the leader is gone), the guard samples `sessionPids(rec)`, `singletonLive()` refreshes vnc.js's fact before every verdict.** **r3: a stop DURING the bring-up — `stopping` FIRST (the bring-up reads it at every await), teardown, WAIT for the in-flight bring-up (bounded by its own deadline), teardown again, THEN the verdict (terminal still means torn down); `onPart` on a record that died kills the part at once; `bringUp`'s `finally` reaps on every exit; the boot belt `reapTerminalLeftovers` = ONE marker census over this store's ids (the only layer that survives a SIGKILL mid-stop). `partIsOurs` = ONE identity ladder (live handle → pid+starttime → unproven ⇒ never signalled; marker members only).
