### cli-identity.js

cli-identity.js — THE agent-CLI process identity, ONE rule in two spellings (B-3185 r3): `isCliProcess(pid,name)` (JS, used by discovery-facts ⇒ bundled into the daemon) beside `cliIdentityShellFns()` (the POSIX vs_is_cli the writer sweep and the ssh discovery CO leg embed verbatim; writer-sweep only RE-EXPORTS it). Three rungs — argv[0] basename / the interpreter's first non-flag operand / `/proc/exe` (version-image rung narrowed by the presentation, ` (deleted)` stripped: auto-update replaces the image of a LIVE session; **the strip's pattern is QUOTED because ssh runs this text under the REMOTE LOGIN SHELL — in zsh an unquoted `(deleted)` is a glob GROUP and strips nothing**). NEVER a substring of the whole argv (measured: the retired rule said YES to 106 of 4277 processes vs 16 real CLIs). **argv是NUL分隔的词表且一个词里可以有换行(r4): shell那半原来"NUL换成换行再取第N行"=第N个词的第一行, 与JS双向分歧且两向都有害(读者被杀/真writer躲过sweep), 现在取行前把真换行寄存到`\001`再还原, `ps`回退先压平; 而`$(…)`还会吃掉**结尾**换行(argv[0]/解释器操作数/readlink三处捕获实测全中, 且吃掉后是shell说YES·JS说NO=更宽松那向), 故三处统一走`vs_cap`(子shell内哨兵护尾, 只摘生产者自己那一个换行).** 每条**kill路径**(sweep · hosts.js killPidShell=远程Terminate · /api/kill-pid本地分支)都问这一条规则, 不问comm不问整条argv; **`ps`回退只在无/proc机器上跑, r5才第一次被真跑起来**(重指/proc根+PATH上的替身`ps`+JS孪生在/proc读会抛的子进程里真走自己的回退; 负控=不压平的修前行, 两个换行fixture上与JS相反), **远程Terminate的存在性探针改成正证据梯子**(`kill -0`→`[ -d /proc/N ]`→`ps -p N`; busybox的`ps`没有`-p`, 旧的单条`ps`捕获让每个活pid都答VS_GONE)且新增第四种回答VS_UNKNOWN=活着但读不到任何证据; **r6把这条梯子收进本文件成为唯一定义`pidAliveShellFn()`, sysinfo-wiring的signalProc同样内嵌**(r5清点到它却放它留着自己的`ps -p`, 理由只描述了那个脚本两处`ps -p`里的第二处——第一处在**成功分支**上做杀后存活判定, busybox下对一个`trap "" TERM`的活进程答OK-GONE⇒`{ok:true,gone:true}`, 不是误标是**凭空造**出一个成功; 失败分支同样实测把活着的他人进程答成ESRCH); 无JS孪生是故意的(本地分支读`process.kill(pid,0)`的errno, 那正是shell做不到、梯子才存在的那件事); 不变量=**靠注释活着的孪生仍是孪生, 注释只值它作者数清了几个调用点**, 所以换成STANDING SWEEP(test-writer-sweep §17: 任何kill/signal路径上`ps -p`一律不得作存在性判定, 幸存的每一处按理由列入allowlist, 死条目同样变红); **r7: 那个sweep自己是靠一张手写的七文件清单驱动的** — 手写清单正是本bug已经三次击败的同一件工具(r4没清点到的kill路径/r5清点到却放行/r6发现放行理由只讲了两处里的第二处), 它只在作者已经看过的地方执法, 实测漏掉**47个**真会发信号的文件(server.js·jobs·boot-restore·plugins/vnc/port-forward/opencode-serve·agentd·ws-handler/ws-create); 现在文件集由**grep推导**(src/·data/bin/·scripts/非test + 仓库根, 命中 kill -TERM/-9/-0·SIG*·pkill·process.kill(·killRemotePid·signalProc·vs_alive; 无扩展名的按**shebang**进——`git ls-files data/bin`永远看不见**生成**的vibespace-status), 推导结果由套件**打印**出来, 且故意过包含(i18n词典命中SIGSTOP): 假阳性只是扩大执法范围, 假阴性才是缺陷本身; 两条结构pin(推导不得丢掉r6清单覆盖过的任何一个 + 必须仍覆盖那十条被漏掉的永久kill路径)+ 把**已发布的sweep**按root参数化后对着一棵临时树跑第二遍的六条正负控(退役形状被抓/allowlist条目复制到别的文件仍算stray/干净kill路径保持绿/无信号的`ps -p`不在范围/test-*被排除——这正是本文件能把退役形状写下来当负控的唯一原因/data/bin下的shebang工具被抓) + 对每个导出shell **builder实际发出的文本**再扫一遍(源码扫描结构上看不见运行时拼装的探针), 负控=逐字的修前脚本; 不变量=**standing sweep的价值等于它走过的那个集合, 集合要从性质推导不要枚举, 并且要把走过什么打印出来**. Dependency-free. Parity is functional: test-writer-sweep §6/§12/§14 + test-discovery-interpret §8 drive both spellings over the same live pids. **2026-09-09 增 THE PROCESS TREE, 无 fork**: `readPpid`(/proc/<pid>/stat 第4字段, 从**最后**一个 `)` 起数——comm 里可以有空格和括号)与 `readChildPids`(`/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/children` 的**并集**——children 记在 fork 它的那个**线程**上), 替掉发现 sweep 里**每个锁**一次的 `ps -p -o ppid=` 与**每个活会话**一次的 `pgrep -P`; 代价从来不是等待而是 **fork**(实测一次 `spawn('true')`: 45MB RSS 1.8ms / 543MB 18.8ms / 1.5GB 67-73ms, 页表复制发生在调用线程上, 而 `Promise.all` 把 N 次 fork 排进**同一个 tick**). 无 /proc 那条 rung 是**整趟 sweep 一次** `ps -eo pid=,ppid=`(`parentIndex`, memo `PROC_TABLE_TTL_MS`=2s, 故意小于 /api/sessions 自己的 4.5s 缓存), 绝不每个 pid 一次; `hasProcfs` **只记住 YES**(NO 每 60s 重问——一次 stat 失败不许变成永久降级去 fork); 全部是**取值**读, 答不出就是 `null`/`[]`=没有证据, 存在性仍然只由 `kill -0` 说; `procRoot` 可注入所以无 /proc 的 rung 在 Linux 上**跑得起来**(r5 `vs_argv` 的教训). **r3增 `pidsMatchingCmdline(needle)`=`pgrep -f` 的那个问题(「哪些活 pid 的命令行里带这个串」), 唯一调用者是 ws-handler 的 kill 分支找持有本会话 socket 的 dtach master**: /proc 那级把每个 `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` 读进**同一个**复用的 64 KiB 缓冲(读满即整读该 pid, 巨大的 argv 要被回答而不是被静默截断)并用 `Buffer.indexOf` 逐字节比, 无 /proc 那级是**整个问题一次** `pgrep -f` 绝不逐候选一次; 字面子串比 `pgrep -f` 的 ERE **更窄**=对一个会 SIGTERM 命中者的调用方是安全方向, 而带空格的 needle 按拼接形匹配(/proc 用 NUL 分词). 代价与 readPpid 那条不同所以要**说出来**: 这个扫描对服务器自身大小是**平的**(3,400 进程 23.6-23.7 ms), 而它替掉的 fork 不是(58 MB 阻塞 2.0 ms / 559 MB 24.4 / 1,564 MB 69.4, 端到端 87.6/110.6/155.2) ⇒ 事故那台机器上阻塞 69→24 ms、延迟 155→24 ms, 诚实代价=刚开机的 58 MB 服务器把 2 ms 阻塞换成 24 ms. Gate: scripts/test-discovery-spawn.mjs + test-architecture §45. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **B-eac2 residual (c) 把第四种拼写也收了进来**: `readPsIdentity(pid)`(/proc 优先, 无 /proc 走 `ps -p <pid> -o uid=,args=`, 1s per-pid memo)与它的两个读者 `procCmdline`/`procUid` 现在住在这里, opencode-serve 的 keeper 直接 require 它, 而 data/bin/vibespace-opencode-op 保留唯一一份**孪生**(无 checkout 的 ssh 主机 require 不了, 与 usage-scanner 同一条成文例外; scripts/test-opencode-remote.mjs 两侧同输入对比). 它是**取值**不是存在性探针 —答不出就是 `null`=没有证据, 绝不是'没了'; 谁还活着只由 `kill -0` 说. **2026-09-14 增 `readSid`/`sessionIndex({fresh})`/`sessionMembers` = THE SESSION TABLE (one /proc walk, memoised; a detached leader's sid is its pid) for the desktop-app keeper's stop/sample/socket-owner questions; no `ps` rung on purpose.** **2026-09-14: `procSample` also returns `reapedTicks` (cutime+cstime); which ticks a guard sums is the consumer's rule (a SET counts own+reaped once; a single-pid guard keeps `cpuTicks`).**

**CS SEPARATION RULE (2.276.0): `hostId` is a PARAMETER, never a branch.** Server-side logic is written ONCE against a machine handle; the only difference between this machine, an ssh host and a dialed-in device is the transport underneath it. `hosts.device(falsy)` returns device #0 (the local daemon has been a full DeviceManager since 2.158.0 — same binary/mux/op surface — but was unreachable through the API, so every feature was written twice BY CONSTRUCTION). Migration table: docs/design-cs-unification.md — the metric is PARALLEL IMPLEMENTATIONS (9 twin-sets → 0 unjustified as of 2.279.1), not branch count (branches that select a transport for ONE shared implementation are fine). Live keystone proof: scripts/test-local-device.mjs (real daemon; absence THROWS). Documented exceptions require a table row + a drift/parity guard: the shipped single-file usage scanner (checkout-less host) and local file ops (SafeFs FUSE-hang isolation is load-bearing; the daemon carries live session pipes — revisit only with daemon-side worker isolation).

sidebar.js — Sidebar shell (filter/sort/merge pipeline, tab switching). **`LIVE_SESSION_FACTS` + `liveSessionFacts()` (2026-09-07 r3) = THE list of per-session live facts the `active-sessions` payload publishes under the names every client surface reads them by.** `_merge()` REBUILDS the row (webui half renamed into webuiId/webuiName/webuiMode, `cwd` composed into the display/grouping key, `status` derived) and `/api/sessions` discovery carries none of them, so a fact not on this list is DROPPED — the whitelist-drift class, sixth strike: `worktree`/`worktreePath` (badge dead, Session Properties said "not isolated in this run" about a session the server reported isolated WITH a path, and the fork's `worktreePick` live half had no producer), `outputStyle` (2.369.58) and `remoteState` (2.219.1) were all dead here. ONE list spread into BOTH branches; the drift guard in scripts/test-worktree-userchan-ui.mjs re-derives the payload's own key set from server.js so the seventh strike fails at build. **2026-09-07 r4: reaching `_merge()` is only HALF the hop** — `_mergeAndRender()` re-renders only when its DIGEST changes, and the digest named none of these, so the `worktree-path` broadcast added to keep the badge honest repainted nothing (neither the badge nor the remote chip has a partial-update path — both exist only inside `renderSessionCard`). Each row therefore declares BOTH halves (`{digest: <projection>|null}`): the four cheap scalars that change at most once per session GATE the render (worktree/worktreePath/remoteState/outputStyle), while the object-valued `todo`/`auth` stay carried-only ON PURPOSE (they change several times per turn / are re-pointed by the pool — gating on them is the 2.72.0/2.106.1 churn, so their surfaces still repaint late: a separate change with its own churn measurement). 2026-09-21: LIVE_SESSION_FACTS gained `vcs` (digest kind:branch:at) and `prLinks` (digest url@action list) — both drawn on the card, both gate.

### channel-chrome.js

channel-chrome.js — CLIENT (a4, 2026-09-21): the THREE DOM primitives every channel surface builds with, so the panel, the window, the card, the editors and the Integrations window draw the SAME glyph the same way — `icon(name, px, cls)` = one `<span class="chan-ic">` holding an SVG from src/lib/icons.js sized by font-size (the ONLY innerHTML this feature writes, and it is the library's own static string, never a string from the wire), `el(tag, cls, text)` = a textContent element (the XSS law), `btn(label, onClick, cls)` = a house `mounts-btn` (`mounts-btn-primary` = the ONE primary; the old 10px `chan-btn` family is gone), `noteLine(cls, text, {warn})` = a sentence line that carries the alert glyph when it warns. Gate: test-channels-e2e ⑫ (c) — every `.chan-ic` holds an `<svg>`, no text symbol on the surfaces.

### channel-words.js

channel-words.js — CLIENT (a3 i18n, 2026-09-18): THE words for every channel/outbox/integration route CODE (`routeErrorText` — the engine's `error` sentence is the agent's contract, the toast words the `code`; the sentence is shown only where it is the vendor's or the validator's own detail), `principalKindText`, `policyModeText` via `tc('policy', …)` (`review` is also the code-review status elsewhere), `groupTitle` (a Task Group's `title`, never a `name` it lacks — every group showed as its id, a1 A5; pinned by test-channels-e2e ⑮ on the Assign "Wake" select and the Reach roster + a name-less grant, with the store's refusal of a name-only group as the control). **2026-09-22 (the account model):** the two new route codes are worded here — `unknown-credential` ("not one this instance offers — pick another") and `no-such-adapter` ("That account no longer exists"). Gate: test-channels-i18n (heavy, zh+ja census over the a1 driver). **g3: `groupErrorText` (the groups routes' codes), `notifyModeText` (the four modes, billed ones said), `wakeEchoText` (woke N = N billed turns, said at 0; refused not billed; who reads it next turn).** **r3: `store-blocked`, `wake-count-mismatch` and `rate-floor` worded in `routeErrorText` (+ `store-blocked` in `groupErrorText`; a group 409 that carries the fresh view says the preview was updated).**

### channels-panel.js + channel-window.js
 **2.369.147 r3: the wizard's credential step is drawn whenever ≥ 1 credential is offered; an unavailable `own` row (fields missing) sends the user to the Integrations card on Continue.**
channels-panel.js + channel-window.js — CLIENT: the Channels rail panel (adapters as sections, **a FRESHNESS CHIP on every row** — the one number a user needs before handing something to a lane, drawn from the lane ACTUALLY carrying it — the `channel-row` menu and the ⚙ row as CONTRIBUTIONS registered by the owning module so gear-menu.js stays byte-identical to its pinned legacy list) and the conversation WINDOW (registered window type, singleton per CONVERSATION, restored from its openSpec; plain text through textContent on every path; a composer ONLY where `offers()` allows one and a NAMED reason where it does not). The panel repaints from the broadcast digest with no fetch; the window re-reads its own tail when its id is named (§10.4). **r2 four rules: marking read is a USER action** (on open and on touch, never as a repaint side effect — the render-driven POST plus an unconditional notify was a self-feeding loop measured at ~490 req/s with ONE window open, which also destroyed the mark it set), **the ws handler is removed BY NAME on close** (`onGlobal` returned undefined so `off?.()` was a silent no-op and a CLOSED window kept fetching, kept POSTing over the user's mark and held its detached DOM; the LOAD-BEARING half is `onGlobal` now returning its own unsubscribe — measured, the named-const teardown alone is a belt), **the page boundary is a RECORD** (`before` + `beforeId`), **and the freshness/identity SENTENCES are composed here** from the server's structure, with the device's own `t`. **r3: the title bar names the conversation through `wm.setTitle`** (`winInfo.setTitle?.(…)` was a permanent no-op — the literal has no such member — so every channel window read "Channel"; jobs-panel had the identical call; test-window-types censuses the idiom), **an untracked row's chip says "not polling" / "not scanning"** (never "within 5m" about a fetch nothing will make), and a disabled adapter's section says `disabled`. **P1a (2026-09-16): the adapter's OWN controls on its section, every fact from the digest and no fetch on repaint — the connect wizard's THREE COPY PATHS (§10.1: `none` opens the Integrations card FIRST and never a consent page; `cluster` says "Provided by the cluster · <label>" beside the button; `user` says nothing more; a `409 needs-credentials` from the route opens that card too), the flow dialog (the consent page as a LINK the user clicks — a window opened after an await is popup-blocked — the named `port-busy` refusal, PASTE-BACK + Cancel, closed by the adapter's own broadcast), the four-valued auth line with its `re-authorize in <eta>` countdown (`reauthEta`, the clock an argument) and a Re-authorize / Open Integrations / Connect verb chosen by the STATE, the spoken last connect failure and the filed "For you" note, the TRACKED PICKER (a checkbox per discovered conversation — tracked is opt-in), the OPTIONS editor over the adapter's DECLARED schema (a select for `choices`), Disconnect (confirmed) and Enable/Disable; strings through textContent, zh+ja shipped.** **P1b: the push line (`pushLaneText`, amber when demoted/unavailable) + "Re-declare exclusive and retry" beside a demotion + the Push… dialog (the exclusivity declaration with each claim's consequence in words; the switch itself on an opt-in lane) — gated on the digest's `push`, never a kind; saving a claim IS a re-declaration so it is sent only when changed or demoted.** **P2 (+ src/lib/channel-filter-editor.js): the "Assign & filter…" row on a TRACKED conversation (panel menu + window bar) opens ONE dialog — who is woken (a live agent session or a task group, round-robin), on what (every message / a filter of the PURE module's CLOSED rule kinds, validated with the same code the route refuses with), how (a wake per batch / one digest per window), with what authority (`send` drawn ONLY when both caps allow it, else the reason; a stored send the policy now forbids says it reads as draft), the per-assignment daily wake cap; a LIVE server-side estimate (debounced, the corpus never reaches the browser) that PRINTS `sampled`/`truncated` and, once assigned, "estimated ~X/day when set; actually Y/day since"; and the HONEST per-lane latency sentence worded from the digest's `wakeLatency`. The row's sub-line = `assignmentSummary` (who / what / how / authority / hits per 7d), amber when the last wake was held or stashed.** **WINDOW FALLBACK (2.369.125, design-mobile-gaps #2/#14): the ⚙ row's `when: _railEl` gate is GONE — on a phone the rail is never built, so the whole Communication panel had no entry point. `focusChannelsPanel(app, {forceWindow, syncId})` carries openJobsWindow's ladder: the rail panel where it exists, else `openChannelsWindow` = ONE singleton `channels` window (openSpec `openChannels`, registered here with registerWindowType) hosting the very same `renderChannelsPanel(app, c)`, its broadcast unsubscribe tied to the window's listener controller. `app.openChannels(opts)` passes the options through.** **a3 i18n (2026-09-18, the comm-panel polish): every code the digest carries is worded HERE with the device's `t` — `auth.why` (authWhyText), `lane.why` (laneWhyText: `SCAN · NO-STORE-ON-PLATFORM` was the raw code uppercased), `lastPass.code` (errorCodeText), a held wake's `refused` (wakeRefusalText), a scan `source`; the built-in row reads "connected — this instance" off `auth.self` (never the seeded English `user: 'you'`); a `needs-credentials` line words the store's `credential.whyCode` (PURE `integration-registry.credentialWhyText`); an adapter's declared option `label`/`help` are KEYS rendered through `t()`; every route failure toasts by CODE (`src/lib/channel-words.js routeErrorText`) — the engine's sentence is the agent's contract, never the user's chrome; the window's meta names the adapter by LABEL and an UNTRACKED conversation's footer says "Not tracked — messages are fetched once you track it." with the Track verb (untracked ≠ "capability unknown"); the Propose toast words the policy's reason ENUM through `reasonLabel`; the window-type labels go through `t()`. Gate: scripts/test-channels-i18n.mjs (heavy) — zh AND ja through the a1 driver, zero Latin-only visible text outside a PRINTED allowlist, with a planted-literal negative control.** **r3: a composer whose adapter `sendStartsTurn` says the cost and sends `expectWakes:1`; the group composer repaints from a 409's `group` view; a `chan-quarantine-note` line per `digest.quarantined` entry above the group list.**

**a4 UI (2026-09-21, docs/design-communication-panel-ui.md §4 — direction A, the Folders / Tasks idiom; owner "界面很乱，没有层次"):** the panel is a LIST — a bar (`{n} conversations · {k} tracked` + the Outbox button = outbox glyph · label · accent count, the label hidden under a 200px container because the 260px default sidebar leaves 172px for the bar, MEASURED), one collapsible `folder-header` section per adapter (chevron · kind glyph from the digest's FACTS — `builtin` ⇒ robot, thread/mailbox rows ⇒ mail, else chat — · name 11/600 sentence-case · a 6px STATE DOT whose tooltip is the lane note + the observed-identity proof · `tracked/total` · a ⋯ `icon-btn`), and EVERY adapter verb lives in the `channel-adapter` contribution menu (Track… / Options / Push… / the Sender line as a CHECKABLE row + Use instance default / Connect|Re-authorize / Disconnect / Enable|Disable — state-driven `when`s); a `.chan-sec-note` line appears ONLY when the adapter has something to say beyond "connected" (not connected + Connect, needs re-authorization + Re-authorize, credential missing + Open Integrations, a re-auth due within 7 d, disabled + Enable, failing passes, a withdrawn push claim), wrapping at 10px with its ONE verb, amber (`--warn-text`) when it needs the user, and a NON-connectable adapter with an unknown auth says nothing (a "not connected" claim about a control that does not exist); rows are bordered `session-item-card`s on ONE grid — line 1 = title + the ONE freshness pill (neutral tint for an age, green for `live`, dimmer for off/never), line 2 = participants + the needs-you badges right-aligned (awaiting = accent-outline pill with the check glyph, unread = accent-filled count; `not tracked` as 9px text), line 3 only when assigned (amber + "last wake held" when the last wake was refused); under a 180px container (the 200px sidebar) the two badges collapse to ONE accent pill carrying their sum with the breakdown in its tooltip (the account roster's rule at this panel's own threshold); the fresh instance shows `.empty-hint` + the Connect section of full-width `mounts-btn` rows (kind glyph + "Connect X" / "Set up X credentials…", the credential path as the note under each); the flow dialog is a STEPPER (Credential ✓ → Consent → Track): "Open the consent page" as the ONE primary + a Copy-link button, the port-busy refusal as a NAMED amber line with the alert glyph, paste-back as a collapsed `<details>` that opens itself when nothing listens, and a finished flow becomes step 3 = the Track picker in the same dialog; the window bar is three tiers (title 13/600 + ONE ⋯ = the `channel-row` menu with `inWindow`, meta 11 dim, the assignment as an accent-tint CHIP that opens the editor — "Assign to an agent…" when unassigned, amber when the last wake was held), the list groups same-author lines within 5 min under one head with `Today` / `Yesterday` / date separators, the composer is `font: inherit` 12px with a short placeholder + one policy note + the Propose primary (Ctrl/⌘+Enter proposes), and the identity warning lives on the CARD only. Text tokens per MEANING (`--ok-text` / `--warn-text` / `--bad-text` / `--attn-text` = the raw hue mixed toward `--text`, AA in both themes); every glyph is an SVG through `src/lib/channel-chrome.js icon()`. **Round-3 invariants:** the panel is a NAMED container (`container: chan-panel / inline-size`) and every width rule queries it BY NAME — the rows are `session-item-card`s, inline-size containers themselves, so an unnamed query resolved against the 166px ROW and collapsed the badge pair at the default width (test-channels-e2e ⑫ pins the pair at 260 and the one-pill collapse at 200); on a row the freshness pill yields only after the title reached its 60px floor (shrink weight 0.05 vs 1) and then ellipsizes rather than spilling (ja's `ポーリングしていません` is 87px); the day separator's date is `toLocaleDateString(LOCALE_TAG[resolveLang()])` — the DEVICE's language, never the browser's (the census caught "Sep 22" between zh messages); a long title carries itself as its tooltip. Gate: test-channels-e2e ⑫ (row grid ±1px, 375px no sideways overflow, SVG-only glyphs, one colour per state) + the driver's shots.

**r4 (2026-09-21, the verifier's findings on a4, each reproduced on the rendered chrome first):** ① THE PANEL REPAINTS IN PLACE — sidebar-rail.js no longer removes + re-renders `.rail-panel-channels` on `channels-updated` (its own `onBroadcast` already draws from `msg.digest`); `draw()` builds the tree into a fragment, swaps it in with ONE `replaceChildren` and restores the nearest scroller's scrollTop, so a broadcast never empties the list, never refetches `/api/channels` and never clamps the scroll to 0 (a1 D12: measured 7 teardowns / 7 fetches / scroll 0 for 7 broadcasts; test-channels-e2e ⑬ counts removals = 0, fetches = 0, scroll and a fold intact). ② AN UNTRACKED ROW CARRIES NO FRESHNESS PILL (design §4.3): nothing is fetched, so there is no evidence to claim and its `not tracked` text is the claim — the pill there was the one that truncated (ja `ポーリングしていま…` read as "polling" when the truth was "not polling"); on a TRACKED row the pill is UNSHRINKABLE (`flex: 0 0 auto`, the title yields to its 60px floor) and only a pill wider than the space left ellipsizes (`max-width: calc(100% − 66px)`) rather than clipping; the ja off words shortened (ポーリングなし / スキャンなし); the wire still carries the untracked claim (`freshness.state === 'off'`). ③ the warning line's alert glyph is a fixed `flex: 0 0 auto` slot — `.chan-sec-note > span:not(.chan-ic)` takes the sentence rule (an unqualified `> span` made the icon a 124px box and pushed the sentence ~110px right or onto its own line; ⑭ measures gap ≤ 8px at 260/340/500). ④ under the 180px container the pill HIDES (its sentence rides the title's tooltip) and the head hides the NAME, keeping the kind glyph + dot + count with the label as the head's tooltip (a "5…" claim and a "fak…" stub said nothing). ⑤ the needs-credentials line words a CODE on every path — `credential.whyCode` for a real adapter, `auth.whyCode` for one that resolves its own credential (fake.js + `authState` pass the store's code through) — never the raw `why` sentence. ⑥ the state dot's identity-observation instant is formatted with `deviceLocale()` (i18n.js), the same rule as the day separator. ⑦ the row's assignment line prepends the `filter` SVG glyph; `assignmentSummary` carries no `→` text symbol (§17). Gate: test-channels-e2e ⑬ (in-place repaint), ⑭ (glyph beside sentence), ⑮ (group title), ⑯ (every tracked pill drawn whole at 260 in zh/ja/en; no pill on an untracked row). **g3 (design §22): the panel is an IM — the FIRST SCREEN is the group list (agent groups + TRACKED conversations by activity; `.chan-grow` rows), Accounts and the Message watcher are folded secondary sections (`channelsPanelFolds` in user state), New group; the window's composer by `composerMode` (external: direct Send as you when `sendAsUser`, Propose when only the bot; a GROUP: direct as You with the @-autocomplete + the wake preview); the narrow threshold 160 px.** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

the normalizer is the reconcile's ONE owner and its taskInfo edit reaches `updateTask` like every other outcome), `updateTask` patches a done-tail row by `toolCallId` when a later verdict lands after the soft `finished` (the set drops a task ~2 records before its outcome record), the tail draws `finished` as a dim ○ titled "finished (outcome not reported)" (never ✗), and the dropdown lists the set's rows the cards never learned about ("reported by the harness").** **IN-PLACE CHIPS (design-accessibility-tree §3 row 8 (b) / §8 lean, chunk a3, 2026-09-22): `render()` builds the chip SET as descriptors (`chip(key, cls, title, html, {style, attrs})`) and `_reconcile` keeps ONE `<span data-chip=key>` per key across renders — class / title / style / data-* patched through setAttribute (raw strings, no HTML escaping on the way) only when they differ, the inner markup re-written only when its string changed, a node moved only when its position changed, a key that left the set removed — so a context% / cost / turn-state tick touches only the chips that changed and never re-creates the bar's subtree (the whole-bar `innerHTML` rebuild it replaced was one accessibility subtree remove+insert per window per update, the "stale" 20 % of the owner's 50,150 nodes). The click handling stays the ONE delegated listener (`_onClick` + `closest`) — nothing is bound per chip, so nothing is re-bound. The bar is a flex row: the whitespace text nodes the old join(' ') put between chips were never rendered, so nothing visual moves. Gate: scripts/test-status-bar-chips.mjs (fast — the REAL class through a counting fake DOM: identity across 20 ticks, appear/disappear with the neighbours' identity intact, attribute parity, a neutered-copy negative control, wiring pins).**

### design-account-hardening.md

design-account-hardening.md — 2026-09-08 DESIGN (owner decisions pending, no code yet): the root fix for the 5-incident money batch (auto-resume's 130 billed continues / readings keyed by the spawn org / unseen login deadlines / unretracted warnings / inc-mts8a8mr-ulmm's in-flight-on-the-new-slot cascade). Thesis: we MUTATE the binding between a running CLI and a credential dir, then spend money on INFERENCES about it — 4 rival derivations, and the COST one (`resolveUsageKey`, per RECORD, feeding persisted rates.json) was never pinned at all. Target = ONE durable LEASE (promoting slot-transitions.js, carrying both id namespaces + a credential-MATERIAL fingerprint) read by ONE `identityOf`, moved only at TURN BOUNDARIES (not mint-once+respawn — that costs a full context re-send per switch); ONE usage-cache write choke point with a caps-gated weekly-phase falsifier (`quotaWindowFingerprint`, null for codex — measured 53 clusters, rolling window); ONE spend authorizer in front of all 7 unattended-turn producers; ledger↔OTel AGGREGATE reconciliation kept (the refutation was about routing ONE reading). 12 principles = 12 enforceable invariants, 3 grep-derived build censuses (derivations / cache writers / spend paths), 5 phases each with its gate, and the per-incident test + negative control. §6 = 12 numbered owner decisions.
**P1b (2026-09-16): the push line + the Push… dialog.** Gated on the digest's
`push` (the capability ROW's answer), never on a kind: the section draws
`pushLaneText(a.push, a.lane, {t, now})` (amber when demoted or unavailable),
a "Re-declare exclusive and retry" verb beside a demotion (a demotion is
cleared by the party that made the claim, never by the counters), and Push…
— the exclusivity DECLARATION (unknown / shared / exclusive, each with its
consequence in words) plus, on an opt-in lane, the switch itself; the claim
is sent only when it changed or the lane is demoted, because saving a claim
IS a re-declaration. zh + ja shipped.

**P2 — the Assign & filter editor (`src/lib/channel-filter-editor.js`).**
One sentence per invariant: the "Assign & filter…" / "Assign to an agent…"
row exists only on a TRACKED conversation (nothing is fetched for an untracked
one, so nobody could be woken) — on the panel's `channel-row` menu and as the
window bar's button; the dialog offers live agent sessions
(`app.sidebar._webuiSessions`, cid = `backendSessionId || claudeSessionId`)
and task groups (`app.sidebar._tasks`, round-robin) as principals, and a
principal no longer live is still listed so the assignment can be edited;
rule kinds and validation come from the PURE module (the closed set the route
refuses with); the estimate is asked of the server on every edit (250 ms
debounce; the corpus never reaches the browser) and PRINTS `sampled` /
`truncated`, and once assigned "estimated ~X/day when set; actually Y/day
since" beside it; `send` is drawn ONLY when `authorityCap(conv.authorityCaps)`
is null, otherwise the reason is drawn, and a stored send the policy now
forbids says it reads as draft; the latency line is `wakeLatencyText` over
the digest's structured `wakeLatency` (push with/without coalescing, kick,
poll, reconcile, scan, no-source); Save writes the filter first (when
filtered) then the assignment with `estimateAtSet`, Unassign is its own
button, and nothing re-renders itself — the engine's broadcast repaints the
panel row (`assignmentSummary`, amber when the last wake was held/stashed)
and the window bar. Gate: test-channels-e2e (heavy) owes the browser leg.

### src/lib/channel-outbox.js + src/lib/channel-reach-editor.js (CLIENT)

P3 (design §8, §9.2, §9.5, §10.1). `renderProposalCard` is the ONE approval
card — the inline section a conversation window draws above its composer
(`renderInlineProposals`) and the singleton Outbox window (`channel-outbox`
type, `openChannelOutbox`, ⚙ "Outbox…", the panel's Outbox button carrying
the digest's `awaitingTotal`) both render it from the same store, so they
cannot disagree. Every card carries the identity row ("Will send as you/the
bot") and, when `identityMarking` is not `none`, the warning composed from
the digest's `identityWarning` structure through `chanCaps.identityWarningText`
(`unknown` as loud as `marked`); the policy's reasons in words; the `why`
reference; the original text under an edited one; approve / edit (approve
edited) / reject with a reason; the receipt-delivery line; and for `unknown`
the sentence that it is never retried. Decisions POST and let
`channel-outbox-updated` repaint (never waiting for the echo). Every server
string is textContent. The reach dialog lists every grant WITH its origin
(only `user` rows removable — an assignment's row leaves with the assignment,
a request's stays as the approval), grants to a live session or a Task Group
from the SAME roster the Assign editor uses, approves/denies open requests,
and sets the policy (review / direct / the adapter's default). The composer
now PROPOSES (user-drafted, `send` authority) and its note names the policy
that governs the reply.

P4: the card shows the exact sender line that WILL be appended before the
approval (and the one that WAS after), the "Checked N× — last answer" line,
and a Check outcome button only where `canReconcile` (else the reason in
words); a read-only footer says WHY in words (`sendWhyText`, so
`send-scope-not-granted` names the re-consent). The panel row carries the
per-channel Sender line switch (OFF / instance default) and the observed-
identity line once a real send has been read.

**r3 (agent groups, 2026-09-23):** an awaiting card whose proposal `wakes` (the Agents adapter: approving IS a billed turn) says "Approving wakes this agent: 1 billed turn" on its meta line, and Approve sends `expectWakes: p.wakes` (the engine refuses a missing echo `wake-count-mismatch`, and — auth off — paces it `rate-floor`; both leave the proposal awaiting, worded by `routeErrorText`).

### src/agent-env.js (PURE)

THE SPAWN-ENV SANITIZER, one rule for two processes (2026-09-14, the P0b
round-1 verifier's HIGH). `agentEnv(base, {keep})` drops every `VIBESPACE_*`
not in the keep set (secrets + server config), every `npm_*` (nested-npm
hazard) and `AGENT_ENV_DROP` (PORT/HOST/NODE_ENV/NODE_OPTIONS + the ambient
`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` pair); `daemonEnv(base)` is the same rule with
`DAEMON_ENV_KEEP` = `AGENT_ENV_KEEP` ∪ the two names the daemon tier itself
reads (`VIBESPACE_NODE_MODULES`, `VIBESPACE_AGENTD_VERSION`) — DERIVED from
the daemon tier's own `process.env.VIBESPACE_*` reads and pinned that way by
test-agentd-session, never typed from memory. Imports nothing, reads no
process: `src/ws-handler.js` re-exports it as the `agentEnv` every spawn site
already requires from there (with its `process.env` default), and the daemon
bundles it. **Why two processes**: the daemon is a SECOND HOLDER of the
server env — `DeviceManager._spawnLocal` spawned it with `{...process.env}`
and `agentd.spawnEnv()` laid the server's sanitized session env OVER the
daemon's raw `process.env`, so every daemon child (a pipe-session claude, an
`open-session` pty, `run-cmd`) inherited whatever the daemon was born with;
measured by the verifier on a worktree server with `agentd.localPipeSessions:
true`: a real `claude` CLI whose /proc/<pid>/environ carried the full 40-char
cluster integration secret, handed down by a daemon spawned by a PREVIOUS
server life (the daemon survives restarts by design, so a WITHDRAWN cluster
default kept flowing into new sessions), plus the drive presets. §14.11.1's
"by construction cannot reach any agent child" was true of the dtach path
only. Now a daemon is born sanitized at all THREE birth sites (`_spawnLocal`,
the `--stdio` bridge's spawn, the upgrade re-exec — the one moment a RUNNING
daemon's environ can be cleaned; honest count: the re-exec that INSTALLS
this bundle is run by the OLDER daemon's code with the raw env, so a daemon
born under an older build is cleaned at the FOLLOWING re-exec or a restart)
and `spawnEnv()` sanitizes its BASE on every child spawn regardless — so a
daemon's CHILDREN are protected from the moment this bundle runs, whatever
the daemon itself still holds; HOME/USER/LANG/PATH from the daemon's own environment
survive, because remote daemons run under launchd/systemd with an env the
server never sees. Gates: test-agentd-session (a real daemon born from the
real `_spawnLocal` under the secret — daemon environ clean, a pty child AND a
pipe-session child see 0 secret lines with a canary proving the read; a
daemon spawned BY HAND holding the secret — the previous-life shape — whose
children still see nothing; the PRE-FIX bundle, `...process.env` as the base,
handing it straight down as the control that makes the leg red-capable; the
keep-set derivation; the three wiring pins) + test-integration-registry §6(h)
(the HOLDERS census: no `env: process.env` / `env: { ...process.env` literal
in src/agentd/{client,agentd}.js, with both retired spellings as controls) +
test-architecture (PURE set).

### src/secret-box.js (SHARED)

THE ONE at-rest encryption primitive, N key files (design §14.7, decision 24).
`secretBox(keyFile)` is a factory: mounts keeps `data/.mounts-key`
byte-for-byte, the integrations store gets `data/.integrations-key`, the
channels token store (P1) gets `data/.channels-key`. A key file is a
per-STORE blast radius — moving one is an irreversible data-loss path, and a
corrupted or rotated key must never take a second store with it. The
ciphertext is BYTE-IDENTICAL to mounts' former inline `_enc`/`_dec`
(aes-256-gcm, `iv.tag.data` as three base64 segments): test-secret-box's
PARITY leg encrypts with a patched copy of the pre-fix bytes and decrypts with
the box, and the reverse, so nothing an older build stored needs re-encrypting.

**THE DEFECT IT MUST NOT INHERIT (read off `src/mounts.js:360-367`, not
assumed):** mounts' `_key()` wrapped `readFileSync` in a BARE catch and minted
a fresh key on ANY read failure — right for exactly one errno, ENOENT; for
EACCES, EMFILE, EIO, a truncated or emptied file it OVERWROTE the key and
every stored ciphertext became undecryptable for ever, silently. Hidden only
because the file is 0600, owned by the service and rarely read; fd
exhaustion, a read-only mount or a crash mid-write all reach it. The box
creates the key ONLY on ENOENT; every other errno is a TYPED `SecretBoxError`
(`key-unreadable` / `key-malformed` — a 64-hex check, because an emptied file
is NOT a fresh key / `bad-ciphertext`) that a caller renders as "the key file
could not be read", the OPPOSITE sentence from "nothing configured"; it writes
tmp + `link(2)` (EEXIST refuses to clobber, so two minters land on ONE key)
with a rename-into-absence fallback, 0600, and never overwrites an existing
key file. The standing negative control is the bare-catch copy itself: on an
injected EACCES it mints, and the old ciphertext stops decrypting.
**`describeJsonError(e)` (r2, 2026-09-14)** lives here because it is the same
discipline one layer up: V8's `SyntaxError.message` quotes the source around
the error position, so logging `e.message` for a mistyped secret-bearing JSON
env printed the tail of the secret (six characters of a 40-char cluster key,
where masking permits four); the helper answers the class + the position
when V8 states one and never a quoted fragment, and BOTH readers of such an
env (the integrations store's cluster block and `MountManager.drivePresets`'
OAuth client presets) log it. Gate: scripts/test-secret-box.mjs (40; ⑦ = the
retired `e.message` carrying the tail as the control).

### src/channel-filter.js

src/channel-filter.js — PURE (imports only channel-record for the frame neutering; bundled into the editor like channel-caps) THE FILTER + THE ASSIGNMENT MODEL + WHAT AN AGENT IS HANDED (design §7, P2): `RULE_KINDS` a CLOSED set of eight, `matchRecord` → `{hit, why[]}` where **`why` IS A CONTRACT** (the wake and the panel show the same string — a wake that cannot say why cannot be tuned), `estimate` HONEST about its window (`sampled` = the reader's cap, `truncated` = a corpus shorter than the window, rated over the span it saw), `validateAssignment`/`authorityCap`/`effectiveAuthority` = `authority:'send'` capped by TWO facts that only narrow (channel policy requires review; `offers()` says no) and CLAMPED AT READ TIME so a stored value never silently becomes a permission, `pickRoundRobin` (no live member ⇒ null, never "wake them all"), `paceVerdict` (the per-assignment daily cap = PACING; only wakes that happened count), `renderWakeBlock`/`renderDigestBlock` (≤6 records, ≤400 chars, byte-budgeted, every vendor line QUOTED and frame-inert so an outsider cannot forge a heading or a `<system-reminder>` in an agent's context). ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### src/channel-policy.js

src/channel-policy.js — PURE (imports only channel-record; bundled into the Outbox card) THE OUTBOX POLICY (design §9, P3): the proposal state machine (every transition names its actor; `unknown` leaves only through reconcile — a lost outcome is NEVER auto-retried), `decideOutbound` (guards stack ON the channel policy and only TIGHTEN it; unknown policy / unparseable guard ⇒ review; off-hours is OFF without a zone, never guessed), the §9.3 receipt with sentAs / identityMarking / identityMarkingText. **P4:** `sending→unknown` also by `boot`; `honestyLine`/`withHonestyLine` (OFF by default, agent drafts only); `canReconcile` (`none` cannot be asked) + `reconcileVerdict` (landed ⇒ sent / not-landed ⇒ failed / else stay). ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### src/channel-acl.js

src/channel-acl.js — PURE (imports only msg-acl) AGENT REACH (design §8, P3): hidden < requestable < visible, everything hidden by default, MAX over grants, widen-only, ONE row per (principal, scope, origin) so unassign removes only its own row, a request approval = exactly one visible grant, the uniform not-found (hidden ≡ nonexistent). ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

src/integration-registry.js — PURE (imports nothing; bundled into the browser AND required by the server store) THE table of integration rows (design §14.2, P0b): `{id, label, fields[{key,label,secret,required,placeholder,help,validate}], clusterEnv{json,prefix} | delegate{to:'drive-presets',prefer,multi}, setup{callbackUrl,callbackNote,prerequisites}, test{kind,describe,caveat}, consumers, wiredIn?, docs}` for `fake` (the test adapter's own row — user > cluster > none walked end to end in P0 with a real consumer and a real setup block), `lark`, `gmail` (DELEGATING to the existing `VIBESPACE_GDRIVE_CLIENTS` presets, `prefer:'channels'`, `multi:true`, NO env of its own — decision 5) and `cloak`. Nothing here is a setting. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md **r0 rebase onto 2.369.130 (2026-09-21): the five `cloud:*` rows declare every label / help / describe / caveat through `i18nKey(…)` like every other row (the a3 i18n census renders them on the Integrations surface; zh + ja entries beside them) and their helps no longer append TRIM_NOTE; a WIRED row whose consumer has not registered a runner in THIS process answers the store's `no-test-runner` 501 — test-integration-registry's harness boots no browser wiring, so its cloak leg pins that wording while its §804 leg proves the six runners through the real store.**

### oauth-loopback.js

oauth-loopback.js — SHARED (http+crypto+the PURE registry) THE ONE consent-flow machine, DUAL-MODE (design §12.4, P1): `ephemeral` (Gmail — `listen(0)`, redirect_uri the bare loopback origin, exactly gmail-sync's flow) / `fixed` (Lark — the registry's `LARK_CALLBACK_URL` IMPORTED never spelled, the port bound ONLY for one flow, `EADDRINUSE` = a NAMED `port-busy` refusal that falls straight through to PASTE-BACK, which needs no port at all); the two gmail-sync `state` checks carried VERBATIM (handler + `forwardCallback`), one exchange per flow, released on completion/cancel/timeout; a vendor's consent URL and token exchange are the CALLER's functions. ### channels/lark.js

channels/lark.js — ORCH (design §6.3/§12.1/§13, P1a) THE LARK / 飞书 READ adapter behind the §4 contract: a USER token minted by the loopback's FIXED mode (the registry's callback URL, imported never spelled), `im/v1/chats` discovery (paged), `im/v1/messages` per tracked chat NEWEST-FIRST paging TO THE STORED ANCHOR across several `history()` calls of one pass (both `page_token`/`next_page_token` spellings; a fresh chat takes `FIRST_INGEST_MAX`=200 and re-anchors on the newest; an anchor the vendor no longer serves is read PAST and SAID, never an endless incomplete pass), every `msg_type` to plain text, `@_user_N` ordinals, attachments as METADATA. `auth.state()` is four-valued with the credential question FIRST — it takes `resolveIntegration('lark')` as an INPUT (never `process.env`), so a withdrawn app credential is `needs-credentials` however fresh the token, a dead/refused refresh token is `needs-reauth` (`invalidGrantAt` stamped ON the token record so a dead grant is not retried every pass). Typed failures from Lark's own codes (auth/rate/forbidden/not-found/transport). `OPTIONS` = `brand` (feishu|lark, `rebuild:true` — every host follows it). `integrationTest` = the `credential-exchange` runner (one tenant_access_token per brand; the row's caveat rides beside the verdict). `EGRESS` declares its four hosts for test-channels-egress. `caps.sendAs` = [] (P4), **`receive:'push'` since P1b — the `live` half is src/channels/live/lark.js (the official SDK's long connection, built in `create()` from the adapter's own credential resolver + normalizer).** **P4 (send):** `sendAs ['user']`, convCaps NARROWS to [] with `send-scope-not-granted` until BOTH dotted send scopes are held; `uuid` = the proposal id (hashed past 50), a lost answer is `detail.lost`; reconcile scans the chat then re-issues the SAME uuid inside the hour; `identityMarking` stays `unknown` until one real send's sender_type is read (§21 item 3). **2026-09-22:** every `resolveIntegration('lark', {credentialKey})` carries THE ACCOUNT's key (`deps.credentialKey`, else the live record's) so consent, refresh, status and Test name ONE tenant app; `auth.state()` carries `credentialKey`/`whyCode`. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### channels/gmail.js

channels/gmail.js — ORCH (design §6.3/§12.2/§14.2, P1a) THE GMAIL READ adapter — the DELEGATING row: the OAuth client comes from `resolveIntegration('gmail')` which resolves through the existing `VIBESPACE_GDRIVE_CLIENTS` presets (decision 5: `prefer:'channels'`; on a cluster-only two-preset env `org1`+`channels` with no `'default'` it answers `cluster/channels` and connects END TO END). EPHEMERAL loopback flow (gmail-sync's parameters verbatim, refresh_token required), a CONVERSATION IS A THREAD under the include query (`OPTIONS.query`, default `label:INBOX`, read LIVE off the record), ONE memoised `history.list?startHistoryId&historyTypes=messageAdded` per pass (nothing changed = one request; 404 = RESEED from the profile and walk every tracked thread once; a thread the vendor no longer serves is SKIPPED and said, never a frozen pass), the mailbox cursor IN MEMORY ON PURPOSE (it is mailbox-wide and only provably safe to advance once every named thread was walked — untracked ones never are), `threads.get?format=full` paged oldest-first past the anchor, the MIME tree to plain text (first text/plain, else stripped HTML, else the snippet), `identityMarking:'marked'` at `raw-headers`. `invalid_grant` on refresh is stamped ⇒ `needs-reauth`. `integrationTest` = `shape-only` (ZERO network; a Google client cannot be exchanged for anything alone). `EGRESS` declares its four hosts. **P1b: `receive:'push'` + `pushOptIn:true` — the Pub/Sub pull lane (src/channels/live/gmail.js) is OFF until `push.enabled === true`; `OPTIONS` gained `pushTopic`/`pushSubscription` (`relive:true` = restarts the LANE only); enabling adds the pubsub scope to the NEXT consent.** **P4 (send):** `sendAs ['user']` behind `gmail.send`; `idempotency two-phase` = drafts.create (the handle via `onHandle` BEFORE the send) → drafts.send, threading headers off the anchor's Message-ID; reconcile = draft still exists ⇒ never sent (discarded) / our SENT message in the thread ⇒ landed / else unknown. **2026-09-22:** every `resolveIntegration('gmail', {credentialKey})` carries THE ACCOUNT's key (`deps.credentialKey`, else the live record's) so consent, refresh, status and Test name ONE OAuth client — two Gmail accounts under two presets refresh with their own client ids; `auth.state()` carries `credentialKey`/`whyCode`. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### channels/live/lane.js + live/lark.js + live/gmail.js

channels/live/lane.js + live/lark.js + live/gmail.js — ORCH (design §6.4 / fence 11 / decisions 18+20, P1b) THE PUSH LANES: `lane.js` = the vendor-free CORE (liveness is POSITIVE evidence; THE ACK IS THE RETURN — a transport acks only after the engine's `onEvent()` resolved, which is after the record is durable; `stop()` is TERMINAL for an arm in flight — a connect landing after it is closed on the spot and `event()` answers `{ok:false, why:'stopped'}` WITHOUT calling the engine so the vendor redelivers; single-use; `err.permanent` ⇒ a named `unavailable` park); `live/lark.js` = the SDK long connection, required LAZILY (missing = `sdk-not-installed`, never a boot crash), the v2 event mapped to the REST item shape and the handler THROWING on a stopped lane (the app's view, not the user's — a chat the bot is not in is what the measurement demotes); `live/gmail.js` = `users.watch` (renewed daily) + a Pub/Sub PULL of THIS instance's subscription, a pulled note = a CURSOR KICK never mail, scope/options refused by name. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### server/integration-store.js + server/integrations-wiring.js + routes/integrations.js

**2.369.165 (integrations chunk 2): an account-bound row is not a card — `list()` omits it, every card verb `404 binds-per-account`, `own` retired, `presetsFor` / `legacyOwnValues`; full text under the (ORCH) heading above.**
 **2.369.147 r3: `offeredCredentials(id)` ALWAYS lists `own` with `available` + `missing`; the engine's `assertOffered` refuses an unavailable key as 409 needs-credentials (never a silent preset).**
server/integration-store.js + server/integrations-wiring.js + routes/integrations.js — ORCH (design §14.3/§14.4, P0b): `data/integrations.json` (writeJsonAtomic) holds `values` (secrets through secret-box on `data/.integrations-key`) + `clusterKey` and NOTHING else — **`source` is DERIVED at read time, never stored**, and a cluster default's VALUES are read from the env at the moment of the question and never copied to disk (rotate the Secret ⇒ every consumer follows; inject-then-withdraw ⇒ `none` WITH the reason, never the old value). THE ONLY reader of `VIBESPACE_INTEGRATIONS` (JSON) and `VIBESPACE_INTEGRATION_<ID>_<FIELD>` (single-field; JSON wins, said once; unparseable = "no default", never a crash); the delegating gmail row resolves through the INJECTED `MountManager.drivePresets` with a saved `clusterKey` over `prefer` and a vanished saved key ⇒ `none` naming it. `resolveIntegration(id)` is the consumers' call and the only thing that leaves with plaintext (the channels engine hands it to every adapter and re-asks `auth.state()` on `onChange` — a withdrawn credential flips the ADAPTERS row to `needs-credentials`, not only the card); `publicView(id)` is THE one masked view every route + the `integrations-updated` broadcast carry. `clearUserValues` (DELETE, always) and `useClusterDefault` (PUT `{use:'cluster'}`, a NAMED refusal without a default) are TWO functions; `setClusterKey` stores the selector only; `test(id)` constructs NO vendor request — the CONSUMER registers the runner (the fake's fixture switch; lark/gmail/cloak = named `not-wired`), one in flight, 15 s, human-triggered only (censused). An unreadable key file is a TYPED `storeError`, never "nothing configured". The named twin: frp's relay token stays in its plugin card (§14.6). Routes: GET/GET one/PUT/POST test/DELETE behind the cookie auth; no route returns a secret's plaintext or calls `resolveIntegration` (pinned). Wiring = one `create(deps)` stanza in server.js (+4 lines). **r2 (2026-09-14): ONLY ENOENT MEANS "FRESH" — an unreadable existing store file is a TYPED `store-unreadable` (500) on every view/`list()`, logged once per transition, never cached, refused by every writer through `assertWritable()` (the former bare catch cached an empty state and the next unrelated write destroyed every stored credential); a not-a-store file is ARCHIVED as `integrations.json.corrupt-<ts>` first; the named twin `src/mounts.js _load()` is NOT fixed here. A non-delegating row's vanished saved `'default'` re-binds to the env's ONLY preset (`rebindSingle`, said in `why`); the mistyped-env log goes through `describeJsonError`.** **r3 (2026-09-15): a user secret the CURRENT key file cannot open NEVER falls through to the cluster — while any stored field is undecryptable the row answers `none` with the reason naming the fields (consumers included), `hasOwnValues` is a fact about the RECORD (Clear my keys shows; DELETE lands on the cluster because the user decided), the view carries a per-row `storeError {code:'values-undecryptable', message: <remedy>, fields}` (store-level codes outrank it), logged once per row per transition; and `envFieldName` lives HERE, the one resolver, censused out of every other file.** **THE ACCOUNT KEY (2026-09-22):** `resolveIntegration(id, {credentialKey})` — `cluster:<k>` INDEXES the preset list (`clusterPresetsFor`, factored out of `clusterDefaultFor`; a key the env stopped offering answers `none`/`preset-gone` naming it, NEVER another preset), `own` = the user's saved values alone (`own-missing` when absent), an unknown key `unknown-credential`, no key = today's precedence with `credentialKey` (the key a NEW account would be stamped with) on the answer; `offeredCredentials(id)` = the presets as `cluster:<k>` + `own` only while the values are complete and readable (key + label only); `test(id, {credentialKey})` probes one account's key. ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### server/migrations.js

**`2026-09-channel-custom-client-inline` (2.369.165, integrations chunk 2).** Calls the engine's `inlineLegacyClients()` (the SAME copy the engine runs reader-side): every `own` account's saved client re-sealed under `.channels-key` onto its record, stamped `custom` after the write; a failure (e.g. `integration-key-missing`) FAILS the run by name and the record keeps `own`; no engine + an `own` record ⇒ fails by name; a fresh instance is a dry run. Gate: test-migrations (idempotent twice, the write order, reader-side, the missing key, the pre-r4 engine as the control).

**`2026-09-backfill-ledger-by-slot` (B-f69c ②, 2.369.163).** Runs src/ledger-slot-backfill.js over the instance's own stores (slot transitions, members and roster read off disk — no AccountManager exists yet), logs ONE `[migrate] ledger-by-slot:` line, returns `{rows, candidates, rekeyed, archived, untouched, confirmed, corrective, relearned}` for the ledger's report row and files one info notice when a row moved. server.js's post-migration `usageHistory.reloadEvents()` already covers a shard rewritten in place. Since quota r2 the returned counts are the WHOLE repair (`report.total` — a pass that resumes a crashed one counts both, `resumed: true` + `thisPass`), and the notice is filed on those totals, so a retry that finds only the remainder (or nothing) still says what was repaired. Since quota r3 that includes a retry after a FINISHED pass whose id the runner never recorded (killed between the marker and migrations.json): it states the marker's totals (`recovered: true`).

server/migrations.js — the instance's one-shot migration REGISTRY (2.328.0) through src/migration-runner.js (ledger-keyed, run at most once, failed = retry next boot, never block); `create({rootDir, serverNotice, homeDir, channels})` — `channels` (2026-09-22) is the CHANNELS ENGINE handle, because `data/channels/adapters.json` has ONE writer (the engine's serialized door) and a migration reshaping an adapter record must go through it, never a second store instance; `2026-09-channel-credential-key` stamps every legacy adapter record via `engine.stampCredentialKeys()` with the client its OWN TOKEN names when this instance still offers it (evidence `token` — a Gmail token records the preset key it was exchanged under), else its integration's CURRENT pick (evidence `row-pick`, what refreshed it until now), the [migrate] line naming the evidence per record (a record whose token names nothing offered and whose integration resolves to nothing stays unstamped; without an engine a legacy real record FAILS the run by name so a later boot retries it). ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

**`2026-09-spend-notices-expire` (2.369.152) + `userTodos`.** `create({…, userTodos})` takes the LIVE UserTodoManager (or a getter) — server.js builds it long before the migrations run and holds the file in memory, so the row reshapes through `userTodos.reshapeItems()` (one save, one broadcast) and then calls the store's synchronous `flush()` on BOTH paths — the live store's save is a 500 ms debounce, and the atomic write must land BEFORE the runner records `applied[id]` (a crash in between would otherwise lose the reshaping with the ledger saying it ran; verifier LOW-1); with none (a suite, a boot without the inbox) it builds a PRIVATE manager on the same file with `expirySweepMs: 0`, flushes it through the store's own tmp+rename writer and stops it before returning; no file on disk = `store: 'absent'`, nothing created. The rule: `sessionName === 'Spending' && sessionKey === 'accounts'` — the name spend-guard's one `fileInbox` freezes on every item it files; on the owner's store it selects exactly the same 19 records as the text rule (/unattended turns|VibeSpace refused/ + by agent + accounts) and, unlike a text rule, survives a rewording. Every match becomes `kind: 'notice'` (resolved ones too — their status/resolvedAt/resolvedBy untouched — so a later ↺ reopens a notice, not an action); an OPEN match without `expiresAt` gets the end of the window it was ABOUT, through spend-guard's own `noticeExpiry(about, createdAt)` — `about` read from the detail spend-guard wrote (`Scope: hour` ⇒ +1 h, `Scope: day|instance` ⇒ +24 h, a `Refusal:` line ⇒ +6 h, none ⇒ +24 h, the longest window any spend notice talks about): an end already past ⇒ resolved `done`/`expired` with `resolvedAt` = THAT END (when it should have died — never the upgrade boot, so the retirements sort as old history instead of filling the popup's Recently-resolved slots; verifier LOW-2), kept, never deleted; an end still ahead ⇒ stamped as its `expiresAt`. Measured on a copy of the owner's store (876 items): 19 matched, 17 re-kinded, 13 retired (ends 1 h / 6 h / 24 h after filing), 2 fresh stamped (1 h, 6 h), 857 byte-identical, a second run a no-op. It RETURNS `{matched, rekinded, expired, stamped, store}` and the shared runner (src/migration-runner.js, since 2.369.152) records a plain-object return under `ledger.reports[id] = {at, …}` beside the `applied[id]` timestamp (which stays a number — every reader tests it for truth). Gate: test-migrations (live store — the FILE carries the change when run() returns / private store / absent / run-at-most-once / the scope-derived ends / controls = the registry without the row keeps 14 badge actions, and a patched copy with the flush behind `if (priv)` leaves the file unchanged with the ledger row written until the debounce fires).

### channel-outbox.js + channel-reach-editor.js

**a3 i18n (2026-09-18):** the card words the server's `outcome` STRUCTURE (PURE `channel-policy.outcomeOf` → `outcomeText`, one sentence per `kind` with the adapter's/vendor's verbatim INSIDE it) and never prints `p.reason` — that string is the agent's contract (receipt, CLI, the outbox suite pins it), so the a1 "same sentence twice" card is gone; a reconcile refusal is a `code` (`reconcileWhyText`), the receipt's `lane` a code (`deliveryLaneText`), a rejection's default reason the exported `REJECTED_DEFAULT_REASON` constant (never a magic string compared in the client); the reach dialog words `policy.mode` through `tc('policy', …)` (`review` is also the code-review status elsewhere) and names a Task Group by its `title` (`groupTitle` — the store has no `name`, so every group showed as its id).

**a4 UI (2026-09-21, design-communication-panel-ui.md §4.2/§4.3):** the card is FIVE lines — head (state pill 9/700 sentence-case · drafter · age) → the text (or the editor) → ONE `.chan-prop-meta` line (why · the policy verdict · "Will send as" · expiry · the sender line) → the identity warning ONCE with the alert glyph, only when it warns and only while the card still has an Approve (honesty is owed to the one pressing it; a decided card keeps the identity FACT on its meta line) → the outcome sentence → a quiet `.chan-prop-foot` (reconcile facts, the receipt) → actions RIGHT-aligned as reject · edit · approve with ONE `mounts-btn-primary` (`data-reject` / `data-edit` / `data-approve` — suites click by attribute, never by position; the reject box opens under the row, Enter submits); state colour = meaning — awaiting accent, sent green, failed red, UNKNOWN amber (the one state §9.4 says is not a failure), rejected/expired neutral; the inline section shows the cards that need the user (awaiting, then unknown/failed) plus the newest two decided ones with "{n} more in the Outbox" / "Open the Outbox"; the Outbox window is a `jobs-toolbar` (summary + an Awaiting | All segment, the store picks the first view) over cards — Awaiting = the queue, All = grouped by STATE with a 6px dot per head so an unknown outcome is never buried under sent ones; the reach dialog is ONE bordered list (who 12px with the kind dim · a neutral level pill — never the panel's green, which means live · the origin dim · × for the user's own rows), a grant that carries no name is named from the roster (an assignment's grant is `{kind,id}` only), the add row a 3-column grid, an open request a bordered block with Deny · Approve; the filter editor pairs its short fields on a two-column grid (On / Deliver, Authority / Wakes per day), rule rows carry their OWN kind selector + ×, Add rule sits under the list, and the estimate is ONE bold stat with its honesty (`sampled` / `truncated` / the measured rate) as the hint line under it; the receipt-wake checkbox is a house `dialog-check-row`; every dialog of the family is `.chan-dialog` (one 520px width token).

channel-outbox.js + channel-reach-editor.js — CLIENT (design §8 / §9.2 / §9.5, P3): ONE approval-card renderer for the inline section of a conversation window AND the singleton Outbox window (`channel-outbox` type, ⚙ row, panel button carrying the awaiting count) — identity row + the identityMarking warning (`unknown` as loud as `marked`), the policy's reasons, edit/approve/reject, the receipt-delivery line, `unknown` says it is never retried; the Reach & policy dialog = every grant WITH its origin (only user rows removable), open access requests approve/deny, the policy select. **P4:** the "A sender line will be appended" note BEFORE approval, the "Checked N× — last answer" line, Check outcome only where `canReconcile`; the panel row's Sender line switch + the observed-identity line. **r3: a proposal that `wakes` says "Approving wakes this agent: 1 billed turn" and Approve echoes `expectWakes`.** ⇒ kb-file-structure.md

### src/lib/terminal.js — NET ZOOM 1 under the UI scale (2.369.118)

xterm.js maps the pointer by `clientX - rect.left` (ZOOMED px under `document.body.style.zoom`, the "UI scale (DPI)" setting) over a cell size it measured in LAYOUT px (`TextMetricsMeasureStrategy`, canvas `measureText`), so under a body zoom a drag at row 20 selected row 20×scale (measured on the real build: 1.25 → 25, 0.8 → 16; userW inc-mu92zsgw-6c9y). The fix is inc-mtdrm922's rule (the VNC canvas): `.terminal-container` gets `style.zoom = COUNTER_ZOOM` (`calc(1 / var(--ui-scale, 1))`, the ONE definition in utils.js, re-exported by vnc-view.js) and the xterm font size is the VISUAL px × `uiScale()` through `_xtermPx` — the constructor's option, `applyOverride('fontSize')`, `rescale()` (called by app.js `_refitAllTerminals` on a scale change) and app.js's global font-size row (through `applyOverride`) all go through it; a raw `options.fontSize = n` is 1/scale too small. Nothing visible changes (screen within 3 %); FitAddon's grid is computed in the container's own px so cols are unchanged (rows ±1 from line-height rounding at fractional sizes). Gates: test-terminal-ui-scale (fast pins, enumerates the writers) + test-terminal-zoom-select (heavy chrome: the pre-fix page vs the fixed page under real CDP drags).

### src/harness-settings.js — THE DECLARED HARNESS SETTINGS TABLES (PURE, docs/design-harness-settings.zh.md §2, 2.369.123)

**2.369.157 — `codex.limitResetCredit` = `off | ask | auto` (default `off`, never auto by default; docs/design-reset-credits.zh.md §3).** `ask` files ONE For-you decision per limit event when the verdict says a credit is worth it; `auto` consumes it through the spend ceiling; WHEN is src/reset-credit.js's call and the ladder forks by warmth. The description states both vendors' mechanics (a consumed credit re-opens the window; Claude's web reset refills in place, the weekly reset unchanged). THE CLAUDE TABLE HAS NO SUCH ROW, deliberately: this table cannot express a declared-but-disabled row (every row is a working control — the settings law), and Claude Code offers only the interactive `/limit-reset`; the greyed control with its reason belongs to p2's Manage-Agents button, not here. test-harness-settings names the change against the 2.369.120 snapshot (`CHANGED_SINCE`, options + description only) and has a control that the snapshot's vocabulary refuses `ask`.

PURE (imports nothing; CJS so the SAME file is bundled into the browser, required by the server and carried by the daemon bundle). `HARNESS_SETTINGS = { claude, codex, opencode }`, each `{ prefix, category, files: { <id>: {rel, format} }, rows: [ROW] }`. A ROW is pure data — `key, type (boolean|number|string|text|enum), default, options, min/max/step, combobox, label, description, apply` — and its persisted path is `settingPath(prefix, key)` = `${prefix}.${key}`, **byte-identical to the old literal schema keys**, so data/settings.json needs no migration. `apply` is the CLOSED union: `{kind:'spawn', how, via?, live?, mode?}` (consumed by `adapter.buildSessionArgs` as `opts.settings.<key>`, or through the named top-level field when `via` is set — model/effort/permissionMode/extraArgs/outputStyle ride ws-create's resume ladder; `how` is DISPLAY TEXT, never the transport; `live` = the adapter verb the server writes to every running chat session of that harness on change; `mode` restricts to chat|terminal), `{kind:'server', how}` (read at a decision point through `harnessSetting()`), `{kind:'cli-config', file, path, off, onUninstall}` (written INTO the harness's own config file; a value equal to `off` is NOT written and never deleted). `checkTable(table, ctx)` is THE validator (type in the closed set, enum default among its options, no functions in a row, ≤50 rows, cli-config `file` ∈ `files` AND ∈ the descriptor's `configFiles` with the SAME `rel` object, read-only file refused by name, toml path `[section,key]|[key]` bare names + string/boolean/integer rows only, `off` required, `onUninstall` keep|strip, `rel` without `..`/separators, prefix = the descriptor's, a contributed table only its own id and never a built-in prefix); `coerce(row, raw)` = THE typed read (the row's default for unset/unreadable — the 36500 that lived twice; numbers clamped to min/max; booleans strict; **an `enum` row's domain IS its options (2026-09-21, verifier r7): a value outside them falls back to the row default — checkTable guarantees the default is listed — EXCEPT a `combobox` row, whose options are suggestions and whose typed value is the point. The old "closed vocabularies are validated where they become argv" was only true of argv: a cli-config row's value reached config.toml unchecked, codex 0.154.0 refuses to load an unknown `history.persistence` variant, and every receipt said ✓ applied while the prelude fanned `bogus` out to every remote host**; `refusedValue(row, raw)` names the dropped string so the ORCH half can warn at every sync); `checkRel` is exported (its TWIN lives in harness-config.js — the helper embeds that file's text alone; test-harness-settings §6b pins the two texts identical); `buildConfigPlan(specs)` = the plan `{v:1, files:[{harness, id, rel, format, createIfMissing, hooks?, set:[{key, path, value, onUninstall}]}]}`. `GENERIC_LEGACY_KEYS.autoResumeOnLimit = 'claude.autoResumeOnLimit'` — the one generic feature under a legacy `claude.` spelling, deliberately NOT a row (auto-resume is generic; the key stays because every per-session override is recorded against it), read by NAME so the server never spells a harness literal. **The codex `historyPersistence` row (the ONE managed config.toml row, owner D4)** carries its 0.154.0 evidence in the row comment: the binary's resolved-config template embeds `[history]` / `persistence = "save-all"` (5×), the `HistoryPersistence` struct name and the "(Session persistence is disabled; cannot …" branch; default 'save-all' (VibeSpace enforces rollouts persist), '' = leave config.toml alone. Gates: test-harness-settings §1/§2, test-harness-contract (identity + spawn conformance), test-architecture §46.

**2.369.155 — `claude.autoContinueAtUsageLimit` (boolean, default false, `apply:{kind:'spawn', how:'--settings autoContinueAtUsageLimit=false (while off)'}`).** Claude Code's own wait-and-continue at a usage limit, spawned OFF (owner ruling 2026-09-22). What it changes is PER MODE: chat sessions never run the CLI's continue (non-interactive launch — piped stdout), so there the row changes nothing and VibeSpace's auto-resume is the only producer; terminal sessions did run it and it was their ONLY automatic continue, so OFF leaves them stopped at a wall for the user (the row description says exactly this — pinned by test-fallback-policy §5b). A SPAWN row, deliberately not cli-config: the CLI reads the key from policy > `--settings` > user settings, and writing `~/.claude/settings.json` would also switch it off for the user's own non-VibeSpace sessions. Value ON = pass nothing (Claude Code's own setting governs). Coerce is the strict boolean (the string "true" is not on). The adapter consumes it (see the src/adapters/claude-code.js spawn-flags essay); test-harness-settings §3 pins the row, test-harness-contract proves it changes the spawn.

### src/harness-config.js — THE SHARED CLI-CONFIG APPLIER (fs/path/os only; design §6, 2.369.123)

ONE implementation of "write these managed keys (and our hook entries) into a harness's own config file" for EVERY machine: required by the server for device #0 and **embedded as FILE TEXT into the shipped `data/bin/vibespace-hook-register.mjs`** (createRequire mints its `require`; never `Function.toString` — a closure reference would become a free identifier, the 2.340.2/2.341.1 lost-binding class), so it must never use `__dirname`/`__filename`, never require ORCH, and every export must survive evaluation inside a function body. `cliConfigFile(spec, {createIfMissing})` = the descriptor-side file object over a table's `files.<id>` entry (the SAME `rel` array — one spelling — plus `file()` and the create policy); `writeJsonManaged(file, {createIfMissing}, mutate)` = the CAS writer moved verbatim out of agent-tool-generators (read → mutate → compare-and-swap re-read → tmp+rename; invalid JSON refused by name and never overwritten; a missing file created only when the plan says so and NEVER its directory — a missing `~/.codex` means codex is not installed; **it re-serialises the WHOLE file** — 2-space JSON + trailing newline, `\uXXXX` escapes decoded, exactly as Claude Code itself rewrites settings.json — so "only the touched line" is the TOML writer's promise, not this one's); **THE BYTES LAND ON THE REAL FILE (2026-09-21, verifier r7 — both writers share `readManaged` / `writeTarget` / `commitWrite`):** a symlinked config (the dotfiles pattern, `~/.codex/config.toml → dotfiles/codex.toml`) is written THROUGH — the tmp file goes beside the link's real target and the rename lands on the target, so the link survives and the dotfile keeps governing (before, a tmp+rename on the link path replaced it with a regular file at every boot, remote install, ssh-spawn prelude and dial spawn, receipts ✓); a dangling link is refused by name, never replaced; an existing-but-unreadable path (a directory, EACCES) is refused rather than "created" over; the file's own mode survives the rename (a 0600 config.toml carrying MCP tokens stays 0600 — chmod on the tmp beats the umask; a new file takes the umask's mode). `checkRel(rel)` — a TWIN of harness-settings.checkRel, text-identical (this file cannot require the PURE one) — re-checks every plan `rel` at `applyConfigPlan` / `readConfigPlan` (a `..`, separator or `~` segment ⇒ a `refused` receipt naming it and NOTHING joined under $HOME; `files[].file` null) and `decodePlan` drops such a plan whole (the helper then applies its hooks-only DEFAULT_PLAN). `findOurHookIn` / `registerHookEntries(root, events, hookCmd)` / `stripHookEntries(root, events)` = the hook-entry mutators the server's ensureAgentHooks/stripAgentHookEntries AND the remote helper share (the helper's private copy of the event table is gone — the plan's `hooks.events` carries it). **The TOML setter** `tomlSet(text, section, key, value)` → `{text, changed} | {refused}`: a conservative line tokenizer (blank | `[table]` | `[[aot]]` | `key = value` | opaque lines inside a multi-line string or multi-line array; anything else = refuse), edits ONE line — replaces the value in place keeping indentation/spacing/the trailing comment, or inserts `key = value` after the section's last key line, or replaces the dotted `section.key = …` spelling in place when the file already uses it, or appends `[section]` + the line at the end (top-level keys go after the last root key, before the first header) — string (basic-string escaped) / boolean / safe-integer values only, byte-identical output when the value is already there (idempotent), CRLF preserved; REFUSES BY NAME an inline table (`section = {…}` or the value itself), an array of tables, a multi-line string, an array/float/date value, a duplicate key, a `[section.key]` sub-table where the key should be, **a root scalar named like the section (`history = 5` — appending `[history]` after it is a duplicate key; codex 0.154.0 refuses the file), and a table defined BOTH by dotted root keys and a `[section]` header (already invalid TOML — never reported applied)**; dotted root keys alone (`history.max_bytes = 5`, no header) get the new line in THAT spelling (`history.persistence = …` after the last such line) because a `[history]` header after them is the same duplicate-key refusal (2026-09-21, both orders verified on 0.154.0). `tomlGet` reads one scalar for the receipts. `writeTomlManaged(file, {createIfMissing}, sets)` = the same CAS + tmp+rename law (any refusal throws by name and nothing is written). `applyConfigPlan(plan, {home, hookCmd, uninstall})` → `{receipts, files}` (managed keys always; hook entries only with a `hookCmd` = the remote helper; `uninstall` strips ONLY hook entries, never a managed key — the retention a user asked for is not "our entry"); `readConfigPlan(plan, {home})` = READ-ONLY receipts (applied | differs(current) | missing | unreadable(reason)); `ensureCliConfig({plan, home})` = the design's name for the local apply; receipt lines `CFG|harness|key|state|current|want|reason` (the three free fields encodeURIComponent(JSON) so a `|`/newline in a value cannot shear a line; `CFG|*|*|unknown|` = an older helper, `no-node` = no interpreter) with `formatReceiptLines`/`parseReceiptLines`; `encodePlan`/`decodePlan` = base64 JSON (shell-safe bare, refuses a foreign `v`). Gates: test-harness-settings §5–§7 (+ §5b symlinks/modes/unreadable with the old-write CONTROL, §5c the duplicate-key shapes and the REAL codex loading every file the writer produces + the two broken-shape controls — evidence-SKIP without the binary, §6b the rel re-check at apply/read/decode + the checkRel twin pin), test-claude-retention §1–§4 (§2 also drives a symlinked settings.json and a `..` plan through the shipped helper).

### src/server/harness-config-sync.js — THE ORCH HALF (design §5/§6, 2.369.123)

`create({serverSetting, harnesses, adapterRegistry, activeSessions, hookRegistrationSafe, log, warn, home})` → `harnessSetting(id, key)` (typed; an undeclared key THROWS — a decision point asking a harness for a knob it never declared is a bug, not a false), `harnessDeclares(id, key)`, `harnessSpawnSettings(id)` (every spawn row → the `settings` bag ws-create hands `buildSessionArgs`), `cliConfigKeys()`, `cliConfigPlan({hooksOnly})` (built through the module-level `configPlanSpecs(harnessList, {valueOf, hooksOnly})` — ONE spelling shared with the generator's embedded hooks-only DEFAULT_PLAN; which file is ALSO the hook file is decided by IDENTITY `inject.hookFile === configFiles.<id>`), `cliConfigPlanB64()`, `syncCliConfig({reason})` (in-process apply on this machine — **guarded by `hookRegistrationSafe()`, which the old retention write did NOT honour: a /tmp worktree server could write the real HOME's settings.json**; first `warnRefusedValues()` names, safe or not, every cli-config enum row whose stored value is outside its options — `codex.historyPersistence = "bogus" is not one of ""|"save-all"|"none" — the default "save-all" rides instead` — the one visible trace of an API/import write the Settings window cannot produce), `cliConfigStatus()` (D2: FRESH receipts — every probe re-reads the target file; the last local write lives in memory only, with its reason, never persisted; `off` rows listed apart; `safe`), `onSettingsWrite(next, prev)` (any cli-config path changed ⇒ sync; any spawn row with a `live` verb changed ⇒ the verb is written to every running CHAT session with a pty of THAT harness whose adapter has the method — the old `sess.backend !== 'claude'` fallback loop generalised by adapter capability), `contributedTables()` (non-built-in harnesses' tables for /api/home). Literal harness ids are forbidden in this tier — every id arrives from a session, an account or the registry (test-architecture §46). Wired in server.js beside serverSetting; threaded to ws-create through the WS_CTX_CONTRACT (`harnessSetting/harnessDeclares/harnessSpawnSettings/cliConfigPlanB64`) and to the pool engine via deps (`limitResetCredit`, `disableModelFallback` read off `session.backend`). `createHookHelper()` generates `data/bin/vibespace-hook-register.mjs` (TRACKED, regenerated every boot — run the generator with the repo as rootDir before committing a template change): ESM host + `const require = createRequire(import.meta.url)` + the SHARED applier `src/harness-config.js` embedded from its FILE TEXT inside an IIFE with its own `module`/`exports`, an embedded hooks-only `DEFAULT_PLAN` (from `configPlanSpecs(listHarnesses(), {hooksOnly:true})`), then: default = `applyConfigPlan(plan, {home, hookCmd})` (our hook entries + managed keys, one `CFG|` receipt per key on stdout), `--status` = `readConfigPlan` (READ-ONLY; hosts.agentToolsStatus grep-gates on the env NAME so an older helper — which would treat `--status` as a registration RUN — is never asked), `--uninstall` = strip our hook entries only. ### src/lib/cli-config-chips.js — THE WORDING of a CLI-config receipt (PURE, DOM-free, `t` injected; design §4.3, 2.369.123)

`receiptLine(r, {t, where, lastWriteAt, now, remote})` → `{tone: ok|warn|bad|dim, text}` for one managed key on one machine (applied/unchanged = "✓ <where>: ~/file → key = value · written N min ago"; differs = "⚠ … is X (wanted Y) — written again at the next start or setting change" / on a remote host "…at the next tool install or session start on that machine"; missing = "? … not found — start the CLI once"; unreadable/refused = "⚠ … is not valid after a hand edit — not touched"; unknown = "? … not checked — reinstall the agent tools"; the `no-node` marker = "✗ node missing"), `offLine` ("Leaving the CLI's own value alone (~/file → key)"), `applyHead(apply)` (spawn: "Applies to new sessions · <how>" (+ terminal mode / running sessions follow); server: "Read by VibeSpace · <how>"; cli-config: "Written into the CLI config").
